And for you is half of what your wives leave, if they have no child; but if they have a child, then for you is a fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they bequeath or debt. And for them [wives] is a fourth of what you leave if you have no child; but if you have a child, then for them is an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you bequeath or debt.﴾ "And for them" means: and for the wives. ﴿And if a man leaves an estate to be inherited by kalalah, or a woman...﴾ The structure of the verse: "and if there is a man or a woman who is inherited by kalala." It is in the accusative as a verbal noun, and it is said to be a circumstantial accusative, and it is said to be the predicate of the passive form, its estimate being: "and if a man's wealth is inherited by kalala."

Al-Hasan and 'Isa read ﴿yuwarithu﴾ with a kasra on the ra', making it an active verb with him as subject.

They differed about kalala:
Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: it is the deceased. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the heirs. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: it is the property. They also differed on its meaning and its ruling:

It is narrated from Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about kalala, and he recited the end of Surat al-Nisa', and the questioner objected, so he (ﷺ) said: "I will not increase your knowledge until I am increased."[[Ta'wil Mukhtalif al-Hadith: 185 (with variation).]] [254]

Shu'ba narrated from 'Asim al-Ahwal, who said: I heard al-Sha'bi say: Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said concerning kalala: "I give a judgment on it; if it is correct, it is from Allah, and if it is wrong, it is from Satan and from me, and Allah is free of it: it is what is other than the father and the child." He said: then when 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) came after him, he said: "I am ashamed before Allah to contradict Abu Bakr: it is what is apart from the father and the child."

Tawus said: it is what is other than the child. Al-Hakam: it is what is other than the father. 'Atiyya: they are the maternal siblings. 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr: they are the paternal siblings. It is also said: they are the brothers and sisters.

Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah said: "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, only two sisters of mine are to inherit; so what about the inheritance?' Then there was revealed: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning kalala.﴾"

Al-Akhfash said: whoever is not inherited by a father or mother is kalala.

The people of language said: it is from "takallalahu al-nasab," when kinship surrounds someone like a crown (iklil).

Imru' al-Qays said:
"Do you see a lightning flash whose gleam I show you,
like the glimmer of two hands in a striped cloak?"

They were named kalala because they surround the deceased from his sides, yet they are neither of him nor is he of them, and their surrounding him is that they are related to him alongside.

Al-Farazdaq said:
"You inherited the spear of kingship, not as kalala,
from the two sons of Manaf, 'Abd Shams and Hashim."

Someone else said:
"The father of the man protects, and he has
a client of kalala who does not get angry."

﴿And he has a brother or a sister﴾: He did not say "and they two" (wa-lahuma), though the man and woman have been mentioned, following the custom of the Arabs: when they mention two names and then speak of them, they are equal in ruling; sometimes they attribute it to one of them, and sometimes to both together. One says: "Whoever has a boy and a girl, let him be good to him and to her, and to both of them; all of this is permissible." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is difficult﴾ and similar examples. He intended by this the brother and the sister from the mother's side, as is shown by the reading of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas: "And he has a brother or a sister from the mother," ﴿then for each one of them is a sixth. But if they are more than that, they are sharers in the third, equally among them, males and females alike, after any bequest that is bequeathed or debt.﴾

'Ali (peace be upon him) said: "You recite the bequest before the debt, but the Messenger of Allah began with the debt before the bequest."

This is the view of the majority of jurists; the meaning of the verse is joint, not sequential. ﴿Without causing harm﴾, bringing harm upon the heirs.

Al-Hasan said: this is to bequeath a debt that is not owed, ﴿as a directive from Allah.﴾

Al-A'mash recited: "without causing harm, a bequest from Allah," with idafa.

﴿And Allah is Knowing and Forbearing.﴾

Qatada said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, disliked harm during life and at death, forbade it, and decreed it. Harm is not proper in life or in death."

And in a report: "Whoever cuts off an inheritance, Allah will cut off his share in Paradise."
[[See: Kashf al-Khafa': 2/310.]]

﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾ up to His saying:

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verses 7–14 (part 1 of 2):

﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave﴾ — the verse, and the reason for its revelation: Aws ibn Thabit al-Ansari died and left a wife called Umm Kahha and three daughters by her. Two men, who were the cousins (sons of the paternal uncle) of the deceased and his executors, rose up. The scholars differ over their names. Al-Kalbi and Qatada said they were ʿArfaṭa, while others said they were Suwayd and ʿArfaja. They took his property and gave his wife and daughters nothing. In the Jahiliyya (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance) they did not give inheritance to women or to young children, even if they were male. They gave inheritance only to adult men, saying: "We give only to one who fights on horseback and is able to take part in the distribution." He said: Umm Kahha came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was in the Mosque of al-Faḍīḥ, and she said: "O Messenger of Allah, Aws ibn Thabit died and left me three daughters, and I am his wife. I have nothing with which to support them. Their father left good property, and it is in the hands of Suwayd and ʿArfaja. They have given me and his daughters nothing of the property, and the girls are in my care. They are not fed or given drink, and no attention is paid to them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned the two men, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, her sons do not ride horses, do not carry burdens, and do not strike an enemy." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: «Go away until I see what Allah will reveal to me concerning them.» [[Asbab al-Nuzul (The Occasions of Revelation): 96.]] [246] So they left, and Allah the Most High revealed this verse.

﴿For men﴾ means the males among the children of the deceased and his relatives. ﴿There is a share﴾ means a portion and a lot, a part of ﴿what the parents and close relatives leave﴾ as inheritance. The females also have a portion of the inheritance.

﴿Of what is little of it or much﴾ of the property, ﴿a share ordained﴾, a known and obligatory portion. Its parallel is in His saying: ﴿I will surely take from Your servants an ordained share﴾. [[Surat al-Nisa’: 118.]] The word ﴿a share﴾ is in the accusative because it comes in the manner of a verbal noun (maṣdar), like the saying of one speaker: "You have a right over me, a binding right," and "I have a dirham, a gifted one that has been received." This is the view of al-Farra’.

Abu ʿUbayda said: it is accusative by way of exit (khurūj). Al-Kisa’i said: it is accusative as a detachment (qaṭʿ). Al-Akhfash said: He made that a share, and so established for them in the inheritance a right, without specifying how much it is.

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent to Suwayd and ʿArfaja: «Do not divide any of the property of Aws ibn Thabit. Allah the Most High has made a share for his daughters from what he left, and has not specified how much it is, until we see what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reveals concerning them.» Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children﴾ up to His saying ﴿That is the great triumph﴾. When it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah sent to Suwayd and ʿArfaja: «Give Umm Kahha an eighth of what was left, and give his daughters two-thirds, and the remainder of the property is for you both.» [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/47.]]

﴿And when the distribution is present﴾, meaning the distribution of inheritances, ﴿those of kinship﴾ who do not inherit, ﴿and the orphans and the needy﴾, ﴿provide for them from it﴾, meaning give them something from the property before the division. The scholars differ over the ruling of this verse:

Some people said: it is abrogated (mansūkha). Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Abu Malik said: this was before the verse of inheritance. When the verse of inheritance was revealed, the inheritance was given to its rightful people, the bequest was established, and this verse was abrogated. It was made for those close relatives who are present but do not inherit, the orphans and the needy. This is the narration of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Others said: it is definitive (muḥkama), and this is the view of al-Ash‘ari, al-Nakha‘i, al-Sha‘bi, al-Zuhri, and the narration of ʿIkrima and Muqatil from Ibn ʿAbbas. Mujahid said: it is obligatory upon the heirs, if their hearts are content with it.

Qatada, from al-Hasan: It is not abrogated, but people became stingy and miserly.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated from Maʿmar from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa: that his father gave him from the inheritance of Musʿab when he divided his property. This was said by al-Hasan.

The Successors (tabiʿun) said: They used to give the chest, the vessels, the rest of the goods, the clothes, and the thing from whose division one is ashamed. If some of the heirs were children, they differed:

Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Suddi and others said: when these present ones attend the division, if the deceased bequeathed something to them, his bequest is carried out for them. If the heirs are adults, they are given something. If they are children, excuse is made to them, and the guardian and the executor say: "I do not possess this; it belongs to these weak, young children who do not understand what right they have over it. If I had any of the inheritance I would give it to you. When they grow up, they will know your right. If they die and we inherit from them, we will give you your right." This is the well-known statement.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: this verse is one that people neglect. There are two guardians: a guardian who inherits, who is the one who gives and clothes, and a guardian who does not inherit, to whom "a kind word" is said.

Some of them said: that is a binding right in the property of the young and the old. If they are adults, they themselves give it, and if they are children, their guardian gives it.

Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated: that ʿUbayda al-Salmani divided the property of orphans, and he ordered a sheep to be slaughtered and made food for the people of this verse, and said: "Had it not been for this verse, this would have come from my own property."

Qatada narrated from Yahya ibn Yaʿmur, who said: "Those are definitive verses, Medinan, which people have abandoned: this verse, the verse of seeking permission, ﴿O you who believe, let those whom your right hands possess seek your permission﴾ [[Surat al-Nur: 58.]], and His saying ﴿O mankind, We created you from male and female﴾. [[Surat al-Hujurat: 13.]]"

Some of them said: this is recommended (nadb) and desirable (istihbab), not obligatory (ḥatm) and binding (ījāb), and this is the most correct of the sayings.

Ibn Zayd and others said: this concerns the bequest, not the inheritance. A man, when he made a bequest, would say: "So-and-so's property, he was commanded to bequeath a third of his property to those whom Allah named in this verse."

Ibn Abi Mulayka narrated from Asma’ bint ʿAbd al-Rahman, Abu Bakr and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, who reported: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr divided the inheritance of his father ʿAbd al-Rahman while ʿA’isha was alive. They said: "He left no needy person or relative in the house without giving them from his father's property," and he recited this verse: ﴿And when the distribution is present﴾.

Al-Qasim said: I mentioned that to Ibn ʿAbbas, and he said: "He did not do right; that is not his to do. That is only in the bequest."

﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them﴾ — the verse.

Most of the exegetes said: this concerns a man whom death approaches, and those present with him, at his bequest, say: "Consider for yourself, for your children and heirs will avail you nothing. So send ahead for yourself: free slaves, give charity, and give so-and-so such-and-such, and so-and-so such-and-such," until he has consumed most of his property and exhausted it, leaving nothing for his heirs. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade them from this, and commanded them to tell him to leave something for his children, not to exceed one-third in his bequest, and not to harm his heirs, just as if this dying man were himself the one making the bequest. He would be pleased for someone present to urge him to preserve his property for his children, and not to leave them destitute in their weakness, driving them to dependence and scheming.

Muqatil al-Hadrami said: a man whom death approaches, and someone present says to him: "Fear Allah and keep your property for yourself, for no one has a better right to your property than your children," and forbids him from bequeathing to his relatives, to the orphans and the poor. Had this been the one bequeathing, it would have pleased him to bequeath to them.

Al-Kalbi said: this address is to the guardians of orphans. It says: whoever has an orphan in his care, let him treat him well, let him speak and act well, and let him deal with him as he would wish to be dealt with regarding his own offspring after him. This is the narration of ʿAṭiyya from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Al-Sha‘ari said: We were in Constantinople during the days of Maslama ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, and among us were Ibn Muhabbarin, Ibn al-Daylami and Hani ibn Maktum. We began to discuss what would happen at the end of time. I became distressed when I heard it, and I said to Ibn al-Daylami: "O Abu Bashir, I wish I would never have a child." He struck my shoulder with his hand and said: "O my nephew, do not do that, for there is no portion decreed by the Books of Allah to come out of a man's loins except that it will come out, whether we wish it or not. Shall I not direct you to a matter which, if you attain it, Allah will save you from it, and if you leave a child after you, Allah will protect them because of you?" I said: "Yes." He recited this verse: ﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them. So let them fear Allah and speak words of rectitude﴾. Al-Sadid means justice and what is right of speech.

﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly﴾ — the verse.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It was revealed concerning a man from Ghatafan called Murthid ibn Zayd, who was in charge of the property of his nephew, an orphan child, and consumed it. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning him: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly﴾, meaning forbiddenly, without right, ﴿they only consume into their bellies fire﴾. He informed about his property and informed about his condition. The Arabs say of a thing which leads to another thing: "This is such-and-such, because of what it leads to," like their saying: "This is death," meaning it leads to it.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning one who drinks from vessels of gold and silver: «He only swallows into his belly the fire of Hell.» [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/112; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/212.]] [247]

He (peace be upon him) also said: «The sea is fire within fire,» [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/211.]] [248] meaning its consequence is likewise. Mention of the bellies is for emphasis, as one says: "I saw with my eye, I said with my tongue, I took with my hand, I walked with my foot." ﴿And they will burn in a blaze﴾, meaning fuel.

The common readers recited it with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, meaning they will enter, confirmed by His saying ﴿except one who is destined for the Blazing Fire﴾ and His saying ﴿None will enter it but the most wretched﴾. [[Surat al-Layl: 15.]]

Abu Rajaʾ, al-Hasan, Ibn ʿAmir, ʿAsim and Abu Jaʿfar read it with a ḍamma on the yāʾ, meaning they will enter the Fire and be burned. Its parallel is His saying ﴿I will cast him into Saqar﴾ [[Surat al-Muddaththir: 26.]] and His saying ﴿We will surely cast him into a Fire﴾. [[Surat al-Nisa’: 30.]]

Ḥumayd ibn Qays read ﴿wa-sayuṣallūna﴾ with a ḍamma on the yāʾ and tashdid on the lām, from the causative form (tasliya), for the frequency of the action, meaning time after time, as evidenced by His saying ﴿Then into Hell cast him﴾. [[Surat al-Haqqa: 31.]] All of it is correct. It is said: "I roasted (ṣallaytu) the thing" when I roasted it.

In a ḥadīth: a roasted sheep was brought (shāt muṣallāh), and "I roasted it" (fa-aṣlaytuhu) means I threw it into the fire; "I roasted it" (ṣallaytuhu) means I roasted it time after time. "Ṣliyat" with a kasra on the lām means entered the Fire, and "tasallaytu" means warmed myself at the fire. The poet said:

"I have warmed myself in the heat of their war, as one who is chilled warms himself from the cold."

[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/54.]]

Al-Suddi said: The consumer of an orphan's property unjustly will be raised on the Day of Resurrection, and flame and smoke will come out of his mouth, his ears, his nose and his eyes. Everyone who sees him will recognize him as one who consumed an orphan's property.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: «On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I saw people who had lips like the lips of camels, one of them hanging over his nostrils and the other on his belly. The guardians of the Fire were stuffing them with the embers of Hell and its stones, and it came out from their lower parts. I said: "O Jibril, who are these?" He said: "Those who consume the property of orphans unjustly."» [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/263 (with variation).]] [249]

﴿Allah enjoins you﴾.

A section explaining the verse in detail:

Know that inheritance in the Jahiliyya was by manhood and strength. They would give inheritance to men and not to women and children. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, nullified that by His saying: ﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave, and for women there is a share﴾. Inheritance also existed in the Jahiliyya, and Islam began with alliance (muḥālafa). Allah said: ﴿And those whom your oaths have bound — give them their share﴾, meaning the allies, and give them their portion of the inheritance. Then after the Hijra it became: Allah the Most High said: ﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate — you have no guardianship over them at all until they emigrate﴾. [[Surat al-Anfal: 72.]] So all of that was abrogated, and inheritance became of two kinds: by cause and by lineage. As for cause, it is marriage and clientage (walāʾ). This is a broad field of knowledge.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: «Hold fast to the fara'id (the obligatory shares of inheritance), for they are half of knowledge, and it is the first knowledge to be taken from my community.» [[Fath al-Bari: 12/4; Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 11/3, with slight variation.]] [250]

That cannot be known except by knowing the heirs and the shares. I have written a brief comprehensive treatment of it, as suits the condition of this book, and Allah is the One who grants success in what is correct.

Know that when a person dies, first the funeral preparations are made, then his debts are paid, then his bequests are carried out. What remains is divided among the heirs. The heirs are of three categories: some inherit by fixed share (farḍ), some by agnatic succession (taʿṣīb, i.e. taking the residue as male relatives through the father's line), and some by both together. The owner of a fixed share is one who has a known portion and a determined allotment, such as daughters, sisters, mothers, grandmothers, husbands and wives. The agnate (ʿaṣaba) is one who takes the whole property when there are no owners of fixed shares, or who takes the surplus after them, and is excluded if nothing remains after the owners of shares, such as a brother, a paternal uncle and the like. One who inherits by both ways is the father together with a daughter or a son's daughter: he takes his determined share, which is a sixth, and then takes what remains of the two.

The total number of heirs is seventeen: ten of the men are the son, the son's son however low, the father, the father's father however high, the brother, the brother's son, the paternal uncle, the uncle's son, the husband, and the freed slave's patron. Of the women there are seven: the daughter, the son's daughter, the mother, the grandmother, the sister, the wife, and the freed slave's female patron. Those who are not excluded from inheritance by any of the six are the two parents, the children, and the spouses.

The reason for this is that there is no intermediary between them and the deceased. Those who never inherit are six: the slave, the mudabbar (a slave whose master has made him free upon his death), the mukātab (a slave under a contract of manumission), the mother of a child by her master (umm walad), the one who commits intentional murder, and those of two differing religions. The fixed shares defined in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are six: half, a quarter, an eighth, two-thirds, a third, and a sixth.

The half is the fixed share of five: the daughter of the loins, the son's daughter when there is no daughter of the loins, the full sister, the consanguine sister when there is no full sister, and the husband when the deceased has no child or son's child.

The quarter is the fixed share of two: the husband when the deceased has a child or son's child, and the wife or wives when the deceased has no child or son's child.

The eighth is the fixed share of one: the wife or wives when the deceased has a child or son's child.

Two-thirds is the fixed share of every two or more of those whose share is a half.

The third is the fixed share of three: the mother when the deceased has no child, no son's child, and not two or more of the brothers and sisters, except in two cases: one is a husband and two parents, the other is a wife and two parents. In these two the mother takes a third of what remains after the husband's share, which in reality is a sixth of the whole property, and the wife takes a quarter of the whole property. The share of two maternal siblings, males and females alike, is equal. The grandfather's share with brothers and sisters is when division is better for him than a third.

The sixth is the fixed share of seven: the son's daughter with the daughter of the loins, the consanguine sister with the full sister, the single maternal sibling, the mother when the deceased has a child or a son's child, or two or more brothers and sisters. The share of the grandmother and grandmothers, and the share of the father with a child and a son's child, [....] [[Blank space in the original.]] with a son and a son's son. As for the agnates, the nearest of them are the sons, then their sons, then their sons' sons however low, [ ... ] [[Blank space in the original.]] their sisters: "to the male a portion like the share of two females." Then the father, who has three states: a state in which he takes the agnatic share alone, which is when there is no child or son's child; a state in which he takes only the fixed share, which is with a son or son's son; and a state in which he combines the fixed share and the agnatic share, which is with a daughter or a son's daughter. Then the grandfather, if he has no brothers. If he has brothers, he shares with them. Then the full brothers and sisters. Then the consanguine brothers and sisters, who divide the property among them: "to the male a portion like the share of two females." A single one of them is an agnate together with the daughters. The rest of the agnates: their males alone take by agnatic succession, to the exclusion of the females. Then the sons of the full brothers, then the sons of the consanguine brothers, then the full paternal uncles, then the consanguine paternal uncles, then the sons of the full paternal uncles, then the sons of the consanguine paternal uncles, then the sons of the full paternal uncles, then the sons of the consanguine paternal uncles, then the paternal uncles of the father in the same manner, then the paternal uncles of the grandfather. In this order, the sons of a higher ancestor do not inherit while the sons of a nearer ancestor exist. Then the freed slave's patron, then his agnates in this order. This is a summary of this branch of knowledge.

Returning to the explanation of the verse: the exegetes differed over the occasion of its revelation.

Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir reported that he heard Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah say: "I fell ill, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) visited me while they were walking. I fainted, and he called for water, performed ablution, and poured it over me, and I regained consciousness. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how shall I dispose of my property? What shall I do with my property?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent, and then the verse of inheritance was revealed concerning me."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verse 7–14 (part 2 of 2):

Ata' said: Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' (al-naqib, the chief) was martyred on the day of Uhud, leaving a wife, two daughters and a brother. The brother took the wealth, so Sa'd's wife came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, these two are the daughters of Sa'd. Sa'd was killed as a martyr with you at Uhud, and their paternal uncle has taken their wealth, and they cannot be married except when they have wealth." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Return, perhaps Allah will decide concerning this." [251] She remained for a while, then came back complaining and weeping. Then there was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children...﴾ to its end.

So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned their uncle and said: "Give Sa'd's two daughters two-thirds, their mother one-eighth, and what remains is yours." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 3/280; Irwa' al-Ghalil: 6/121–122.]] [252]

This was the first inheritance distributed in Islam.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning Umm Kahha, and its story has already passed.

Al-Suddi said: it was revealed concerning 'Abd al-Rahman, brother of the poet Hassan, for he died leaving a wife and five sisters. The heirs came, took his property, and gave his wife nothing. She complained of this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah revealed the verse of inheritance.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The inheritance used to go to the children, and the bequest was for parents and relatives. Then Allah abrogated that, and revealed the verse of inheritance. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah was not content that any angel brought near or any prophet sent should divide the estates until He Himself took charge of the distribution of inheritances and gave each one who has a right his right. Truly, there is no bequest to an heir." [[Majma' al-Bayan: 3/29, which does not contain the final part of the narration.]] [253]

As for His saying, ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children﴾: that is, He enjoins and makes obligatory upon you, ﴿concerning your children﴾, meaning regarding the matter of your children after you die: ﴿for the male, the equivalent of the share of two females. And if there are [only] daughters, two or more, then for them is two-thirds of what he left﴾, and "fawq" (above) is supplementary, like His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So strike [them] upon the necks﴾ [[Surah al-Anfal: 12.]].

﴿And if there is only one﴾, meaning a daughter.

The majority recited it in the accusative as the predicate of kana (was). The people of Madina read it in the nominative, meaning: "if one [daughter] occurs"; in that case it has no predicate.

﴿then for her is half.﴾ Then He said: ﴿And for his parents﴾, meaning the two parents of the deceased, a pronoun referring to what is not mentioned, ﴿for each one of them is a sixth of what he left, if he has children, or [more than one] child.﴾ Here "father" is a sharer by fixed portion. ﴿But if he has no children and his parents inherit from him, then for his mother is a third.﴾ The people of Kufa read ﴿fa-li-ummihi﴾ with a kasra on the hamza, and the rest read it with a damma, as the original form.

﴿And if he has brothers﴾, two or more, male or female, ﴿then for his mother is a sixth.﴾ This is the view of the majority of jurists. Ibn 'Abbas would not reduce the mother's share from a third to a sixth with fewer than three siblings, and he said regarding parents and two siblings: the mother has a third and the remainder is for the father, following the apparent wording.

It is narrated that Ibn 'Abbas entered upon 'Uthman and said: "Why do two brothers reduce the mother to a sixth, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿and if he has brothers﴾, and in the language of your people two are not 'brothers'?" 'Uthman said: "Can I annul a matter that was decided before me, which people have inherited by and which has continued in the cities?" Ibn 'Abbas's opinion on this is not acted upon. As for the verse, the Arabs use the plural form for the dual, because the plural is the joining of one thing to another; the least plural is two, and its maximum has no limit. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Your hearts have indeed inclined﴾ [[Surah al-Tahrim: 4.]].

The Arabs say: "I struck from Zayd and 'Amr, their heads, and hurt from your brothers, their backs." Al-Akhfash recited:

"When the two women brought us the news
that the matter among us had become known."

Al-Tha'alabi said: Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to me, who said: Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rimah al-Zaydi recited to me:

"Yahya gives greeting to the rich of a people,
and withholds greeting from the poor.
Is not death between them equal,
when they die and enter the graves?"

﴿after a bequest he bequeaths or a debt.﴾ Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim read ﴿yuwsa﴾ with a fatha on the sad; the rest read it with a kasra, and likewise the second. The transmission from 'Asim differs on both. The kasra is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim, because mention of the deceased has occurred before this. Al-Akhfash said: what confirms the kasra is ﴿yuwsin﴾ and ﴿yuwasna﴾.

﴿Your parents and your children — you do not know which of them are nearer to you in benefit.﴾ Mujahid said: "in this world." Some read ﴿ayyuhuma aqrabu lakum nafʿan﴾ [with ayyuhuma]: here it is nominative as the subject, and the particle before it does not govern it, since it is an interrogative, and ﴿aqrabu﴾ is its predicate and ﴿nafʿan﴾ is an accusative of specification. It is as if he says: "You do not know which of the heirs and the deceased will die first so that the other inherits from him; so do not wish for the death of the one who will be inherited from, nor hasten it."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "The most obedient of you to Allah among parents and children, the highest of you in rank on the Day of Resurrection, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intercedes for believers on behalf of one another. If the father is higher in rank in Paradise than his child, Allah raises his child to his rank so that his eye may be comforted by that; and if the child is higher in rank than his parents, Allah raises his parents to his rank so that both their eyes may be comforted."

Al-Hasan said: "You do not know which of them you are happier with in religion and in this world."

﴿An obligation from Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise. And for you is half of what your wives leave, if they have no child; but if they have a child, then for you is a fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they bequeath or debt. And for them [wives] is a fourth of what you leave if you have no child; but if you have a child, then for them is an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you bequeath or debt.﴾ "And for them" means: and for the wives. ﴿And if a man leaves an estate to be inherited by kalalah, or a woman...﴾ The structure of the verse: "and if there is a man or a woman who is inherited by kalala." It is in the accusative as a verbal noun, and it is said to be a circumstantial accusative, and it is said to be the predicate of the passive form, its estimate being: "and if a man's wealth is inherited by kalala."

Al-Hasan and 'Isa read ﴿yuwarithu﴾ with a kasra on the ra', making it an active verb with him as subject.

They differed about kalala:
Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: it is the deceased. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the heirs. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: it is the property. They also differed on its meaning and its ruling:

It is narrated from Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about kalala, and he recited the end of Surat al-Nisa', and the questioner objected, so he (ﷺ) said: "I will not increase your knowledge until I am increased."[[Ta'wil Mukhtalif al-Hadith: 185 (with variation).]] [254]

Shu'ba narrated from 'Asim al-Ahwal, who said: I heard al-Sha'bi say: Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said concerning kalala: "I give a judgment on it; if it is correct, it is from Allah, and if it is wrong, it is from Satan and from me, and Allah is free of it: it is what is other than the father and the child." He said: then when 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) came after him, he said: "I am ashamed before Allah to contradict Abu Bakr: it is what is apart from the father and the child."

Tawus said: it is what is other than the child. Al-Hakam: it is what is other than the father. 'Atiyya: they are the maternal siblings. 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr: they are the paternal siblings. It is also said: they are the brothers and sisters.

Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah said: "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, only two sisters of mine are to inherit; so what about the inheritance?' Then there was revealed: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning kalala.﴾"

Al-Akhfash said: whoever is not inherited by a father or mother is kalala.

The people of language said: it is from "takallalahu al-nasab," when kinship surrounds someone like a crown (iklil).

Imru' al-Qays said:
"Do you see a lightning flash whose gleam I show you,
like the glimmer of two hands in a striped cloak?"

They were named kalala because they surround the deceased from his sides, yet they are neither of him nor is he of them, and their surrounding him is that they are related to him alongside.

Al-Farazdaq said:
"You inherited the spear of kingship, not as kalala,
from the two sons of Manaf, 'Abd Shams and Hashim."

Someone else said:
"The father of the man protects, and he has
a client of kalala who does not get angry."

﴿And he has a brother or a sister﴾: He did not say "and they two" (wa-lahuma), though the man and woman have been mentioned, following the custom of the Arabs: when they mention two names and then speak of them, they are equal in ruling; sometimes they attribute it to one of them, and sometimes to both together. One says: "Whoever has a boy and a girl, let him be good to him and to her, and to both of them; all of this is permissible." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is difficult﴾ and similar examples. He intended by this the brother and the sister from the mother's side, as is shown by the reading of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas: "And he has a brother or a sister from the mother," ﴿then for each one of them is a sixth. But if they are more than that, they are sharers in the third, equally among them, males and females alike, after any bequest that is bequeathed or debt.﴾

'Ali (peace be upon him) said: "You recite the bequest before the debt, but the Messenger of Allah began with the debt before the bequest."

This is the view of the majority of jurists; the meaning of the verse is joint, not sequential. ﴿Without causing harm﴾, bringing harm upon the heirs.

Al-Hasan said: this is to bequeath a debt that is not owed, ﴿as a directive from Allah.﴾

Al-A'mash recited: "without causing harm, a bequest from Allah," with idafa.

﴿And Allah is Knowing and Forbearing.﴾

Qatada said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, disliked harm during life and at death, forbade it, and decreed it. Harm is not proper in life or in death."

And in a report: "Whoever cuts off an inheritance, Allah will cut off his share in Paradise."
[[See: Kashf al-Khafa': 2/310.]]

﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾ up to His saying:

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verses 7–14 (part 1 of 2):

﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave﴾ — the verse, and the reason for its revelation: Aws ibn Thabit al-Ansari died and left a wife called Umm Kahha and three daughters by her. Two men, who were the cousins (sons of the paternal uncle) of the deceased and his executors, rose up. The scholars differ over their names. Al-Kalbi and Qatada said they were ʿArfaṭa, while others said they were Suwayd and ʿArfaja. They took his property and gave his wife and daughters nothing. In the Jahiliyya (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance) they did not give inheritance to women or to young children, even if they were male. They gave inheritance only to adult men, saying: "We give only to one who fights on horseback and is able to take part in the distribution." He said: Umm Kahha came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was in the Mosque of al-Faḍīḥ, and she said: "O Messenger of Allah, Aws ibn Thabit died and left me three daughters, and I am his wife. I have nothing with which to support them. Their father left good property, and it is in the hands of Suwayd and ʿArfaja. They have given me and his daughters nothing of the property, and the girls are in my care. They are not fed or given drink, and no attention is paid to them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned the two men, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, her sons do not ride horses, do not carry burdens, and do not strike an enemy." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: «Go away until I see what Allah will reveal to me concerning them.» [[Asbab al-Nuzul (The Occasions of Revelation): 96.]] [246] So they left, and Allah the Most High revealed this verse.

﴿For men﴾ means the males among the children of the deceased and his relatives. ﴿There is a share﴾ means a portion and a lot, a part of ﴿what the parents and close relatives leave﴾ as inheritance. The females also have a portion of the inheritance.

﴿Of what is little of it or much﴾ of the property, ﴿a share ordained﴾, a known and obligatory portion. Its parallel is in His saying: ﴿I will surely take from Your servants an ordained share﴾. [[Surat al-Nisa’: 118.]] The word ﴿a share﴾ is in the accusative because it comes in the manner of a verbal noun (maṣdar), like the saying of one speaker: "You have a right over me, a binding right," and "I have a dirham, a gifted one that has been received." This is the view of al-Farra’.

Abu ʿUbayda said: it is accusative by way of exit (khurūj). Al-Kisa’i said: it is accusative as a detachment (qaṭʿ). Al-Akhfash said: He made that a share, and so established for them in the inheritance a right, without specifying how much it is.

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent to Suwayd and ʿArfaja: «Do not divide any of the property of Aws ibn Thabit. Allah the Most High has made a share for his daughters from what he left, and has not specified how much it is, until we see what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reveals concerning them.» Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children﴾ up to His saying ﴿That is the great triumph﴾. When it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah sent to Suwayd and ʿArfaja: «Give Umm Kahha an eighth of what was left, and give his daughters two-thirds, and the remainder of the property is for you both.» [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/47.]]

﴿And when the distribution is present﴾, meaning the distribution of inheritances, ﴿those of kinship﴾ who do not inherit, ﴿and the orphans and the needy﴾, ﴿provide for them from it﴾, meaning give them something from the property before the division. The scholars differ over the ruling of this verse:

Some people said: it is abrogated (mansūkha). Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Abu Malik said: this was before the verse of inheritance. When the verse of inheritance was revealed, the inheritance was given to its rightful people, the bequest was established, and this verse was abrogated. It was made for those close relatives who are present but do not inherit, the orphans and the needy. This is the narration of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Others said: it is definitive (muḥkama), and this is the view of al-Ash‘ari, al-Nakha‘i, al-Sha‘bi, al-Zuhri, and the narration of ʿIkrima and Muqatil from Ibn ʿAbbas. Mujahid said: it is obligatory upon the heirs, if their hearts are content with it.

Qatada, from al-Hasan: It is not abrogated, but people became stingy and miserly.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated from Maʿmar from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa: that his father gave him from the inheritance of Musʿab when he divided his property. This was said by al-Hasan.

The Successors (tabiʿun) said: They used to give the chest, the vessels, the rest of the goods, the clothes, and the thing from whose division one is ashamed. If some of the heirs were children, they differed:

Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Suddi and others said: when these present ones attend the division, if the deceased bequeathed something to them, his bequest is carried out for them. If the heirs are adults, they are given something. If they are children, excuse is made to them, and the guardian and the executor say: "I do not possess this; it belongs to these weak, young children who do not understand what right they have over it. If I had any of the inheritance I would give it to you. When they grow up, they will know your right. If they die and we inherit from them, we will give you your right." This is the well-known statement.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: this verse is one that people neglect. There are two guardians: a guardian who inherits, who is the one who gives and clothes, and a guardian who does not inherit, to whom "a kind word" is said.

Some of them said: that is a binding right in the property of the young and the old. If they are adults, they themselves give it, and if they are children, their guardian gives it.

Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated: that ʿUbayda al-Salmani divided the property of orphans, and he ordered a sheep to be slaughtered and made food for the people of this verse, and said: "Had it not been for this verse, this would have come from my own property."

Qatada narrated from Yahya ibn Yaʿmur, who said: "Those are definitive verses, Medinan, which people have abandoned: this verse, the verse of seeking permission, ﴿O you who believe, let those whom your right hands possess seek your permission﴾ [[Surat al-Nur: 58.]], and His saying ﴿O mankind, We created you from male and female﴾. [[Surat al-Hujurat: 13.]]"

Some of them said: this is recommended (nadb) and desirable (istihbab), not obligatory (ḥatm) and binding (ījāb), and this is the most correct of the sayings.

Ibn Zayd and others said: this concerns the bequest, not the inheritance. A man, when he made a bequest, would say: "So-and-so's property, he was commanded to bequeath a third of his property to those whom Allah named in this verse."

Ibn Abi Mulayka narrated from Asma’ bint ʿAbd al-Rahman, Abu Bakr and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, who reported: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr divided the inheritance of his father ʿAbd al-Rahman while ʿA’isha was alive. They said: "He left no needy person or relative in the house without giving them from his father's property," and he recited this verse: ﴿And when the distribution is present﴾.

Al-Qasim said: I mentioned that to Ibn ʿAbbas, and he said: "He did not do right; that is not his to do. That is only in the bequest."

﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them﴾ — the verse.

Most of the exegetes said: this concerns a man whom death approaches, and those present with him, at his bequest, say: "Consider for yourself, for your children and heirs will avail you nothing. So send ahead for yourself: free slaves, give charity, and give so-and-so such-and-such, and so-and-so such-and-such," until he has consumed most of his property and exhausted it, leaving nothing for his heirs. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade them from this, and commanded them to tell him to leave something for his children, not to exceed one-third in his bequest, and not to harm his heirs, just as if this dying man were himself the one making the bequest. He would be pleased for someone present to urge him to preserve his property for his children, and not to leave them destitute in their weakness, driving them to dependence and scheming.

Muqatil al-Hadrami said: a man whom death approaches, and someone present says to him: "Fear Allah and keep your property for yourself, for no one has a better right to your property than your children," and forbids him from bequeathing to his relatives, to the orphans and the poor. Had this been the one bequeathing, it would have pleased him to bequeath to them.

Al-Kalbi said: this address is to the guardians of orphans. It says: whoever has an orphan in his care, let him treat him well, let him speak and act well, and let him deal with him as he would wish to be dealt with regarding his own offspring after him. This is the narration of ʿAṭiyya from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Al-Sha‘ari said: We were in Constantinople during the days of Maslama ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, and among us were Ibn Muhabbarin, Ibn al-Daylami and Hani ibn Maktum. We began to discuss what would happen at the end of time. I became distressed when I heard it, and I said to Ibn al-Daylami: "O Abu Bashir, I wish I would never have a child." He struck my shoulder with his hand and said: "O my nephew, do not do that, for there is no portion decreed by the Books of Allah to come out of a man's loins except that it will come out, whether we wish it or not. Shall I not direct you to a matter which, if you attain it, Allah will save you from it, and if you leave a child after you, Allah will protect them because of you?" I said: "Yes." He recited this verse: ﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them. So let them fear Allah and speak words of rectitude﴾. Al-Sadid means justice and what is right of speech.

﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly﴾ — the verse.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It was revealed concerning a man from Ghatafan called Murthid ibn Zayd, who was in charge of the property of his nephew, an orphan child, and consumed it. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning him: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly﴾, meaning forbiddenly, without right, ﴿they only consume into their bellies fire﴾. He informed about his property and informed about his condition. The Arabs say of a thing which leads to another thing: "This is such-and-such, because of what it leads to," like their saying: "This is death," meaning it leads to it.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning one who drinks from vessels of gold and silver: «He only swallows into his belly the fire of Hell.» [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/112; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/212.]] [247]

He (peace be upon him) also said: «The sea is fire within fire,» [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/211.]] [248] meaning its consequence is likewise. Mention of the bellies is for emphasis, as one says: "I saw with my eye, I said with my tongue, I took with my hand, I walked with my foot." ﴿And they will burn in a blaze﴾, meaning fuel.

The common readers recited it with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, meaning they will enter, confirmed by His saying ﴿except one who is destined for the Blazing Fire﴾ and His saying ﴿None will enter it but the most wretched﴾. [[Surat al-Layl: 15.]]

Abu Rajaʾ, al-Hasan, Ibn ʿAmir, ʿAsim and Abu Jaʿfar read it with a ḍamma on the yāʾ, meaning they will enter the Fire and be burned. Its parallel is His saying ﴿I will cast him into Saqar﴾ [[Surat al-Muddaththir: 26.]] and His saying ﴿We will surely cast him into a Fire﴾. [[Surat al-Nisa’: 30.]]

Ḥumayd ibn Qays read ﴿wa-sayuṣallūna﴾ with a ḍamma on the yāʾ and tashdid on the lām, from the causative form (tasliya), for the frequency of the action, meaning time after time, as evidenced by His saying ﴿Then into Hell cast him﴾. [[Surat al-Haqqa: 31.]] All of it is correct. It is said: "I roasted (ṣallaytu) the thing" when I roasted it.

In a ḥadīth: a roasted sheep was brought (shāt muṣallāh), and "I roasted it" (fa-aṣlaytuhu) means I threw it into the fire; "I roasted it" (ṣallaytuhu) means I roasted it time after time. "Ṣliyat" with a kasra on the lām means entered the Fire, and "tasallaytu" means warmed myself at the fire. The poet said:

"I have warmed myself in the heat of their war, as one who is chilled warms himself from the cold."

[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/54.]]

Al-Suddi said: The consumer of an orphan's property unjustly will be raised on the Day of Resurrection, and flame and smoke will come out of his mouth, his ears, his nose and his eyes. Everyone who sees him will recognize him as one who consumed an orphan's property.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: «On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I saw people who had lips like the lips of camels, one of them hanging over his nostrils and the other on his belly. The guardians of the Fire were stuffing them with the embers of Hell and its stones, and it came out from their lower parts. I said: "O Jibril, who are these?" He said: "Those who consume the property of orphans unjustly."» [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/263 (with variation).]] [249]

﴿Allah enjoins you﴾.

A section explaining the verse in detail:

Know that inheritance in the Jahiliyya was by manhood and strength. They would give inheritance to men and not to women and children. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, nullified that by His saying: ﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave, and for women there is a share﴾. Inheritance also existed in the Jahiliyya, and Islam began with alliance (muḥālafa). Allah said: ﴿And those whom your oaths have bound — give them their share﴾, meaning the allies, and give them their portion of the inheritance. Then after the Hijra it became: Allah the Most High said: ﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate — you have no guardianship over them at all until they emigrate﴾. [[Surat al-Anfal: 72.]] So all of that was abrogated, and inheritance became of two kinds: by cause and by lineage. As for cause, it is marriage and clientage (walāʾ). This is a broad field of knowledge.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: «Hold fast to the fara'id (the obligatory shares of inheritance), for they are half of knowledge, and it is the first knowledge to be taken from my community.» [[Fath al-Bari: 12/4; Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 11/3, with slight variation.]] [250]

That cannot be known except by knowing the heirs and the shares. I have written a brief comprehensive treatment of it, as suits the condition of this book, and Allah is the One who grants success in what is correct.

Know that when a person dies, first the funeral preparations are made, then his debts are paid, then his bequests are carried out. What remains is divided among the heirs. The heirs are of three categories: some inherit by fixed share (farḍ), some by agnatic succession (taʿṣīb, i.e. taking the residue as male relatives through the father's line), and some by both together. The owner of a fixed share is one who has a known portion and a determined allotment, such as daughters, sisters, mothers, grandmothers, husbands and wives. The agnate (ʿaṣaba) is one who takes the whole property when there are no owners of fixed shares, or who takes the surplus after them, and is excluded if nothing remains after the owners of shares, such as a brother, a paternal uncle and the like. One who inherits by both ways is the father together with a daughter or a son's daughter: he takes his determined share, which is a sixth, and then takes what remains of the two.

The total number of heirs is seventeen: ten of the men are the son, the son's son however low, the father, the father's father however high, the brother, the brother's son, the paternal uncle, the uncle's son, the husband, and the freed slave's patron. Of the women there are seven: the daughter, the son's daughter, the mother, the grandmother, the sister, the wife, and the freed slave's female patron. Those who are not excluded from inheritance by any of the six are the two parents, the children, and the spouses.

The reason for this is that there is no intermediary between them and the deceased. Those who never inherit are six: the slave, the mudabbar (a slave whose master has made him free upon his death), the mukātab (a slave under a contract of manumission), the mother of a child by her master (umm walad), the one who commits intentional murder, and those of two differing religions. The fixed shares defined in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are six: half, a quarter, an eighth, two-thirds, a third, and a sixth.

The half is the fixed share of five: the daughter of the loins, the son's daughter when there is no daughter of the loins, the full sister, the consanguine sister when there is no full sister, and the husband when the deceased has no child or son's child.

The quarter is the fixed share of two: the husband when the deceased has a child or son's child, and the wife or wives when the deceased has no child or son's child.

The eighth is the fixed share of one: the wife or wives when the deceased has a child or son's child.

Two-thirds is the fixed share of every two or more of those whose share is a half.

The third is the fixed share of three: the mother when the deceased has no child, no son's child, and not two or more of the brothers and sisters, except in two cases: one is a husband and two parents, the other is a wife and two parents. In these two the mother takes a third of what remains after the husband's share, which in reality is a sixth of the whole property, and the wife takes a quarter of the whole property. The share of two maternal siblings, males and females alike, is equal. The grandfather's share with brothers and sisters is when division is better for him than a third.

The sixth is the fixed share of seven: the son's daughter with the daughter of the loins, the consanguine sister with the full sister, the single maternal sibling, the mother when the deceased has a child or a son's child, or two or more brothers and sisters. The share of the grandmother and grandmothers, and the share of the father with a child and a son's child, [....] [[Blank space in the original.]] with a son and a son's son. As for the agnates, the nearest of them are the sons, then their sons, then their sons' sons however low, [ ... ] [[Blank space in the original.]] their sisters: "to the male a portion like the share of two females." Then the father, who has three states: a state in which he takes the agnatic share alone, which is when there is no child or son's child; a state in which he takes only the fixed share, which is with a son or son's son; and a state in which he combines the fixed share and the agnatic share, which is with a daughter or a son's daughter. Then the grandfather, if he has no brothers. If he has brothers, he shares with them. Then the full brothers and sisters. Then the consanguine brothers and sisters, who divide the property among them: "to the male a portion like the share of two females." A single one of them is an agnate together with the daughters. The rest of the agnates: their males alone take by agnatic succession, to the exclusion of the females. Then the sons of the full brothers, then the sons of the consanguine brothers, then the full paternal uncles, then the consanguine paternal uncles, then the sons of the full paternal uncles, then the sons of the consanguine paternal uncles, then the sons of the full paternal uncles, then the sons of the consanguine paternal uncles, then the paternal uncles of the father in the same manner, then the paternal uncles of the grandfather. In this order, the sons of a higher ancestor do not inherit while the sons of a nearer ancestor exist. Then the freed slave's patron, then his agnates in this order. This is a summary of this branch of knowledge.

Returning to the explanation of the verse: the exegetes differed over the occasion of its revelation.

Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir reported that he heard Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah say: "I fell ill, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) visited me while they were walking. I fainted, and he called for water, performed ablution, and poured it over me, and I regained consciousness. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how shall I dispose of my property? What shall I do with my property?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent, and then the verse of inheritance was revealed concerning me."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verse 7–14 (part 2 of 2):

Ata' said: Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' (al-naqib, the chief) was martyred on the day of Uhud, leaving a wife, two daughters and a brother. The brother took the wealth, so Sa'd's wife came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, these two are the daughters of Sa'd. Sa'd was killed as a martyr with you at Uhud, and their paternal uncle has taken their wealth, and they cannot be married except when they have wealth." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Return, perhaps Allah will decide concerning this." [251] She remained for a while, then came back complaining and weeping. Then there was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children...﴾ to its end.

So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned their uncle and said: "Give Sa'd's two daughters two-thirds, their mother one-eighth, and what remains is yours." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 3/280; Irwa' al-Ghalil: 6/121–122.]] [252]

This was the first inheritance distributed in Islam.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning Umm Kahha, and its story has already passed.

Al-Suddi said: it was revealed concerning 'Abd al-Rahman, brother of the poet Hassan, for he died leaving a wife and five sisters. The heirs came, took his property, and gave his wife nothing. She complained of this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah revealed the verse of inheritance.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The inheritance used to go to the children, and the bequest was for parents and relatives. Then Allah abrogated that, and revealed the verse of inheritance. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah was not content that any angel brought near or any prophet sent should divide the estates until He Himself took charge of the distribution of inheritances and gave each one who has a right his right. Truly, there is no bequest to an heir." [[Majma' al-Bayan: 3/29, which does not contain the final part of the narration.]] [253]

As for His saying, ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children﴾: that is, He enjoins and makes obligatory upon you, ﴿concerning your children﴾, meaning regarding the matter of your children after you die: ﴿for the male, the equivalent of the share of two females. And if there are [only] daughters, two or more, then for them is two-thirds of what he left﴾, and "fawq" (above) is supplementary, like His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So strike [them] upon the necks﴾ [[Surah al-Anfal: 12.]].

﴿And if there is only one﴾, meaning a daughter.

The majority recited it in the accusative as the predicate of kana (was). The people of Madina read it in the nominative, meaning: "if one [daughter] occurs"; in that case it has no predicate.

﴿then for her is half.﴾ Then He said: ﴿And for his parents﴾, meaning the two parents of the deceased, a pronoun referring to what is not mentioned, ﴿for each one of them is a sixth of what he left, if he has children, or [more than one] child.﴾ Here "father" is a sharer by fixed portion. ﴿But if he has no children and his parents inherit from him, then for his mother is a third.﴾ The people of Kufa read ﴿fa-li-ummihi﴾ with a kasra on the hamza, and the rest read it with a damma, as the original form.

﴿And if he has brothers﴾, two or more, male or female, ﴿then for his mother is a sixth.﴾ This is the view of the majority of jurists. Ibn 'Abbas would not reduce the mother's share from a third to a sixth with fewer than three siblings, and he said regarding parents and two siblings: the mother has a third and the remainder is for the father, following the apparent wording.

It is narrated that Ibn 'Abbas entered upon 'Uthman and said: "Why do two brothers reduce the mother to a sixth, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿and if he has brothers﴾, and in the language of your people two are not 'brothers'?" 'Uthman said: "Can I annul a matter that was decided before me, which people have inherited by and which has continued in the cities?" Ibn 'Abbas's opinion on this is not acted upon. As for the verse, the Arabs use the plural form for the dual, because the plural is the joining of one thing to another; the least plural is two, and its maximum has no limit. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Your hearts have indeed inclined﴾ [[Surah al-Tahrim: 4.]].

The Arabs say: "I struck from Zayd and 'Amr, their heads, and hurt from your brothers, their backs." Al-Akhfash recited:

"When the two women brought us the news
that the matter among us had become known."

Al-Tha'alabi said: Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to me, who said: Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rimah al-Zaydi recited to me:

"Yahya gives greeting to the rich of a people,
and withholds greeting from the poor.
Is not death between them equal,
when they die and enter the graves?"

﴿after a bequest he bequeaths or a debt.﴾ Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim read ﴿yuwsa﴾ with a fatha on the sad; the rest read it with a kasra, and likewise the second. The transmission from 'Asim differs on both. The kasra is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim, because mention of the deceased has occurred before this. Al-Akhfash said: what confirms the kasra is ﴿yuwsin﴾ and ﴿yuwasna﴾.

﴿Your parents and your children — you do not know which of them are nearer to you in benefit.﴾ Mujahid said: "in this world." Some read ﴿ayyuhuma aqrabu lakum nafʿan﴾ [with ayyuhuma]: here it is nominative as the subject, and the particle before it does not govern it, since it is an interrogative, and ﴿aqrabu﴾ is its predicate and ﴿nafʿan﴾ is an accusative of specification. It is as if he says: "You do not know which of the heirs and the deceased will die first so that the other inherits from him; so do not wish for the death of the one who will be inherited from, nor hasten it."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "The most obedient of you to Allah among parents and children, the highest of you in rank on the Day of Resurrection, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intercedes for believers on behalf of one another. If the father is higher in rank in Paradise than his child, Allah raises his child to his rank so that his eye may be comforted by that; and if the child is higher in rank than his parents, Allah raises his parents to his rank so that both their eyes may be comforted."

Al-Hasan said: "You do not know which of them you are happier with in religion and in this world."

﴿An obligation from Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise. And for you is half of what your wives leave, if they have no child; but if they have a child, then for you is a fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they bequeath or debt. And for them [wives] is a fourth of what you leave if you have no child; but if you have a child, then for them is an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you bequeath or debt.﴾ "And for them" means: and for the wives. ﴿And if a man leaves an estate to be inherited by kalalah, or a woman...﴾ The structure of the verse: "and if there is a man or a woman who is inherited by kalala." It is in the accusative as a verbal noun, and it is said to be a circumstantial accusative, and it is said to be the predicate of the passive form, its estimate being: "and if a man's wealth is inherited by kalala."

Al-Hasan and 'Isa read ﴿yuwarithu﴾ with a kasra on the ra', making it an active verb with him as subject.

They differed about kalala:
Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: it is the deceased. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the heirs. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: it is the property. They also differed on its meaning and its ruling:

It is narrated from Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about kalala, and he recited the end of Surat al-Nisa', and the questioner objected, so he (ﷺ) said: "I will not increase your knowledge until I am increased."[[Ta'wil Mukhtalif al-Hadith: 185 (with variation).]] [254]

Shu'ba narrated from 'Asim al-Ahwal, who said: I heard al-Sha'bi say: Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said concerning kalala: "I give a judgment on it; if it is correct, it is from Allah, and if it is wrong, it is from Satan and from me, and Allah is free of it: it is what is other than the father and the child." He said: then when 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) came after him, he said: "I am ashamed before Allah to contradict Abu Bakr: it is what is apart from the father and the child."

Tawus said: it is what is other than the child. Al-Hakam: it is what is other than the father. 'Atiyya: they are the maternal siblings. 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr: they are the paternal siblings. It is also said: they are the brothers and sisters.

Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah said: "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, only two sisters of mine are to inherit; so what about the inheritance?' Then there was revealed: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning kalala.﴾"

Al-Akhfash said: whoever is not inherited by a father or mother is kalala.

The people of language said: it is from "takallalahu al-nasab," when kinship surrounds someone like a crown (iklil).

Imru' al-Qays said:
"Do you see a lightning flash whose gleam I show you,
like the glimmer of two hands in a striped cloak?"

They were named kalala because they surround the deceased from his sides, yet they are neither of him nor is he of them, and their surrounding him is that they are related to him alongside.

Al-Farazdaq said:
"You inherited the spear of kingship, not as kalala,
from the two sons of Manaf, 'Abd Shams and Hashim."

Someone else said:
"The father of the man protects, and he has
a client of kalala who does not get angry."

﴿And he has a brother or a sister﴾: He did not say "and they two" (wa-lahuma), though the man and woman have been mentioned, following the custom of the Arabs: when they mention two names and then speak of them, they are equal in ruling; sometimes they attribute it to one of them, and sometimes to both together. One says: "Whoever has a boy and a girl, let him be good to him and to her, and to both of them; all of this is permissible." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is difficult﴾ and similar examples. He intended by this the brother and the sister from the mother's side, as is shown by the reading of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas: "And he has a brother or a sister from the mother," ﴿then for each one of them is a sixth. But if they are more than that, they are sharers in the third, equally among them, males and females alike, after any bequest that is bequeathed or debt.﴾

'Ali (peace be upon him) said: "You recite the bequest before the debt, but the Messenger of Allah began with the debt before the bequest."

This is the view of the majority of jurists; the meaning of the verse is joint, not sequential. ﴿Without causing harm﴾, bringing harm upon the heirs.

Al-Hasan said: this is to bequeath a debt that is not owed, ﴿as a directive from Allah.﴾

Al-A'mash recited: "without causing harm, a bequest from Allah," with idafa.

﴿And Allah is Knowing and Forbearing.﴾

Qatada said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, disliked harm during life and at death, forbade it, and decreed it. Harm is not proper in life or in death."

And in a report: "Whoever cuts off an inheritance, Allah will cut off his share in Paradise."
[[See: Kashf al-Khafa': 2/310.]]

﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾ up to His saying:

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verses 7–14 (part 1 of 2):

﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave﴾ — the verse, and the reason for its revelation: Aws ibn Thabit al-Ansari died and left a wife called Umm Kahha and three daughters by her. Two men, who were the cousins (sons of the paternal uncle) of the deceased and his executors, rose up. The scholars differ over their names. Al-Kalbi and Qatada said they were ʿArfaṭa, while others said they were Suwayd and ʿArfaja. They took his property and gave his wife and daughters nothing. In the Jahiliyya (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance) they did not give inheritance to women or to young children, even if they were male. They gave inheritance only to adult men, saying: "We give only to one who fights on horseback and is able to take part in the distribution." He said: Umm Kahha came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was in the Mosque of al-Faḍīḥ, and she said: "O Messenger of Allah, Aws ibn Thabit died and left me three daughters, and I am his wife. I have nothing with which to support them. Their father left good property, and it is in the hands of Suwayd and ʿArfaja. They have given me and his daughters nothing of the property, and the girls are in my care. They are not fed or given drink, and no attention is paid to them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned the two men, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, her sons do not ride horses, do not carry burdens, and do not strike an enemy." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: «Go away until I see what Allah will reveal to me concerning them.» [[Asbab al-Nuzul (The Occasions of Revelation): 96.]] [246] So they left, and Allah the Most High revealed this verse.

﴿For men﴾ means the males among the children of the deceased and his relatives. ﴿There is a share﴾ means a portion and a lot, a part of ﴿what the parents and close relatives leave﴾ as inheritance. The females also have a portion of the inheritance.

﴿Of what is little of it or much﴾ of the property, ﴿a share ordained﴾, a known and obligatory portion. Its parallel is in His saying: ﴿I will surely take from Your servants an ordained share﴾. [[Surat al-Nisa’: 118.]] The word ﴿a share﴾ is in the accusative because it comes in the manner of a verbal noun (maṣdar), like the saying of one speaker: "You have a right over me, a binding right," and "I have a dirham, a gifted one that has been received." This is the view of al-Farra’.

Abu ʿUbayda said: it is accusative by way of exit (khurūj). Al-Kisa’i said: it is accusative as a detachment (qaṭʿ). Al-Akhfash said: He made that a share, and so established for them in the inheritance a right, without specifying how much it is.

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent to Suwayd and ʿArfaja: «Do not divide any of the property of Aws ibn Thabit. Allah the Most High has made a share for his daughters from what he left, and has not specified how much it is, until we see what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reveals concerning them.» Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children﴾ up to His saying ﴿That is the great triumph﴾. When it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah sent to Suwayd and ʿArfaja: «Give Umm Kahha an eighth of what was left, and give his daughters two-thirds, and the remainder of the property is for you both.» [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/47.]]

﴿And when the distribution is present﴾, meaning the distribution of inheritances, ﴿those of kinship﴾ who do not inherit, ﴿and the orphans and the needy﴾, ﴿provide for them from it﴾, meaning give them something from the property before the division. The scholars differ over the ruling of this verse:

Some people said: it is abrogated (mansūkha). Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Abu Malik said: this was before the verse of inheritance. When the verse of inheritance was revealed, the inheritance was given to its rightful people, the bequest was established, and this verse was abrogated. It was made for those close relatives who are present but do not inherit, the orphans and the needy. This is the narration of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Others said: it is definitive (muḥkama), and this is the view of al-Ash‘ari, al-Nakha‘i, al-Sha‘bi, al-Zuhri, and the narration of ʿIkrima and Muqatil from Ibn ʿAbbas. Mujahid said: it is obligatory upon the heirs, if their hearts are content with it.

Qatada, from al-Hasan: It is not abrogated, but people became stingy and miserly.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated from Maʿmar from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa: that his father gave him from the inheritance of Musʿab when he divided his property. This was said by al-Hasan.

The Successors (tabiʿun) said: They used to give the chest, the vessels, the rest of the goods, the clothes, and the thing from whose division one is ashamed. If some of the heirs were children, they differed:

Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Suddi and others said: when these present ones attend the division, if the deceased bequeathed something to them, his bequest is carried out for them. If the heirs are adults, they are given something. If they are children, excuse is made to them, and the guardian and the executor say: "I do not possess this; it belongs to these weak, young children who do not understand what right they have over it. If I had any of the inheritance I would give it to you. When they grow up, they will know your right. If they die and we inherit from them, we will give you your right." This is the well-known statement.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: this verse is one that people neglect. There are two guardians: a guardian who inherits, who is the one who gives and clothes, and a guardian who does not inherit, to whom "a kind word" is said.

Some of them said: that is a binding right in the property of the young and the old. If they are adults, they themselves give it, and if they are children, their guardian gives it.

Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated: that ʿUbayda al-Salmani divided the property of orphans, and he ordered a sheep to be slaughtered and made food for the people of this verse, and said: "Had it not been for this verse, this would have come from my own property."

Qatada narrated from Yahya ibn Yaʿmur, who said: "Those are definitive verses, Medinan, which people have abandoned: this verse, the verse of seeking permission, ﴿O you who believe, let those whom your right hands possess seek your permission﴾ [[Surat al-Nur: 58.]], and His saying ﴿O mankind, We created you from male and female﴾. [[Surat al-Hujurat: 13.]]"

Some of them said: this is recommended (nadb) and desirable (istihbab), not obligatory (ḥatm) and binding (ījāb), and this is the most correct of the sayings.

Ibn Zayd and others said: this concerns the bequest, not the inheritance. A man, when he made a bequest, would say: "So-and-so's property, he was commanded to bequeath a third of his property to those whom Allah named in this verse."

Ibn Abi Mulayka narrated from Asma’ bint ʿAbd al-Rahman, Abu Bakr and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, who reported: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr divided the inheritance of his father ʿAbd al-Rahman while ʿA’isha was alive. They said: "He left no needy person or relative in the house without giving them from his father's property," and he recited this verse: ﴿And when the distribution is present﴾.

Al-Qasim said: I mentioned that to Ibn ʿAbbas, and he said: "He did not do right; that is not his to do. That is only in the bequest."

﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them﴾ — the verse.

Most of the exegetes said: this concerns a man whom death approaches, and those present with him, at his bequest, say: "Consider for yourself, for your children and heirs will avail you nothing. So send ahead for yourself: free slaves, give charity, and give so-and-so such-and-such, and so-and-so such-and-such," until he has consumed most of his property and exhausted it, leaving nothing for his heirs. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade them from this, and commanded them to tell him to leave something for his children, not to exceed one-third in his bequest, and not to harm his heirs, just as if this dying man were himself the one making the bequest. He would be pleased for someone present to urge him to preserve his property for his children, and not to leave them destitute in their weakness, driving them to dependence and scheming.

Muqatil al-Hadrami said: a man whom death approaches, and someone present says to him: "Fear Allah and keep your property for yourself, for no one has a better right to your property than your children," and forbids him from bequeathing to his relatives, to the orphans and the poor. Had this been the one bequeathing, it would have pleased him to bequeath to them.

Al-Kalbi said: this address is to the guardians of orphans. It says: whoever has an orphan in his care, let him treat him well, let him speak and act well, and let him deal with him as he would wish to be dealt with regarding his own offspring after him. This is the narration of ʿAṭiyya from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Al-Sha‘ari said: We were in Constantinople during the days of Maslama ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, and among us were Ibn Muhabbarin, Ibn al-Daylami and Hani ibn Maktum. We began to discuss what would happen at the end of time. I became distressed when I heard it, and I said to Ibn al-Daylami: "O Abu Bashir, I wish I would never have a child." He struck my shoulder with his hand and said: "O my nephew, do not do that, for there is no portion decreed by the Books of Allah to come out of a man's loins except that it will come out, whether we wish it or not. Shall I not direct you to a matter which, if you attain it, Allah will save you from it, and if you leave a child after you, Allah will protect them because of you?" I said: "Yes." He recited this verse: ﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them. So let them fear Allah and speak words of rectitude﴾. Al-Sadid means justice and what is right of speech.

﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly﴾ — the verse.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It was revealed concerning a man from Ghatafan called Murthid ibn Zayd, who was in charge of the property of his nephew, an orphan child, and consumed it. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning him: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly﴾, meaning forbiddenly, without right, ﴿they only consume into their bellies fire﴾. He informed about his property and informed about his condition. The Arabs say of a thing which leads to another thing: "This is such-and-such, because of what it leads to," like their saying: "This is death," meaning it leads to it.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning one who drinks from vessels of gold and silver: «He only swallows into his belly the fire of Hell.» [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/112; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/212.]] [247]

He (peace be upon him) also said: «The sea is fire within fire,» [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/211.]] [248] meaning its consequence is likewise.
