And from Abu Hadrad al-Aslami, who said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) seeking his help regarding the bridal gift of a woman. He said: "How much are you giving her?" I said: "Two hundred dirhams." He said: "Even if you were scooping from the valley of Bathan, you would not have exceeded it." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 22/352.]] [274]

Muslim ibn Rumman, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever gives, as bridal gift, a handful of sawiq or dates has made it lawful (istahalla)." [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/468; Fath al-Bari: 9/173.]] [275]

And from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married a woman for ten dirhams.

Ahmad ibn Hanbal, from al-Hasan ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, who said: Damrah wrote to us, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah al-Kinani, that Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib married his daughter for two dirhams.

Waki', from Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shaybah, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever makes lawful with a dirham has made it lawful." [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 7/238; Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah: 3/317.]] [276] Waki' said: in marriage.

And from 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid, client of al-Aswad, that a man took a slave-girl as a concubine (tasarrara) but disliked her, so a man said to him: "Give her to me," and he gave her to him. This was mentioned to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: "Gifting is not permitted to anyone after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and even if he gave her a whip as bridal gift, she would be lawful."

Al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: The sunnah regarding the bridal gift is a ratl of silver (al-waraq). They disliked that the bridal gift of free women be like the bridal gifts of prostitutes, for a dirham or two dirhams, and they preferred it to be twenty dirhams.

And those of your women who commit lewdness (al-fahisha), that is, fornication (al-zina); in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud it reads "al-fahisha" with the same meaning, among your women, call four witnesses against them from among you, that is, from among the Muslims. If they testify against them for fornication, then confine them (fa-amsikuhunna), that is, imprison them, in the houses until death takes them or God appoints a way for them. This was only before the prescribed penalties (al-hudud) were revealed. In the early days of Islam, if a woman committed a sin she would be confined to the house until she died, and if she had a husband, her dowry remained his. Then the words of Him came down: ﴿The fornicatress and the fornicator, flog each one of them﴾ [[Surat al-Nur: 2.]].

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Take from me, take from me; God has appointed a way for them. The previously married (thayyib) for the previously married: a hundred lashes and stoning with stones; and the virgin (bikr) for the virgin: a hundred lashes and exile for a year." [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/476 and Sahih Muslim: 5/115, with some variation in order.]] [255]

So that verse abrogated part of this verse, namely the confinement in houses, and part of it remained in force, namely the requirement of witnesses.

And as for the two of you who commit it (wa-alladhani ya'tiyaniha minkum), that is, the man and the woman, the masculine and the feminine, when they come together, the masculine is applied to the feminine, and the pronoun ("ha") refers back to lewdness (al-fahisha).

The exegetes said: they are the two virgins who commit fornication. ﴿Harm them﴾ (fa-adhuhuma). Ata, Qatada and al-Suddi said: that is, rebuke and reproach them verbally: "Do you not fear God? Are you not ashamed before God when you committed fornication?" and the like. Mujahid said: revile and abuse them. Ibn Abbas said: it is with the tongue and the hand, such as harming with rebuke and striking with sandals.

﴿But if they repent and reform their conduct thereafter, leave them alone and do not harm them.﴾ This was before the prescribed penalties were revealed; when the penalties were revealed, this verse was abrogated. The confinement in the first verse was abrogated by stoning for the married woman, and flogging and exile for the virgin; flogging is in the Qur'an, while exile and stoning are in the Sunnah.

Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utba ibn Mas'ud related from Abu Hurayra and Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani that they informed him: two men disputed before the Prophet (ﷺ). One of them said: "O Messenger of God, judge between us by the Book of God." The other, who was more learned of the two, said: "Yes, O Messenger of God, judge between us by the Book of God, and permit me to speak."

He said: "Speak." He said: "My son was a laborer (asif) for this man" (Malik said: the 'asif is the hired worker), "and he committed fornication with his wife. They informed me that my son deserved stoning, so I ransomed him with a hundred sheep and a slave girl. Then I asked the people of knowledge, and they informed me that my son deserved a hundred lashes and a year's exile, and that stoning is only for his wife."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, I will certainly judge between you by the Book of God. As for your sheep and your slave girl, they are returned to you, and your son is to receive a hundred lashes and a year's exile." [[Musnad al-Tayalisi: 128; al-Sunan al-Kubra: 3/477.]] [256]

He also commanded Unays al-Aslami to go to the man's wife, and if she confessed, to stone her. She confessed, and he stoned her.

Al-Zuhri related from Abu Salama from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) exiled for fornication, and this practice continued until Marwan exiled during his governorship.

Al-Zuhri related from Abu Salama from Jabir ibn Abd Allah: a man from the tribe of Aslam came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and confessed to fornication before him. He turned away from him, then he confessed again, and he turned away again, until he testified against himself four times. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Are you insane?" He said: "No." He said: "Are you married (ahsanta)?" He said: "Yes." So the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded that he be stoned at the place of prayer (al-musalla). When the stones made him feel their pain, he fled, but he was overtaken and stoned until he died.

The Prophet (ﷺ) spoke well of him and did not lead the funeral prayer over him.

Sulayman ibn Buraydah related from his father: Maiz ibn Malik came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, purify me." He said: "Woe to you, return, seek forgiveness from God and repent to Him." He returned not far off and said the same, until on the fourth time the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "From what should I purify you?" He said: "From fornication." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Are you insane?" And he was informed that he was not insane. He said: "Did you drink wine?" A man stood up, smelled his breath, and found no smell of wine.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Did you commit fornication?" He said: "Yes." So the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded that he be stoned. The Prophet (ﷺ) then came and said: "Ask forgiveness for Maiz ibn Malik." They said: "Will God forgive Maiz ibn Malik?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Maiz has repented with a repentance which, if it were divided among a nation, would suffice for them." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 13/592-593; Sharh Musnad Abi Hanifa: 252.]] [257]

Al-Zuhri related from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah from Ibn Abbas from Umar ibn al-Khattab who said: "I feared that people would be left a long time until someone says, 'We do not find stoning in the Book of God,' and they would go astray by abandoning an obligation God revealed. Indeed, stoning is a truth upon whoever commits fornication when he is married (ahsan), if there is evidence, or pregnancy, or confession. I had recited it: 'The elderly man and the elderly woman, stone them absolutely.' And indeed the Messenger of God (ﷺ) stoned, and we stoned after him."

﴿Repentance is only incumbent upon God for those who do evil in ignorance﴾. Al-Hasan said: it means the repentance which God accepts, so "upon" (ala) here carries the sense of "with" (inda), and he put it in the position of a description.

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: I heard Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash say: "upon" (ala) here means "from" (min), saying: repentance is only from God for those who do evil in ignorance (bi-jahala). The exegetes differed on the meaning of ignorance (jahala):

Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: it means deliberately. Al-Kalbi said: he did not ignore that it was a sin, but he ignored its punishment. The rest of the exegetes said: it means all sins; whoever disobeys his Lord is ignorant until he desists from his disobedience.

Qatada: the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gathered and held that everything by which one disobeys his Lord is ignorance, whether deliberate or otherwise.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of His words "in ignorance" is that they chose fleeting pleasure over lasting pleasure. A parallel is in al-An'am: ﴿Whoever among you does evil in ignorance﴾ [[Surat al-An'am: 54.]]. "Then they repent soon" means before they nullify the evil with good deeds, which would nullify it.

Al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said: "soon" means while he is still in good health, before illness and death. Ikrima and Ibn Zayd: whatever comes before death is soon. Abu Majlaz and al-Dahhak: before witnessing the angel of death. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari: it is to repent before his death by the span of a she-camel's milking interval.

Zayd ibn Aslam related from Abd al-Rahman [al-Salmani]: four of the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gathered, and one of them said: "I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, accepts the repentance of a servant before he dies by a day.'" [258]

The second said: "And I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, accepts the repentance of a servant before he dies by half a day.'" [259]

The third said: "And I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, accepts the repentance of a servant before he dies by the forenoon.'" [260]

The fourth said: "And I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, accepts the repentance of a servant as long as he has not yet reached the death rattle.'" [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/425; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/474.]] [261]

Khalid ibn [Sa'dan] related from Ubada ibn al-Samit who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever repents a year before his death, God accepts his repentance." Then he said: "Indeed a year is long. Whoever repents a month before his death, God accepts his repentance." Then he said: "Indeed a month is long. Whoever repents a week before his death, God accepts his repentance." Then he said: "Indeed a week is long. Whoever repents an hour before his death, God accepts his repentance." Then he said: "Indeed an hour is long. Whoever repents before his death, before the death rattle comes upon him, God accepts his repentance." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 4/223, no. 10265.]] [262]

Al-Musayyib ibn Shurayk related from Amr ibn Ubayd from al-Hasan who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When Iblis descended, he said: 'By Your might and Your majesty, I will not leave the son of Adam until his soul leaves his body.' God, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'By My might and My majesty, I will not withhold repentance from My servant until he reaches the death rattle.'" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/93, with slight variation.]] [263]

And from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Satan said: 'By Your might, I will not cease misleading Your servants as long as their souls are in their bodies.' The Lord, blessed and exalted, said: 'By My might, My majesty and the loftiness of My station, I will not cease forgiving them as long as they ask My forgiveness.'" [[al-'Uhud al-Muhammadiyya, al-Sha'rani: 274.]] [264]

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami say: I heard Abu Bakr al-Razi say: I heard Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar say: It is said to the sincere penitent in his repentance, even if it be the length of an hour of the day or the length of one breath before his death: "How quickly you have come."

﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds (al-sayyi'at)﴾, meaning sins, ﴿until when death comes to one of them﴾ and he falls into the death throes, ﴿he says: Indeed I repent now.﴾ At that point, the faith of a disbeliever is not accepted, nor the repentance of a disobedient person. ﴿Nor of those who die while they are disbelievers; for those We have prepared a painful punishment.﴾ The word "those" (alladhina) is in the genitive position, meaning: nor for those who repent while they are disbelievers. ﴿Those, We have prepared (a'tadna) for them a painful punishment﴾, that is, We have readied it; the noun derived from it is "ata'd" (equipment).

Adi ibn al-Raqqa' said:
"Her spoils of the noble are taken by force, compelled,
and provisions for wars are gathered."
[[Aslab: what is seized in war. The verse is in Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/42.]]

And "'attada" and "'atad" are used of a horse prepared for war.

The Ja'fi poet said:
"They carried their insights upon their shoulders,
while my insight runs upon it, a prepared horse and I."
[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/396; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/57.]]

﴿O you who believe, it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾, that is, against their unwillingness.

The exegetes said: In the Jahiliyya and in the early days of Islam, when a man died leaving a wife, his son by another wife or his relative of the same lineage would come and cast his garment over that woman or over her tent, and he became more entitled to her than she was to herself and than anyone else. If he wished to marry her, he married her without a dowry, except the original dowry the deceased had given her. If he wished, he would marry her to someone else and take her dowry, giving her none of it. If he wished, he would restrain her and prevent her from marrying, making life hard for her and harming her, so that she would ransom herself with what she had inherited from the deceased, or she would die and he would inherit her. If the woman went back to her family before the guardian of her husband cast his garment over her, she was more entitled to herself. They continued doing this until Abu Qays ibn Sult al-Ansari died and left his wife Kabisha bint Ma'n al-Ansariyya; his son by another wife, called (Hisn), stood up.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: his name was Qays ibn Abi Qays. He cast his garment over her, thereby inheriting her marriage. Then he left her, did not approach her, and did not spend on her, harming her so that she would ransom herself with her property. They did this whenever one of them inherited a wife: if she was beautiful and wealthy, he consummated with her; if she was not beautiful, he made life hard for her so she would ransom herself from him. Kabisha came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, Abu Qays died and his son inherited my marriage, and Hisn has harmed me and made life hard for me. He neither spends on me, nor consummates with me, nor releases me." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to her: "Stay in your house until the command of God comes concerning you." [[Asbab al-Nuzul: 98.]] [265] She said: So she left, and the women of Medina heard of this; they came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) while he was in the Mosque of al-Fadih and said: "O Messenger of God, we are only in the situation of Kabisha, except that our sons do not marry us, while our paternal cousins do." Then God, Exalted, revealed: ﴿O you who believe, it is not lawful for you...﴾ the verse.

Al-Kisa'i, al-A'mash and Yahya ibn Wathhab read the "k" with a dammah here and in al-Tawba. The rest read it with a fatha. Al-Kisa'i said: they are two dialects. Al-Farra' said: "al-kurh" and "al-ikrah" differ; what one is compelled to do is "kurh" with a fatha, and what comes from one's own self is "kurh" with a dammah.

﴿Nor restrain them in order to take away part of what you have given them﴾, as the people of the Jahiliyya did (namely, preventing their remarriage, as mentioned above).

On the authority of al-Dahhak: this verse was revealed concerning a man who has an orphan girl in his guardianship, and he dislikes marrying her for her wealth; she is then under him as an old woman while he desires the young one. He dislikes divorcing the old woman, anticipating her death so he can inherit her property, while he withholds from her bed.

Ibn Abbas said: this is about a man who has a wife whom he dislikes keeping as a companion, and she has a dowry from him; he makes life hard for her and harms her so that she will ransom herself with the dowry or return to him what he gave her as dowry. God, Mighty and Majestic, forbade that, then said:

﴿Unless they commit a clear lewdness﴾, then at that point it becomes lawful for you to harm them so they will ransom themselves from you, and to restrain them, ﴿in order to take away part of what you have given them.﴾ They differed concerning the lewdness:

Some said: it is fornication. Al-Hasan said: if she commits fornication, it is lawful for her husband to ask for khul' (divorce by ransom). Ata said: when a man's wife committed lewdness, he would take back what he had given her and expel her; this was abrogated by the hudud (prescribed penalties).

Ibn Mas'ud, al-Dahhak and Qatada said: it is nushuz (disobedience/defiance by the wife).
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 94-95.]]

Ja'far ibn Muhammad related from his father from Jabir ibn Abd Allah that the Prophet (ﷺ) addressed the people and said: "Fear God regarding women, for you have taken them under the trust of God and made their private parts lawful by the word of God. Your right over them is that they not allow anyone you dislike to tread upon your bedding; if they do that, then strike them with a light blow that does not wound. Their right over you is their provision and clothing in a fair manner." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/412; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/172.]] [266]

As for His words "clear" (mubayyina) with a fatha on the ya', this was read by Ibn Abbas, Asim and Ibn Kathir; the rest read it with a kasra.

﴿And consort with them in kindness.﴾ Al-Hasan said: this returns to the beginning of the discussion, meaning ﴿And give the women their dowries as a gift﴾ and ﴿consort with them in kindness﴾. Some said: it means to treat them as you wish to be treated.

﴿But if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and God places in it much good﴾, which may be a righteous child, or God may incline him toward her afterward. So said the exegetes.

Makhul al-Azdi said: I heard Ibn Umar say: a man asks God for guidance and is guided, then he becomes resentful toward his Lord, but it is not long before he looks at the outcome and finds that it was good for him.

﴿And if you wish to exchange one wife for another, and you have given one of them a qintar (a large amount of wealth), then take nothing from it﴾, that is, from the qintar nothing at all. ﴿Would you take it, slandering and a clear sin?﴾ "Would you take it" is an interrogative of prohibition and rebuke. "Slandering" (buhtanan) and "a clear sin" (ithman mubinan) are in the accusative for two reasons: one is by removing the preposition, and the other by an implied verb; the sense being: you would incur, in taking it, slander and a clear sin. Then He said: ﴿And how would you take it﴾, in the sense of magnifying the wrong, like His words: ﴿How do you disbelieve in God?﴾ [[Surat al-Baqara: 28.]] ﴿When you have gone in to one another.﴾

The exegetes said: it means intercourse, but God is generous and alludes by what He wills to what He wills. The root of "ifda" is arriving at something without an intermediary.

﴿And they took from you a solemn covenant.﴾ Al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, al-Dahhak, Qatada and al-Suddi said: it is their words at the contract: "I have married her to you upon what God has taken from women for men: retaining in kindness or releasing in goodness." Mujahid said: it is the word of marriage by which intimacy is made lawful, like his saying "I married him." Al-Sha'bi, Ikrima and al-Rabi' said: it is his words: "You have taken them under the trust of God and made their private parts lawful by the word of God."

Chapter on what has been reported concerning permission to pay high dowries, based on His words: ﴿and you have given one of them a qintar﴾.

From Ata al-Khurasani: Umar proposed to Ali for his daughter Umm Kulthum, who was from Fatima bint the Messenger of God (ﷺ). He said: "She is young." Umar said: "I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'Every lineage and every marital relation will be cut off on the Day of Resurrection except my lineage and my marital relation.'" [[Fath al-Qadir: 2/502.]] So for that reason I desire her. [267]

Ali (may God be pleased with him) said: "I will send her to you so you may see her youth." He sent her to him, and she came to him and said: "My father says to you: Are you pleased with the nihla (dowry)?" He said: "I am pleased with it." So he married him to his daughter, and Umar gave a dowry of forty thousand dirhams. [[There is room for scrutiny and reflection concerning this account.]]

From Ibn Sirin: al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) married a woman, and sent her a hundred slave girls, each with a thousand dirhams.

Murshid ibn Abd Allah al-Barni related from Uqba ibn Amir al-Juhani that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The best marriage is the easiest of it."

And he (ﷺ) said to a man: "Are you pleased that I marry you to so-and-so?" [268] He said: "Yes." He said to the woman:

"Are you pleased that I marry you to so-and-so?" She said: "Yes." So he married one of them to the other. The man went in to her, but he had not set a bridal gift (mahr) for her and had not given her anything. He was among those who witnessed al-Hudaybiyyah and had a share (sahm) at Khaybar. When his death approached, he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married me to so-and-so, and I did not set a bridal gift for her and did not give her anything, and I have now given her my share at Khaybar as her bridal gift." So she took that share and sold it for one hundred thousand. [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/470; Sahih Ibn Hibban: 9/281.]]

And on the authority of Damrah ibn Habib: Umm Habibah was in the land of Abyssinia with Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), and the Messenger of Allah married her, and al-Najashi paid the bridal gift on his behalf, four hundred dinars.

With the same chain, from Ibn Sirin, from Ibn Abbas: he married Sulaymah al-Sulamiyyah for ten thousand dirhams.

Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ibn Bishr: that 'Urwah al-Bariqi married the daughter of Hani ibn Qabisah for one thousand dirhams.

And from Ghaylan ibn Jarir: that Mutarrif married a woman for ten thousand awqiyah.

Chapter on those who disliked this, and discussion of the minimum bridal gift.

From Ibn Sirin, who said: Abu al-'Ajfa al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: I heard 'Umar while he was addressing the people; he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "Beware, do not exaggerate in the bridal gifts of women, for if it were a point of honour in this world or of piety before Allah, the one most entitled to it would be the Prophet (ﷺ). He never gave any of his wives or daughters a bridal gift exceeding twelve awqiyah. Indeed, one of you will so overpay for a woman's bridal gift that resentment remains in his soul, and he says: 'You were a leather water-bag's handle (hilq al-qirbah) or its sweat (irq al-qirbah).'"

'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from 'A'ishah, that she said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among the blessings of a woman is the ease of her bridal gift and the ease of her womb." [[Al-Mustadrak: 2/181; Irwa' al-Ghalil: 6/350.]] [270]

'Urwah said: And I say on my own: among the ill omens of a woman is that her bridal gift be great.

Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Our bridal gift, from the time the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among us, was ten awqiyah, which is four hundred dirhams.

Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw on 'Abd al-Rahman a trace of yellow (saffron) and said: "What is this?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I married a woman for the weight of a date-stone of gold." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May Allah bless you. Hold a walimah, even with a sheep." [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/227.]] [271]

It is said: it was five dirhams.

And from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi that a woman came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have given myself to you," and she stood for a long time. A man stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, marry her to me if you have no need of her." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you have anything to give her as a bridal gift?" He said: "I have nothing except this waist-wrapper of mine." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you give it to her, you will sit without a waist-wrapper, so seek something else." He said: "I find nothing." He said: "Seek, even an iron ring." He sought but found nothing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Do you have any of the Qur'an with you?" He said: "Yes, surah so-and-so and surah so-and-so," naming surahs. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have married her to you for what you have of the Qur'an." [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/336; Ahkam al-Qur'an: 3/480.]] [272]

And on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir, from his father: that a man married a woman for two sandals, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Are you content to give your property for these two sandals?" He said: "Yes," so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permitted it. [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/445; Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 2/290, no. 1120.]]

And from Abu Hadrad al-Aslami, who said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) seeking his help regarding the bridal gift of a woman. He said: "How much are you giving her?" I said: "Two hundred dirhams." He said: "Even if you were scooping from the valley of Bathan, you would not have exceeded it." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 22/352.]] [274]

Muslim ibn Rumman, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever gives, as bridal gift, a handful of sawiq or dates has made it lawful (istahalla)." [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/468; Fath al-Bari: 9/173.]] [275]

And from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married a woman for ten dirhams.

Ahmad ibn Hanbal, from al-Hasan ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, who said: Damrah wrote to us, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah al-Kinani, that Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib married his daughter for two dirhams.

Waki', from Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shaybah, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever makes lawful with a dirham has made it lawful." [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 7/238; Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah: 3/317.]] [276] Waki' said: in marriage.

And from 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid, client of al-Aswad, that a man took a slave-girl as a concubine (tasarrara) but disliked her, so a man said to him: "Give her to me," and he gave her to him. This was mentioned to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: "Gifting is not permitted to anyone after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and even if he gave her a whip as bridal gift, she would be lawful."

Al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: The sunnah regarding the bridal gift is a ratl of silver (al-waraq). They disliked that the bridal gift of free women be like the bridal gifts of prostitutes, for a dirham or two dirhams, and they preferred it to be twenty dirhams.

And those of your women who commit lewdness (al-fahisha), that is, fornication (al-zina); in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud it reads "al-fahisha" with the same meaning, among your women, call four witnesses against them from among you, that is, from among the Muslims. If they testify against them for fornication, then confine them (fa-amsikuhunna), that is, imprison them, in the houses until death takes them or God appoints a way for them. This was only before the prescribed penalties (al-hudud) were revealed. In the early days of Islam, if a woman committed a sin she would be confined to the house until she died, and if she had a husband, her dowry remained his. Then the words of Him came down: ﴿The fornicatress and the fornicator, flog each one of them﴾ [[Surat al-Nur: 2.]].

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Take from me, take from me; God has appointed a way for them. The previously married (thayyib) for the previously married: a hundred lashes and stoning with stones; and the virgin (bikr) for the virgin: a hundred lashes and exile for a year." [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/476 and Sahih Muslim: 5/115, with some variation in order.]] [255]

So that verse abrogated part of this verse, namely the confinement in houses, and part of it remained in force, namely the requirement of witnesses.

And as for the two of you who commit it (wa-alladhani ya'tiyaniha minkum), that is, the man and the woman, the masculine and the feminine, when they come together, the masculine is applied to the feminine, and the pronoun ("ha") refers back to lewdness (al-fahisha).

The exegetes said: they are the two virgins who commit fornication. ﴿Harm them﴾ (fa-adhuhuma). Ata, Qatada and al-Suddi said: that is, rebuke and reproach them verbally: "Do you not fear God? Are you not ashamed before God when you committed fornication?" and the like. Mujahid said: revile and abuse them. Ibn Abbas said: it is with the tongue and the hand, such as harming with rebuke and striking with sandals.

﴿But if they repent and reform their conduct thereafter, leave them alone and do not harm them.﴾ This was before the prescribed penalties were revealed; when the penalties were revealed, this verse was abrogated. The confinement in the first verse was abrogated by stoning for the married woman, and flogging and exile for the virgin; flogging is in the Qur'an, while exile and stoning are in the Sunnah.

Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utba ibn Mas'ud related from Abu Hurayra and Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani that they informed him: two men disputed before the Prophet (ﷺ). One of them said: "O Messenger of God, judge between us by the Book of God." The other, who was more learned of the two, said: "Yes, O Messenger of God, judge between us by the Book of God, and permit me to speak."

He said: "Speak." He said: "My son was a laborer (asif) for this man" (Malik said: the 'asif is the hired worker), "and he committed fornication with his wife. They informed me that my son deserved stoning, so I ransomed him with a hundred sheep and a slave girl. Then I asked the people of knowledge, and they informed me that my son deserved a hundred lashes and a year's exile, and that stoning is only for his wife."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, I will certainly judge between you by the Book of God. As for your sheep and your slave girl, they are returned to you, and your son is to receive a hundred lashes and a year's exile." [[Musnad al-Tayalisi: 128; al-Sunan al-Kubra: 3/477.]] [256]

He also commanded Unays al-Aslami to go to the man's wife, and if she confessed, to stone her. She confessed, and he stoned her.

Al-Zuhri related from Abu Salama from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) exiled for fornication, and this practice continued until Marwan exiled during his governorship.

Al-Zuhri related from Abu Salama from Jabir ibn Abd Allah: a man from the tribe of Aslam came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and confessed to fornication before him. He turned away from him, then he confessed again, and he turned away again, until he testified against himself four times. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Are you insane?" He said: "No." He said: "Are you married (ahsanta)?" He said: "Yes." So the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded that he be stoned at the place of prayer (al-musalla). When the stones made him feel their pain, he fled, but he was overtaken and stoned until he died.

The Prophet (ﷺ) spoke well of him and did not lead the funeral prayer over him.

Sulayman ibn Buraydah related from his father: Maiz ibn Malik came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, purify me." He said: "Woe to you, return, seek forgiveness from God and repent to Him." He returned not far off and said the same, until on the fourth time the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "From what should I purify you?" He said: "From fornication." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Are you insane?" And he was informed that he was not insane. He said: "Did you drink wine?" A man stood up, smelled his breath, and found no smell of wine.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Did you commit fornication?" He said: "Yes." So the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded that he be stoned. The Prophet (ﷺ) then came and said: "Ask forgiveness for Maiz ibn Malik." They said: "Will God forgive Maiz ibn Malik?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Maiz has repented with a repentance which, if it were divided among a nation, would suffice for them." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 13/592-593; Sharh Musnad Abi Hanifa: 252.]] [257]

Al-Zuhri related from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah from Ibn Abbas from Umar ibn al-Khattab who said: "I feared that people would be left a long time until someone says, 'We do not find stoning in the Book of God,' and they would go astray by abandoning an obligation God revealed. Indeed, stoning is a truth upon whoever commits fornication when he is married (ahsan), if there is evidence, or pregnancy, or confession. I had recited it: 'The elderly man and the elderly woman, stone them absolutely.' And indeed the Messenger of God (ﷺ) stoned, and we stoned after him."

﴿Repentance is only incumbent upon God for those who do evil in ignorance﴾. Al-Hasan said: it means the repentance which God accepts, so "upon" (ala) here carries the sense of "with" (inda), and he put it in the position of a description.

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: I heard Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash say: "upon" (ala) here means "from" (min), saying: repentance is only from God for those who do evil in ignorance (bi-jahala). The exegetes differed on the meaning of ignorance (jahala):

Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: it means deliberately. Al-Kalbi said: he did not ignore that it was a sin, but he ignored its punishment. The rest of the exegetes said: it means all sins; whoever disobeys his Lord is ignorant until he desists from his disobedience.

Qatada: the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gathered and held that everything by which one disobeys his Lord is ignorance, whether deliberate or otherwise.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of His words "in ignorance" is that they chose fleeting pleasure over lasting pleasure. A parallel is in al-An'am: ﴿Whoever among you does evil in ignorance﴾ [[Surat al-An'am: 54.]]. "Then they repent soon" means before they nullify the evil with good deeds, which would nullify it.

Al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said: "soon" means while he is still in good health, before illness and death. Ikrima and Ibn Zayd: whatever comes before death is soon. Abu Majlaz and al-Dahhak: before witnessing the angel of death. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari: it is to repent before his death by the span of a she-camel's milking interval.

Zayd ibn Aslam related from Abd al-Rahman [al-Salmani]: four of the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gathered, and one of them said: "I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, accepts the repentance of a servant before he dies by a day.'" [258]

The second said: "And I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, accepts the repentance of a servant before he dies by half a day.'" [259]

The third said: "And I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, accepts the repentance of a servant before he dies by the forenoon.'" [260]

The fourth said: "And I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, accepts the repentance of a servant as long as he has not yet reached the death rattle.'" [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/425; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/474.]] [261]

Khalid ibn [Sa'dan] related from Ubada ibn al-Samit who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever repents a year before his death, God accepts his repentance." Then he said: "Indeed a year is long. Whoever repents a month before his death, God accepts his repentance." Then he said: "Indeed a month is long. Whoever repents a week before his death, God accepts his repentance." Then he said: "Indeed a week is long. Whoever repents an hour before his death, God accepts his repentance." Then he said: "Indeed an hour is long. Whoever repents before his death, before the death rattle comes upon him, God accepts his repentance." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 4/223, no. 10265.]] [262]

Al-Musayyib ibn Shurayk related from Amr ibn Ubayd from al-Hasan who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When Iblis descended, he said: 'By Your might and Your majesty, I will not leave the son of Adam until his soul leaves his body.' God, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'By My might and My majesty, I will not withhold repentance from My servant until he reaches the death rattle.'" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/93, with slight variation.]] [263]

And from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Satan said: 'By Your might, I will not cease misleading Your servants as long as their souls are in their bodies.' The Lord, blessed and exalted, said: 'By My might, My majesty and the loftiness of My station, I will not cease forgiving them as long as they ask My forgiveness.'" [[al-'Uhud al-Muhammadiyya, al-Sha'rani: 274.]] [264]

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami say: I heard Abu Bakr al-Razi say: I heard Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar say: It is said to the sincere penitent in his repentance, even if it be the length of an hour of the day or the length of one breath before his death: "How quickly you have come."

﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds (al-sayyi'at)﴾, meaning sins, ﴿until when death comes to one of them﴾ and he falls into the death throes, ﴿he says: Indeed I repent now.﴾ At that point, the faith of a disbeliever is not accepted, nor the repentance of a disobedient person. ﴿Nor of those who die while they are disbelievers; for those We have prepared a painful punishment.﴾ The word "those" (alladhina) is in the genitive position, meaning: nor for those who repent while they are disbelievers. ﴿Those, We have prepared (a'tadna) for them a painful punishment﴾, that is, We have readied it; the noun derived from it is "ata'd" (equipment).

Adi ibn al-Raqqa' said:
"Her spoils of the noble are taken by force, compelled,
and provisions for wars are gathered."
[[Aslab: what is seized in war. The verse is in Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/42.]]

And "'attada" and "'atad" are used of a horse prepared for war.

The Ja'fi poet said:
"They carried their insights upon their shoulders,
while my insight runs upon it, a prepared horse and I."
[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/396; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/57.]]

﴿O you who believe, it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾, that is, against their unwillingness.

The exegetes said: In the Jahiliyya and in the early days of Islam, when a man died leaving a wife, his son by another wife or his relative of the same lineage would come and cast his garment over that woman or over her tent, and he became more entitled to her than she was to herself and than anyone else. If he wished to marry her, he married her without a dowry, except the original dowry the deceased had given her. If he wished, he would marry her to someone else and take her dowry, giving her none of it. If he wished, he would restrain her and prevent her from marrying, making life hard for her and harming her, so that she would ransom herself with what she had inherited from the deceased, or she would die and he would inherit her. If the woman went back to her family before the guardian of her husband cast his garment over her, she was more entitled to herself. They continued doing this until Abu Qays ibn Sult al-Ansari died and left his wife Kabisha bint Ma'n al-Ansariyya; his son by another wife, called (Hisn), stood up.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: his name was Qays ibn Abi Qays. He cast his garment over her, thereby inheriting her marriage. Then he left her, did not approach her, and did not spend on her, harming her so that she would ransom herself with her property. They did this whenever one of them inherited a wife: if she was beautiful and wealthy, he consummated with her; if she was not beautiful, he made life hard for her so she would ransom herself from him. Kabisha came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, Abu Qays died and his son inherited my marriage, and Hisn has harmed me and made life hard for me. He neither spends on me, nor consummates with me, nor releases me." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to her: "Stay in your house until the command of God comes concerning you." [[Asbab al-Nuzul: 98.]] [265] She said: So she left, and the women of Medina heard of this; they came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) while he was in the Mosque of al-Fadih and said: "O Messenger of God, we are only in the situation of Kabisha, except that our sons do not marry us, while our paternal cousins do." Then God, Exalted, revealed: ﴿O you who believe, it is not lawful for you...﴾ the verse.

Al-Kisa'i, al-A'mash and Yahya ibn Wathhab read the "k" with a dammah here and in al-Tawba. The rest read it with a fatha. Al-Kisa'i said: they are two dialects. Al-Farra' said: "al-kurh" and "al-ikrah" differ; what one is compelled to do is "kurh" with a fatha, and what comes from one's own self is "kurh" with a dammah.

﴿Nor restrain them in order to take away part of what you have given them﴾, as the people of the Jahiliyya did (namely, preventing their remarriage, as mentioned above).

On the authority of al-Dahhak: this verse was revealed concerning a man who has an orphan girl in his guardianship, and he dislikes marrying her for her wealth; she is then under him as an old woman while he desires the young one. He dislikes divorcing the old woman, anticipating her death so he can inherit her property, while he withholds from her bed.

Ibn Abbas said: this is about a man who has a wife whom he dislikes keeping as a companion, and she has a dowry from him; he makes life hard for her and harms her so that she will ransom herself with the dowry or return to him what he gave her as dowry. God, Mighty and Majestic, forbade that, then said:

﴿Unless they commit a clear lewdness﴾, then at that point it becomes lawful for you to harm them so they will ransom themselves from you, and to restrain them, ﴿in order to take away part of what you have given them.﴾ They differed concerning the lewdness:

Some said: it is fornication. Al-Hasan said: if she commits fornication, it is lawful for her husband to ask for khul' (divorce by ransom). Ata said: when a man's wife committed lewdness, he would take back what he had given her and expel her; this was abrogated by the hudud (prescribed penalties).

Ibn Mas'ud, al-Dahhak and Qatada said: it is nushuz (disobedience/defiance by the wife).
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 94-95.]]

Ja'far ibn Muhammad related from his father from Jabir ibn Abd Allah that the Prophet (ﷺ) addressed the people and said: "Fear God regarding women, for you have taken them under the trust of God and made their private parts lawful by the word of God. Your right over them is that they not allow anyone you dislike to tread upon your bedding; if they do that, then strike them with a light blow that does not wound. Their right over you is their provision and clothing in a fair manner." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/412; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/172.]] [266]

As for His words "clear" (mubayyina) with a fatha on the ya', this was read by Ibn Abbas, Asim and Ibn Kathir; the rest read it with a kasra.

﴿And consort with them in kindness.﴾ Al-Hasan said: this returns to the beginning of the discussion, meaning ﴿And give the women their dowries as a gift﴾ and ﴿consort with them in kindness﴾. Some said: it means to treat them as you wish to be treated.

﴿But if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and God places in it much good﴾, which may be a righteous child, or God may incline him toward her afterward. So said the exegetes.

Makhul al-Azdi said: I heard Ibn Umar say: a man asks God for guidance and is guided, then he becomes resentful toward his Lord, but it is not long before he looks at the outcome and finds that it was good for him.

﴿And if you wish to exchange one wife for another, and you have given one of them a qintar (a large amount of wealth), then take nothing from it﴾, that is, from the qintar nothing at all. ﴿Would you take it, slandering and a clear sin?﴾ "Would you take it" is an interrogative of prohibition and rebuke. "Slandering" (buhtanan) and "a clear sin" (ithman mubinan) are in the accusative for two reasons: one is by removing the preposition, and the other by an implied verb; the sense being: you would incur, in taking it, slander and a clear sin. Then He said: ﴿And how would you take it﴾, in the sense of magnifying the wrong, like His words: ﴿How do you disbelieve in God?﴾ [[Surat al-Baqara: 28.]] ﴿When you have gone in to one another.﴾

The exegetes said: it means intercourse, but God is generous and alludes by what He wills to what He wills. The root of "ifda" is arriving at something without an intermediary.

﴿And they took from you a solemn covenant.﴾ Al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, al-Dahhak, Qatada and al-Suddi said: it is their words at the contract: "I have married her to you upon what God has taken from women for men: retaining in kindness or releasing in goodness." Mujahid said: it is the word of marriage by which intimacy is made lawful, like his saying "I married him." Al-Sha'bi, Ikrima and al-Rabi' said: it is his words: "You have taken them under the trust of God and made their private parts lawful by the word of God."

Chapter on what has been reported concerning permission to pay high dowries, based on His words: ﴿and you have given one of them a qintar﴾.

From Ata al-Khurasani: Umar proposed to Ali for his daughter Umm Kulthum, who was from Fatima bint the Messenger of God (ﷺ). He said: "She is young." Umar said: "I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'Every lineage and every marital relation will be cut off on the Day of Resurrection except my lineage and my marital relation.'" [[Fath al-Qadir: 2/502.]] So for that reason I desire her. [267]

Ali (may God be pleased with him) said: "I will send her to you so you may see her youth." He sent her to him, and she came to him and said: "My father says to you: Are you pleased with the nihla (dowry)?" He said: "I am pleased with it." So he married him to his daughter, and Umar gave a dowry of forty thousand dirhams. [[There is room for scrutiny and reflection concerning this account.]]

From Ibn Sirin: al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) married a woman, and sent her a hundred slave girls, each with a thousand dirhams.

Murshid ibn Abd Allah al-Barni related from Uqba ibn Amir al-Juhani that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The best marriage is the easiest of it."

And he (ﷺ) said to a man: "Are you pleased that I marry you to so-and-so?" [268] He said: "Yes." He said to the woman:

"Are you pleased that I marry you to so-and-so?" She said: "Yes." So he married one of them to the other. The man went in to her, but he had not set a bridal gift (mahr) for her and had not given her anything. He was among those who witnessed al-Hudaybiyyah and had a share (sahm) at Khaybar. When his death approached, he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married me to so-and-so, and I did not set a bridal gift for her and did not give her anything, and I have now given her my share at Khaybar as her bridal gift." So she took that share and sold it for one hundred thousand. [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/470; Sahih Ibn Hibban: 9/281.]]

And on the authority of Damrah ibn Habib: Umm Habibah was in the land of Abyssinia with Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), and the Messenger of Allah married her, and al-Najashi paid the bridal gift on his behalf, four hundred dinars.

With the same chain, from Ibn Sirin, from Ibn Abbas: he married Sulaymah al-Sulamiyyah for ten thousand dirhams.

Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ibn Bishr: that 'Urwah al-Bariqi married the daughter of Hani ibn Qabisah for one thousand dirhams.

And from Ghaylan ibn Jarir: that Mutarrif married a woman for ten thousand awqiyah.

Chapter on those who disliked this, and discussion of the minimum bridal gift.

From Ibn Sirin, who said: Abu al-'Ajfa al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: I heard 'Umar while he was addressing the people; he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "Beware, do not exaggerate in the bridal gifts of women, for if it were a point of honour in this world or of piety before Allah, the one most entitled to it would be the Prophet (ﷺ). He never gave any of his wives or daughters a bridal gift exceeding twelve awqiyah. Indeed, one of you will so overpay for a woman's bridal gift that resentment remains in his soul, and he says: 'You were a leather water-bag's handle (hilq al-qirbah) or its sweat (irq al-qirbah).'"

'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from 'A'ishah, that she said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among the blessings of a woman is the ease of her bridal gift and the ease of her womb." [[Al-Mustadrak: 2/181; Irwa' al-Ghalil: 6/350.]] [270]

'Urwah said: And I say on my own: among the ill omens of a woman is that her bridal gift be great.

Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Our bridal gift, from the time the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among us, was ten awqiyah, which is four hundred dirhams.

Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw on 'Abd al-Rahman a trace of yellow (saffron) and said: "What is this?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I married a woman for the weight of a date-stone of gold." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May Allah bless you. Hold a walimah, even with a sheep." [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/227.]] [271]

It is said: it was five dirhams.

And from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi that a woman came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have given myself to you," and she stood for a long time. A man stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, marry her to me if you have no need of her." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you have anything to give her as a bridal gift?" He said: "I have nothing except this waist-wrapper of mine." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you give it to her, you will sit without a waist-wrapper, so seek something else." He said: "I find nothing." He said: "Seek, even an iron ring." He sought but found nothing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Do you have any of the Qur'an with you?" He said: "Yes, surah so-and-so and surah so-and-so," naming surahs. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have married her to you for what you have of the Qur'an." [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/336; Ahkam al-Qur'an: 3/480.]] [272]

And on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir, from his father: that a man married a woman for two sandals, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Are you content to give your property for these two sandals?" He said: "Yes," so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permitted it. [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/445; Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 2/290, no. 1120.]]

And from Abu Hadrad al-Aslami, who said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) seeking his help regarding the bridal gift of a woman. He said: "How much are you giving her?" I said: "Two hundred dirhams." He said: "Even if you were scooping from the valley of Bathan, you would not have exceeded it." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 22/352.]] [274]

Muslim ibn Rumman, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever gives, as bridal gift, a handful of sawiq or dates has made it lawful (istahalla)." [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/468; Fath al-Bari: 9/173.]] [275]

And from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married a woman for ten dirhams.

Ahmad ibn Hanbal, from al-Hasan ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, who said: Damrah wrote to us, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah al-Kinani, that Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib married his daughter for two dirhams.

Waki', from Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shaybah, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever makes lawful with a dirham has made it lawful." [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 7/238; Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah: 3/317.]] [276] Waki' said: in marriage.

And from 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid, client of al-Aswad, that a man took a slave-girl as a concubine (tasarrara) but disliked her, so a man said to him: "Give her to me," and he gave her to him. This was mentioned to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: "Gifting is not permitted to anyone after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and even if he gave her a whip as bridal gift, she would be lawful."

Al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: The sunnah regarding the bridal gift is a ratl of silver (al-waraq). They disliked that the bridal gift of free women be like the bridal gifts of prostitutes, for a dirham or two dirhams, and they preferred it to be twenty dirhams.

And those of your women who commit lewdness (al-fahisha), that is, fornication (al-zina); in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud it reads "al-fahisha" with the same meaning, among your women, call four witnesses against them from among you, that is, from among the Muslims. If they testify against them for fornication, then confine them (fa-amsikuhunna), that is, imprison them, in the houses until death takes them or God appoints a way for them. This was only before the prescribed penalties (al-hudud) were revealed. In the early days of Islam, if a woman committed a sin she would be confined to the house until she died, and if she had a husband, her dowry remained his. Then the words of Him came down: ﴿The fornicatress and the fornicator, flog each one of them﴾ [[Surat al-Nur: 2.]].

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Take from me, take from me; God has appointed a way for them. The previously married (thayyib) for the previously married: a hundred lashes and stoning with stones; and the virgin (bikr) for the virgin: a hundred lashes and exile for a year." [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/476 and Sahih Muslim: 5/115, with some variation in order.]] [255]

So that verse abrogated part of this verse, namely the confinement in houses, and part of it remained in force, namely the requirement of witnesses.

And as for the two of you who commit it (wa-alladhani ya'tiyaniha minkum), that is, the man and the woman, the masculine and the feminine, when they come together, the masculine is applied to the feminine, and the pronoun ("ha") refers back to lewdness (al-fahisha).

The exegetes said: they are the two virgins who commit fornication. ﴿Harm them﴾ (fa-adhuhuma). Ata, Qatada and al-Suddi said: that is, rebuke and reproach them verbally: "Do you not fear God? Are you not ashamed before God when you committed fornication?" and the like. Mujahid said: revile and abuse them. Ibn Abbas said: it is with the tongue and the hand, such as harming with rebuke and striking with sandals.

﴿But if they repent and reform their conduct thereafter, leave them alone and do not harm them.﴾ This was before the prescribed penalties were revealed; when the penalties were revealed, this verse was abrogated. The confinement in the first verse was abrogated by stoning for the married woman, and flogging and exile for the virgin; flogging is in the Qur'an, while exile and stoning are in the Sunnah.

Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utba ibn Mas'ud related from Abu Hurayra and Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani that they informed him: two men disputed before the Prophet (ﷺ). One of them said: "O Messenger of God, judge between us by the Book of God." The other, who was more learned of the two, said: "Yes, O Messenger of God, judge between us by the Book of God, and permit me to speak."

He said: "Speak." He said: "My son was a laborer (asif) for this man" (Malik said: the 'asif is the hired worker), "and he committed fornication with his wife. They informed me that my son deserved stoning, so I ransomed him with a hundred sheep and a slave girl. Then I asked the people of knowledge, and they informed me that my son deserved a hundred lashes and a year's exile, and that stoning is only for his wife."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, I will certainly judge between you by the Book of God. As for your sheep and your slave girl, they are returned to you, and your son is to receive a hundred lashes and a year's exile." [[Musnad al-Tayalisi: 128; al-Sunan al-Kubra: 3/477.]] [256]

He also commanded Unays al-Aslami to go to the man's wife, and if she confessed, to stone her. She confessed, and he stoned her.

Al-Zuhri related from Abu Salama from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) exiled for fornication, and this practice continued until Marwan exiled during his governorship.

Al-Zuhri related from Abu Salama from Jabir ibn Abd Allah: a man from the tribe of Aslam came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and confessed to fornication before him. He turned away from him, then he confessed again, and he turned away again, until he testified against himself four times. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Are you insane?" He said: "No." He said: "Are you married (ahsanta)?" He said: "Yes." So the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded that he be stoned at the place of prayer (al-musalla). When the stones made him feel their pain, he fled, but he was overtaken and stoned until he died.

The Prophet (ﷺ) spoke well of him and did not lead the funeral prayer over him.

Sulayman ibn Buraydah related from his father: Maiz ibn Malik came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, purify me." He said: "Woe to you, return, seek forgiveness from God and repent to Him." He returned not far off and said the same, until on the fourth time the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "From what should I purify you?" He said: "From fornication." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Are you insane?" And he was informed that he was not insane. He said: "Did you drink wine?" A man stood up, smelled his breath, and found no smell of wine.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Did you commit fornication?" He said: "Yes." So the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded that he be stoned. The Prophet (ﷺ) then came and said: "Ask forgiveness for Maiz ibn Malik." They said: "Will God forgive Maiz ibn Malik?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Maiz has repented with a repentance which, if it were divided among a nation, would suffice for them." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 13/592-593; Sharh Musnad Abi Hanifa: 252.]] [257]

Al-Zuhri related from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah from Ibn Abbas from Umar ibn al-Khattab who said: "I feared that people would be left a long time until someone says, 'We do not find stoning in the Book of God,' and they would go astray by abandoning an obligation God revealed. Indeed, stoning is a truth upon whoever commits fornication when he is married (ahsan), if there is evidence, or pregnancy, or confession. I had recited it: 'The elderly man and the elderly woman, stone them absolutely.' And indeed the Messenger of God (ﷺ) stoned, and we stoned after him."

﴿Repentance is only incumbent upon God for those who do evil in ignorance﴾. Al-Hasan said: it means the repentance which God accepts, so "upon" (ala) here carries the sense of "with" (inda), and he put it in the position of a description.

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: I heard Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash say: "upon" (ala) here means "from" (min), saying: repentance is only from God for those who do evil in ignorance (bi-jahala). The exegetes differed on the meaning of ignorance (jahala):

Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: it means deliberately. Al-Kalbi said: he did not ignore that it was a sin, but he ignored its punishment. The rest of the exegetes said: it means all sins; whoever disobeys his Lord is ignorant until he desists from his disobedience.

Qatada: the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gathered and held that everything by which one disobeys his Lord is ignorance, whether deliberate or otherwise.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of His words "in ignorance" is that they chose fleeting pleasure over lasting pleasure. A parallel is in al-An'am: ﴿Whoever among you does evil in ignorance﴾ [[Surat al-An'am: 54.]]. "Then they repent soon" means before they nullify the evil with good deeds, which would nullify it.

Al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said: "soon" means while he is still in good health, before illness and death. Ikrima and Ibn Zayd: whatever comes before death is soon. Abu Majlaz and al-Dahhak: before witnessing the angel of death. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari: it is to repent before his death by the span of a she-camel's milking interval.

Zayd ibn Aslam related from Abd al-Rahman [al-Salmani]: four of the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gathered, and one of them said: "I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, accepts the repentance of a servant before he dies by a day.'" [258]

The second said: "And I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, accepts the repentance of a servant before he dies by half a day.'" [259]

The third said: "And I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, accepts the repentance of a servant before he dies by the forenoon.'" [260]

The fourth said: "And I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, accepts the repentance of a servant as long as he has not yet reached the death rattle.'" [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/425; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/474.]] [261]

Khalid ibn [Sa'dan] related from Ubada ibn al-Samit who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever repents a year before his death, God accepts his repentance." Then he said: "Indeed a year is long. Whoever repents a month before his death, God accepts his repentance." Then he said: "Indeed a month is long. Whoever repents a week before his death, God accepts his repentance." Then he said: "Indeed a week is long. Whoever repents an hour before his death, God accepts his repentance." Then he said: "Indeed an hour is long. Whoever repents before his death, before the death rattle comes upon him, God accepts his repentance." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 4/223, no. 10265.]] [262]

Al-Musayyib ibn Shurayk related from Amr ibn Ubayd from al-Hasan who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When Iblis descended, he said: 'By Your might and Your majesty, I will not leave the son of Adam until his soul leaves his body.' God, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'By My might and My majesty, I will not withhold repentance from My servant until he reaches the death rattle.'" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/93, with slight variation.]] [263]

And from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Satan said: 'By Your might, I will not cease misleading Your servants as long as their souls are in their bodies.' The Lord, blessed and exalted, said: 'By My might, My majesty and the loftiness of My station, I will not cease forgiving them as long as they ask My forgiveness.'" [[al-'Uhud al-Muhammadiyya, al-Sha'rani: 274.]] [264]

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami say: I heard Abu Bakr al-Razi say: I heard Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar say: It is said to the sincere penitent in his repentance, even if it be the length of an hour of the day or the length of one breath before his death: "How quickly you have come."

﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds (al-sayyi'at)﴾, meaning sins, ﴿until when death comes to one of them﴾ and he falls into the death throes, ﴿he says: Indeed I repent now.﴾ At that point, the faith of a disbeliever is not accepted, nor the repentance of a disobedient person. ﴿Nor of those who die while they are disbelievers; for those We have prepared a painful punishment.﴾ The word "those" (alladhina) is in the genitive position, meaning: nor for those who repent while they are disbelievers. ﴿Those, We have prepared (a'tadna) for them a painful punishment﴾, that is, We have readied it; the noun derived from it is "ata'd" (equipment).

Adi ibn al-Raqqa' said:
"Her spoils of the noble are taken by force, compelled,
and provisions for wars are gathered."
[[Aslab: what is seized in war. The verse is in Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/42.]]

And "'attada" and "'atad" are used of a horse prepared for war.

The Ja'fi poet said:
"They carried their insights upon their shoulders,
while my insight runs upon it, a prepared horse and I."
[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/396; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/57.]]

﴿O you who believe, it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾, that is, against their unwillingness.

The exegetes said: In the Jahiliyya and in the early days of Islam, when a man died leaving a wife, his son by another wife or his relative of the same lineage would come and cast his garment over that woman or over her tent, and he became more entitled to her than she was to herself and than anyone else. If he wished to marry her, he married her without a dowry, except the original dowry the deceased had given her. If he wished, he would marry her to someone else and take her dowry, giving her none of it. If he wished, he would restrain her and prevent her from marrying, making life hard for her and harming her, so that she would ransom herself with what she had inherited from the deceased, or she would die and he would inherit her. If the woman went back to her family before the guardian of her husband cast his garment over her, she was more entitled to herself. They continued doing this until Abu Qays ibn Sult al-Ansari died and left his wife Kabisha bint Ma'n al-Ansariyya; his son by another wife, called (Hisn), stood up.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: his name was Qays ibn Abi Qays. He cast his garment over her, thereby inheriting her marriage. Then he left her, did not approach her, and did not spend on her, harming her so that she would ransom herself with her property. They did this whenever one of them inherited a wife: if she was beautiful and wealthy, he consummated with her; if she was not beautiful, he made life hard for her so she would ransom herself from him. Kabisha came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, Abu Qays died and his son inherited my marriage, and Hisn has harmed me and made life hard for me. He neither spends on me, nor consummates with me, nor releases me." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to her: "Stay in your house until the command of God comes concerning you." [[Asbab al-Nuzul: 98.]] [265] She said: So she left, and the women of Medina heard of this; they came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) while he was in the Mosque of al-Fadih and said: "O Messenger of God, we are only in the situation of Kabisha, except that our sons do not marry us, while our paternal cousins do." Then God, Exalted, revealed: ﴿O you who believe, it is not lawful for you...﴾ the verse.

Al-Kisa'i, al-A'mash and Yahya ibn Wathhab read the "k" with a dammah here and in al-Tawba. The rest read it with a fatha. Al-Kisa'i said: they are two dialects. Al-Farra' said: "al-kurh" and "al-ikrah" differ; what one is compelled to do is "kurh" with a fatha, and what comes from one's own self is "kurh" with a dammah.

﴿Nor restrain them in order to take away part of what you have given them﴾, as the people of the Jahiliyya did (namely, preventing their remarriage, as mentioned above).

On the authority of al-Dahhak: this verse was revealed concerning a man who has an orphan girl in his guardianship, and he dislikes marrying her for her wealth; she is then under him as an old woman while he desires the young one. He dislikes divorcing the old woman, anticipating her death so he can inherit her property, while he withholds from her bed.

Ibn Abbas said: this is about a man who has a wife whom he dislikes keeping as a companion, and she has a dowry from him; he makes life hard for her and harms her so that she will ransom herself with the dowry or return to him what he gave her as dowry. God, Mighty and Majestic, forbade that, then said:

﴿Unless they commit a clear lewdness﴾, then at that point it becomes lawful for you to harm them so they will ransom themselves from you, and to restrain them, ﴿in order to take away part of what you have given them.﴾ They differed concerning the lewdness:

Some said: it is fornication. Al-Hasan said: if she commits fornication, it is lawful for her husband to ask for khul' (divorce by ransom). Ata said: when a man's wife committed lewdness, he would take back what he had given her and expel her; this was abrogated by the hudud (prescribed penalties).

Ibn Mas'ud, al-Dahhak and Qatada said: it is nushuz (disobedience/defiance by the wife).
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 94-95.]]

Ja'far ibn Muhammad related from his father from Jabir ibn Abd Allah that the Prophet (ﷺ) addressed the people and said: "Fear God regarding women, for you have taken them under the trust of God and made their private parts lawful by the word of God. Your right over them is that they not allow anyone you dislike to tread upon your bedding; if they do that, then strike them with a light blow that does not wound. Their right over you is their provision and clothing in a fair manner." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/412; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/172.]] [266]

As for His words "clear" (mubayyina) with a fatha on the ya', this was read by Ibn Abbas, Asim and Ibn Kathir; the rest read it with a kasra.

﴿And consort with them in kindness.﴾ Al-Hasan said: this returns to the beginning of the discussion, meaning ﴿And give the women their dowries as a gift﴾ and ﴿consort with them in kindness﴾. Some said: it means to treat them as you wish to be treated.

﴿But if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and God places in it much good﴾, which may be a righteous child, or God may incline him toward her afterward. So said the exegetes.

Makhul al-Azdi said: I heard Ibn Umar say: a man asks God for guidance and is guided, then he becomes resentful toward his Lord, but it is not long before he looks at the outcome and finds that it was good for him.

﴿And if you wish to exchange one wife for another, and you have given one of them a qintar (a large amount of wealth), then take nothing from it﴾, that is, from the qintar nothing at all. ﴿Would you take it, slandering and a clear sin?﴾ "Would you take it" is an interrogative of prohibition and rebuke. "Slandering" (buhtanan) and "a clear sin" (ithman mubinan) are in the accusative for two reasons: one is by removing the preposition, and the other by an implied verb; the sense being: you would incur, in taking it, slander and a clear sin. Then He said: ﴿And how would you take it﴾, in the sense of magnifying the wrong, like His words: ﴿How do you disbelieve in God?﴾ [[Surat al-Baqara: 28.]] ﴿When you have gone in to one another.﴾

The exegetes said: it means intercourse, but God is generous and alludes by what He wills to what He wills. The root of "ifda" is arriving at something without an intermediary.

﴿And they took from you a solemn covenant.﴾ Al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, al-Dahhak, Qatada and al-Suddi said: it is their words at the contract: "I have married her to you upon what God has taken from women for men: retaining in kindness or releasing in goodness." Mujahid said: it is the word of marriage by which intimacy is made lawful, like his saying "I married him." Al-Sha'bi, Ikrima and al-Rabi' said: it is his words: "You have taken them under the trust of God and made their private parts lawful by the word of God."

Chapter on what has been reported concerning permission to pay high dowries, based on His words: ﴿and you have given one of them a qintar﴾.

From Ata al-Khurasani: Umar proposed to Ali for his daughter Umm Kulthum, who was from Fatima bint the Messenger of God (ﷺ). He said: "She is young." Umar said: "I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'Every lineage and every marital relation will be cut off on the Day of Resurrection except my lineage and my marital relation.'" [[Fath al-Qadir: 2/502.]] So for that reason I desire her. [267]

Ali (may God be pleased with him) said: "I will send her to you so you may see her youth." He sent her to him, and she came to him and said: "My father says to you: Are you pleased with the nihla (dowry)?" He said: "I am pleased with it." So he married him to his daughter, and Umar gave a dowry of forty thousand dirhams. [[There is room for scrutiny and reflection concerning this account.]]

From Ibn Sirin: al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) married a woman, and sent her a hundred slave girls, each with a thousand dirhams.

Murshid ibn Abd Allah al-Barni related from Uqba ibn Amir al-Juhani that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The best marriage is the easiest of it."

And he (ﷺ) said to a man: "Are you pleased that I marry you to so-and-so?" [268] He said: "Yes." He said to the woman:

"Are you pleased that I marry you to so-and-so?" She said: "Yes." So he married one of them to the other. The man went in to her, but he had not set a bridal gift (mahr) for her and had not given her anything. He was among those who witnessed al-Hudaybiyyah and had a share (sahm) at Khaybar. When his death approached, he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married me to so-and-so, and I did not set a bridal gift for her and did not give her anything, and I have now given her my share at Khaybar as her bridal gift." So she took that share and sold it for one hundred thousand. [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/470; Sahih Ibn Hibban: 9/281.]]

And on the authority of Damrah ibn Habib: Umm Habibah was in the land of Abyssinia with Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), and the Messenger of Allah married her, and al-Najashi paid the bridal gift on his behalf, four hundred dinars.

With the same chain, from Ibn Sirin, from Ibn Abbas: he married Sulaymah al-Sulamiyyah for ten thousand dirhams.

Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ibn Bishr: that 'Urwah al-Bariqi married the daughter of Hani ibn Qabisah for one thousand dirhams.

And from Ghaylan ibn Jarir: that Mutarrif married a woman for ten thousand awqiyah.

Chapter on those who disliked this, and discussion of the minimum bridal gift.

From Ibn Sirin, who said: Abu al-'Ajfa al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: I heard 'Umar while he was addressing the people; he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "Beware, do not exaggerate in the bridal gifts of women, for if it were a point of honour in this world or of piety before Allah, the one most entitled to it would be the Prophet (ﷺ). He never gave any of his wives or daughters a bridal gift exceeding twelve awqiyah. Indeed, one of you will so overpay for a woman's bridal gift that resentment remains in his soul, and he says: 'You were a leather water-bag's handle (hilq al-qirbah) or its sweat (irq al-qirbah).'"

'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from 'A'ishah, that she said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among the blessings of a woman is the ease of her bridal gift and the ease of her womb." [[Al-Mustadrak: 2/181; Irwa' al-Ghalil: 6/350.]] [270]

'Urwah said: And I say on my own: among the ill omens of a woman is that her bridal gift be great.

Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Our bridal gift, from the time the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among us, was ten awqiyah, which is four hundred dirhams.

Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw on 'Abd al-Rahman a trace of yellow (saffron) and said: "What is this?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I married a woman for the weight of a date-stone of gold." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May Allah bless you. Hold a walimah, even with a sheep." [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/227.]] [271]

It is said: it was five dirhams.

And from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi that a woman came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have given myself to you," and she stood for a long time. A man stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, marry her to me if you have no need of her." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you have anything to give her as a bridal gift?" He said: "I have nothing except this waist-wrapper of mine." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you give it to her, you will sit without a waist-wrapper, so seek something else." He said: "I find nothing." He said: "Seek, even an iron ring." He sought but found nothing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Do you have any of the Qur'an with you?" He said: "Yes, surah so-and-so and surah so-and-so," naming surahs. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have married her to you for what you have of the Qur'an." [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/336; Ahkam al-Qur'an: 3/480.]] [272]

And on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir, from his father: that a man married a woman for two sandals, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Are you content to give your property for these two sandals?" He said: "Yes," so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permitted it. [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/445; Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 2/290, no. 1120.]]

And from Abu Hadrad al-Aslami, who said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) seeking his help regarding the bridal gift of a woman. He said: "How much are you giving her?" I said: "Two hundred dirhams." He said: "Even if you were scooping from the valley of Bathan, you would not have exceeded it." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 22/352.]] [274]

Muslim ibn Rumman, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever gives, as bridal gift, a handful of sawiq or dates has made it lawful (istahalla)." [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/468; Fath al-Bari: 9/173.]] [275]

And from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married a woman for ten dirhams.

Ahmad ibn Hanbal, from al-Hasan ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, who said: Damrah wrote to us, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah al-Kinani, that Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib married his daughter for two dirhams.

Waki', from Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shaybah, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever makes lawful with a dirham has made it lawful." [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 7/238; Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah: 3/317.]] [276] Waki' said: in marriage.

And from 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid, client of al-Aswad, that a man took a slave-girl as a concubine (tasarrara) but disliked her, so a man said to him: "Give her to me," and he gave her to him. This was mentioned to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: "Gifting is not permitted to anyone after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and even if he gave her a whip as bridal gift, she would be lawful."

Al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: The sunnah regarding the bridal gift is a ratl of silver (al-waraq). They disliked that the bridal gift of free women be like the bridal gifts of prostitutes, for a dirham or two dirhams, and they preferred it to be twenty dirhams.

And those of your women who commit lewdness (al-fahisha), that is, fornication (al-zina); in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud it reads "al-fahisha" with the same meaning, among your women, call four witnesses against them from among you, that is, from among the Muslims. If they testify against them for fornication, then confine them (fa-amsikuhunna), that is, imprison them, in the houses until death takes them or God appoints a way for them. This was only before the prescribed penalties (al-hudud) were revealed. In the early days of Islam, if a woman committed a sin she would be confined to the house until she died, and if she had a husband, her dowry remained his. Then the words of Him came down: ﴿The fornicatress and the fornicator, flog each one of them﴾ [[Surat al-Nur: 2.]].

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Take from me, take from me; God has appointed a way for them. The previously married (thayyib) for the previously married: a hundred lashes and stoning with stones; and the virgin (bikr) for the virgin: a hundred lashes and exile for a year." [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/476 and Sahih Muslim: 5/115, with some variation in order.]] [255]

So that verse abrogated part of this verse, namely the confinement in houses, and part of it remained in force, namely the requirement of witnesses.
