'Ata' said: it was revealed concerning Muhammad (ﷺ) when he married the wife of Zayd ibn Haritha.

"And that you should combine two sisters," whether free women by contract or slave women by intercourse, "except what has already passed."

'Ata' and al-Suddi said: meaning, except what was of Ya'qub (peace be upon him), for he combined Lay'a, the mother of Yahudha, and Rahil, the mother of Yusuf, and they were two sisters.

"Indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful."

"And the married women among women..." the verse.

'Amr ibn Murra said: a man said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Did you not see Ibn 'Abbas when he was asked about this verse, 'and the married women among women,' and he said nothing about it?" Sa'id said: "He did not know it."

Mujahid said: "If I knew who could explain this verse, I would have driven camels' livers to him." His saying, Exalted is He: "and the married women among women."

The commentators said: this is the seventh of the women forbidden by cause.

The common readers recited "wa-l-muhsanat" with a fatha on the sad, meaning, in the cessation of husbands: their husbands made them muhsanat.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: it was revealed concerning women who used to migrate to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while they had husbands, and some Muslims married them; then their husbands came, migrating. So Allah forbade the Muslims from marrying them, then made an exception, saying: "except what your right hands possess," meaning the captives taken who had husbands in the land of war; it is lawful for their owners to have intercourse with them after istibra'.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri also said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent an army on the day of Hunayn to Awtas, and they encountered the enemy and took captives who had husbands among the polytheists. They disliked having intercourse with them and felt sinful about it, so Allah, Exalted, revealed this verse.

'Alqama recited "wa-l-muhsinat" with a kasra on the sad, and its evidence is the saying of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), 'Ubayda, Abu al-'Aliya and al-Suddi. They said: "the muhsanat" in this verse are the chaste ones, and its meaning: the chaste women among you are forbidden, except what your right hands possess of them through marriage or ownership by right hand and price. It was also said: its meaning is free women.

Al-Baqir and Yaman said: its meaning: "and the married women among women are forbidden to you," beyond the four; "except what your right hands possess," for there is no limit upon you regarding them.

Ibn Jurayj said: we asked 'Ata' about it, and he said: the meaning of His saying "except what your right hands possess" is that you have a slave-woman whom another slave of yours has married, and you may take her from him if you wish.

"The Book of Allah upon you": accusative as a verbal noun, i.e., Allah prescribed a prescription upon you. It was also said: accusative as a warning, i.e., hold fast to and fear the Book of Allah upon you.

Ibn al-Sumay' recited "kataba Allah 'alaykum," i.e., ordained. These are fourteen women, forbidden by the Book.

As for the six: two women are forbidden together, and this is what

Hisham narrated from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "A woman shall not be married to a man together with her paternal aunt or her maternal aunt." [[Sahih Muslim: 4/136; Ta'wil Mukhtalif al-Hadith: 181.]] [284]

"And lawful to you": Abu Ja'far and the people of Kufa recited "wa-uhilla" with a damma on the alif. The rest read it with a fatha; this is the recitation of 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas, and the choice of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim. Whoever reads it with a damma does so because of His saying "are forbidden," and whoever reads it with a fatha does so because of its proximity to the mention of Allah in His saying "the Book of Allah."

"Beyond that, what is other than those mentioned": the forbidden ones you have been told of. "That you seek" is a substitute for "ma" (what). According to the one who reads "uhilla" with a damma, "an" is in the nominative position; according to the one who reads with a fatha, "an" is in the accusative position.

Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: its position is accusative in both readings, by removing the preposition, meaning: "that you may seek and desire."

"With your wealth": either by marriage with a dowry, or by ownership and price. "Chaste, not fornicators": "muhsinin" means those who abstain; "musafihin" means adulterers, and the root is from the emission of madhi and semen.

"So for what you have enjoyed of them": scholars differed regarding the meaning of the verse. Mujahid and al-Hasan said: it means what you have benefited from and found pleasure in of women for intercourse through a valid marriage.

"Then give them their wages": that is, their dowries. So if he has intercourse with her even once, the full dowry becomes due to her.

Others said: it is the marriage of temporary pleasure (nikah al-mut'a). Then they differed whether the verse is muhkam (non-abrogated) or mansukh (abrogated).

Ibn 'Abbas said: it is muhkam, and he permitted temporary marriage, which is that a man marries a woman with a guardian and two witnesses for a known term. When the term ends, he has no claim over her, she is free of him, she must observe her waiting period, and there is no inheritance between them.

Habib ibn Abi Thabit said: Ibn 'Abbas gave me a mushaf and said: "This is according to the recitation of Ubayy." I saw in the mushaf: "So for what you have enjoyed of them up to a specified term."

Dawud narrated from Abu Nadra who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about temporary marriage, and he said: "Do you not recite Surat al-Nisa'?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then what do you recite: 'So for what you have enjoyed of them up to a specified term'?" I said: "I do not recite it like that." Ibn 'Abbas said: "By Allah, thus was it revealed," three times.

'Isa ibn 'Umar narrated from Talha ibn Musarrif that he recited: "So for what you have enjoyed of them up to a specified term."

'Amr ibn Murra narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he recited it: "So for what you have enjoyed of them up to a specified term."

Shu'ba narrated from al-Hakam who said: I asked him about this verse, "So for what you have enjoyed of them," whether it is abrogated. He said: No. Al-Hakam said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah honor his face, said: "Had 'Umar not forbidden temporary marriage, none would commit fornication except a wretch."

Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi narrated from 'Imran ibn Husayn who said: this verse (on temporary marriage) was revealed in the Book of Allah, and no verse came after it abrogating it. We were commanded by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to it, and we enjoyed temporary marriage with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he did not forbid us from it. Then a man said after that what he wished by his own opinion! Al-Tha'labi said: I say: none permitted temporary marriage except 'Imran ibn Husayn, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, some of his companions, and a group from the People of the House. [[Abu 'Umar said: the companions of Ibn 'Abbas from Makka and Yemen all held temporary marriage to be lawful (Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/133).]] And it is in the view of Ibn 'Abbas.

The poet says:
"Aqulu lil-rakbi idha tal al-thawa' bina... ya sahi hal laka fi fatwa Ibn 'Abbas
Hal laka fi rukhsat al-atraf na'ima... takunu mathwaka hatta marji' al-nas"

But the rest of the scholars, jurists, Companions, Successors and the righteous predecessors hold that this verse is abrogated and temporary marriage with women is forbidden.

Al-Rabi' ibn Subra al-Juhani narrated from his father who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on his 'umra, and we complained to him of celibacy. He said: "O people, enjoy these women." Then I accompanied the Messenger of Allah in the morning, and he was saying: "O people, I had commanded you to enjoy these women, but Allah has forbidden that until the Day of Resurrection." [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/406.]] [285]

Khusayf said: I asked al-Hasan about temporary marriage, and he said: It was only for three days in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger (ﷺ) forbade it.

Al-Kalbi said: This was at the beginning of Islam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permitted it for three days, then forbade it. When the term agreed between them ended, he would give her the wage that had been stipulated for her, then say: "Extend me in days and I will increase you in the wage." If she agreed, that was done; when the agreed term ended, he gave her the wage and separated from her. Then it was abrogated by the verse of divorce, the waiting period, and death.

Al-Zuhri narrated from al-Hasan and Abd Allah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, from their father, that Ali said to Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade temporary marriage (mut'ah) with women on the day of Khaybar, and forbade eating domestic donkeys.

Al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated from al-Bara' ibn Abd Allah al-Qass, from Abu Nadrah, from Ibn Abbas, that Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) forbade the mut'ah mentioned in Surat al-Nisa'. He said: Allah permitted it during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when women were few. Then He prohibited it to them after He had forbidden it.

From Salim ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar, from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), that he ascended the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: What is the matter with men who marry through this mut'ah, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has forbidden it? I will not find a man marrying it except that I will stone him.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Marriage, divorce, the waiting period and inheritance demolish mut'ah." [Musnad Abi Ya'la: 11/504, and Fath al-Bari: 9/138.] [286]

Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: I asked Aishah about mut'ah, and she said: "Between me and them is the Book of Allah: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess﴾ [Surat al-Mu'minun: 5–6]."

From Aishah: "By Allah, we find in the Book of Allah only marriage and concubinage." Ibn Umar said: Mut'ah is fornication (sifah).

Ata': Mut'ah is forbidden, like carrion, blood and the flesh of swine.

Al-Tha'alabi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Jubayr say: I heard Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Khayyat say: I heard Abu Nu'aym ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn Adi say: I heard [...] [an illegible word in the manuscript] say:

Al-Shafi'i said: I know of nothing in Islam that was made lawful, then made unlawful, then made lawful, then made unlawful, except mut'ah.

﴿So give them their wages as an obligation﴾: that is, their dowries. The dower was called "wage" (ajr) because it is the price of the womb (bud') and the wage of enjoyment. Do you not see that it becomes firmly due by seclusion (khalwah) and consummation?

The scholars differed about its minimum. As for its maximum, it has no limit. As for its minimum, Abu Hanifah said: There is no dower less than ten dirhams or their value in gold, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿that you seek with your wealth﴾, and the term "wealth" is not applied to less than this amount.

According to al-Shafi'i, it has no minimum. He permitted even a trivial thing, such as a handful of food. Likewise, any act that is worth a wage, whether small or large, and a surah or a verse of the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, based on His words: ﴿so give them their wages﴾.

From Salamah ibn Wardan, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked one of his companions: "O so-and-so, have you married?" He said: No, and I do not have anything to marry with. He said: "Do you not have ﴿Say: He is Allah, One﴾ [Surat al-Ikhlas: 1]?" He said: Yes. He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have ﴿When the help of Allah comes﴾ [Surat al-Nasr: 1]?" He said: Yes. He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾ [Surat al-Kafirun: 1]?" He said: Yes. He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have ﴿When the earth is shaken﴾ [Surat al-Zalzalah: 1]?" He said: Yes. He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have the Verse of the Throne?" He said: Yes. He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Marry, marry, marry." [Musnad Ahmad: 3/221, Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/135.] [287]

The arguments of both sides have been mentioned in what has been said.

﴿And there is no blame upon you in what you agree upon after the obligation﴾: that is, in what the woman ransoms herself with. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾

﴿And whoever among you is not able to marry free, believing women﴾: that is, lacks means and wealth (tawl).

Al-Musayyab ibn Sharik, from Imran ibn Jarir, from al-Nazzal ibn Sabrah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Whoever possesses three hundred dirhams, the pilgrimage becomes obligatory for him, and marrying slave women becomes forbidden to him.

﴿to marry believing free women (al-muhsanat)﴾: free women. Al-Kisa'i read (al-muhsinat) with a kasrah on the sad, throughout the Qur'an except at the beginning of this surah. The others read it with a fathah.

﴿...believing women, then from what your right hands possess of your believing maidens...﴾ up to His words ﴿with the permission of their people﴾: their masters. ﴿So give them their wages﴾: their dowries ﴿according to what is reasonable﴾, without withholding. ﴿Chaste (muhsanat)﴾: modest. ﴿Not unchaste (musafihat)﴾: fornicators. ﴿Nor taking secret lovers (akhdan)﴾: lovers with whom they fornicate in secret.

﴿And when they become chaste (uhsinna)﴾: the people of Kufa read it with a fathah on the alif, meaning they guarded their private parts. The others read it with a dammah, meaning they became chaste through their husbands. ﴿And if they commit an immorality﴾: that is, fornication, ﴿then upon them is half the punishment for free women﴾ if they commit fornication. ﴿Of the punishment﴾: that is, the hadd (prescribed penalty). Its parallel is: ﴿and it averts from her the punishment﴾ [Surat al-Nur: 8]. It is fifty lashes and exile for half a year, according to the correct view of the school of al-Shafi'i. The adulterer must be exiled to a place from which the prayer may be shortened. The master has the right to carry out the hadd for fornication upon his male and female slaves.

From Sa'id al-Maqbari, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If one of your slave women commits fornication, let him lash her and not reproach her. If she repeats it, let him lash her and not reproach her. If she repeats it, let him lash her and not reproach her. If she repeats it a fourth time, let him sell her, even for a braid of hair or a rope." [Sharh Muslim: 11/211, and Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah: 8/369.] [288]

﴿That﴾: that is, marrying slave women when one lacks means, ﴿is for one who fears sin from among you﴾: that is, sin and harm through overpowering desire. ﴿But to be patient is better for you﴾: refraining from marrying slave women while remaining chaste. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

From Yunus ibn Mirdas, who was a servant of Anas, who said: I was between Anas and Abu Hurayrah. Anas said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever loves to meet Allah pure and purified, let him marry free women."

Abu Hurayrah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Free women are the goodness of the household, and slave women are the corruption of the household." [Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/598.] [289]

﴿Allah intends to make clear to you﴾: that is, that He may make clear. The lam here means "that" (an). The Arabs interchange the lam of purpose (kay) with an, placing one in the place of the other, as in His words: ﴿And I have been commanded to be just among you﴾ [Surat al-Shura: 15], and His words: ﴿And we were commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Surat al-An'am: 73]. Then He said in another place: ﴿And I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Surat Ghafir: 66]. And He said: ﴿They wish to extinguish the light of Allah﴾ [Surat al-Saff: 8], then He said in another place: ﴿They wish to extinguish the light of Allah﴾ [Surat al-Tawbah: 32].

The poet said:
I wish to forget her remembrance, but Layla appears to me in every path.
He means: "that I forget." The meaning of the verse: Allah wishes to make clear the laws of your religion and the interests of your affairs.

Al-Hasan: He teaches you what you do and what you leave. Ata': He makes clear to you what brings you near to Him. Al-Kalbi: That He may make clear to you that patience from marrying slave women is better for you.

﴿And guide you to the ways (sunan)﴾: the laws (sharai') of those before you, in the prohibition of mothers, daughters and sisters, as mentioned in the two verses. Thus He prohibited them for those among the nations before you. ﴿And accept your repentance﴾: He overlooks what you committed before it was made clear to you, as said by al-Kalbi.

Muhammad ibn Jarir said: That is, He brings you back from the disobedience in which you were before this, to His obedience which He commanded you in this verse. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what benefits His servants in the matters of their religion and their worldly life, Wise in His management of them.﴾ ﴿And Allah wishes to accept your repentance﴾ if shortcoming occurs from you in His command. ﴿But those who follow their desires wish that you deviate into a great deviation﴾ by your committing what He has forbidden to you. The scholars differed about who are described as following desires:

Al-Suddi said: They are the Jews and the Christians.

Some said: They are the Jews, because they used to marry the daughters of a brother and the daughters of a sister. When Allah forbade these, they said: "You make lawful the daughters of a maternal aunt and a paternal aunt, while the maternal aunt and paternal aunt are forbidden to you. So marry the daughters of a brother and a sister as you marry the daughters of maternal and paternal aunts." Then Allah revealed this verse.

Mujahid said: They are the fornicators, who wish that you incline away from the truth so that you become like them, fornicating as they fornicate.

Ibn Zayd said: They are all the People of the Book in their religion.

﴿Allah wishes to lighten for you﴾ in marrying slave women when you do not find the means to marry free women, and in all the rulings of the Sharia. ﴿And mankind was created weak﴾ in everything.

Tawus, al-Kalbi and most of the exegetes said: That is, in the matter of intercourse, he cannot be patient with women, and a person is not weaker in anything than in the matter of women.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: Satan has never despaired of the sons of Adam except that he came to them through women. Eighty years have passed over me, one of my eyes has gone, and I am blind in the other, and what I fear most for myself is the trial of women.

Malik ibn Shurahbil said: Ubadah ibn al-Samit said: Do you not see me, that I do not stand except with support, and do not eat except what is soft for me, and my companion has died long ago? It does not please me that I be alone with a woman who is not lawful for me, even if I possessed all that the sun rises upon, out of fear that Satan might come to me and tell me, while he has neither hearing nor sight.

Al-Hasan said: That is, He created him from a despicable water. The proof is the saying of Allah: ﴿He who created you from weakness﴾ [Surat al-Rum: 54].

Ibn Kaysan: ﴿and mankind was created weak﴾: his desire and his lust sway him, and his fear and sorrow unsettle him.

Ibn Abbas said: Eight verses in Surat al-Nisa' are better for this ummah than everything the sun rises and sets upon: ﴿Allah wishes to make clear to you﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 26], ﴿and Allah wishes to accept your repentance﴾, ﴿Allah wishes to lighten for you﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 28], ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 31], ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 48], ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 40], ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 110], ﴿What would Allah do with your punishment?﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 147].

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verse 22–28 (part 1 of 2):

Surah al-Nisa' 4:22: "And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women," was revealed concerning Hisn ibn Abi Qays, who married his father's wife Kabisha bint Ma'n; concerning al-Aswad ibn Khalaf, who married his father's wife; concerning Safwan ibn Umayya ibn Khalaf, who married his father's wife Fakhita bint al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib; concerning Mansur ibn Mazin, who married his father's wife Mulayka bint Kharija; and concerning [Abu Makil] al-'Adawi, who married his father's wife.

Al-Ash'ath ibn Yasar said: Abu Qays died, and he was one of the righteous Ansar. His son Qays proposed to his father's wife. She said: "I consider you a son, and you are one of the righteous of your people, but I will go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and seek his counsel." She went to him and informed him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Return to your house." [277] Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And do not marry those whom your fathers married." [[Asbab al-Nuzul: 55.]]

"Ma" (ما) here means "man" (من). It has also been said: "And do not marry" means the marriage itself, i.e., "what your fathers married of women" is a generic noun, so that it includes free women and slave women. Free women are made unlawful by the contract, and slave women by sexual intercourse.

"Except what has already passed." Al-Mufaddal said: meaning, after what has passed, so leave it and avoid it.

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Zakariyya al-'Anbari say: its meaning is "as has already passed." "Indeed, it was an indecency and hatred," which brings about the hatred of Allah, and "hatred" is the most intense detestation, "and an evil way" [[An unreadable word.]], and an evil course. The Arabs used to say of a man's son from his father's wife: "muqayt" and "muqay." Among them were al-Ash'ath ibn Qays and Abu Mu'it ibn 'Amr ibn Umayya.

Al-Suddi, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara', who said: I met my maternal uncle carrying the banner, and I said: "Where are you going?" He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me to a man who married his father's wife after him, to strike his neck or kill him."

"Forbidden to you are your mothers." It is the plural of umm (أم). The original form of umm was "ummah," on the pattern of fi'lah, like qabrah and hamrah, so the "h" dropped, and it returned in the plural, as in their saying shah and miyah.

The poet said:
"Ummahati Khindif wa al-Rus abi" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/107.]]

It has also been said: the origin of umm is ummah, and they recited:
"Taqabbaltuha 'an ummatin laka taliman... tathubu ilayha fi al-nawaib ajma'a" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/107, and Lisan al-'Arab: 12/30.]]

Then the plural would be ummahat. Its parallel in speech is 'ammah and 'ammat.

Al-Ra'i said:
"Kanat najaʼib Mundhir wa Muhriq... ummatuhunna wa turuquhunna fahhala" [[Lisan al-'Arab: 11/516.]]

In this verse Allah forbade marriage to fourteen women: seven by lineage and seven by cause. As for lineage, His saying "your mothers" refers to the mothers by birth; "your daughters," the plural of daughter; "your sisters," the plural of sister; "your paternal aunts and maternal aunts," the plurals of paternal aunt and maternal aunt; "daughters of the brother" and "daughters of the sister."

As for cause, His saying: "and your mothers who nursed you," which are the mothers by fosterage, as in His saying: "and his wives are their mothers" [[Surat al-Ahzab: 6.]], then He said: "nor that you should marry his wives after him, ever" [[Surat al-Ahzab: 53.]]. And 'Abd Allah recited "wa-llay" without the "ta'," like His saying: "and those of your women who have despaired of menstruation" [[Surat al-Talaq: 4.]].

The poet said:
"Min al-lda' lam yahajjan yabghayna hisbatan... wa lakin liyaqtulanna al-bari' al-mughfala"

'Urwa, from 'A'isha, from the Prophet (ﷺ), said: "What birth makes unlawful, nursing makes unlawful." [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 3/295.]] [278]

Malik ibn Anas, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from 'Umayra, from 'A'isha, from the Prophet (ﷺ), said: "What is unlawful by lineage is unlawful by nursing." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/108; Ahkam al-Qur'an: 2/157.]] [279]

Al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn 'Ubayda, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from 'Ali, may Allah honor his face, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is with you that you are fond of the Quraysh and leave us?" He said: "Is there anyone with you?" I said: "Yes, the daughter of Hamza." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "She is not lawful to me; she is the daughter of my foster-brother." [[Sahih Muslim: 4/164; Sunan al-Nasa'i: 3/297.]] [280]

Wahb ibn Kaysan, from 'Urwa, from 'A'isha: that Abu al-Qu'ays, who was Aflah, asked permission to enter upon 'A'isha after the verse of hijab, but she refused to permit him. This was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Permit him, for he is your uncle." She said: "The woman nursed me, not the man." He said: "He is your uncle, so let him enter upon you." [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/194; Sahih al-Bukhari: 6/160.]]

Fosterage makes unlawful only under two conditions. The first: that there be five known sucklings which make unlawful, which were then abrogated by five known sucklings, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died while it was still among what is recited from the Qur'an.

'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith narrated from Umm al-Fadl: that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about nursing and said: "A single suckling does not make unlawful, nor two sucklings." [[Sunan al-Daraqutni: 4/101 and 106.]] [281]

Qatada said: "The single suck and the two sucks."

The second condition: that it be within the two years. What is after the two years does not make unlawful. Abu Hanifa held that it is six months after the two years, and Malik: one month after the two years. The evidence that what comes after the two years is not nursing is His saying: "The mothers shall nurse their children for two complete years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing" [[Surat al-Baqara: 233.]], and nothing comes after completeness and perfection.

And the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "There is no nursing after two years; nursing is only that which makes the flesh grow and raises the bones." [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/432; Sunan al-Daraqutni: 4/101, with variation in wording.]] [282]

"And the mothers of your wives." The mother of a woman is unlawful, whether or not one has consummated the marriage with her; this is the view of most jurists, and upon it the ruling and fatwa rest. The people of Iraq were strict regarding it, to the point that they said: if he has intercourse with her, or kisses her, or touches her with desire, her daughter becomes unlawful to him. Our view is that it is made unlawful only by a valid marriage, and the unlawful does not make the lawful unlawful. Ibn 'Abbas used to recite "and the mothers of your wives to whom you have gone in" and swore by Allah that it was not revealed except thus, and he said: she is in the position of the stepdaughters. Just as stepdaughters are not made unlawful by the contract with their mothers without intercourse, so the mothers of wives are not made unlawful by the contract with their daughters without intercourse. This is the view of 'Ali, Zayd, Jabir, Ibn 'Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr, who said: marrying the mothers of wives with whom one has not consummated is lawful. The first view is the more correct.

Ibn Jurayj said: I said to 'Ata': "A man marries a woman, then sees her but does not have intercourse with her until he divorces her; is her mother lawful to him?" He said: "No, she is unrestricted, whether he has consummated the marriage or not." I said to him: "Ibn 'Abbas used to recite: 'and the mothers of your wives to whom you have gone in.'" He said: "No."

'Amr ibn al-Musayyab narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "If a man marries a woman, it is not lawful for him to marry her mother, whether or not he has consummated with the daughter. And if he marries the mother and does not consummate with her, then divorces her, he may marry the daughter if he wishes."

"And your stepdaughters (rabaʼib)": the plural of rabiba, who is the daughter of the woman. She was called rabiba because of his raising (tarbiyatihi) of her; it is fa'ila in the sense of maf'ula. "Who are in your guardianship": that is, in your protection and upbringing. It is said: "So-and-so is in the custody (hijr) of so-and-so" when he is responsible for raising her. It is said: a woman of good custody (tayyibat al-hijr) when she has raised no child except one of good offspring.

Al-Kumayt said:
"Al-karimat [nisba] fi Quraysh... [wa siwahum] wa al-tayyibat al-hujura"

From this comes the saying that restriction is hijr, and the original meaning of it is the side; it is said: "So-and-so eats in his hijr and grazes his hijr."

"From your women to whom you have gone in": that is, have had intercourse with them. "But if you have not gone in to them, there is no blame upon you" in marrying their daughters, if you have divorced them or they have died leaving you.

Al-Zuhri narrated from 'Urwa: that Zaynab bint Abi Salama, and her mother Umm Salama, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), informed him that Umm Habiba bint Abi Sufyan had told her that she said: "O Messenger of Allah, marry my sister." She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "Would you like that?" I said: "Yes, you are not one to be left alone, and I love that the one who shares me in good should be my sister."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, that is not lawful to me." I said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we have been hearing that you intend to marry Durra bint Abi Salama." He said: "The daughter of Umm Salama?" I said: "Yes." He said: "By Allah, even if she were not my stepdaughter in my custody, she would still not be lawful to me; she is the daughter of my foster-brother, Thuwayba nursed me and Abu Salama. So do not offer me your daughters or your sisters." [[Musnad al-Shamiyyin: 4/208; al-Sunan al-Kubra: 3/290.]] [283]

"And the wives of your sons (halail abna'ikum)": meaning the wives of your sons. The male is halil, and its plural is ahillah and ahilla'; like 'aziz, 'azza and a'izza'. It was so named because each of the two is lawful (halal) to the other. It is said: halla and he is halil, like sahha and he is sahih. It was also said: it was so named because each of them alights where the other alights, from hulul, which is descent; and it was said: because each of them unties the waist-wrapper of the other, from hall, which is the opposite of tying.

The poet said:
"Yudafi'u qawman 'ala majdihim... difa'a al-halilati 'anha al-halila
Yudafi'uhu yawman tara... wa yumkinuhu rijluha an yashula"

"Who are of your loins": excluding those whom you have adopted.

'Ata' said: it was revealed concerning Muhammad (ﷺ) when he married the wife of Zayd ibn Haritha.

"And that you should combine two sisters," whether free women by contract or slave women by intercourse, "except what has already passed."

'Ata' and al-Suddi said: meaning, except what was of Ya'qub (peace be upon him), for he combined Lay'a, the mother of Yahudha, and Rahil, the mother of Yusuf, and they were two sisters.

"Indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful."

"And the married women among women..." the verse.

'Amr ibn Murra said: a man said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Did you not see Ibn 'Abbas when he was asked about this verse, 'and the married women among women,' and he said nothing about it?" Sa'id said: "He did not know it."

Mujahid said: "If I knew who could explain this verse, I would have driven camels' livers to him." His saying, Exalted is He: "and the married women among women."

The commentators said: this is the seventh of the women forbidden by cause.

The common readers recited "wa-l-muhsanat" with a fatha on the sad, meaning, in the cessation of husbands: their husbands made them muhsanat.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: it was revealed concerning women who used to migrate to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while they had husbands, and some Muslims married them; then their husbands came, migrating. So Allah forbade the Muslims from marrying them, then made an exception, saying: "except what your right hands possess," meaning the captives taken who had husbands in the land of war; it is lawful for their owners to have intercourse with them after istibra'.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri also said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent an army on the day of Hunayn to Awtas, and they encountered the enemy and took captives who had husbands among the polytheists. They disliked having intercourse with them and felt sinful about it, so Allah, Exalted, revealed this verse.

'Alqama recited "wa-l-muhsinat" with a kasra on the sad, and its evidence is the saying of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), 'Ubayda, Abu al-'Aliya and al-Suddi. They said: "the muhsanat" in this verse are the chaste ones, and its meaning: the chaste women among you are forbidden, except what your right hands possess of them through marriage or ownership by right hand and price. It was also said: its meaning is free women.

Al-Baqir and Yaman said: its meaning: "and the married women among women are forbidden to you," beyond the four; "except what your right hands possess," for there is no limit upon you regarding them.

Ibn Jurayj said: we asked 'Ata' about it, and he said: the meaning of His saying "except what your right hands possess" is that you have a slave-woman whom another slave of yours has married, and you may take her from him if you wish.

"The Book of Allah upon you": accusative as a verbal noun, i.e., Allah prescribed a prescription upon you. It was also said: accusative as a warning, i.e., hold fast to and fear the Book of Allah upon you.

Ibn al-Sumay' recited "kataba Allah 'alaykum," i.e., ordained. These are fourteen women, forbidden by the Book.

As for the six: two women are forbidden together, and this is what

Hisham narrated from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "A woman shall not be married to a man together with her paternal aunt or her maternal aunt." [[Sahih Muslim: 4/136; Ta'wil Mukhtalif al-Hadith: 181.]] [284]

"And lawful to you": Abu Ja'far and the people of Kufa recited "wa-uhilla" with a damma on the alif. The rest read it with a fatha; this is the recitation of 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas, and the choice of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim. Whoever reads it with a damma does so because of His saying "are forbidden," and whoever reads it with a fatha does so because of its proximity to the mention of Allah in His saying "the Book of Allah."

"Beyond that, what is other than those mentioned": the forbidden ones you have been told of. "That you seek" is a substitute for "ma" (what). According to the one who reads "uhilla" with a damma, "an" is in the nominative position; according to the one who reads with a fatha, "an" is in the accusative position.

Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: its position is accusative in both readings, by removing the preposition, meaning: "that you may seek and desire."

"With your wealth": either by marriage with a dowry, or by ownership and price. "Chaste, not fornicators": "muhsinin" means those who abstain; "musafihin" means adulterers, and the root is from the emission of madhi and semen.

"So for what you have enjoyed of them": scholars differed regarding the meaning of the verse. Mujahid and al-Hasan said: it means what you have benefited from and found pleasure in of women for intercourse through a valid marriage.

"Then give them their wages": that is, their dowries. So if he has intercourse with her even once, the full dowry becomes due to her.

Others said: it is the marriage of temporary pleasure (nikah al-mut'a). Then they differed whether the verse is muhkam (non-abrogated) or mansukh (abrogated).

Ibn 'Abbas said: it is muhkam, and he permitted temporary marriage, which is that a man marries a woman with a guardian and two witnesses for a known term. When the term ends, he has no claim over her, she is free of him, she must observe her waiting period, and there is no inheritance between them.

Habib ibn Abi Thabit said: Ibn 'Abbas gave me a mushaf and said: "This is according to the recitation of Ubayy." I saw in the mushaf: "So for what you have enjoyed of them up to a specified term."

Dawud narrated from Abu Nadra who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about temporary marriage, and he said: "Do you not recite Surat al-Nisa'?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then what do you recite: 'So for what you have enjoyed of them up to a specified term'?" I said: "I do not recite it like that." Ibn 'Abbas said: "By Allah, thus was it revealed," three times.

'Isa ibn 'Umar narrated from Talha ibn Musarrif that he recited: "So for what you have enjoyed of them up to a specified term."

'Amr ibn Murra narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he recited it: "So for what you have enjoyed of them up to a specified term."

Shu'ba narrated from al-Hakam who said: I asked him about this verse, "So for what you have enjoyed of them," whether it is abrogated. He said: No. Al-Hakam said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah honor his face, said: "Had 'Umar not forbidden temporary marriage, none would commit fornication except a wretch."

Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi narrated from 'Imran ibn Husayn who said: this verse (on temporary marriage) was revealed in the Book of Allah, and no verse came after it abrogating it. We were commanded by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to it, and we enjoyed temporary marriage with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he did not forbid us from it. Then a man said after that what he wished by his own opinion! Al-Tha'labi said: I say: none permitted temporary marriage except 'Imran ibn Husayn, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, some of his companions, and a group from the People of the House. [[Abu 'Umar said: the companions of Ibn 'Abbas from Makka and Yemen all held temporary marriage to be lawful (Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/133).]] And it is in the view of Ibn 'Abbas.

The poet says:
"Aqulu lil-rakbi idha tal al-thawa' bina... ya sahi hal laka fi fatwa Ibn 'Abbas
Hal laka fi rukhsat al-atraf na'ima... takunu mathwaka hatta marji' al-nas"

But the rest of the scholars, jurists, Companions, Successors and the righteous predecessors hold that this verse is abrogated and temporary marriage with women is forbidden.

Al-Rabi' ibn Subra al-Juhani narrated from his father who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on his 'umra, and we complained to him of celibacy. He said: "O people, enjoy these women." Then I accompanied the Messenger of Allah in the morning, and he was saying: "O people, I had commanded you to enjoy these women, but Allah has forbidden that until the Day of Resurrection." [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/406.]] [285]

Khusayf said: I asked al-Hasan about temporary marriage, and he said: It was only for three days in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger (ﷺ) forbade it.

Al-Kalbi said: This was at the beginning of Islam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permitted it for three days, then forbade it. When the term agreed between them ended, he would give her the wage that had been stipulated for her, then say: "Extend me in days and I will increase you in the wage." If she agreed, that was done; when the agreed term ended, he gave her the wage and separated from her. Then it was abrogated by the verse of divorce, the waiting period, and death.

Al-Zuhri narrated from al-Hasan and Abd Allah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, from their father, that Ali said to Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade temporary marriage (mut'ah) with women on the day of Khaybar, and forbade eating domestic donkeys.

Al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated from al-Bara' ibn Abd Allah al-Qass, from Abu Nadrah, from Ibn Abbas, that Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) forbade the mut'ah mentioned in Surat al-Nisa'. He said: Allah permitted it during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when women were few. Then He prohibited it to them after He had forbidden it.

From Salim ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar, from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), that he ascended the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: What is the matter with men who marry through this mut'ah, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has forbidden it? I will not find a man marrying it except that I will stone him.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Marriage, divorce, the waiting period and inheritance demolish mut'ah." [Musnad Abi Ya'la: 11/504, and Fath al-Bari: 9/138.] [286]

Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: I asked Aishah about mut'ah, and she said: "Between me and them is the Book of Allah: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess﴾ [Surat al-Mu'minun: 5–6]."

From Aishah: "By Allah, we find in the Book of Allah only marriage and concubinage." Ibn Umar said: Mut'ah is fornication (sifah).

Ata': Mut'ah is forbidden, like carrion, blood and the flesh of swine.

Al-Tha'alabi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Jubayr say: I heard Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Khayyat say: I heard Abu Nu'aym ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn Adi say: I heard [...] [an illegible word in the manuscript] say:

Al-Shafi'i said: I know of nothing in Islam that was made lawful, then made unlawful, then made lawful, then made unlawful, except mut'ah.

﴿So give them their wages as an obligation﴾: that is, their dowries. The dower was called "wage" (ajr) because it is the price of the womb (bud') and the wage of enjoyment. Do you not see that it becomes firmly due by seclusion (khalwah) and consummation?

The scholars differed about its minimum. As for its maximum, it has no limit. As for its minimum, Abu Hanifah said: There is no dower less than ten dirhams or their value in gold, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿that you seek with your wealth﴾, and the term "wealth" is not applied to less than this amount.

According to al-Shafi'i, it has no minimum. He permitted even a trivial thing, such as a handful of food. Likewise, any act that is worth a wage, whether small or large, and a surah or a verse of the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, based on His words: ﴿so give them their wages﴾.

From Salamah ibn Wardan, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked one of his companions: "O so-and-so, have you married?" He said: No, and I do not have anything to marry with. He said: "Do you not have ﴿Say: He is Allah, One﴾ [Surat al-Ikhlas: 1]?" He said: Yes. He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have ﴿When the help of Allah comes﴾ [Surat al-Nasr: 1]?" He said: Yes. He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾ [Surat al-Kafirun: 1]?" He said: Yes. He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have ﴿When the earth is shaken﴾ [Surat al-Zalzalah: 1]?" He said: Yes. He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have the Verse of the Throne?" He said: Yes. He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Marry, marry, marry." [Musnad Ahmad: 3/221, Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/135.] [287]

The arguments of both sides have been mentioned in what has been said.

﴿And there is no blame upon you in what you agree upon after the obligation﴾: that is, in what the woman ransoms herself with. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾

﴿And whoever among you is not able to marry free, believing women﴾: that is, lacks means and wealth (tawl).

Al-Musayyab ibn Sharik, from Imran ibn Jarir, from al-Nazzal ibn Sabrah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Whoever possesses three hundred dirhams, the pilgrimage becomes obligatory for him, and marrying slave women becomes forbidden to him.

﴿to marry believing free women (al-muhsanat)﴾: free women. Al-Kisa'i read (al-muhsinat) with a kasrah on the sad, throughout the Qur'an except at the beginning of this surah. The others read it with a fathah.

﴿...believing women, then from what your right hands possess of your believing maidens...﴾ up to His words ﴿with the permission of their people﴾: their masters. ﴿So give them their wages﴾: their dowries ﴿according to what is reasonable﴾, without withholding. ﴿Chaste (muhsanat)﴾: modest. ﴿Not unchaste (musafihat)﴾: fornicators. ﴿Nor taking secret lovers (akhdan)﴾: lovers with whom they fornicate in secret.

﴿And when they become chaste (uhsinna)﴾: the people of Kufa read it with a fathah on the alif, meaning they guarded their private parts. The others read it with a dammah, meaning they became chaste through their husbands. ﴿And if they commit an immorality﴾: that is, fornication, ﴿then upon them is half the punishment for free women﴾ if they commit fornication. ﴿Of the punishment﴾: that is, the hadd (prescribed penalty). Its parallel is: ﴿and it averts from her the punishment﴾ [Surat al-Nur: 8]. It is fifty lashes and exile for half a year, according to the correct view of the school of al-Shafi'i. The adulterer must be exiled to a place from which the prayer may be shortened. The master has the right to carry out the hadd for fornication upon his male and female slaves.

From Sa'id al-Maqbari, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If one of your slave women commits fornication, let him lash her and not reproach her. If she repeats it, let him lash her and not reproach her. If she repeats it, let him lash her and not reproach her. If she repeats it a fourth time, let him sell her, even for a braid of hair or a rope." [Sharh Muslim: 11/211, and Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah: 8/369.] [288]

﴿That﴾: that is, marrying slave women when one lacks means, ﴿is for one who fears sin from among you﴾: that is, sin and harm through overpowering desire. ﴿But to be patient is better for you﴾: refraining from marrying slave women while remaining chaste. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

From Yunus ibn Mirdas, who was a servant of Anas, who said: I was between Anas and Abu Hurayrah. Anas said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever loves to meet Allah pure and purified, let him marry free women."

Abu Hurayrah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Free women are the goodness of the household, and slave women are the corruption of the household." [Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/598.] [289]

﴿Allah intends to make clear to you﴾: that is, that He may make clear. The lam here means "that" (an). The Arabs interchange the lam of purpose (kay) with an, placing one in the place of the other, as in His words: ﴿And I have been commanded to be just among you﴾ [Surat al-Shura: 15], and His words: ﴿And we were commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Surat al-An'am: 73]. Then He said in another place: ﴿And I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Surat Ghafir: 66]. And He said: ﴿They wish to extinguish the light of Allah﴾ [Surat al-Saff: 8], then He said in another place: ﴿They wish to extinguish the light of Allah﴾ [Surat al-Tawbah: 32].

The poet said:
I wish to forget her remembrance, but Layla appears to me in every path.
He means: "that I forget." The meaning of the verse: Allah wishes to make clear the laws of your religion and the interests of your affairs.

Al-Hasan: He teaches you what you do and what you leave. Ata': He makes clear to you what brings you near to Him. Al-Kalbi: That He may make clear to you that patience from marrying slave women is better for you.

﴿And guide you to the ways (sunan)﴾: the laws (sharai') of those before you, in the prohibition of mothers, daughters and sisters, as mentioned in the two verses. Thus He prohibited them for those among the nations before you. ﴿And accept your repentance﴾: He overlooks what you committed before it was made clear to you, as said by al-Kalbi.

Muhammad ibn Jarir said: That is, He brings you back from the disobedience in which you were before this, to His obedience which He commanded you in this verse. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what benefits His servants in the matters of their religion and their worldly life, Wise in His management of them.﴾ ﴿And Allah wishes to accept your repentance﴾ if shortcoming occurs from you in His command. ﴿But those who follow their desires wish that you deviate into a great deviation﴾ by your committing what He has forbidden to you. The scholars differed about who are described as following desires:

Al-Suddi said: They are the Jews and the Christians.

Some said: They are the Jews, because they used to marry the daughters of a brother and the daughters of a sister. When Allah forbade these, they said: "You make lawful the daughters of a maternal aunt and a paternal aunt, while the maternal aunt and paternal aunt are forbidden to you. So marry the daughters of a brother and a sister as you marry the daughters of maternal and paternal aunts." Then Allah revealed this verse.

Mujahid said: They are the fornicators, who wish that you incline away from the truth so that you become like them, fornicating as they fornicate.

Ibn Zayd said: They are all the People of the Book in their religion.

﴿Allah wishes to lighten for you﴾ in marrying slave women when you do not find the means to marry free women, and in all the rulings of the Sharia. ﴿And mankind was created weak﴾ in everything.

Tawus, al-Kalbi and most of the exegetes said: That is, in the matter of intercourse, he cannot be patient with women, and a person is not weaker in anything than in the matter of women.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: Satan has never despaired of the sons of Adam except that he came to them through women. Eighty years have passed over me, one of my eyes has gone, and I am blind in the other, and what I fear most for myself is the trial of women.

Malik ibn Shurahbil said: Ubadah ibn al-Samit said: Do you not see me, that I do not stand except with support, and do not eat except what is soft for me, and my companion has died long ago? It does not please me that I be alone with a woman who is not lawful for me, even if I possessed all that the sun rises upon, out of fear that Satan might come to me and tell me, while he has neither hearing nor sight.

Al-Hasan said: That is, He created him from a despicable water. The proof is the saying of Allah: ﴿He who created you from weakness﴾ [Surat al-Rum: 54].

Ibn Kaysan: ﴿and mankind was created weak﴾: his desire and his lust sway him, and his fear and sorrow unsettle him.

Ibn Abbas said: Eight verses in Surat al-Nisa' are better for this ummah than everything the sun rises and sets upon: ﴿Allah wishes to make clear to you﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 26], ﴿and Allah wishes to accept your repentance﴾, ﴿Allah wishes to lighten for you﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 28], ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 31], ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 48], ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 40], ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 110], ﴿What would Allah do with your punishment?﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 147].

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verse 22–28 (part 1 of 2):

Surah al-Nisa' 4:22: "And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women," was revealed concerning Hisn ibn Abi Qays, who married his father's wife Kabisha bint Ma'n; concerning al-Aswad ibn Khalaf, who married his father's wife; concerning Safwan ibn Umayya ibn Khalaf, who married his father's wife Fakhita bint al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib; concerning Mansur ibn Mazin, who married his father's wife Mulayka bint Kharija; and concerning [Abu Makil] al-'Adawi, who married his father's wife.

Al-Ash'ath ibn Yasar said: Abu Qays died, and he was one of the righteous Ansar. His son Qays proposed to his father's wife. She said: "I consider you a son, and you are one of the righteous of your people, but I will go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and seek his counsel." She went to him and informed him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Return to your house." [277] Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And do not marry those whom your fathers married." [[Asbab al-Nuzul: 55.]]

"Ma" (ما) here means "man" (من). It has also been said: "And do not marry" means the marriage itself, i.e., "what your fathers married of women" is a generic noun, so that it includes free women and slave women. Free women are made unlawful by the contract, and slave women by sexual intercourse.

"Except what has already passed." Al-Mufaddal said: meaning, after what has passed, so leave it and avoid it.

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Zakariyya al-'Anbari say: its meaning is "as has already passed." "Indeed, it was an indecency and hatred," which brings about the hatred of Allah, and "hatred" is the most intense detestation, "and an evil way" [[An unreadable word.]], and an evil course. The Arabs used to say of a man's son from his father's wife: "muqayt" and "muqay." Among them were al-Ash'ath ibn Qays and Abu Mu'it ibn 'Amr ibn Umayya.

Al-Suddi, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara', who said: I met my maternal uncle carrying the banner, and I said: "Where are you going?" He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me to a man who married his father's wife after him, to strike his neck or kill him."

"Forbidden to you are your mothers." It is the plural of umm (أم). The original form of umm was "ummah," on the pattern of fi'lah, like qabrah and hamrah, so the "h" dropped, and it returned in the plural, as in their saying shah and miyah.

The poet said:
"Ummahati Khindif wa al-Rus abi" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/107.]]

It has also been said: the origin of umm is ummah, and they recited:
"Taqabbaltuha 'an ummatin laka taliman... tathubu ilayha fi al-nawaib ajma'a" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/107, and Lisan al-'Arab: 12/30.]]

Then the plural would be ummahat. Its parallel in speech is 'ammah and 'ammat.

Al-Ra'i said:
"Kanat najaʼib Mundhir wa Muhriq... ummatuhunna wa turuquhunna fahhala" [[Lisan al-'Arab: 11/516.]]

In this verse Allah forbade marriage to fourteen women: seven by lineage and seven by cause. As for lineage, His saying "your mothers" refers to the mothers by birth; "your daughters," the plural of daughter; "your sisters," the plural of sister; "your paternal aunts and maternal aunts," the plurals of paternal aunt and maternal aunt; "daughters of the brother" and "daughters of the sister."

As for cause, His saying: "and your mothers who nursed you," which are the mothers by fosterage, as in His saying: "and his wives are their mothers" [[Surat al-Ahzab: 6.]], then He said: "nor that you should marry his wives after him, ever" [[Surat al-Ahzab: 53.]]. And 'Abd Allah recited "wa-llay" without the "ta'," like His saying: "and those of your women who have despaired of menstruation" [[Surat al-Talaq: 4.]].

The poet said:
"Min al-lda' lam yahajjan yabghayna hisbatan... wa lakin liyaqtulanna al-bari' al-mughfala"

'Urwa, from 'A'isha, from the Prophet (ﷺ), said: "What birth makes unlawful, nursing makes unlawful." [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 3/295.]] [278]

Malik ibn Anas, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from 'Umayra, from 'A'isha, from the Prophet (ﷺ), said: "What is unlawful by lineage is unlawful by nursing." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/108; Ahkam al-Qur'an: 2/157.]] [279]

Al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn 'Ubayda, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from 'Ali, may Allah honor his face, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is with you that you are fond of the Quraysh and leave us?" He said: "Is there anyone with you?" I said: "Yes, the daughter of Hamza." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "She is not lawful to me; she is the daughter of my foster-brother." [[Sahih Muslim: 4/164; Sunan al-Nasa'i: 3/297.]] [280]

Wahb ibn Kaysan, from 'Urwa, from 'A'isha: that Abu al-Qu'ays, who was Aflah, asked permission to enter upon 'A'isha after the verse of hijab, but she refused to permit him. This was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Permit him, for he is your uncle." She said: "The woman nursed me, not the man." He said: "He is your uncle, so let him enter upon you." [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/194; Sahih al-Bukhari: 6/160.]]

Fosterage makes unlawful only under two conditions. The first: that there be five known sucklings which make unlawful, which were then abrogated by five known sucklings, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died while it was still among what is recited from the Qur'an.

'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith narrated from Umm al-Fadl: that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about nursing and said: "A single suckling does not make unlawful, nor two sucklings." [[Sunan al-Daraqutni: 4/101 and 106.]] [281]

Qatada said: "The single suck and the two sucks."

The second condition: that it be within the two years. What is after the two years does not make unlawful. Abu Hanifa held that it is six months after the two years, and Malik: one month after the two years. The evidence that what comes after the two years is not nursing is His saying: "The mothers shall nurse their children for two complete years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing" [[Surat al-Baqara: 233.]], and nothing comes after completeness and perfection.

And the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "There is no nursing after two years; nursing is only that which makes the flesh grow and raises the bones." [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/432; Sunan al-Daraqutni: 4/101, with variation in wording.]] [282]

"And the mothers of your wives." The mother of a woman is unlawful, whether or not one has consummated the marriage with her; this is the view of most jurists, and upon it the ruling and fatwa rest. The people of Iraq were strict regarding it, to the point that they said: if he has intercourse with her, or kisses her, or touches her with desire, her daughter becomes unlawful to him. Our view is that it is made unlawful only by a valid marriage, and the unlawful does not make the lawful unlawful. Ibn 'Abbas used to recite "and the mothers of your wives to whom you have gone in" and swore by Allah that it was not revealed except thus, and he said: she is in the position of the stepdaughters. Just as stepdaughters are not made unlawful by the contract with their mothers without intercourse, so the mothers of wives are not made unlawful by the contract with their daughters without intercourse. This is the view of 'Ali, Zayd, Jabir, Ibn 'Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr, who said: marrying the mothers of wives with whom one has not consummated is lawful. The first view is the more correct.

Ibn Jurayj said: I said to 'Ata': "A man marries a woman, then sees her but does not have intercourse with her until he divorces her; is her mother lawful to him?" He said: "No, she is unrestricted, whether he has consummated the marriage or not." I said to him: "Ibn 'Abbas used to recite: 'and the mothers of your wives to whom you have gone in.'" He said: "No."

'Amr ibn al-Musayyab narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "If a man marries a woman, it is not lawful for him to marry her mother, whether or not he has consummated with the daughter. And if he marries the mother and does not consummate with her, then divorces her, he may marry the daughter if he wishes."

"And your stepdaughters (rabaʼib)": the plural of rabiba, who is the daughter of the woman. She was called rabiba because of his raising (tarbiyatihi) of her; it is fa'ila in the sense of maf'ula. "Who are in your guardianship": that is, in your protection and upbringing. It is said: "So-and-so is in the custody (hijr) of so-and-so" when he is responsible for raising her. It is said: a woman of good custody (tayyibat al-hijr) when she has raised no child except one of good offspring.

Al-Kumayt said:
"Al-karimat [nisba] fi Quraysh... [wa siwahum] wa al-tayyibat al-hujura"

From this comes the saying that restriction is hijr, and the original meaning of it is the side; it is said: "So-and-so eats in his hijr and grazes his hijr."

"From your women to whom you have gone in": that is, have had intercourse with them. "But if you have not gone in to them, there is no blame upon you" in marrying their daughters, if you have divorced them or they have died leaving you.

Al-Zuhri narrated from 'Urwa: that Zaynab bint Abi Salama, and her mother Umm Salama, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), informed him that Umm Habiba bint Abi Sufyan had told her that she said: "O Messenger of Allah, marry my sister." She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "Would you like that?" I said: "Yes, you are not one to be left alone, and I love that the one who shares me in good should be my sister."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, that is not lawful to me." I said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we have been hearing that you intend to marry Durra bint Abi Salama." He said: "The daughter of Umm Salama?" I said: "Yes." He said: "By Allah, even if she were not my stepdaughter in my custody, she would still not be lawful to me; she is the daughter of my foster-brother, Thuwayba nursed me and Abu Salama. So do not offer me your daughters or your sisters." [[Musnad al-Shamiyyin: 4/208; al-Sunan al-Kubra: 3/290.]] [283]

"And the wives of your sons (halail abna'ikum)": meaning the wives of your sons. The male is halil, and its plural is ahillah and ahilla'; like 'aziz, 'azza and a'izza'. It was so named because each of the two is lawful (halal) to the other. It is said: halla and he is halil, like sahha and he is sahih. It was also said: it was so named because each of them alights where the other alights, from hulul, which is descent; and it was said: because each of them unties the waist-wrapper of the other, from hall, which is the opposite of tying.

The poet said:
"Yudafi'u qawman 'ala majdihim... difa'a al-halilati 'anha al-halila
Yudafi'uhu yawman tara... wa yumkinuhu rijluha an yashula"

"Who are of your loins": excluding those whom you have adopted.

'Ata' said: it was revealed concerning Muhammad (ﷺ) when he married the wife of Zayd ibn Haritha.

"And that you should combine two sisters," whether free women by contract or slave women by intercourse, "except what has already passed."

'Ata' and al-Suddi said: meaning, except what was of Ya'qub (peace be upon him), for he combined Lay'a, the mother of Yahudha, and Rahil, the mother of Yusuf, and they were two sisters.

"Indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful."

"And the married women among women..." the verse.

'Amr ibn Murra said: a man said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Did you not see Ibn 'Abbas when he was asked about this verse, 'and the married women among women,' and he said nothing about it?" Sa'id said: "He did not know it."

Mujahid said: "If I knew who could explain this verse, I would have driven camels' livers to him." His saying, Exalted is He: "and the married women among women."

The commentators said: this is the seventh of the women forbidden by cause.

The common readers recited "wa-l-muhsanat" with a fatha on the sad, meaning, in the cessation of husbands: their husbands made them muhsanat.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: it was revealed concerning women who used to migrate to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while they had husbands, and some Muslims married them; then their husbands came, migrating. So Allah forbade the Muslims from marrying them, then made an exception, saying: "except what your right hands possess," meaning the captives taken who had husbands in the land of war; it is lawful for their owners to have intercourse with them after istibra'.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri also said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent an army on the day of Hunayn to Awtas, and they encountered the enemy and took captives who had husbands among the polytheists. They disliked having intercourse with them and felt sinful about it, so Allah, Exalted, revealed this verse.

'Alqama recited "wa-l-muhsinat" with a kasra on the sad, and its evidence is the saying of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), 'Ubayda, Abu al-'Aliya and al-Suddi. They said: "the muhsanat" in this verse are the chaste ones, and its meaning: the chaste women among you are forbidden, except what your right hands possess of them through marriage or ownership by right hand and price. It was also said: its meaning is free women.

Al-Baqir and Yaman said: its meaning: "and the married women among women are forbidden to you," beyond the four; "except what your right hands possess," for there is no limit upon you regarding them.

Ibn Jurayj said: we asked 'Ata' about it, and he said: the meaning of His saying "except what your right hands possess" is that you have a slave-woman whom another slave of yours has married, and you may take her from him if you wish.

"The Book of Allah upon you": accusative as a verbal noun, i.e., Allah prescribed a prescription upon you. It was also said: accusative as a warning, i.e., hold fast to and fear the Book of Allah upon you.

Ibn al-Sumay' recited "kataba Allah 'alaykum," i.e., ordained. These are fourteen women, forbidden by the Book.

As for the six: two women are forbidden together, and this is what

Hisham narrated from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "A woman shall not be married to a man together with her paternal aunt or her maternal aunt." [[Sahih Muslim: 4/136; Ta'wil Mukhtalif al-Hadith: 181.]] [284]

"And lawful to you": Abu Ja'far and the people of Kufa recited "wa-uhilla" with a damma on the alif. The rest read it with a fatha; this is the recitation of 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas, and the choice of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim. Whoever reads it with a damma does so because of His saying "are forbidden," and whoever reads it with a fatha does so because of its proximity to the mention of Allah in His saying "the Book of Allah."

"Beyond that, what is other than those mentioned": the forbidden ones you have been told of. "That you seek" is a substitute for "ma" (what). According to the one who reads "uhilla" with a damma, "an" is in the nominative position; according to the one who reads with a fatha, "an" is in the accusative position.

Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: its position is accusative in both readings, by removing the preposition, meaning: "that you may seek and desire."

"With your wealth": either by marriage with a dowry, or by ownership and price. "Chaste, not fornicators": "muhsinin" means those who abstain; "musafihin" means adulterers, and the root is from the emission of madhi and semen.

"So for what you have enjoyed of them": scholars differed regarding the meaning of the verse. Mujahid and al-Hasan said: it means what you have benefited from and found pleasure in of women for intercourse through a valid marriage.

"Then give them their wages": that is, their dowries. So if he has intercourse with her even once, the full dowry becomes due to her.

Others said: it is the marriage of temporary pleasure (nikah al-mut'a). Then they differed whether the verse is muhkam (non-abrogated) or mansukh (abrogated).

Ibn 'Abbas said: it is muhkam, and he permitted temporary marriage, which is that a man marries a woman with a guardian and two witnesses for a known term. When the term ends, he has no claim over her, she is free of him, she must observe her waiting period, and there is no inheritance between them.

Habib ibn Abi Thabit said: Ibn 'Abbas gave me a mushaf and said: "This is according to the recitation of Ubayy." I saw in the mushaf: "So for what you have enjoyed of them up to a specified term."

Dawud narrated from Abu Nadra who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about temporary marriage, and he said: "Do you not recite Surat al-Nisa'?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then what do you recite: 'So for what you have enjoyed of them up to a specified term'?" I said: "I do not recite it like that." Ibn 'Abbas said: "By Allah, thus was it revealed," three times.

'Isa ibn 'Umar narrated from Talha ibn Musarrif that he recited: "So for what you have enjoyed of them up to a specified term."

'Amr ibn Murra narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he recited it: "So for what you have enjoyed of them up to a specified term."

Shu'ba narrated from al-Hakam who said: I asked him about this verse, "So for what you have enjoyed of them," whether it is abrogated. He said: No. Al-Hakam said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah honor his face, said: "Had 'Umar not forbidden temporary marriage, none would commit fornication except a wretch."

Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi narrated from 'Imran ibn Husayn who said: this verse (on temporary marriage) was revealed in the Book of Allah, and no verse came after it abrogating it. We were commanded by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to it, and we enjoyed temporary marriage with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he did not forbid us from it. Then a man said after that what he wished by his own opinion! Al-Tha'labi said: I say: none permitted temporary marriage except 'Imran ibn Husayn, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, some of his companions, and a group from the People of the House. [[Abu 'Umar said: the companions of Ibn 'Abbas from Makka and Yemen all held temporary marriage to be lawful (Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/133).]] And it is in the view of Ibn 'Abbas.

The poet says:
"Aqulu lil-rakbi idha tal al-thawa' bina... ya sahi hal laka fi fatwa Ibn 'Abbas
Hal laka fi rukhsat al-atraf na'ima... takunu mathwaka hatta marji' al-nas"

But the rest of the scholars, jurists, Companions, Successors and the righteous predecessors hold that this verse is abrogated and temporary marriage with women is forbidden.

Al-Rabi' ibn Subra al-Juhani narrated from his father who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on his 'umra, and we complained to him of celibacy. He said: "O people, enjoy these women." Then I accompanied the Messenger of Allah in the morning, and he was saying: "O people, I had commanded you to enjoy these women, but Allah has forbidden that until the Day of Resurrection." [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/406.]] [285]

Khusayf said: I asked al-Hasan about temporary marriage, and he said: It was only for three days in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger (ﷺ) forbade it.

Al-Kalbi said: This was at the beginning of Islam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permitted it for three days, then forbade it. When the term agreed between them ended, he would give her the wage that had been stipulated for her, then say: "Extend me in days and I will increase you in the wage." If she agreed, that was done; when the agreed term ended, he gave her the wage and separated from her. Then it was abrogated by the verse of divorce, the waiting period, and death.

Al-Zuhri narrated from al-Hasan and Abd Allah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, from their father, that Ali said to Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade temporary marriage (mut'ah) with women on the day of Khaybar, and forbade eating domestic donkeys.

Al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated from al-Bara' ibn Abd Allah al-Qass, from Abu Nadrah, from Ibn Abbas, that Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) forbade the mut'ah mentioned in Surat al-Nisa'. He said: Allah permitted it during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when women were few. Then He prohibited it to them after He had forbidden it.

From Salim ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar, from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), that he ascended the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: What is the matter with men who marry through this mut'ah, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has forbidden it? I will not find a man marrying it except that I will stone him.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Marriage, divorce, the waiting period and inheritance demolish mut'ah." [Musnad Abi Ya'la: 11/504, and Fath al-Bari: 9/138.] [286]

Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: I asked Aishah about mut'ah, and she said: "Between me and them is the Book of Allah: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess﴾ [Surat al-Mu'minun: 5–6]."

From Aishah: "By Allah, we find in the Book of Allah only marriage and concubinage." Ibn Umar said: Mut'ah is fornication (sifah).

Ata': Mut'ah is forbidden, like carrion, blood and the flesh of swine.

Al-Tha'alabi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Jubayr say: I heard Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Khayyat say: I heard Abu Nu'aym ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn Adi say: I heard [...] [an illegible word in the manuscript] say:

Al-Shafi'i said: I know of nothing in Islam that was made lawful, then made unlawful, then made lawful, then made unlawful, except mut'ah.

﴿So give them their wages as an obligation﴾: that is, their dowries. The dower was called "wage" (ajr) because it is the price of the womb (bud') and the wage of enjoyment. Do you not see that it becomes firmly due by seclusion (khalwah) and consummation?

The scholars differed about its minimum. As for its maximum, it has no limit. As for its minimum, Abu Hanifah said: There is no dower less than ten dirhams or their value in gold, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿that you seek with your wealth﴾, and the term "wealth" is not applied to less than this amount.

According to al-Shafi'i, it has no minimum. He permitted even a trivial thing, such as a handful of food. Likewise, any act that is worth a wage, whether small or large, and a surah or a verse of the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, based on His words: ﴿so give them their wages﴾.

From Salamah ibn Wardan, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked one of his companions: "O so-and-so, have you married?" He said: No, and I do not have anything to marry with. He said: "Do you not have ﴿Say: He is Allah, One﴾ [Surat al-Ikhlas: 1]?" He said: Yes. He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have ﴿When the help of Allah comes﴾ [Surat al-Nasr: 1]?" He said: Yes. He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾ [Surat al-Kafirun: 1]?" He said: Yes. He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have ﴿When the earth is shaken﴾ [Surat al-Zalzalah: 1]?" He said: Yes. He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have the Verse of the Throne?" He said: Yes. He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Marry, marry, marry." [Musnad Ahmad: 3/221, Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/135.] [287]

The arguments of both sides have been mentioned in what has been said.

﴿And there is no blame upon you in what you agree upon after the obligation﴾: that is, in what the woman ransoms herself with. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾

﴿And whoever among you is not able to marry free, believing women﴾: that is, lacks means and wealth (tawl).

Al-Musayyab ibn Sharik, from Imran ibn Jarir, from al-Nazzal ibn Sabrah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Whoever possesses three hundred dirhams, the pilgrimage becomes obligatory for him, and marrying slave women becomes forbidden to him.

﴿to marry believing free women (al-muhsanat)﴾: free women. Al-Kisa'i read (al-muhsinat) with a kasrah on the sad, throughout the Qur'an except at the beginning of this surah. The others read it with a fathah.

﴿...believing women, then from what your right hands possess of your believing maidens...﴾ up to His words ﴿with the permission of their people﴾: their masters. ﴿So give them their wages﴾: their dowries ﴿according to what is reasonable﴾, without withholding. ﴿Chaste (muhsanat)﴾: modest. ﴿Not unchaste (musafihat)﴾: fornicators. ﴿Nor taking secret lovers (akhdan)﴾: lovers with whom they fornicate in secret.

﴿And when they become chaste (uhsinna)﴾: the people of Kufa read it with a fathah on the alif, meaning they guarded their private parts. The others read it with a dammah, meaning they became chaste through their husbands. ﴿And if they commit an immorality﴾: that is, fornication, ﴿then upon them is half the punishment for free women﴾ if they commit fornication. ﴿Of the punishment﴾: that is, the hadd (prescribed penalty). Its parallel is: ﴿and it averts from her the punishment﴾ [Surat al-Nur: 8]. It is fifty lashes and exile for half a year, according to the correct view of the school of al-Shafi'i. The adulterer must be exiled to a place from which the prayer may be shortened. The master has the right to carry out the hadd for fornication upon his male and female slaves.

From Sa'id al-Maqbari, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If one of your slave women commits fornication, let him lash her and not reproach her. If she repeats it, let him lash her and not reproach her. If she repeats it, let him lash her and not reproach her. If she repeats it a fourth time, let him sell her, even for a braid of hair or a rope." [Sharh Muslim: 11/211, and Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah: 8/369.] [288]

﴿That﴾: that is, marrying slave women when one lacks means, ﴿is for one who fears sin from among you﴾: that is, sin and harm through overpowering desire. ﴿But to be patient is better for you﴾: refraining from marrying slave women while remaining chaste. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

From Yunus ibn Mirdas, who was a servant of Anas, who said: I was between Anas and Abu Hurayrah. Anas said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever loves to meet Allah pure and purified, let him marry free women."

Abu Hurayrah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Free women are the goodness of the household, and slave women are the corruption of the household." [Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/598.] [289]

﴿Allah intends to make clear to you﴾: that is, that He may make clear. The lam here means "that" (an). The Arabs interchange the lam of purpose (kay) with an, placing one in the place of the other, as in His words: ﴿And I have been commanded to be just among you﴾ [Surat al-Shura: 15], and His words: ﴿And we were commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Surat al-An'am: 73]. Then He said in another place: ﴿And I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Surat Ghafir: 66]. And He said: ﴿They wish to extinguish the light of Allah﴾ [Surat al-Saff: 8], then He said in another place: ﴿They wish to extinguish the light of Allah﴾ [Surat al-Tawbah: 32].

The poet said:
I wish to forget her remembrance, but Layla appears to me in every path.
He means: "that I forget." The meaning of the verse: Allah wishes to make clear the laws of your religion and the interests of your affairs.

Al-Hasan: He teaches you what you do and what you leave. Ata': He makes clear to you what brings you near to Him. Al-Kalbi: That He may make clear to you that patience from marrying slave women is better for you.

﴿And guide you to the ways (sunan)﴾: the laws (sharai') of those before you, in the prohibition of mothers, daughters and sisters, as mentioned in the two verses. Thus He prohibited them for those among the nations before you. ﴿And accept your repentance﴾: He overlooks what you committed before it was made clear to you, as said by al-Kalbi.

Muhammad ibn Jarir said: That is, He brings you back from the disobedience in which you were before this, to His obedience which He commanded you in this verse. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what benefits His servants in the matters of their religion and their worldly life, Wise in His management of them.﴾ ﴿And Allah wishes to accept your repentance﴾ if shortcoming occurs from you in His command. ﴿But those who follow their desires wish that you deviate into a great deviation﴾ by your committing what He has forbidden to you. The scholars differed about who are described as following desires:

Al-Suddi said: They are the Jews and the Christians.
