﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted and Grand.﴾ ﴿And if you fear a breach between the two, appoint an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family, who intend reconciliation; Allah will bring about harmony between them.﴾ That is, dispute between the spouses. ﴿Appoint an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family; they intend reconciliation (islah)⁠⁠—⁠the spouses, it was said, or the two arbiters—⁠Allah will bring about harmony between them, through reform and affection. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Acquainted.

It is narrated from 'Ubaydah al-Salmani that a man and a woman came to 'Ali (peace be upon him), each accompanied by a group of people. 'Ali said: "What is the matter with these two?" They said: "A breach has occurred between them." 'Ali said: ﴿Appoint an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family.﴾ So they appointed an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family. 'Ali said to the two arbiters: "Do you know what is upon you? If you see that they should be brought together, then bring them together; and if you see that they should be separated, then separate them." The woman said: "I am content with the Book of Allah, with whatever is upon me and for me." The man said: "As for separation, no." 'Ali said: "You lie, by Allah. You will not leave me until you acknowledge what she has acknowledged." [Source: al-Tabari 5/101.]

﴿And worship Allah;﴾ affirm the oneness of Allah and obey Him. The wise said: servitude is abandoning disobedience and constantly maintaining humility and submission. It was also said: servitude consists of four things: fulfilling covenants, observing limits, contentment with what exists, and patience over what is lost.

﴿And associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents⁠⁠—⁠kindness towards them, showing them tenderness.⁠⁠﴾ Ibn Jinni read (إحسانٌ) ["kindness"] in the nominative, meaning: kindness to them has become obligatory. ﴿And to relatives, orphans, the needy,⁠⁠—⁠﴾

It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah that a man complained to the Prophet (ﷺ) about the hardness of his heart. He said: "If you want your heart to soften, feed the needy and wipe the head of the orphan and feed him." [310] [Source: al-Jami' al-Saghir 1/407.]

﴿And the neighbor who is near⁠⁠—⁠﴾: the majority read it in the genitive, as a continuation of the previous statement. Ibn Abi 'Ablah read (والجارَ) and what follows it in the accusative. ﴿The neighbor who is near﴾ means a neighbor by kinship. ﴿And the neighbor who is distant (al-junub)﴾ means one who is far, with whom you have no kinship. Al-Dahhak said: he is a stranger from another people. Al-A'mash and al-Fadl read (وَالْجَارِ الْجَنْبِ) with a fatha on the jim and sukun on the nun; both are dialects. A man is called janb, junub, janib, ajnab, and ajnabi when he is not a relative. Their plural is ajanib. Al-A'sha said:

"I came to Huraythah as a visitor from a distance, but Huraythah was stingy with my gifts."

That is, from a distance without kinship. From this is derived "ijtanaba fulanun fulanan" (someone avoided someone), meaning he kept far from him. From this also the person in ritual impurity is called junub, because he is set apart from prayer and kept far from the mosque until he bathes. Nawf al-Bakali said: "The distant neighbor" is the disbeliever. ﴿And the companion by your side﴾ means the fellow traveler.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Abu Ja'far, 'Ikrimah and Qatadah said, from Sa'id ibn Ma'ruf ibn Rafi', from his father, from his grandfather: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Seek out a neighbor before a house, and a companion before a journey." [311] [Source: Kanz al-Ummal 15/388, no. 41495.]

Some said: "The distant neighbor" is the neighbor whose house is adjoining yours, so he is beside you. 'Ali, 'Abd Allah, Ibn Abi Layla and al-Nakha'i said: it is the woman who is with him beside him.

Ibn Zayd and Ibn Jurayj said: it is the one who stays with you and accompanies you, hoping for your kindness and gifts. Ibn 'Abbas said: "I am ashamed for a man to step on my carpet three times without any trace of my kindness being seen on him." Al-Muhallab said: "If a man comes to you in the morning and leaves in the evening, that is enough of a request and a reminder for himself."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The best companions before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are those best to their companion; the best neighbors before Allah are those best to their neighbor." [312] [Source: al-Jami' al-Saghir 1/617, no. 3998.]

'Uthman ibn 'Ata', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He is not a believer whose neighbor is not safe from his harms. Whoever closes his doors on his neighbor, fearing for his family and property, is not a believer." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of the neighbor?" He said: "If he calls you, answer him; if he is in need, help him; if he asks you for a loan, lend to him; if good comes to him, congratulate him; if he is ill, visit him; if calamity strikes him, console him; if he dies, attend his funeral. Do not raise your building above his to block the wind from him except with his permission. Do not harm him with the smell of your cooking pot, unless you give him some of it. If you buy fruit, send him some of it, and if you do not, bring it in secretly, and do not let your child carry it out in a way that provokes his child." [Source: al-Nihayah fi Gharib al-Hadith 4/12, s.v. q-t-r: "qatar" is the smell of a cooking pot.]

"Then the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) said: 'Neighbours are of three kinds: among them is one who has three rights, among them is one who has two rights, and among them is one who has one right. As for the one with three rights: it is the Muslim neighbour who is a relative, who has the right of Islam, the right of neighbourhood and the right of kinship. As for the one with two rights: it is the Muslim neighbour, who has the right of Islam and the right of the neighbour. As for the one with one right: it is the polytheist neighbour, who has the right of neighbourhood, even if he is a polytheist.'" [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 9/185, no. 25613, with variation; and Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/184.]] [313].

Abu Hisham al-Qattan, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) said: "Whoever harms his neighbour has harmed me, and whoever harms me has harmed Allah, and whoever wars against his neighbour has waged war against me, and whoever wars against me has waged war against Allah, Mighty and Majestic." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 9/56, no. 24927.]] [314].

﴿And the wayfarer, and what your right hands possess﴾: meaning the slaves (al-mamalik).

From Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) gave Abu Dharr a young slave, and said: "O Abu Dharr, feed him from what you eat, and clothe him from what you wear." He said: He had only one garment, so he cut it in two halves and went to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ). He said: "What is the matter with this garment of yours?" He replied: "The youth whom you gave me, you commanded me to feed him from what I eat and to clothe him from what I wear, and I had only this garment, so I shared it with him." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) said: "I advise you to free him." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) said: "What has your young man done?" He said: "I have no young man; I have freed him." He said: "May Allah reward you, O Abu Dharr." [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 4/237, with variation.]] [315].

Al-A'mash, from 'Atiq, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) said: "Sheep are a blessing, camels are a glory to their owners, and horses have goodness tied to their forelocks until the Day of Resurrection, and the slave is your brother, so if he is unable, help him." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/325, no. 35228, with slight variation.]]

And from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The last words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) were: Prayer, and fear Allah regarding what your right hands possess." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 8/6, no. 21625.]] [316].

﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is arrogant and boastful.﴾

﴿O you who believe, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly﴾, that is, with what is forbidden (ḥarām), namely usury (ribā), gambling (qimār), robbery by cutting off the road (qaṭʿ), seizure by force (ghaṣb), theft (sariqa), and betrayal (khiyāna).

Ibn ʿAbbās said: this refers to a man who buys a garment from another man and says, "If I am pleased, I take it; otherwise I return it and return a dirham with it."

Then He said: ﴿except that it be trade﴾, meaning, but if it is trade. This is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), since trade is not falsehood.

The people of Kufa read (tijāratan) in the accusative, and this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. The rest read it in the nominative, and this is the choice of Abū Ḥātim. Whoever reads it in the accusative takes it as the predicate of kāna, its implied meaning being: "except that the wealth be trade," as in the words of the poet:

"If he was a spearman among them and a wrestler..." [[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī: 3/179.]]

Whoever reads it in the nominative takes it to mean "except that a trade occurs," and in that case it has no predicate, as in the words of the poet:

"My she-camel is a ransom for the Banū Dhuhl ibn Shaybān, when there is a day of many stars and a grey-white sky..." [[Lisān al-ʿArab: 1/509.]]

Then He described the trade: ﴿by mutual consent among you﴾, each party being content with what is in the other's hand.

Most of the exegetes said: it means that each of the two contracting parties gives the other the option after the sale is concluded, until they separate from the meeting place where they made the contract. As the Prophet ﷺ said: "The two parties to a sale have the option (to cancel) as long as they have not separated." [[Musnad Aḥmad: 4/402.]] [290]

He ﷺ also said: "Sale by mutual consent carries an option after the transaction, and it is not lawful for a Muslim to deceive a Muslim." [[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī: 5/45; Tafsir Ibn Kathīr: 1/491.]] [291]

Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The two parties to a sale have the option as long as they have not separated. If they are truthful and clarify (the defects), their sale is blessed for them; but if they conceal and lie, the blessing of their sale is erased." [[Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī: 3/18; Musnad Aḥmad: 3/402.]] [292]

ʿUmar ibn Jarīr bought a horse, then gave his counterparty the option after the sale, and then said: "I heard Abū Hurayra say: 'This is a sale by mutual consent.'"

﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾, meaning your brethren, that is, do not let some of you kill others.

Al-Thaʿlabī said: I heard Abū al-Qāsim al-Ḥabībī say: I heard my father, from my grandfather, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Hilālī, who said: I heard Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ash'ath say: Al-Faḍl ibn ʿIyāḍ was asked about the words of God: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾. He said: "Do not be heedless of the share of your souls (ḥaẓẓ anfusikum). Whoever is heedless of his own share has, as it were, killed it."

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you﴾.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr narrated from ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ that he said: When the Prophet sent him in the year of Dhāt al-Salāsil, he said: "I had a wet dream on a very cold night, and I feared that if I performed the ritual bath I would perish. So I performed tayammum and then led my companions in the dawn prayer. When we came back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I mentioned that to him, and he said: 'O ʿAmr, you led your companions in prayer while you were in a state of major impurity (junub)?'"

I said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah. I had a wet dream on a very cold night, and I feared that if I bathed I would perish, and I remembered the words of God: ﴿And do not kill yourselves; indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you﴾. So I performed tayammum and then prayed." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed and said nothing. [[Musnad Aḥmad: 4/203; al-Mustadrak: 1/177.]]

It is narrated from al-Ḥasan that al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd Allāh was alone with a group of his companions and said: "These people have plunged into their own blood. Let no one among you be prevented from Paradise by a handful of the blood of a Muslim that he has spilled, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'A man from among those before you had a sore on his hand; he took a knife and cut his hand with it until he severed it, and its blood did not stop until he died. Your Lord, may He be exalted, said: "My servant hastened to take his own life, so I have forbidden Paradise to him."'" [[Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim: 1/75.]] [294]

Simāk narrated from Jābir ibn Samura that a man slaughtered himself, and the Prophet ﷺ did not pray over him.

Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated from ʿĀṣim al-Asadī: it is mentioned that Masrūq ibn al-Ajdaʿ came to Ṣiffīn, stood between the two lines, and said: "O people, be silent!" Then he said: "Tell me, if a herald called to you from the sky, and you heard his speech and saw him, saying: 'Allah forbids you from what you are engaged in, would you obey Him?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'By God, that would indeed have been revealed to Muḥammad by Gabriel, and he continued to come with this (prohibition).'" Then he recited: ﴿O you who believe, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly﴾ to the end of the verse, then he slipped away into the crowd and departed. [[Fully in al-Ṭabaqāt al-Kubrā: 6/78.]]

﴿And whoever does that out of transgression and injustice, We will drive him into the Fire, and that is ever easy for Allah﴾, meaning: We will make him enter the Fire in the Hereafter, and that is easy and simple for Allah.

﴿If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾, the verse.

The scholars differed concerning the major sins whose avoidance Allah made an expiation for minor sins.

ʿAmr ibn Sharḥabīl narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?" He said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you." I said: "Then what?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbor's wife." [[Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī: 7/75; Musnad Aḥmad: 1/380.]] [295] This hadith is from the words of God: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾ [[Sūrat al-Furqān: 68.]], the verse.

Ṣāliḥ ibn Ḥayyān narrated from Abū Burayda, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The greatest of the major sins are associating partners with Allah, disobedience to parents, and withholding surplus water after one has had enough." [[Tafsir Ibn Kathīr: 1/497.]]

Al-Shaʿbī narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The major sins are associating partners with Allah, the perjury that plunges one into the Fire (al-yamīn al-ghamūs), disobedience to parents, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden, and false speech, or he said: false testimony." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhī: 4/303, no. 5009.]] [296]

Sufyān narrated from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr who said: Among the major sins is that a man curses his parents. They said: "How does a man curse his parents?" He said: "He insults the father of a man, and so he insults his father, and insults his mother, and so he insults his mother."

Abū al-Ṭufayl narrated from Ibn Masʿūd who said: The major sins are four: associating partners with Allah, despairing of the mercy of Allah, despairing of the rest of Allah, and feeling secure from the plan of Allah.

ʿIkrima narrated from ʿAmmār, who said: Ṭaysala ibn ʿAlī al-Nahdī narrated to us: I asked Ibn ʿUmar about the major sins, and he said: "They are nine." I said: "What are they?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah, the Most High; killing a believer intentionally; disobedience to believing parents; consuming usury; consuming the wealth of orphans; slandering chaste women; fleeing from the battlefield; sorcery; and making lawful the carrion and the blood (that was) before you, living and dead." (The text is corrupted here as in the source.)

Ja'far al-Ṣādiq said: The major sins are three: abandoning your religion, altering your sunna, and fighting the people of your covenant (ṣafqa).

Farqad al-Masīḥī said: I read in the Torah: "The mother sins are three: the first sin by which one disobeys God is pride, and that was for Iblīs, may he be cursed; and greed, and that was for Ādam (peace be upon him); and envy, and that was for Qābīl when he killed Hābīl."

ʿUmar ibn Abī Salama narrated from his father, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The major sins are, first among them: associating partners with Allah; killing a soul without right; consuming usury; consuming the wealth of an orphan out of haste before he grows up; fleeing from the battlefield; accusing a chaste woman; and reverting to the desert (after emigration) as an apostate. These are seven." [[Zād al-Masīr: 2/114.]] [297]

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that a man asked him about the seven major sins. He said: "They are closer to seven hundred than to seven, except that there is no major sin with seeking forgiveness, and no minor sin with persistence."

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa al-Wālibī narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: The major sins are twenty: associating partners with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; disobedience to parents; killing a believer; despairing of the mercy of Allah; feeling secure from the plan of Allah; despairing of the rest of Allah; sorcery; adultery; usury; theft; consuming the wealth of orphans; abandoning prayer; withholding zakāt; false testimony; killing a child for fear that it will eat with you; envy; pride; slander; greed; injustice in bequest; and belittling Muslims.

Al-Suddī narrated from Ibn Mālik who said: The major sins were mentioned in the presence of ʿAbd Allāh, and ʿAbd Allāh said: "Open Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: everything Allah has forbidden, up to thirty-three verses, is a major sin." Then he said: "The confirmation of this is: ﴿If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden...﴾, the verse."

Ibn Sīrīn said: The major sins were mentioned in the presence of Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: "Everything Allah has forbidden is a major sin, even a glance (al-ṭarfa), which is a look."

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from him: Every act in which one disobeys Allah is a major sin. Whoever commits any of them should seek forgiveness, for Allah does not keep in the Fire, from this community, anyone except one who has turned away from Islam, or denies an obligation, or denies predestination.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from him: Every sin which Allah concluded with a fire, or wrath, or a curse, or a punishment.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: Every sin which Allah attributed to the Fire and threatened with the Fire is a major sin.

al-Ḥasan: those that necessitate the prescribed punishments (ḥudūd).

al-Ḍaḥḥāk: whatever Allah has promised a prescribed punishment for in this world and a punishment in the Hereafter.

al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl: whatever Allah called in His Book "great" or "mighty," like His saying: ﴿Indeed, it was a great sin﴾ [[Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 2.]], ﴿Indeed, their killing was a great sin﴾ [[Sūrat al-Isrāʾ: 31.]], ﴿Indeed, association is a great injustice﴾ [[Sūrat Luqmān: 13.]], ﴿Indeed, your plotting is great﴾ [[Sūrat Yūsuf: 28.]], ﴿Glory be to You, this is a great slander﴾ [[Sūrat al-Nūr: 16.]], ﴿Indeed, that was with Allah a great (matter)﴾ [[Sūrat al-Aḥzāb: 53.]].

Mālik ibn Miʿwal said: The major sins are the sins of the people of innovation (ahl al-bidaʿ), and the misdeeds are the sins of the people of blemish (al-shīna).

Wakīʿ said: Every sin which a servant persists in is a major sin, and what a servant repents of and seeks forgiveness for is not among the major sins.

Aḥmad ibn ʿĀṣim al-Anṭākī said: The major sins are the sins committed deliberately; the misdeeds are errors, forgetfulness, compulsion, the promptings of the soul, and what is raised (forgiven) from this community.

Sufyān al-Thawrī said: The major sins are those involving wrongs between you and the servants, and the minor sins are those between you and Allah, the Most High, because Allah is Generous and forgives them. He argued by the words of the Prophet ﷺ: "On the Day of Resurrection a herald will call from the depths of the Throne: 'O community of Muḥammad, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: As for what was due to Me from you, I have forgiven it. But the dues between people remain, so grant them to one another and enter Paradise by My mercy.'" [[ʿUddat al-Dāʿī: 136.]] [298]

al-Maḥāribī said: The major sins are the sins of those who sin and make them lawful, like the sin of Iblīs; and the minor sins are the sins of those who seek forgiveness, like the sin of Ādam.

al-Suddī said: The major sins are what Allah has forbidden of great sins, and the misdeeds are their preliminaries, and their consequences are what the righteous and the wicked both share, such as the glance, the touch, the kiss, and similar things.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "The two eyes commit adultery, the two hands commit adultery, and the private part makes it true or false." [[Musnad Abī Yaʿlā: 11/309.]] [299]

Some people said: The major sin is what is repugnant to reason and nature, such as killing, injustice, adultery, lying, and the like; and the minor sin is what Allah has forbidden by revealed law and by hearing.

He also said: Every sin for which Allah overlooks by His grace on the Day of Resurrection is a minor sin, and every sin for which He punishes by His justice is a major sin. It was said: the major sins are the hidden sins, and the misdeeds are the open sins.

Some of them said: The minor sins are what people consider trivial, and the major sins are what they regard as grave, so they fear its occurrence.

Anas ibn Mālik said: You perform deeds which in your eyes are finer than a hair; we used to count them as major sins during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Some of them said: The major sins are associating partners with Allah and what leads to it; and what is below association is among the misdeeds. Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [[Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 48.]].

Section detailing the views of the people of interpretation on the number of major sins, gathered from the Book and the Sunna, accompanied by evidence and proof:

First: associating partners with Allah, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise﴾ [[Sūrat al-Māʾida: 72.]].

Second: despairing of the rest of Allah, based on His saying: ﴿And do not despair of the rest of Allah﴾ [[Sūrat Yūsuf: 87.]], the verse.

Third: despairing of the mercy of Allah, based on His saying: ﴿And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except the astray?﴾ [[Sūrat al-Ḥijr: 56.]]

Fourth: feeling secure from the plan of Allah, based on His saying: ﴿So none feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people﴾.

Fifth: disobedience to parents, based on His saying: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment﴾ [[Sūrat al-Isrāʾ: 23.]].

Sixth: killing a soul which Allah has forbidden, based on His saying: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell﴾ [[Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 93.]].

Seventh: slandering a chaste woman, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women﴾ [[Sūrat al-Nūr: 23.]], the verse.

Eighth: fleeing from the battlefield, based on His saying: ﴿O you who believe, when you meet those who disbelieve advancing (in battle)﴾ [[Sūrat al-Anfāl: 15.]], the verse.

Ninth: consuming usury, based on His saying: ﴿Those who consume usury﴾ [[Sūrat al-Baqara: 275.]], the verse.

Tenth: sorcery, based on His saying: ﴿And they had certainly known that whoever purchased it﴾ [[Sūrat al-Baqara: 102.]], the verse.

Eleventh: adultery: ﴿And they do not commit adultery; and whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾ [[Sūrat al-Furqān: 68.]].

Twelfth: false oath, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price﴾ [[Sūrat Āl ʿImrān: 77.]].

Thirteenth: withholding zakāt, based on His saying: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾ [[Sūrat al-Tawba: 34.]], the two verses.

Fourteenth: embezzlement (ghulūl), based on His saying: ﴿And whoever embezzles will bring what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [[Sūrat Āl ʿImrān: 161.]].

Fifteenth: false testimony, based on His saying: ﴿And do not conceal testimony﴾ [[Sūrat al-Baqara: 283.]], the verse.

Sixteenth: gambling (maysir), which is qimār, based on His saying: ﴿Gambling and idols and divining arrows﴾ [[Sūrat al-Māʾida: 90.]].

Seventeenth: drinking wine, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, wine and gambling﴾ [[Sūrat al-Māʾida: 90.]], the verse.

Eighteenth: deliberately abandoning prayer, based on His saying: ﴿Guard the prayers﴾ [[Sūrat al-Baqara: 238.]], the verse.

Nineteenth: severing family ties, based on His saying: ﴿And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs﴾ [[Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 1.]], and His saying: ﴿And sever your ties of kinship? Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed﴾ [[Sūrat Muḥammad: 22.]].

Twentieth: injustice in bequest, based on His saying: ﴿But whoever fears from a testator injustice or sin﴾ [[Sūrat al-Baqara: 182.]], the verse.

Twenty-first: consuming the wealth of orphans, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly﴾ [[Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 10.]], the verse.

Twenty-second: reverting to the desert (taʿarrub) after emigration, based on His saying: ﴿And whoever turns back on his heels, he will not harm Allah at all﴾ [[Sūrat Āl ʿImrān: 144.]].

Twenty-third: making lawful the sacred (ḥurum), based on His saying: ﴿Do not violate the rites of Allah﴾ [[Sūrat al-Māʾida: 2.]], and His saying: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation by wrongdoing﴾ [[Sūrat al-Ḥajj: 25.]].

Twenty-fourth: apostasy, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who turned back on their heels after guidance had become clear﴾ [[Sūrat Muḥammad: 25.]], the verse.

Twenty-fifth: breaking the covenant, based on His saying: ﴿And those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification﴾ [[Sūrat al-Raʿd: 25.]].

That is His saying: ﴿If you avoid the major sins﴾.

Ibn Masʿūd recited: "kabar mā tunhawna ʿanhu" in the singular, and in it is the meaning of the plural.

﴿We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾: from one prayer to the next, from one Friday to the next, from Ramaḍān to Ramaḍān, and from Ḥajj to Ḥajj, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "The five prayers are expiations for what is between them, so long as major sins are avoided." [[Musnad Ibn al-Jaʿd: 84; Musnad Ibn Yaʿlā: 39 (with slight variation).]] [300]

﴿And We will admit you to a noble entrance﴾, and it is Paradise.

ʿĀṣim and the people of Madina read (mudkhalan) with a fatḥa on the mīm, meaning the place of entering. The rest read it with a ḍamma, as a verbal noun, meaning the act of entering.

It is narrated from Abū Hurayra and from Abū Saʿīd that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat on the pulpit and then said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul," three times, then fell silent. Then every man among us came forward weeping from sorrow at the oath of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and then he said:

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 4, verses 29–36 (part 2 of 3)**

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No servant performs the five prayers, fasts Ramadan, and avoids the major sins except that the gates of Paradise will be opened for him on the Day of Resurrection, until they nearly clatter." [301] Then he recited: ﴿If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden, We will remove from you your minor misdeeds﴾ [Source: al-Mustadrak 2/240; Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah 1/163.] ... the verse.

﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others...﴾ ... the verse.

It is said: The women's delegation came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, is not Allah the Lord of men and women, and are you not the Messenger of Allah to them all? Why then does Allah mention the men and not mention the women? We fear that there is no good in us and that Allah has no need of us." So Allah revealed this verse, and His saying: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and the Muslim women...﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab 33:35] ... the verse, and His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer...﴾ [Surah al-Nahl 16:97].

It is also said: When Allah made for the male a share equal to the portion of two females in inheritance, the women said: "We are more in need of having two shares and the men one share, because we are weak and they are stronger and more able to seek livelihood than we are." So Allah revealed this verse.

Mujahid said: Umm Salamah said: "O Messenger of Allah, the men go out to fight and we do not fight; we only have half the inheritance. Would that we were men, so that we could fight and attain what men attain." So this verse was revealed.

Qatadah and al-Suddi said: When His saying was revealed, ﴿For the male is the equal of the portion of two females﴾ [Surah al-Nisa 4:11], the men said: "We hope that the women will be given preference over us in the Hereafter for our good deeds, just as we have been given preference over them in inheritance, so our reward will be double the reward of the women." And the women said: "We hope that our burden in the Hereafter will be half of the men's burden, just as we have half their share in inheritance in this world." So Allah revealed: ﴿For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned﴾, meaning reward and punishment. Qatadah said this, and he also said: a man is recompensed tenfold for a good deed, and a woman is recompensed tenfold as well.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿For men is a share of what they have earned﴾ means inheritance, and for women is a share of it, ﴿for the male is the equal of the portion of two females.﴾ On this view, "earning" means acquiring and obtaining. Allah therefore forbade wishing in this manner, because it leads to the causes of envy.

Al-Dahhak said: It is not lawful for a Muslim to wish for another's wealth. Have you not heard those who said: ﴿Oh, would that we had like what Qarun was given﴾ [Surah al-Qasas 28:79], up to His saying: ﴿And those who had wished for his position the day before began to say...﴾ [Surah al-Qasas 28:82], when the earth swallowed up his house and wealth, and they said: ﴿Had Allah not been gracious to us, He would have swallowed us up﴾ [Surah al-Qasas 28:82].

Al-Kalbi said: A man should not wish for his brother's wealth, nor his wife, nor his servant, nor his mount. Rather, let him say: "O Allah, grant me the like of it." This is also how it is in the Torah, and this is His saying in the Qur'an: ﴿And ask Allah of His bounty﴾ [Surah al-Nisa 4:32].

Ibn Kathir, Khalaf and al-Kisa'i read (وسلوا الله) ["and ask Allah"], and (سل) and (فسل) without the hamzah, transferring the vowel of the hamzah to the sin. The rest read with the hamzah.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ask Allah of His bounty, for He loves to be asked, and indeed among the best acts of worship is waiting for relief." [Source: al-Tabari 5/68; al-Qurtubi 5/164.]

Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), said: "Whoever does not ask Allah, Mighty and Majestic, of His bounty, He will be angry with him." [302]

Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, said: "Ask your Lord to the point of satisfaction. Whoever Allah does not make easy, will not find it easy."

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: "He only commanded asking so that He might give."

﴿And for each We have made heirs (mawali)﴾, meaning: for each one, from among men and women, there are heirs, that is, relatives who inherit ﴿from what the parents and close relatives leave behind﴾ from their inheritance. On this interpretation, the parents and close relatives are the ones who are inherited from. It is also said that the meaning is: "For each We have made heirs," that is, relatives of those who left [the estate]. Then He explained the heirs, saying: ﴿the parents and close relatives,﴾ meaning they are the parents and close relatives, a predicate of an omitted subject, so the meaning is: from the estate of the parents and close relatives. On this view, they are the ones who inherit.

﴿And those with whom your oaths have bound you﴾ is in the place of the nominative, as the subject of a sentence. Al-mu'aqadah is mutual pledging between two parties.

The people of Kufa read (ʿaqadat) lightly, without an alif, meaning "they bound for them." Umm Sa'd bint Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' read (ʿaqqadat) with emphasis, meaning "she confirmed and affirmed it." The word "oaths" (aymān) is the plural of yamin, which means the right hand and also the oath. They used to strike the handshake of allegiance with their right hands, so one would take the hand of another as a pledge of fidelity and adherence to the covenant, and they would swear allegiance on it. That is why the oaths are mentioned.

Qatadah and others said: By "those with whom your oaths have bound you" he meant the allies. In the Jahiliyyah, a man would bind himself to another and say: "My blood is your blood, my destruction is your destruction, my vengeance is your vengeance, my war is your war, my peace is your peace; you inherit from me, and I inherit from you; you seek my vengeance and I seek yours; you pay blood-money on my behalf and I pay on yours." Then the ally would receive a sixth of the ally's inheritance. Abu Bakr made such a pact with a client of his and inherited from him on that basis. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿then give them their share﴾, that is, give them their portion of the inheritance. Then this was abrogated (naskh) by His saying: ﴿And blood relatives are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah﴾ [Surah al-Anfal 8:75].

Ibrahim and Mujahid said: He meant ﴿give them their share﴾ of support, assistance and aid, but not inheritance. On this view, the verse is not abrogated, because of His saying: ﴿Fulfill the contracts﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah 5:1], and because of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "Fulfill to allies their covenants which your oaths have bound you to." [303]

And because of his (peace be upon him) statement in his sermon on the day of the conquest of Makkah: "Whatever alliance existed in the Jahiliyyah, hold to it, for Islam has only increased it in strength. Do not create new alliances in Islam." [304] [Source: Musnad Ahmad 5/61; Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3/73, no. 1634.]

'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I witnessed the Alliance of the Perfumed Ones [Hilf al-Mutayyibin] when I was a boy with my paternal uncles, and I would not like to have red camels in exchange for it, and I would still uphold it." [305] [Source: Musnad Ahmad 1/190.]

Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd said: This verse was revealed concerning those whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made brothers, among the Muhajirun and the Ansar, when they came to Madinah. They used to inherit from one another by that brotherhood, and then Allah abrogated that by the obligatory shares.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: It was revealed concerning those who used to adopt the sons of others in the Jahiliyyah, among them Zayd, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). In Islam they were commanded to make a bequest to them at death, and inheritance was returned to blood relatives. Allah refused to make the claimed heirs inherit from those who claimed and adopted them, but He made for them a share through a bequest. This is His saying: ﴿then give them their share.﴾

﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things a witness.﴾

Abu Rawq said: His saying ﴿And for each We have made heirs...﴾ was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and his son 'Abd al-Rahman, who was a disbeliever, that he would not benefit from or inherit any of his wealth. When 'Abd al-Rahman became Muslim, [Abu Bakr] was commanded to give him his share of the wealth.

﴿Men are in charge (qawwamun) of women...﴾ ... the verse.

Muqatil said: This verse was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' ibn 'Amr, one of the nuqaba' [chiefs], and his wife Habibah bint Zayd ibn Abi Zuhayr, both from the Ansar. She became disobedient (nushuz) to him, and he struck her. Her father went with her to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I gave her my noble daughter in marriage, and he struck her." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Let her retaliate against her husband." So she set off with her father to take retaliation (qisas) from him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Let them return; this is Jibril." Then this verse was revealed. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We intended a matter, and Allah intended a matter, and what Allah intended is better." [306] [Source: al-Qurtubi 5/168, with variations.] And the retaliation was lifted.

Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning As'ad ibn al-Rabi' and his wife, the daughter of Muhammad ibn Maslamah.

Abu Rawq mentioned something similar: It was revealed concerning Jamilah bint 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy and her husband Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, because she became disobedient to him and he struck her. She came to the Prophet (ﷺ) seeking redress, and Allah revealed this verse: ﴿Men are in charge of women﴾, that is, they have authority over disciplining women, ﴿by what Allah has given one over the other.﴾ Therefore there is no retaliation between a man and his wife for injuries less than death. If a man wounds his wife or injures her, he is not liable to retaliation (qawd), but he owes blood-money ('aql), except if he kills her, in which case he is killed for her. This was said by al-Zuhri and a group of scholars. Some of them said: There is no retaliation between husband and wife except in cases of death and wounding.

Al-Qawwamun: those who are thorough in their guardianship over women by teaching and disciplining them and arranging their affairs. ﴿By what Allah has given one over the other﴾: it was said, by greater intellect; it was said, by greater religion and certainty; it was said, by greater strength in worship; it was said, by testimony, as Allah says: ﴿If there are not two men, then a man and two women﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah 2:282]. Al-Qurazi said: by business and trade. It was said: by jihad, as Allah says: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah 9:41], and He said to women: ﴿And stay in your houses﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab 33:33]. Al-Rabi' said: by Friday prayer and congregations. Al-Hasan said: by spending on them, as Allah says: ﴿and by what they spend from their wealth.﴾

Some of them said: A man may marry up to four wives, but a woman may not have more than one husband. It was said: divorce is in the hands of men, and women have no part of it. It was said: by the blood-money. It was said: by prophethood. It was said: by the caliphate and leadership.

Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash [.......] [illegible word in manuscript], from some of his shaykhs, traced it to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "A woman is destitute as long as she has no husband." It was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, even if she has wealth?" He said: "Even if she has wealth. ﴿Men are in charge of women.﴾" [307]

Sa'id [from Abu Sa'id al-Maqbari] [supplement from al-Tabari 5/86; the manuscript is damaged] from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best of women is one who, when you look at her, pleases you; when you command her, she obeys you; and when you are absent from her, she guards you in her property and herself." Then he (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Men are in charge of women.﴾ [Source: Kanz al-Ummal 16/282, no. 44477.] [308]

﴿So righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding in the husband's absence what Allah would have them guard.﴾ That is, guarding the absence of their husbands when they are away. It was also said: "He pleases them by what Allah has guarded," that is, by Allah's guarding of them. Abu Ja'far read with a fatha on the ha', and its meaning is: by a guarding from Allah in obedience. This is like the Prophet's (peace be upon him) saying: "Guard Allah, He will guard you." [Source: Musnad Ahmad 1/293.] And (ما) in both readings is verbal-masdariyyah [i.e., it forms a verbal noun with the following verb], like His saying: ﴿by what my Lord has forgiven me﴾ [Surah Ya-Sin 36:27], meaning: that my Lord forgave me.

﴿And those from whom you fear disobedience (nushuz)﴾, meaning their defiance, and its root is movement. ﴿Admonish them;﴾ if they desist, then ﴿leave them alone in bed﴾; and if not, then ﴿strike them﴾ lightly, without severity or disgrace. It was also said: turn your backs to them in bed. If they desist, [well]; otherwise ﴿strike them, a non-severe striking.﴾

Ibn Abi Layla, from Dawud ibn 'Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Hang the whip where the household can see it." [Source: Kanz al-Ummal 16/371, no. 44946.] [309]

Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from Asma' bint Abi Bakr, who said: "I was the fourth of four wives of al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, and when he became angry with one of us, he would strike her with the stick of a clothes rack until he broke it upon her."

﴿Then if they obey you, do not seek a way against them.﴾ That is, do not seek to find fault with them for sins. Ibn 'Uyaynah said: Do not burden them with love.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted and Grand.﴾ ﴿And if you fear a breach between the two, appoint an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family, who intend reconciliation; Allah will bring about harmony between them.﴾ That is, dispute between the spouses. ﴿Appoint an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family; they intend reconciliation (islah)⁠⁠—⁠the spouses, it was said, or the two arbiters—⁠Allah will bring about harmony between them, through reform and affection. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Acquainted.

It is narrated from 'Ubaydah al-Salmani that a man and a woman came to 'Ali (peace be upon him), each accompanied by a group of people. 'Ali said: "What is the matter with these two?" They said: "A breach has occurred between them." 'Ali said: ﴿Appoint an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family.﴾ So they appointed an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family. 'Ali said to the two arbiters: "Do you know what is upon you? If you see that they should be brought together, then bring them together; and if you see that they should be separated, then separate them." The woman said: "I am content with the Book of Allah, with whatever is upon me and for me." The man said: "As for separation, no." 'Ali said: "You lie, by Allah. You will not leave me until you acknowledge what she has acknowledged." [Source: al-Tabari 5/101.]

﴿And worship Allah;﴾ affirm the oneness of Allah and obey Him. The wise said: servitude is abandoning disobedience and constantly maintaining humility and submission. It was also said: servitude consists of four things: fulfilling covenants, observing limits, contentment with what exists, and patience over what is lost.

﴿And associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents⁠⁠—⁠kindness towards them, showing them tenderness.⁠⁠﴾ Ibn Jinni read (إحسانٌ) ["kindness"] in the nominative, meaning: kindness to them has become obligatory. ﴿And to relatives, orphans, the needy,⁠⁠—⁠﴾

It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah that a man complained to the Prophet (ﷺ) about the hardness of his heart. He said: "If you want your heart to soften, feed the needy and wipe the head of the orphan and feed him." [310] [Source: al-Jami' al-Saghir 1/407.]

﴿And the neighbor who is near⁠⁠—⁠﴾: the majority read it in the genitive, as a continuation of the previous statement. Ibn Abi 'Ablah read (والجارَ) and what follows it in the accusative. ﴿The neighbor who is near﴾ means a neighbor by kinship. ﴿And the neighbor who is distant (al-junub)﴾ means one who is far, with whom you have no kinship. Al-Dahhak said: he is a stranger from another people. Al-A'mash and al-Fadl read (وَالْجَارِ الْجَنْبِ) with a fatha on the jim and sukun on the nun; both are dialects. A man is called janb, junub, janib, ajnab, and ajnabi when he is not a relative. Their plural is ajanib. Al-A'sha said:

"I came to Huraythah as a visitor from a distance, but Huraythah was stingy with my gifts."

That is, from a distance without kinship. From this is derived "ijtanaba fulanun fulanan" (someone avoided someone), meaning he kept far from him. From this also the person in ritual impurity is called junub, because he is set apart from prayer and kept far from the mosque until he bathes. Nawf al-Bakali said: "The distant neighbor" is the disbeliever. ﴿And the companion by your side﴾ means the fellow traveler.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Abu Ja'far, 'Ikrimah and Qatadah said, from Sa'id ibn Ma'ruf ibn Rafi', from his father, from his grandfather: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Seek out a neighbor before a house, and a companion before a journey." [311] [Source: Kanz al-Ummal 15/388, no. 41495.]

Some said: "The distant neighbor" is the neighbor whose house is adjoining yours, so he is beside you. 'Ali, 'Abd Allah, Ibn Abi Layla and al-Nakha'i said: it is the woman who is with him beside him.

Ibn Zayd and Ibn Jurayj said: it is the one who stays with you and accompanies you, hoping for your kindness and gifts. Ibn 'Abbas said: "I am ashamed for a man to step on my carpet three times without any trace of my kindness being seen on him." Al-Muhallab said: "If a man comes to you in the morning and leaves in the evening, that is enough of a request and a reminder for himself."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The best companions before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are those best to their companion; the best neighbors before Allah are those best to their neighbor." [312] [Source: al-Jami' al-Saghir 1/617, no. 3998.]

'Uthman ibn 'Ata', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He is not a believer whose neighbor is not safe from his harms. Whoever closes his doors on his neighbor, fearing for his family and property, is not a believer." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of the neighbor?" He said: "If he calls you, answer him; if he is in need, help him; if he asks you for a loan, lend to him; if good comes to him, congratulate him; if he is ill, visit him; if calamity strikes him, console him; if he dies, attend his funeral. Do not raise your building above his to block the wind from him except with his permission. Do not harm him with the smell of your cooking pot, unless you give him some of it. If you buy fruit, send him some of it, and if you do not, bring it in secretly, and do not let your child carry it out in a way that provokes his child." [Source: al-Nihayah fi Gharib al-Hadith 4/12, s.v. q-t-r: "qatar" is the smell of a cooking pot.]

"Then the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) said: 'Neighbours are of three kinds: among them is one who has three rights, among them is one who has two rights, and among them is one who has one right. As for the one with three rights: it is the Muslim neighbour who is a relative, who has the right of Islam, the right of neighbourhood and the right of kinship. As for the one with two rights: it is the Muslim neighbour, who has the right of Islam and the right of the neighbour. As for the one with one right: it is the polytheist neighbour, who has the right of neighbourhood, even if he is a polytheist.'" [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 9/185, no. 25613, with variation; and Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/184.]] [313].

Abu Hisham al-Qattan, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) said: "Whoever harms his neighbour has harmed me, and whoever harms me has harmed Allah, and whoever wars against his neighbour has waged war against me, and whoever wars against me has waged war against Allah, Mighty and Majestic." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 9/56, no. 24927.]] [314].

﴿And the wayfarer, and what your right hands possess﴾: meaning the slaves (al-mamalik).

From Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) gave Abu Dharr a young slave, and said: "O Abu Dharr, feed him from what you eat, and clothe him from what you wear." He said: He had only one garment, so he cut it in two halves and went to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ). He said: "What is the matter with this garment of yours?" He replied: "The youth whom you gave me, you commanded me to feed him from what I eat and to clothe him from what I wear, and I had only this garment, so I shared it with him." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) said: "I advise you to free him." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) said: "What has your young man done?" He said: "I have no young man; I have freed him." He said: "May Allah reward you, O Abu Dharr." [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 4/237, with variation.]] [315].

Al-A'mash, from 'Atiq, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) said: "Sheep are a blessing, camels are a glory to their owners, and horses have goodness tied to their forelocks until the Day of Resurrection, and the slave is your brother, so if he is unable, help him." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/325, no. 35228, with slight variation.]]

And from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The last words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) were: Prayer, and fear Allah regarding what your right hands possess." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 8/6, no. 21625.]] [316].

﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is arrogant and boastful.﴾

﴿O you who believe, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly﴾, that is, with what is forbidden (ḥarām), namely usury (ribā), gambling (qimār), robbery by cutting off the road (qaṭʿ), seizure by force (ghaṣb), theft (sariqa), and betrayal (khiyāna).

Ibn ʿAbbās said: this refers to a man who buys a garment from another man and says, "If I am pleased, I take it; otherwise I return it and return a dirham with it."

Then He said: ﴿except that it be trade﴾, meaning, but if it is trade. This is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), since trade is not falsehood.

The people of Kufa read (tijāratan) in the accusative, and this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. The rest read it in the nominative, and this is the choice of Abū Ḥātim. Whoever reads it in the accusative takes it as the predicate of kāna, its implied meaning being: "except that the wealth be trade," as in the words of the poet:

"If he was a spearman among them and a wrestler..." [[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī: 3/179.]]

Whoever reads it in the nominative takes it to mean "except that a trade occurs," and in that case it has no predicate, as in the words of the poet:

"My she-camel is a ransom for the Banū Dhuhl ibn Shaybān, when there is a day of many stars and a grey-white sky..." [[Lisān al-ʿArab: 1/509.]]

Then He described the trade: ﴿by mutual consent among you﴾, each party being content with what is in the other's hand.

Most of the exegetes said: it means that each of the two contracting parties gives the other the option after the sale is concluded, until they separate from the meeting place where they made the contract. As the Prophet ﷺ said: "The two parties to a sale have the option (to cancel) as long as they have not separated." [[Musnad Aḥmad: 4/402.]] [290]

He ﷺ also said: "Sale by mutual consent carries an option after the transaction, and it is not lawful for a Muslim to deceive a Muslim." [[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī: 5/45; Tafsir Ibn Kathīr: 1/491.]] [291]

Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The two parties to a sale have the option as long as they have not separated. If they are truthful and clarify (the defects), their sale is blessed for them; but if they conceal and lie, the blessing of their sale is erased." [[Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī: 3/18; Musnad Aḥmad: 3/402.]] [292]

ʿUmar ibn Jarīr bought a horse, then gave his counterparty the option after the sale, and then said: "I heard Abū Hurayra say: 'This is a sale by mutual consent.'"

﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾, meaning your brethren, that is, do not let some of you kill others.

Al-Thaʿlabī said: I heard Abū al-Qāsim al-Ḥabībī say: I heard my father, from my grandfather, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Hilālī, who said: I heard Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ash'ath say: Al-Faḍl ibn ʿIyāḍ was asked about the words of God: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾. He said: "Do not be heedless of the share of your souls (ḥaẓẓ anfusikum). Whoever is heedless of his own share has, as it were, killed it."

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you﴾.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr narrated from ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ that he said: When the Prophet sent him in the year of Dhāt al-Salāsil, he said: "I had a wet dream on a very cold night, and I feared that if I performed the ritual bath I would perish. So I performed tayammum and then led my companions in the dawn prayer. When we came back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I mentioned that to him, and he said: 'O ʿAmr, you led your companions in prayer while you were in a state of major impurity (junub)?'"

I said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah. I had a wet dream on a very cold night, and I feared that if I bathed I would perish, and I remembered the words of God: ﴿And do not kill yourselves; indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you﴾. So I performed tayammum and then prayed." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed and said nothing. [[Musnad Aḥmad: 4/203; al-Mustadrak: 1/177.]]

It is narrated from al-Ḥasan that al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd Allāh was alone with a group of his companions and said: "These people have plunged into their own blood. Let no one among you be prevented from Paradise by a handful of the blood of a Muslim that he has spilled, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'A man from among those before you had a sore on his hand; he took a knife and cut his hand with it until he severed it, and its blood did not stop until he died. Your Lord, may He be exalted, said: "My servant hastened to take his own life, so I have forbidden Paradise to him."'" [[Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim: 1/75.]] [294]

Simāk narrated from Jābir ibn Samura that a man slaughtered himself, and the Prophet ﷺ did not pray over him.

Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated from ʿĀṣim al-Asadī: it is mentioned that Masrūq ibn al-Ajdaʿ came to Ṣiffīn, stood between the two lines, and said: "O people, be silent!" Then he said: "Tell me, if a herald called to you from the sky, and you heard his speech and saw him, saying: 'Allah forbids you from what you are engaged in, would you obey Him?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'By God, that would indeed have been revealed to Muḥammad by Gabriel, and he continued to come with this (prohibition).'" Then he recited: ﴿O you who believe, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly﴾ to the end of the verse, then he slipped away into the crowd and departed. [[Fully in al-Ṭabaqāt al-Kubrā: 6/78.]]

﴿And whoever does that out of transgression and injustice, We will drive him into the Fire, and that is ever easy for Allah﴾, meaning: We will make him enter the Fire in the Hereafter, and that is easy and simple for Allah.

﴿If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾, the verse.

The scholars differed concerning the major sins whose avoidance Allah made an expiation for minor sins.

ʿAmr ibn Sharḥabīl narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?" He said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you." I said: "Then what?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbor's wife." [[Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī: 7/75; Musnad Aḥmad: 1/380.]] [295] This hadith is from the words of God: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾ [[Sūrat al-Furqān: 68.]], the verse.

Ṣāliḥ ibn Ḥayyān narrated from Abū Burayda, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The greatest of the major sins are associating partners with Allah, disobedience to parents, and withholding surplus water after one has had enough." [[Tafsir Ibn Kathīr: 1/497.]]

Al-Shaʿbī narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The major sins are associating partners with Allah, the perjury that plunges one into the Fire (al-yamīn al-ghamūs), disobedience to parents, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden, and false speech, or he said: false testimony." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhī: 4/303, no. 5009.]] [296]

Sufyān narrated from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr who said: Among the major sins is that a man curses his parents. They said: "How does a man curse his parents?" He said: "He insults the father of a man, and so he insults his father, and insults his mother, and so he insults his mother."

Abū al-Ṭufayl narrated from Ibn Masʿūd who said: The major sins are four: associating partners with Allah, despairing of the mercy of Allah, despairing of the rest of Allah, and feeling secure from the plan of Allah.

ʿIkrima narrated from ʿAmmār, who said: Ṭaysala ibn ʿAlī al-Nahdī narrated to us: I asked Ibn ʿUmar about the major sins, and he said: "They are nine." I said: "What are they?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah, the Most High; killing a believer intentionally; disobedience to believing parents; consuming usury; consuming the wealth of orphans; slandering chaste women; fleeing from the battlefield; sorcery; and making lawful the carrion and the blood (that was) before you, living and dead." (The text is corrupted here as in the source.)

Ja'far al-Ṣādiq said: The major sins are three: abandoning your religion, altering your sunna, and fighting the people of your covenant (ṣafqa).

Farqad al-Masīḥī said: I read in the Torah: "The mother sins are three: the first sin by which one disobeys God is pride, and that was for Iblīs, may he be cursed; and greed, and that was for Ādam (peace be upon him); and envy, and that was for Qābīl when he killed Hābīl."

ʿUmar ibn Abī Salama narrated from his father, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The major sins are, first among them: associating partners with Allah; killing a soul without right; consuming usury; consuming the wealth of an orphan out of haste before he grows up; fleeing from the battlefield; accusing a chaste woman; and reverting to the desert (after emigration) as an apostate. These are seven." [[Zād al-Masīr: 2/114.]] [297]

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that a man asked him about the seven major sins. He said: "They are closer to seven hundred than to seven, except that there is no major sin with seeking forgiveness, and no minor sin with persistence."

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa al-Wālibī narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: The major sins are twenty: associating partners with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; disobedience to parents; killing a believer; despairing of the mercy of Allah; feeling secure from the plan of Allah; despairing of the rest of Allah; sorcery; adultery; usury; theft; consuming the wealth of orphans; abandoning prayer; withholding zakāt; false testimony; killing a child for fear that it will eat with you; envy; pride; slander; greed; injustice in bequest; and belittling Muslims.

Al-Suddī narrated from Ibn Mālik who said: The major sins were mentioned in the presence of ʿAbd Allāh, and ʿAbd Allāh said: "Open Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: everything Allah has forbidden, up to thirty-three verses, is a major sin." Then he said: "The confirmation of this is: ﴿If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden...﴾, the verse."

Ibn Sīrīn said: The major sins were mentioned in the presence of Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: "Everything Allah has forbidden is a major sin, even a glance (al-ṭarfa), which is a look."

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from him: Every act in which one disobeys Allah is a major sin. Whoever commits any of them should seek forgiveness, for Allah does not keep in the Fire, from this community, anyone except one who has turned away from Islam, or denies an obligation, or denies predestination.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from him: Every sin which Allah concluded with a fire, or wrath, or a curse, or a punishment.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: Every sin which Allah attributed to the Fire and threatened with the Fire is a major sin.

al-Ḥasan: those that necessitate the prescribed punishments (ḥudūd).

al-Ḍaḥḥāk: whatever Allah has promised a prescribed punishment for in this world and a punishment in the Hereafter.

al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl: whatever Allah called in His Book "great" or "mighty," like His saying: ﴿Indeed, it was a great sin﴾ [[Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 2.]], ﴿Indeed, their killing was a great sin﴾ [[Sūrat al-Isrāʾ: 31.]], ﴿Indeed, association is a great injustice﴾ [[Sūrat Luqmān: 13.]], ﴿Indeed, your plotting is great﴾ [[Sūrat Yūsuf: 28.]], ﴿Glory be to You, this is a great slander﴾ [[Sūrat al-Nūr: 16.]], ﴿Indeed, that was with Allah a great (matter)﴾ [[Sūrat al-Aḥzāb: 53.]].

Mālik ibn Miʿwal said: The major sins are the sins of the people of innovation (ahl al-bidaʿ), and the misdeeds are the sins of the people of blemish (al-shīna).

Wakīʿ said: Every sin which a servant persists in is a major sin, and what a servant repents of and seeks forgiveness for is not among the major sins.

Aḥmad ibn ʿĀṣim al-Anṭākī said: The major sins are the sins committed deliberately; the misdeeds are errors, forgetfulness, compulsion, the promptings of the soul, and what is raised (forgiven) from this community.

Sufyān al-Thawrī said: The major sins are those involving wrongs between you and the servants, and the minor sins are those between you and Allah, the Most High, because Allah is Generous and forgives them. He argued by the words of the Prophet ﷺ: "On the Day of Resurrection a herald will call from the depths of the Throne: 'O community of Muḥammad, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: As for what was due to Me from you, I have forgiven it. But the dues between people remain, so grant them to one another and enter Paradise by My mercy.'" [[ʿUddat al-Dāʿī: 136.]] [298]

al-Maḥāribī said: The major sins are the sins of those who sin and make them lawful, like the sin of Iblīs; and the minor sins are the sins of those who seek forgiveness, like the sin of Ādam.

al-Suddī said: The major sins are what Allah has forbidden of great sins, and the misdeeds are their preliminaries, and their consequences are what the righteous and the wicked both share, such as the glance, the touch, the kiss, and similar things.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "The two eyes commit adultery, the two hands commit adultery, and the private part makes it true or false." [[Musnad Abī Yaʿlā: 11/309.]] [299]

Some people said: The major sin is what is repugnant to reason and nature, such as killing, injustice, adultery, lying, and the like; and the minor sin is what Allah has forbidden by revealed law and by hearing.

He also said: Every sin for which Allah overlooks by His grace on the Day of Resurrection is a minor sin, and every sin for which He punishes by His justice is a major sin. It was said: the major sins are the hidden sins, and the misdeeds are the open sins.

Some of them said: The minor sins are what people consider trivial, and the major sins are what they regard as grave, so they fear its occurrence.

Anas ibn Mālik said: You perform deeds which in your eyes are finer than a hair; we used to count them as major sins during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Some of them said: The major sins are associating partners with Allah and what leads to it; and what is below association is among the misdeeds. Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [[Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 48.]].

Section detailing the views of the people of interpretation on the number of major sins, gathered from the Book and the Sunna, accompanied by evidence and proof:

First: associating partners with Allah, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise﴾ [[Sūrat al-Māʾida: 72.]].

Second: despairing of the rest of Allah, based on His saying: ﴿And do not despair of the rest of Allah﴾ [[Sūrat Yūsuf: 87.]], the verse.

Third: despairing of the mercy of Allah, based on His saying: ﴿And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except the astray?﴾ [[Sūrat al-Ḥijr: 56.]]

Fourth: feeling secure from the plan of Allah, based on His saying: ﴿So none feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people﴾.

Fifth: disobedience to parents, based on His saying: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment﴾ [[Sūrat al-Isrāʾ: 23.]].

Sixth: killing a soul which Allah has forbidden, based on His saying: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell﴾ [[Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 93.]].

Seventh: slandering a chaste woman, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women﴾ [[Sūrat al-Nūr: 23.]], the verse.

Eighth: fleeing from the battlefield, based on His saying: ﴿O you who believe, when you meet those who disbelieve advancing (in battle)﴾ [[Sūrat al-Anfāl: 15.]], the verse.

Ninth: consuming usury, based on His saying: ﴿Those who consume usury﴾ [[Sūrat al-Baqara: 275.]], the verse.

Tenth: sorcery, based on His saying: ﴿And they had certainly known that whoever purchased it﴾ [[Sūrat al-Baqara: 102.]], the verse.

Eleventh: adultery: ﴿And they do not commit adultery; and whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾ [[Sūrat al-Furqān: 68.]].

Twelfth: false oath, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price﴾ [[Sūrat Āl ʿImrān: 77.]].

Thirteenth: withholding zakāt, based on His saying: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾ [[Sūrat al-Tawba: 34.]], the two verses.

Fourteenth: embezzlement (ghulūl), based on His saying: ﴿And whoever embezzles will bring what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [[Sūrat Āl ʿImrān: 161.]].

Fifteenth: false testimony, based on His saying: ﴿And do not conceal testimony﴾ [[Sūrat al-Baqara: 283.]], the verse.

Sixteenth: gambling (maysir), which is qimār, based on His saying: ﴿Gambling and idols and divining arrows﴾ [[Sūrat al-Māʾida: 90.]].

Seventeenth: drinking wine, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, wine and gambling﴾ [[Sūrat al-Māʾida: 90.]], the verse.

Eighteenth: deliberately abandoning prayer, based on His saying: ﴿Guard the prayers﴾ [[Sūrat al-Baqara: 238.]], the verse.

Nineteenth: severing family ties, based on His saying: ﴿And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs﴾ [[Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 1.]], and His saying: ﴿And sever your ties of kinship? Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed﴾ [[Sūrat Muḥammad: 22.]].

Twentieth: injustice in bequest, based on His saying: ﴿But whoever fears from a testator injustice or sin﴾ [[Sūrat al-Baqara: 182.]], the verse.

Twenty-first: consuming the wealth of orphans, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly﴾ [[Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 10.]], the verse.

Twenty-second: reverting to the desert (taʿarrub) after emigration, based on His saying: ﴿And whoever turns back on his heels, he will not harm Allah at all﴾ [[Sūrat Āl ʿImrān: 144.]].

Twenty-third: making lawful the sacred (ḥurum), based on His saying: ﴿Do not violate the rites of Allah﴾ [[Sūrat al-Māʾida: 2.]], and His saying: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation by wrongdoing﴾ [[Sūrat al-Ḥajj: 25.]].

Twenty-fourth: apostasy, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who turned back on their heels after guidance had become clear﴾ [[Sūrat Muḥammad: 25.]], the verse.

Twenty-fifth: breaking the covenant, based on His saying: ﴿And those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification﴾ [[Sūrat al-Raʿd: 25.]].

That is His saying: ﴿If you avoid the major sins﴾.

Ibn Masʿūd recited: "kabar mā tunhawna ʿanhu" in the singular, and in it is the meaning of the plural.

﴿We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾: from one prayer to the next, from one Friday to the next, from Ramaḍān to Ramaḍān, and from Ḥajj to Ḥajj, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "The five prayers are expiations for what is between them, so long as major sins are avoided." [[Musnad Ibn al-Jaʿd: 84; Musnad Ibn Yaʿlā: 39 (with slight variation).]] [300]

﴿And We will admit you to a noble entrance﴾, and it is Paradise.

ʿĀṣim and the people of Madina read (mudkhalan) with a fatḥa on the mīm, meaning the place of entering. The rest read it with a ḍamma, as a verbal noun, meaning the act of entering.

It is narrated from Abū Hurayra and from Abū Saʿīd that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat on the pulpit and then said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul," three times, then fell silent. Then every man among us came forward weeping from sorrow at the oath of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and then he said:

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 4, verses 29–36 (part 2 of 3)**

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No servant performs the five prayers, fasts Ramadan, and avoids the major sins except that the gates of Paradise will be opened for him on the Day of Resurrection, until they nearly clatter." [301] Then he recited: ﴿If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden, We will remove from you your minor misdeeds﴾ [Source: al-Mustadrak 2/240; Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah 1/163.] ... the verse.

﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others...﴾ ... the verse.

It is said: The women's delegation came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, is not Allah the Lord of men and women, and are you not the Messenger of Allah to them all? Why then does Allah mention the men and not mention the women? We fear that there is no good in us and that Allah has no need of us." So Allah revealed this verse, and His saying: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and the Muslim women...﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab 33:35] ... the verse, and His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer...﴾ [Surah al-Nahl 16:97].

It is also said: When Allah made for the male a share equal to the portion of two females in inheritance, the women said: "We are more in need of having two shares and the men one share, because we are weak and they are stronger and more able to seek livelihood than we are." So Allah revealed this verse.

Mujahid said: Umm Salamah said: "O Messenger of Allah, the men go out to fight and we do not fight; we only have half the inheritance. Would that we were men, so that we could fight and attain what men attain." So this verse was revealed.

Qatadah and al-Suddi said: When His saying was revealed, ﴿For the male is the equal of the portion of two females﴾ [Surah al-Nisa 4:11], the men said: "We hope that the women will be given preference over us in the Hereafter for our good deeds, just as we have been given preference over them in inheritance, so our reward will be double the reward of the women." And the women said: "We hope that our burden in the Hereafter will be half of the men's burden, just as we have half their share in inheritance in this world." So Allah revealed: ﴿For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned﴾, meaning reward and punishment. Qatadah said this, and he also said: a man is recompensed tenfold for a good deed, and a woman is recompensed tenfold as well.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿For men is a share of what they have earned﴾ means inheritance, and for women is a share of it, ﴿for the male is the equal of the portion of two females.﴾ On this view, "earning" means acquiring and obtaining. Allah therefore forbade wishing in this manner, because it leads to the causes of envy.

Al-Dahhak said: It is not lawful for a Muslim to wish for another's wealth. Have you not heard those who said: ﴿Oh, would that we had like what Qarun was given﴾ [Surah al-Qasas 28:79], up to His saying: ﴿And those who had wished for his position the day before began to say...﴾ [Surah al-Qasas 28:82], when the earth swallowed up his house and wealth, and they said: ﴿Had Allah not been gracious to us, He would have swallowed us up﴾ [Surah al-Qasas 28:82].

Al-Kalbi said: A man should not wish for his brother's wealth, nor his wife, nor his servant, nor his mount. Rather, let him say: "O Allah, grant me the like of it." This is also how it is in the Torah, and this is His saying in the Qur'an: ﴿And ask Allah of His bounty﴾ [Surah al-Nisa 4:32].

Ibn Kathir, Khalaf and al-Kisa'i read (وسلوا الله) ["and ask Allah"], and (سل) and (فسل) without the hamzah, transferring the vowel of the hamzah to the sin. The rest read with the hamzah.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ask Allah of His bounty, for He loves to be asked, and indeed among the best acts of worship is waiting for relief." [Source: al-Tabari 5/68; al-Qurtubi 5/164.]

Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), said: "Whoever does not ask Allah, Mighty and Majestic, of His bounty, He will be angry with him." [302]

Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, said: "Ask your Lord to the point of satisfaction. Whoever Allah does not make easy, will not find it easy."

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: "He only commanded asking so that He might give."

﴿And for each We have made heirs (mawali)﴾, meaning: for each one, from among men and women, there are heirs, that is, relatives who inherit ﴿from what the parents and close relatives leave behind﴾ from their inheritance. On this interpretation, the parents and close relatives are the ones who are inherited from. It is also said that the meaning is: "For each We have made heirs," that is, relatives of those who left [the estate]. Then He explained the heirs, saying: ﴿the parents and close relatives,﴾ meaning they are the parents and close relatives, a predicate of an omitted subject, so the meaning is: from the estate of the parents and close relatives. On this view, they are the ones who inherit.

﴿And those with whom your oaths have bound you﴾ is in the place of the nominative, as the subject of a sentence. Al-mu'aqadah is mutual pledging between two parties.

The people of Kufa read (ʿaqadat) lightly, without an alif, meaning "they bound for them." Umm Sa'd bint Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' read (ʿaqqadat) with emphasis, meaning "she confirmed and affirmed it." The word "oaths" (aymān) is the plural of yamin, which means the right hand and also the oath. They used to strike the handshake of allegiance with their right hands, so one would take the hand of another as a pledge of fidelity and adherence to the covenant, and they would swear allegiance on it. That is why the oaths are mentioned.

Qatadah and others said: By "those with whom your oaths have bound you" he meant the allies. In the Jahiliyyah, a man would bind himself to another and say: "My blood is your blood, my destruction is your destruction, my vengeance is your vengeance, my war is your war, my peace is your peace; you inherit from me, and I inherit from you; you seek my vengeance and I seek yours; you pay blood-money on my behalf and I pay on yours." Then the ally would receive a sixth of the ally's inheritance. Abu Bakr made such a pact with a client of his and inherited from him on that basis. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿then give them their share﴾, that is, give them their portion of the inheritance. Then this was abrogated (naskh) by His saying: ﴿And blood relatives are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah﴾ [Surah al-Anfal 8:75].

Ibrahim and Mujahid said: He meant ﴿give them their share﴾ of support, assistance and aid, but not inheritance. On this view, the verse is not abrogated, because of His saying: ﴿Fulfill the contracts﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah 5:1], and because of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "Fulfill to allies their covenants which your oaths have bound you to." [303]

And because of his (peace be upon him) statement in his sermon on the day of the conquest of Makkah: "Whatever alliance existed in the Jahiliyyah, hold to it, for Islam has only increased it in strength. Do not create new alliances in Islam." [304] [Source: Musnad Ahmad 5/61; Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3/73, no. 1634.]

'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I witnessed the Alliance of the Perfumed Ones [Hilf al-Mutayyibin] when I was a boy with my paternal uncles, and I would not like to have red camels in exchange for it, and I would still uphold it." [305] [Source: Musnad Ahmad 1/190.]

Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd said: This verse was revealed concerning those whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made brothers, among the Muhajirun and the Ansar, when they came to Madinah. They used to inherit from one another by that brotherhood, and then Allah abrogated that by the obligatory shares.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: It was revealed concerning those who used to adopt the sons of others in the Jahiliyyah, among them Zayd, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). In Islam they were commanded to make a bequest to them at death, and inheritance was returned to blood relatives. Allah refused to make the claimed heirs inherit from those who claimed and adopted them, but He made for them a share through a bequest. This is His saying: ﴿then give them their share.﴾

﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things a witness.﴾

Abu Rawq said: His saying ﴿And for each We have made heirs...﴾ was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and his son 'Abd al-Rahman, who was a disbeliever, that he would not benefit from or inherit any of his wealth. When 'Abd al-Rahman became Muslim, [Abu Bakr] was commanded to give him his share of the wealth.

﴿Men are in charge (qawwamun) of women...﴾ ... the verse.

Muqatil said: This verse was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' ibn 'Amr, one of the nuqaba' [chiefs], and his wife Habibah bint Zayd ibn Abi Zuhayr, both from the Ansar. She became disobedient (nushuz) to him, and he struck her. Her father went with her to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I gave her my noble daughter in marriage, and he struck her." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Let her retaliate against her husband." So she set off with her father to take retaliation (qisas) from him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Let them return; this is Jibril." Then this verse was revealed. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We intended a matter, and Allah intended a matter, and what Allah intended is better." [306] [Source: al-Qurtubi 5/168, with variations.] And the retaliation was lifted.

Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning As'ad ibn al-Rabi' and his wife, the daughter of Muhammad ibn Maslamah.

Abu Rawq mentioned something similar: It was revealed concerning Jamilah bint 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy and her husband Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, because she became disobedient to him and he struck her. She came to the Prophet (ﷺ) seeking redress, and Allah revealed this verse: ﴿Men are in charge of women﴾, that is, they have authority over disciplining women, ﴿by what Allah has given one over the other.﴾ Therefore there is no retaliation between a man and his wife for injuries less than death. If a man wounds his wife or injures her, he is not liable to retaliation (qawd), but he owes blood-money ('aql), except if he kills her, in which case he is killed for her. This was said by al-Zuhri and a group of scholars. Some of them said: There is no retaliation between husband and wife except in cases of death and wounding.

Al-Qawwamun: those who are thorough in their guardianship over women by teaching and disciplining them and arranging their affairs. ﴿By what Allah has given one over the other﴾: it was said, by greater intellect; it was said, by greater religion and certainty; it was said, by greater strength in worship; it was said, by testimony, as Allah says: ﴿If there are not two men, then a man and two women﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah 2:282]. Al-Qurazi said: by business and trade. It was said: by jihad, as Allah says: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah 9:41], and He said to women: ﴿And stay in your houses﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab 33:33]. Al-Rabi' said: by Friday prayer and congregations. Al-Hasan said: by spending on them, as Allah says: ﴿and by what they spend from their wealth.﴾
