When 'Abd al-Rahman became Muslim, [Abu Bakr] was commanded to give him his share of the wealth.

﴿Men are in charge (qawwamun) of women...﴾ ... the verse.

Muqatil said: This verse was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' ibn 'Amr, one of the nuqaba' [chiefs], and his wife Habibah bint Zayd ibn Abi Zuhayr, both from the Ansar. She became disobedient (nushuz) to him, and he struck her. Her father went with her to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I gave her my noble daughter in marriage, and he struck her." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Let her retaliate against her husband." So she set off with her father to take retaliation (qisas) from him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Let them return; this is Jibril." Then this verse was revealed. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We intended a matter, and Allah intended a matter, and what Allah intended is better." [306] [Source: al-Qurtubi 5/168, with variations.] And the retaliation was lifted.

Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning As'ad ibn al-Rabi' and his wife, the daughter of Muhammad ibn Maslamah.

Abu Rawq mentioned something similar: It was revealed concerning Jamilah bint 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy and her husband Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, because she became disobedient to him and he struck her. She came to the Prophet (ﷺ) seeking redress, and Allah revealed this verse: ﴿Men are in charge of women﴾, that is, they have authority over disciplining women, ﴿by what Allah has given one over the other.﴾ Therefore there is no retaliation between a man and his wife for injuries less than death. If a man wounds his wife or injures her, he is not liable to retaliation (qawd), but he owes blood-money ('aql), except if he kills her, in which case he is killed for her. This was said by al-Zuhri and a group of scholars. Some of them said: There is no retaliation between husband and wife except in cases of death and wounding.

Al-Qawwamun: those who are thorough in their guardianship over women by teaching and disciplining them and arranging their affairs. ﴿By what Allah has given one over the other﴾: it was said, by greater intellect; it was said, by greater religion and certainty; it was said, by greater strength in worship; it was said, by testimony, as Allah says: ﴿If there are not two men, then a man and two women﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah 2:282]. Al-Qurazi said: by business and trade. It was said: by jihad, as Allah says: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah 9:41], and He said to women: ﴿And stay in your houses﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab 33:33]. Al-Rabi' said: by Friday prayer and congregations. Al-Hasan said: by spending on them, as Allah says: ﴿and by what they spend from their wealth.﴾

Some of them said: A man may marry up to four wives, but a woman may not have more than one husband. It was said: divorce is in the hands of men, and women have no part of it. It was said: by the blood-money. It was said: by prophethood. It was said: by the caliphate and leadership.

Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash [.......] [illegible word in manuscript], from some of his shaykhs, traced it to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "A woman is destitute as long as she has no husband." It was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, even if she has wealth?" He said: "Even if she has wealth. ﴿Men are in charge of women.﴾" [307]

Sa'id [from Abu Sa'id al-Maqbari] [supplement from al-Tabari 5/86; the manuscript is damaged] from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best of women is one who, when you look at her, pleases you; when you command her, she obeys you; and when you are absent from her, she guards you in her property and herself." Then he (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Men are in charge of women.﴾ [Source: Kanz al-Ummal 16/282, no. 44477.] [308]

﴿So righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding in the husband's absence what Allah would have them guard.﴾ That is, guarding the absence of their husbands when they are away. It was also said: "He pleases them by what Allah has guarded," that is, by Allah's guarding of them. Abu Ja'far read with a fatha on the ha', and its meaning is: by a guarding from Allah in obedience. This is like the Prophet's (peace be upon him) saying: "Guard Allah, He will guard you." [Source: Musnad Ahmad 1/293.] And (ما) in both readings is verbal-masdariyyah [i.e., it forms a verbal noun with the following verb], like His saying: ﴿by what my Lord has forgiven me﴾ [Surah Ya-Sin 36:27], meaning: that my Lord forgave me.

﴿And those from whom you fear disobedience (nushuz)﴾, meaning their defiance, and its root is movement. ﴿Admonish them;﴾ if they desist, then ﴿leave them alone in bed﴾; and if not, then ﴿strike them﴾ lightly, without severity or disgrace. It was also said: turn your backs to them in bed. If they desist, [well]; otherwise ﴿strike them, a non-severe striking.﴾

Ibn Abi Layla, from Dawud ibn 'Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Hang the whip where the household can see it." [Source: Kanz al-Ummal 16/371, no. 44946.] [309]

Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from Asma' bint Abi Bakr, who said: "I was the fourth of four wives of al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, and when he became angry with one of us, he would strike her with the stick of a clothes rack until he broke it upon her."

﴿Then if they obey you, do not seek a way against them.﴾ That is, do not seek to find fault with them for sins. Ibn 'Uyaynah said: Do not burden them with love.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted and Grand.﴾ ﴿And if you fear a breach between the two, appoint an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family, who intend reconciliation; Allah will bring about harmony between them.﴾ That is, dispute between the spouses. ﴿Appoint an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family; they intend reconciliation (islah)⁠⁠—⁠the spouses, it was said, or the two arbiters—⁠Allah will bring about harmony between them, through reform and affection. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Acquainted.

It is narrated from 'Ubaydah al-Salmani that a man and a woman came to 'Ali (peace be upon him), each accompanied by a group of people. 'Ali said: "What is the matter with these two?" They said: "A breach has occurred between them." 'Ali said: ﴿Appoint an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family.﴾ So they appointed an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family. 'Ali said to the two arbiters: "Do you know what is upon you? If you see that they should be brought together, then bring them together; and if you see that they should be separated, then separate them." The woman said: "I am content with the Book of Allah, with whatever is upon me and for me." The man said: "As for separation, no." 'Ali said: "You lie, by Allah. You will not leave me until you acknowledge what she has acknowledged." [Source: al-Tabari 5/101.]

﴿And worship Allah;﴾ affirm the oneness of Allah and obey Him. The wise said: servitude is abandoning disobedience and constantly maintaining humility and submission. It was also said: servitude consists of four things: fulfilling covenants, observing limits, contentment with what exists, and patience over what is lost.

﴿And associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents⁠⁠—⁠kindness towards them, showing them tenderness.⁠⁠﴾ Ibn Jinni read (إحسانٌ) ["kindness"] in the nominative, meaning: kindness to them has become obligatory. ﴿And to relatives, orphans, the needy,⁠⁠—⁠﴾

It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah that a man complained to the Prophet (ﷺ) about the hardness of his heart. He said: "If you want your heart to soften, feed the needy and wipe the head of the orphan and feed him." [310] [Source: al-Jami' al-Saghir 1/407.]

﴿And the neighbor who is near⁠⁠—⁠﴾: the majority read it in the genitive, as a continuation of the previous statement. Ibn Abi 'Ablah read (والجارَ) and what follows it in the accusative. ﴿The neighbor who is near﴾ means a neighbor by kinship. ﴿And the neighbor who is distant (al-junub)﴾ means one who is far, with whom you have no kinship. Al-Dahhak said: he is a stranger from another people. Al-A'mash and al-Fadl read (وَالْجَارِ الْجَنْبِ) with a fatha on the jim and sukun on the nun; both are dialects. A man is called janb, junub, janib, ajnab, and ajnabi when he is not a relative. Their plural is ajanib. Al-A'sha said:

"I came to Huraythah as a visitor from a distance, but Huraythah was stingy with my gifts."

That is, from a distance without kinship. From this is derived "ijtanaba fulanun fulanan" (someone avoided someone), meaning he kept far from him. From this also the person in ritual impurity is called junub, because he is set apart from prayer and kept far from the mosque until he bathes. Nawf al-Bakali said: "The distant neighbor" is the disbeliever. ﴿And the companion by your side﴾ means the fellow traveler.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Abu Ja'far, 'Ikrimah and Qatadah said, from Sa'id ibn Ma'ruf ibn Rafi', from his father, from his grandfather: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Seek out a neighbor before a house, and a companion before a journey." [311] [Source: Kanz al-Ummal 15/388, no. 41495.]

Some said: "The distant neighbor" is the neighbor whose house is adjoining yours, so he is beside you. 'Ali, 'Abd Allah, Ibn Abi Layla and al-Nakha'i said: it is the woman who is with him beside him.

Ibn Zayd and Ibn Jurayj said: it is the one who stays with you and accompanies you, hoping for your kindness and gifts. Ibn 'Abbas said: "I am ashamed for a man to step on my carpet three times without any trace of my kindness being seen on him." Al-Muhallab said: "If a man comes to you in the morning and leaves in the evening, that is enough of a request and a reminder for himself."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The best companions before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are those best to their companion; the best neighbors before Allah are those best to their neighbor." [312] [Source: al-Jami' al-Saghir 1/617, no. 3998.]

'Uthman ibn 'Ata', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He is not a believer whose neighbor is not safe from his harms. Whoever closes his doors on his neighbor, fearing for his family and property, is not a believer." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of the neighbor?" He said: "If he calls you, answer him; if he is in need, help him; if he asks you for a loan, lend to him; if good comes to him, congratulate him; if he is ill, visit him; if calamity strikes him, console him; if he dies, attend his funeral. Do not raise your building above his to block the wind from him except with his permission. Do not harm him with the smell of your cooking pot, unless you give him some of it. If you buy fruit, send him some of it, and if you do not, bring it in secretly, and do not let your child carry it out in a way that provokes his child." [Source: al-Nihayah fi Gharib al-Hadith 4/12, s.v. q-t-r: "qatar" is the smell of a cooking pot.]

"Then the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) said: 'Neighbours are of three kinds: among them is one who has three rights, among them is one who has two rights, and among them is one who has one right. As for the one with three rights: it is the Muslim neighbour who is a relative, who has the right of Islam, the right of neighbourhood and the right of kinship. As for the one with two rights: it is the Muslim neighbour, who has the right of Islam and the right of the neighbour. As for the one with one right: it is the polytheist neighbour, who has the right of neighbourhood, even if he is a polytheist.'" [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 9/185, no. 25613, with variation; and Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/184.]] [313].

Abu Hisham al-Qattan, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) said: "Whoever harms his neighbour has harmed me, and whoever harms me has harmed Allah, and whoever wars against his neighbour has waged war against me, and whoever wars against me has waged war against Allah, Mighty and Majestic." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 9/56, no. 24927.]] [314].

﴿And the wayfarer, and what your right hands possess﴾: meaning the slaves (al-mamalik).

From Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) gave Abu Dharr a young slave, and said: "O Abu Dharr, feed him from what you eat, and clothe him from what you wear." He said: He had only one garment, so he cut it in two halves and went to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ). He said: "What is the matter with this garment of yours?" He replied: "The youth whom you gave me, you commanded me to feed him from what I eat and to clothe him from what I wear, and I had only this garment, so I shared it with him." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) said: "I advise you to free him." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) said: "What has your young man done?" He said: "I have no young man; I have freed him." He said: "May Allah reward you, O Abu Dharr." [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 4/237, with variation.]] [315].

Al-A'mash, from 'Atiq, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) said: "Sheep are a blessing, camels are a glory to their owners, and horses have goodness tied to their forelocks until the Day of Resurrection, and the slave is your brother, so if he is unable, help him." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/325, no. 35228, with slight variation.]]

And from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The last words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) were: Prayer, and fear Allah regarding what your right hands possess." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 8/6, no. 21625.]] [316].

﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is arrogant and boastful.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 4, verses 37–42:

Alladhina (الَّذِينَ) is in the accusative position, as a substitute for "man" (مَنْ) in the verse ﴿Allah does not love anyone self-conceited and boastful﴾. It is also said that it refers to "the self-conceited and boastful" (al-mukhtal al-fakhur). ﴿Who are miserly﴾ (yabkhaluna). Bukhl (البخل, miserliness) in the usage of the Arabs means a man withholding from his petitioner what he has in surplus. In the sacred law (shar') it means withholding what is obligatory. There are four dialectal forms (lughat) of the word:

- Bakhl (البخل), with a fatha on the ba and the kha. This is the reading of Anas ibn Malik, Ubayd ibn Umayr, Yahya ibn Ya'mur, Mujahid, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf and al-Mufaddal, and it is the dialect of the Ansar.
- Bakhl (بخل), with a fatha on the ba and a sukun on the kha. This is the reading of Qatada, Abdullah ibn Suraqa, and Ayyub al-Sijistani.
- Bukhl (بخل), with a damma on the ba and the kha. This is the reading of Isa ibn Amr.
- Bukhl (بخل), with a damma on the ba and a sukun on the kha. This is the reading of the rest of the readers, and it is the choice of Abu Ubayd and Abu Muslim, because it is the elevated (standard) dialect. The same pattern occurs in al-Hadid. All of them are dialects, and their parallel in ordinary speech is: "ard jurz, wa jurz, wa jurz" (a barren land).

The scholars differed concerning the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of this verse and its meaning. Most of them said: It was revealed concerning the Jews who concealed the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) and did not make it clear to the people, although they found it written in their Torah.

Yaman reported from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning ﴿who are miserly and enjoin miserliness upon people﴾: He said: "This is about knowledge; it has nothing to do with worldly wealth."

Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd said: It was revealed concerning Kurdam ibn Zayd, Usama ibn Habib, Nafi' ibn Abi Nafi', Yahya ibn Ya'mur, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, and Rifa'a ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut. They would come to men of the Ansar, mix with them and advise them, saying: "Do not spend your wealth, for we fear poverty for you, and we do not know what may happen." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿who are miserly﴾ up to His saying ﴿of His bounty﴾, meaning wealth.

Yaman said: It means they are miserly with charity (sadaqa).

Al-Fadl ibn Fudala reported, from Abu Raja', who said: Imran ibn Husayn came out to us wearing a mutarraf (a striped cloak) of silk (kharz) that we had not seen him wear before or after, and he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, bestows a blessing upon a servant, He loves to see the effect of His blessing upon him." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 18/135.] [317]

﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment. And those who spend...﴾ up to the end. The position of alladhina is accusative, as a conjunction (atf) upon His saying ﴿who are miserly﴾. If you wish, you may make it in the genitive position as a conjunction upon His saying ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers﴾. It was revealed concerning the Jews. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning the hypocrites. It is also said: It was revealed concerning the polytheists of Makkah who were united in enmity toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

﴿And whoever has Satan as a companion (qarin)﴾: a companion and close friend. It is of the pattern fa'il from iqtiran (association). 'Adi ibn Zayd said:

"Do not ask about the man, but ask about his companion,
For every companion is guided by the one he associates with."
[Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/123.]

﴿Evil is the companion﴾: "fa-sa'a qarinan" means "how evil is Satan as a companion." It is in the accusative as a tamyiz (specification). It is also said it is an accusative of state (hal), and it is also said it is an accusative of separation (qat'), with the alif and lam removed from it, as we say: "Ni'ma rajulan 'Abd Allah" (what a fine man is 'Abd Allah). Its meaning is: "Ni'ma al-rajul 'Abd Allah" (the fine man is 'Abd Allah). When the alif and lam are removed, it is put in the accusative, as in His saying ﴿how evil a substitute for the wrongdoers﴾ [Surah al-Kahf 18:50], ﴿how evil a parable﴾ [Surah al-A'raf 7:177], ﴿how evil a resting place﴾ [Surah al-Kahf 18:29], and ﴿how evil a settlement﴾, and ﴿how good are those as companions﴾ [Surah al-Nisa' 4:69], and ﴿how great is their hatred﴾ [Surah Ghafir 40:35; Surah al-Saff 61:2]. The commentators said: ﴿Evil is the companion﴾ means that he (the companion) will say: ﴿Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! How evil is the companion!﴾ [Surah al-Zukhruf 43:38].

﴿And what would it have been upon them, if they had believed in Allah and the Last Day and had spent from what Allah has provided them? And Allah is ever Knowing of them.﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight﴾ up to the end of the verse. ﴿And what would it have been upon them if they had believed in Allah and the Last Day, and had spent from what Allah has provided them?﴾ Indeed, Allah does not wrong, that is, does not diminish or reduce, anyone of His creation in the reward of his deed, even by an atom's weight, for example. Rather, He recompenses him with it and rewards him for it. This is an example: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight﴾, so how much more so would be more than it? The meaning of the statement is: He does not wrong even a little, because wronging the weight of an atom does not benefit the wrongdoer, and its harm to the wronged party is not evident. It is also said: [...] [A blur in the manuscript.] Its evidence from interpretation is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people at all﴾ [Surah Yunus 10:44], in this world.

They differed concerning the dharra (atom). Ibn Abbas said: It is the small red ant, which can barely be seen with the eye. Yazid ibn Harun said: It is claimed that the dharra has no weight. It is related that a man placed bread, and the dharra covered it, concealing it, yet it added nothing to the weight of the bread. The evidence for this interpretation is what Bishr ibn Amr reported from Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud), that he read: "Indeed, Allah does not wrong the weight of an ant (mithqal namla)."

Yazid ibn al-Asamm reported from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿an atom's weight﴾, that he said: Ibn Abbas put his hand into a vessel, then lifted it out, then blew upon it, and then said: "Each one of these is a dharra." Some of them said: The particles of dust (hab') in a window opening, each particle of it is a dharra. It is also said: It is the mustard seed (khardala).

In summary, it is an expression for the smallest and least of things.

Anas reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah does not wrong the believer a good deed for which he is rewarded with provision in this world and recompensed for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is fed with it in this world, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, he will have no good deed." [Musnad Abi Dawud al-Tayalisi: 269.] [318]

Qatada said: Some of the people of knowledge used to say: "If He were to make my good deeds exceed my bad deeds by the weight of an atom, that would be dearer to me than having the whole world."

Ata' ibn Yasar reported from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the believers are delivered from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection and are secure, then the dispute of any one of you with his companion over a right that he had in this world is not more severe than the dispute of the believers with their Lord concerning their brothers who were admitted into the Fire." He said: "They will say: 'Our Lord, our brothers used to pray with us, fast with us, and perform Hajj with us, yet You admitted them into the Fire?' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'Go and bring out whomever you recognize.' So they will come to them and recognize them by their forms. The Fire will not consume their forms. Some of them will be seized by the Fire up to the middle of their shins, and some up to their ankles. They will bring them out and say: 'Our Lord, we have brought out those whom You commanded us to.' Then He, Exalted, will say: 'Bring out whoever has in his heart the weight of a dinar of faith, then whoever has the weight of half a dinar,' until He says: 'Bring out whoever has in his heart the weight of an atom.'" [Musnad Ahmad: 3/94; Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/23.] [319]

Abu Sa'id said: "Whoever does not believe this, let him recite this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong...﴾"

He said: "They will say: 'Our Lord, we have brought out those whom You commanded us to, and no one remains in the Fire in whom there is any good.'" He said: "Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'The angels have interceded, the prophets have interceded, and the believers have interceded, and there remains the Most Merciful of the merciful.'" He said: "Then He will grasp a handful from the Fire, or he said: 'two handfuls,' of those who never did any good for Allah, Mighty and Majestic. They will have been burned until they became charcoal. He said: They will be brought to a water called the Water of Life, and it will be poured over them, and they will sprout just as a seed sprouts in the silt carried by a flood. They will come out, and their bodies [will be] like pearls, with seals upon their necks, (freed ones of Allah, Mighty and Majestic). It will be said to them: 'Enter Paradise. Whatever you wish for or see is yours, and it is better in My sight than this.'"

He said: "They will say: 'Our Lord, You have given us what You have not given anyone among the worlds!'" He said: "He will say: 'Indeed, I have something better than this for you.' They will say: 'Our Lord, and what is better than that?'" He said: "He will say: 'My good pleasure with you, so I will never be angry with you again.'" [Musnad Ahmad: 3/94.]

Others said: This is in a report from Ibn [...] [An illegible word.], from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will gather the first and the last. Then a caller from Allah will call out: "Whoever had a grievance against his brother, let him take it now." He said: By Allah, a man will be glad that he has a right over his father, his child, his wife, or his brother, and he takes it from him, even if it is small. The evidence for this in the Book of Allah, the Exalted, is His saying: ﴿So when the Horn is blown, there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask of one another﴾ [Surah al-Mu'minun 23:101]. Then the servant will be brought, and a caller will call out upon the heads of the witnesses: "The first and the last! This is so-and-so, son of so-and-so, whoever had a right against him, let him come to his side." Then it will be said to him: "Give these people their rights." He will say: "From where? The world has gone!" Allah, Exalted, will say to His angels: "Look at his good deeds and give them from them." If an atom's weight of good deed remains, the angels will say: "Our Lord, You know this better than them. We have given every person with a right his right, and there remains for him an atom's weight of good deed." Then He will say to the angels: "Double it for My servant, and admit him into Paradise by My bounty." The evidence for this in the Book of Allah is: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight; and if it is a good deed, He will double it and give from Himself a great reward﴾.

But if the servant is wretched, the angels will say: "Our God, his good deeds have perished and his evil deeds remain, and there remain many claimants." He, Mighty and Majestic, will say: "Take from their evil deeds and add them to his evil deeds, then write him a document (sakk) to the Fire."

So the meaning of the verse according to this interpretation is: ﴿He does not wrong an atom's weight﴾ against an adversary in favor of an adversary, but He rewards him for it and doubles it for him. This is His saying: ﴿and if it is a good deed, He will double it﴾. The reading of the general body of readers is ḥasanatan (حَسَنَةً) in the accusative, meaning: "if it is the weight of an atom." The people of the Hijaz read it in the nominative, in the sense of "if a good deed occurs or exists." Al-Mubarrad said: Its meaning is: ﴿and if there is a good deed remaining, He will double it.﴾

Al-Hasan read nudha'if'uha (نضاعفها) with a nun, while the rest read it with a ya'. The latter is the correct reading, because of His saying: ﴿and gives from Himself﴾. Abu Raja' and the people of Madina read yudha'ifha (يضعّفها) with tashdid, while the rest read yudha'ifha. Both are dialects, and their meaning is multiplication. Abu Ubayda said: yudha'ifha (يُضاعِفْها) means to make it into many multiples, and yudha''ifha (يضعّفها) with tashdid means to make it double.

﴿And gives from Himself (min ladunhu)﴾: that is, from His presence. Al-Kisa'i said: For ladun (لدن) there are four dialects: ladun, ladaa, lada, and ladun. When they attached it to themselves, they doubled the nun.

﴿A great reward﴾: and that is Paradise.

Abu Uthman reported: It reached me from Abu Hurayra that he said: "Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gives His believing servant for a single good deed a thousand thousand good deeds." Abu Hurayra said: "No, rather I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Indeed, Allah gives him two thousand thousand good deeds.'" [Kanz al-Ummal: 6/352, no. 16019, with variation.] Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight﴾ up to ﴿a great reward﴾. [320]

He also said: "When Allah says 'a great reward,' who after that knows its measure?"

﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness﴾: that is, how will they act when We bring from every nation a witness of truth from among them, who will testify against them concerning what they did? ﴿And We bring you, O Muhammad, as a witness against these?﴾ A parallel to it is in al-Baqara [Surah al-Baqara 2:143: "...and that the Messenger may be a witness over you"], in al-Nahl [Surah al-Nahl 16:89: "And We have brought you as a witness over these"], and in al-Hajj [Surah al-Hajj 22:78: "that the Messenger may be a witness over you"].

Asim reported from Zirr, from Abdullah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: "Recite." So I recited Surah al-Nisa', until when I reached ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness﴾, the eyes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) overflowed with tears, and he said: "Enough (hasbuna)." [Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 5/28.] [321]

﴿On that Day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth would be leveled over them﴾: The people of Madina and Syria read it with a fatha on the ta' and a tashdid on the sin, meaning "tatasawwa" (تتسوّى), so the ta' was assimilated into the sin. The people of Kufa, except Asim, read it with a fatha on the ta' and a takhfif (lightening) on the sin, by deleting the ta' of tafa''ala, as in His saying: ﴿No soul will speak except by His permission﴾ [Surah Hud 11:105]. The rest read it with a damma on the ta' and a lightening on the sin, in the passive voice (majhul). They said: "Sawwayta bihim al-ard" (the earth was leveled with them), and they and the earth become one thing. Qatada and Ubayda said: It means: if the earth were to move, they would walk upon it and return to it as they came out of it, and then it would be leveled over them until it covers them. Ibn Kaysan said: They wish they had not been raised at all, and that they had only been taken from the dust, and the earth had been level with them. Al-Kalbi said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to the beasts, the wild animals, the birds, and the predators: "Be dust," so that the earth may be leveled with them. At that point, the disbelievers wish they were dust walking over them, the people of the gathering. Its explanation is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿The disbeliever will say: "Would that I were dust!"﴾ [Surah al-Naba' 78:40].

Al-Tha'labi said: Our teacher Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn related that he heard someone interpret this verse as: "Nothing on earth would be accepted from them as ransom (fidya)." Its evidence is His saying: ﴿The criminal would wish to ransom himself from the punishment of that Day by his children﴾ [Surah al-Ma'arij 70:11], up to the end of the verse.

﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement?﴾ Qatada said: "They wish the earth would be leveled over them, and they had not concealed the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ) or his description." Others said: Rather, it is a new (independent) sentence, meaning: "And they will not conceal from Allah any statement, because what they did is not hidden from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and they cannot conceal it." Al-Kalbi and a group said: ﴿They will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾, because the guardians of Hell will testify against them.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said: "Things in the Qur'an differ for me. Is it doubt about it?" He said: "No, but it is a difference in verses that seem contradictory to you." He said: "Explain it." Ibn Abbas said: "Listen: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Then their trial will be only that they will say: 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists'﴾ [Surah al-An'am 6:23], and He says: ﴿They will not conceal from Allah any statement,﴾ yet they have concealed." Ibn Abbas said: "As for their saying ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾, when they saw on the Day of Resurrection that Allah forgives the people of Islam, they said: 'Come, let us testify.' So the polytheists denied, saying: 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists,' hoping that He would forgive them. Then their mouths will be sealed, and their hands and feet will speak of what they used to do. At that point, ﴿On that Day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth would be leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah any statement.﴾"

Al-Hasan said: These are occasions (mawatin). In one occasion they do not speak, and no one hears except a whisper. In other occasions they speak and lie, saying: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ and ﴿we did no evil.﴾ In another occasion they confess against themselves, as in His, Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿So they confessed their sin﴾ [Surah al-Mulk 67:11]. In another place they ask for mercy. The last of those occasions is when their mouths are sealed and their limbs speak, and that is His saying, Exalted: ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah any statement.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 4, verses 37–42:

Alladhina (الَّذِينَ) is in the accusative position, as a substitute for "man" (مَنْ) in the verse ﴿Allah does not love anyone self-conceited and boastful﴾. It is also said that it refers to "the self-conceited and boastful" (al-mukhtal al-fakhur). ﴿Who are miserly﴾ (yabkhaluna). Bukhl (البخل, miserliness) in the usage of the Arabs means a man withholding from his petitioner what he has in surplus. In the sacred law (shar') it means withholding what is obligatory. There are four dialectal forms (lughat) of the word:

- Bakhl (البخل), with a fatha on the ba and the kha. This is the reading of Anas ibn Malik, Ubayd ibn Umayr, Yahya ibn Ya'mur, Mujahid, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf and al-Mufaddal, and it is the dialect of the Ansar.
- Bakhl (بخل), with a fatha on the ba and a sukun on the kha. This is the reading of Qatada, Abdullah ibn Suraqa, and Ayyub al-Sijistani.
- Bukhl (بخل), with a damma on the ba and the kha. This is the reading of Isa ibn Amr.
- Bukhl (بخل), with a damma on the ba and a sukun on the kha. This is the reading of the rest of the readers, and it is the choice of Abu Ubayd and Abu Muslim, because it is the elevated (standard) dialect. The same pattern occurs in al-Hadid. All of them are dialects, and their parallel in ordinary speech is: "ard jurz, wa jurz, wa jurz" (a barren land).

The scholars differed concerning the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of this verse and its meaning. Most of them said: It was revealed concerning the Jews who concealed the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) and did not make it clear to the people, although they found it written in their Torah.

Yaman reported from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning ﴿who are miserly and enjoin miserliness upon people﴾: He said: "This is about knowledge; it has nothing to do with worldly wealth."

Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd said: It was revealed concerning Kurdam ibn Zayd, Usama ibn Habib, Nafi' ibn Abi Nafi', Yahya ibn Ya'mur, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, and Rifa'a ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut. They would come to men of the Ansar, mix with them and advise them, saying: "Do not spend your wealth, for we fear poverty for you, and we do not know what may happen." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿who are miserly﴾ up to His saying ﴿of His bounty﴾, meaning wealth.

Yaman said: It means they are miserly with charity (sadaqa).

Al-Fadl ibn Fudala reported, from Abu Raja', who said: Imran ibn Husayn came out to us wearing a mutarraf (a striped cloak) of silk (kharz) that we had not seen him wear before or after, and he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, bestows a blessing upon a servant, He loves to see the effect of His blessing upon him." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 18/135.] [317]

﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment. And those who spend...﴾ up to the end. The position of alladhina is accusative, as a conjunction (atf) upon His saying ﴿who are miserly﴾. If you wish, you may make it in the genitive position as a conjunction upon His saying ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers﴾. It was revealed concerning the Jews. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning the hypocrites. It is also said: It was revealed concerning the polytheists of Makkah who were united in enmity toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

﴿And whoever has Satan as a companion (qarin)﴾: a companion and close friend. It is of the pattern fa'il from iqtiran (association). 'Adi ibn Zayd said:

"Do not ask about the man, but ask about his companion,
For every companion is guided by the one he associates with."
[Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/123.]

﴿Evil is the companion﴾: "fa-sa'a qarinan" means "how evil is Satan as a companion." It is in the accusative as a tamyiz (specification). It is also said it is an accusative of state (hal), and it is also said it is an accusative of separation (qat'), with the alif and lam removed from it, as we say: "Ni'ma rajulan 'Abd Allah" (what a fine man is 'Abd Allah). Its meaning is: "Ni'ma al-rajul 'Abd Allah" (the fine man is 'Abd Allah). When the alif and lam are removed, it is put in the accusative, as in His saying ﴿how evil a substitute for the wrongdoers﴾ [Surah al-Kahf 18:50], ﴿how evil a parable﴾ [Surah al-A'raf 7:177], ﴿how evil a resting place﴾ [Surah al-Kahf 18:29], and ﴿how evil a settlement﴾, and ﴿how good are those as companions﴾ [Surah al-Nisa' 4:69], and ﴿how great is their hatred﴾ [Surah Ghafir 40:35; Surah al-Saff 61:2]. The commentators said: ﴿Evil is the companion﴾ means that he (the companion) will say: ﴿Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! How evil is the companion!﴾ [Surah al-Zukhruf 43:38].

﴿And what would it have been upon them, if they had believed in Allah and the Last Day and had spent from what Allah has provided them? And Allah is ever Knowing of them.﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight﴾ up to the end of the verse. ﴿And what would it have been upon them if they had believed in Allah and the Last Day, and had spent from what Allah has provided them?﴾ Indeed, Allah does not wrong, that is, does not diminish or reduce, anyone of His creation in the reward of his deed, even by an atom's weight, for example. Rather, He recompenses him with it and rewards him for it. This is an example: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight﴾, so how much more so would be more than it? The meaning of the statement is: He does not wrong even a little, because wronging the weight of an atom does not benefit the wrongdoer, and its harm to the wronged party is not evident. It is also said: [...] [A blur in the manuscript.] Its evidence from interpretation is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people at all﴾ [Surah Yunus 10:44], in this world.

They differed concerning the dharra (atom). Ibn Abbas said: It is the small red ant, which can barely be seen with the eye. Yazid ibn Harun said: It is claimed that the dharra has no weight. It is related that a man placed bread, and the dharra covered it, concealing it, yet it added nothing to the weight of the bread. The evidence for this interpretation is what Bishr ibn Amr reported from Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud), that he read: "Indeed, Allah does not wrong the weight of an ant (mithqal namla)."

Yazid ibn al-Asamm reported from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿an atom's weight﴾, that he said: Ibn Abbas put his hand into a vessel, then lifted it out, then blew upon it, and then said: "Each one of these is a dharra." Some of them said: The particles of dust (hab') in a window opening, each particle of it is a dharra. It is also said: It is the mustard seed (khardala).

In summary, it is an expression for the smallest and least of things.

Anas reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah does not wrong the believer a good deed for which he is rewarded with provision in this world and recompensed for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is fed with it in this world, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, he will have no good deed." [Musnad Abi Dawud al-Tayalisi: 269.] [318]

Qatada said: Some of the people of knowledge used to say: "If He were to make my good deeds exceed my bad deeds by the weight of an atom, that would be dearer to me than having the whole world."

Ata' ibn Yasar reported from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the believers are delivered from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection and are secure, then the dispute of any one of you with his companion over a right that he had in this world is not more severe than the dispute of the believers with their Lord concerning their brothers who were admitted into the Fire." He said: "They will say: 'Our Lord, our brothers used to pray with us, fast with us, and perform Hajj with us, yet You admitted them into the Fire?' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'Go and bring out whomever you recognize.' So they will come to them and recognize them by their forms. The Fire will not consume their forms. Some of them will be seized by the Fire up to the middle of their shins, and some up to their ankles. They will bring them out and say: 'Our Lord, we have brought out those whom You commanded us to.' Then He, Exalted, will say: 'Bring out whoever has in his heart the weight of a dinar of faith, then whoever has the weight of half a dinar,' until He says: 'Bring out whoever has in his heart the weight of an atom.'" [Musnad Ahmad: 3/94; Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/23.] [319]

Abu Sa'id said: "Whoever does not believe this, let him recite this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong...﴾"

He said: "They will say: 'Our Lord, we have brought out those whom You commanded us to, and no one remains in the Fire in whom there is any good.'" He said: "Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'The angels have interceded, the prophets have interceded, and the believers have interceded, and there remains the Most Merciful of the merciful.'" He said: "Then He will grasp a handful from the Fire, or he said: 'two handfuls,' of those who never did any good for Allah, Mighty and Majestic. They will have been burned until they became charcoal. He said: They will be brought to a water called the Water of Life, and it will be poured over them, and they will sprout just as a seed sprouts in the silt carried by a flood. They will come out, and their bodies [will be] like pearls, with seals upon their necks, (freed ones of Allah, Mighty and Majestic). It will be said to them: 'Enter Paradise. Whatever you wish for or see is yours, and it is better in My sight than this.'"

He said: "They will say: 'Our Lord, You have given us what You have not given anyone among the worlds!'" He said: "He will say: 'Indeed, I have something better than this for you.' They will say: 'Our Lord, and what is better than that?'" He said: "He will say: 'My good pleasure with you, so I will never be angry with you again.'" [Musnad Ahmad: 3/94.]

Others said: This is in a report from Ibn [...] [An illegible word.], from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will gather the first and the last. Then a caller from Allah will call out: "Whoever had a grievance against his brother, let him take it now." He said: By Allah, a man will be glad that he has a right over his father, his child, his wife, or his brother, and he takes it from him, even if it is small. The evidence for this in the Book of Allah, the Exalted, is His saying: ﴿So when the Horn is blown, there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask of one another﴾ [Surah al-Mu'minun 23:101]. Then the servant will be brought, and a caller will call out upon the heads of the witnesses: "The first and the last! This is so-and-so, son of so-and-so, whoever had a right against him, let him come to his side." Then it will be said to him: "Give these people their rights." He will say: "From where? The world has gone!" Allah, Exalted, will say to His angels: "Look at his good deeds and give them from them." If an atom's weight of good deed remains, the angels will say: "Our Lord, You know this better than them. We have given every person with a right his right, and there remains for him an atom's weight of good deed." Then He will say to the angels: "Double it for My servant, and admit him into Paradise by My bounty." The evidence for this in the Book of Allah is: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight; and if it is a good deed, He will double it and give from Himself a great reward﴾.

But if the servant is wretched, the angels will say: "Our God, his good deeds have perished and his evil deeds remain, and there remain many claimants." He, Mighty and Majestic, will say: "Take from their evil deeds and add them to his evil deeds, then write him a document (sakk) to the Fire."

So the meaning of the verse according to this interpretation is: ﴿He does not wrong an atom's weight﴾ against an adversary in favor of an adversary, but He rewards him for it and doubles it for him. This is His saying: ﴿and if it is a good deed, He will double it﴾. The reading of the general body of readers is ḥasanatan (حَسَنَةً) in the accusative, meaning: "if it is the weight of an atom." The people of the Hijaz read it in the nominative, in the sense of "if a good deed occurs or exists." Al-Mubarrad said: Its meaning is: ﴿and if there is a good deed remaining, He will double it.﴾

Al-Hasan read nudha'if'uha (نضاعفها) with a nun, while the rest read it with a ya'. The latter is the correct reading, because of His saying: ﴿and gives from Himself﴾. Abu Raja' and the people of Madina read yudha'ifha (يضعّفها) with tashdid, while the rest read yudha'ifha. Both are dialects, and their meaning is multiplication. Abu Ubayda said: yudha'ifha (يُضاعِفْها) means to make it into many multiples, and yudha''ifha (يضعّفها) with tashdid means to make it double.

﴿And gives from Himself (min ladunhu)﴾: that is, from His presence. Al-Kisa'i said: For ladun (لدن) there are four dialects: ladun, ladaa, lada, and ladun. When they attached it to themselves, they doubled the nun.

﴿A great reward﴾: and that is Paradise.

Abu Uthman reported: It reached me from Abu Hurayra that he said: "Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gives His believing servant for a single good deed a thousand thousand good deeds." Abu Hurayra said: "No, rather I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Indeed, Allah gives him two thousand thousand good deeds.'" [Kanz al-Ummal: 6/352, no. 16019, with variation.] Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight﴾ up to ﴿a great reward﴾. [320]

He also said: "When Allah says 'a great reward,' who after that knows its measure?"

﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness﴾: that is, how will they act when We bring from every nation a witness of truth from among them, who will testify against them concerning what they did? ﴿And We bring you, O Muhammad, as a witness against these?﴾ A parallel to it is in al-Baqara [Surah al-Baqara 2:143: "...and that the Messenger may be a witness over you"], in al-Nahl [Surah al-Nahl 16:89: "And We have brought you as a witness over these"], and in al-Hajj [Surah al-Hajj 22:78: "that the Messenger may be a witness over you"].

Asim reported from Zirr, from Abdullah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: "Recite." So I recited Surah al-Nisa', until when I reached ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness﴾, the eyes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) overflowed with tears, and he said: "Enough (hasbuna)." [Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 5/28.] [321]

﴿On that Day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth would be leveled over them﴾: The people of Madina and Syria read it with a fatha on the ta' and a tashdid on the sin, meaning "tatasawwa" (تتسوّى), so the ta' was assimilated into the sin. Qatada and Ubayda said: It means: if the earth were to move, they would walk upon it and return to it as they came out of it, and then it would be leveled over them until it covers them. Ibn Kaysan said: They wish they had not been raised at all, and that they had only been taken from the dust, and the earth had been level with them. Al-Kalbi said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to the beasts, the wild animals, the birds, and the predators: "Be dust," so that the earth may be leveled with them. At that point, the disbelievers wish they were dust walking over them, the people of the gathering. Its explanation is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿The disbeliever will say: "Would that I were dust!"﴾ [Surah al-Naba' 78:40].

﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement?﴾ Qatada said: "They wish the earth would be leveled over them, and they had not concealed the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ) or his description." Al-Kalbi and a group said: ﴿They will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾, because the guardians of Hell will testify against them.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said: "Things in the Qur'an differ for me. Is it doubt about it?" He said: "No, but it is a difference in verses that seem contradictory to you." He said: "Explain it." Ibn Abbas said: "Listen: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Then their trial will be only that they will say: 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists'﴾ [Surah al-An'am 6:23], and He says: ﴿They will not conceal from Allah any statement,﴾ yet they have concealed." So the polytheists denied, saying: 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists,' hoping that He would forgive them. Then their mouths will be sealed, and their hands and feet will speak of what they used to do. At that point, ﴿On that Day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth would be leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah any statement.﴾"

In another place they ask for mercy. The last of those occasions is when their mouths are sealed and their limbs speak, and that is His saying, Exalted: ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah any statement.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 4, verses 37–42:

Alladhina (الَّذِينَ) is in the accusative position, as a substitute for "man" (مَنْ) in the verse ﴿Allah does not love anyone self-conceited and boastful﴾. It is also said that it refers to "the self-conceited and boastful" (al-mukhtal al-fakhur). ﴿Who are miserly﴾ (yabkhaluna). Bukhl (البخل, miserliness) in the usage of the Arabs means a man withholding from his petitioner what he has in surplus. In the sacred law (shar') it means withholding what is obligatory. There are four dialectal forms (lughat) of the word:

- Bakhl (البخل), with a fatha on the ba and the kha. This is the reading of Anas ibn Malik, Ubayd ibn Umayr, Yahya ibn Ya'mur, Mujahid, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf and al-Mufaddal, and it is the dialect of the Ansar.
- Bakhl (بخل), with a fatha on the ba and a sukun on the kha. This is the reading of Qatada, Abdullah ibn Suraqa, and Ayyub al-Sijistani.
- Bukhl (بخل), with a damma on the ba and the kha. This is the reading of Isa ibn Amr.
- Bukhl (بخل), with a damma on the ba and a sukun on the kha. This is the reading of the rest of the readers, and it is the choice of Abu Ubayd and Abu Muslim, because it is the elevated (standard) dialect. The same pattern occurs in al-Hadid. All of them are dialects, and their parallel in ordinary speech is: "ard jurz, wa jurz, wa jurz" (a barren land).

The scholars differed concerning the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of this verse and its meaning. Most of them said: It was revealed concerning the Jews who concealed the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) and did not make it clear to the people, although they found it written in their Torah.

Yaman reported from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning ﴿who are miserly and enjoin miserliness upon people﴾: He said: "This is about knowledge; it has nothing to do with worldly wealth."

Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd said: It was revealed concerning Kurdam ibn Zayd, Usama ibn Habib, Nafi' ibn Abi Nafi', Yahya ibn Ya'mur, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, and Rifa'a ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut. They would come to men of the Ansar, mix with them and advise them, saying: "Do not spend your wealth, for we fear poverty for you, and we do not know what may happen." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿who are miserly﴾ up to His saying ﴿of His bounty﴾, meaning wealth.

Yaman said: It means they are miserly with charity (sadaqa).

Al-Fadl ibn Fudala reported, from Abu Raja', who said: Imran ibn Husayn came out to us wearing a mutarraf (a striped cloak) of silk (kharz) that we had not seen him wear before or after, and he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, bestows a blessing upon a servant, He loves to see the effect of His blessing upon him." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 18/135.] [317]

﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment. And those who spend...﴾ up to the end. The position of alladhina is accusative, as a conjunction (atf) upon His saying ﴿who are miserly﴾. If you wish, you may make it in the genitive position as a conjunction upon His saying ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers﴾. It was revealed concerning the Jews. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning the hypocrites. It is also said: It was revealed concerning the polytheists of Makkah who were united in enmity toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

﴿And whoever has Satan as a companion (qarin)﴾: a companion and close friend. It is of the pattern fa'il from iqtiran (association). 'Adi ibn Zayd said:

"Do not ask about the man, but ask about his companion,
For every companion is guided by the one he associates with."
[Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/123.]

﴿Evil is the companion﴾: "fa-sa'a qarinan" means "how evil is Satan as a companion." It is in the accusative as a tamyiz (specification). It is also said it is an accusative of state (hal), and it is also said it is an accusative of separation (qat'), with the alif and lam removed from it, as we say: "Ni'ma rajulan 'Abd Allah" (what a fine man is 'Abd Allah). Its meaning is: "Ni'ma al-rajul 'Abd Allah" (the fine man is 'Abd Allah). When the alif and lam are removed, it is put in the accusative, as in His saying ﴿how evil a substitute for the wrongdoers﴾ [Surah al-Kahf 18:50], ﴿how evil a parable﴾ [Surah al-A'raf 7:177], ﴿how evil a resting place﴾ [Surah al-Kahf 18:29], and ﴿how evil a settlement﴾, and ﴿how good are those as companions﴾ [Surah al-Nisa' 4:69], and ﴿how great is their hatred﴾ [Surah Ghafir 40:35; Surah al-Saff 61:2]. The commentators said: ﴿Evil is the companion﴾ means that he (the companion) will say: ﴿Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! How evil is the companion!﴾ [Surah al-Zukhruf 43:38].

﴿And what would it have been upon them, if they had believed in Allah and the Last Day and had spent from what Allah has provided them? And Allah is ever Knowing of them.﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight﴾ up to the end of the verse. ﴿And what would it have been upon them if they had believed in Allah and the Last Day, and had spent from what Allah has provided them?﴾ Indeed, Allah does not wrong, that is, does not diminish or reduce, anyone of His creation in the reward of his deed, even by an atom's weight, for example. Rather, He recompenses him with it and rewards him for it. This is an example: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight﴾, so how much more so would be more than it? The meaning of the statement is: He does not wrong even a little, because wronging the weight of an atom does not benefit the wrongdoer, and its harm to the wronged party is not evident. It is also said: [...] [A blur in the manuscript.] Its evidence from interpretation is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people at all﴾ [Surah Yunus 10:44], in this world.

They differed concerning the dharra (atom). Ibn Abbas said: It is the small red ant, which can barely be seen with the eye. Yazid ibn Harun said: It is claimed that the dharra has no weight. It is related that a man placed bread, and the dharra covered it, concealing it, yet it added nothing to the weight of the bread. The evidence for this interpretation is what Bishr ibn Amr reported from Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud), that he read: "Indeed, Allah does not wrong the weight of an ant (mithqal namla)."

Yazid ibn al-Asamm reported from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿an atom's weight﴾, that he said: Ibn Abbas put his hand into a vessel, then lifted it out, then blew upon it, and then said: "Each one of these is a dharra." Some of them said: The particles of dust (hab') in a window opening, each particle of it is a dharra. It is also said: It is the mustard seed (khardala).

In summary, it is an expression for the smallest and least of things.

Anas reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah does not wrong the believer a good deed for which he is rewarded with provision in this world and recompensed for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is fed with it in this world, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, he will have no good deed." [Musnad Abi Dawud al-Tayalisi: 269.] [318]

Qatada said: Some of the people of knowledge used to say: "If He were to make my good deeds exceed my bad deeds by the weight of an atom, that would be dearer to me than having the whole world."

Ata' ibn Yasar reported from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the believers are delivered from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection and are secure, then the dispute of any one of you with his companion over a right that he had in this world is not more severe than the dispute of the believers with their Lord concerning their brothers who were admitted into the Fire." He said: "They will say: 'Our Lord, our brothers used to pray with us, fast with us, and perform Hajj with us, yet You admitted them into the Fire?' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'Go and bring out whomever you recognize.' So they will come to them and recognize them by their forms. The Fire will not consume their forms. Some of them will be seized by the Fire up to the middle of their shins, and some up to their ankles. They will bring them out and say: 'Our Lord, we have brought out those whom You commanded us to.' Then He, Exalted, will say: 'Bring out whoever has in his heart the weight of a dinar of faith, then whoever has the weight of half a dinar,' until He says: 'Bring out whoever has in his heart the weight of an atom.'" [Musnad Ahmad: 3/94; Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/23.] [319]

Abu Sa'id said: "Whoever does not believe this, let him recite this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong...﴾"

He said: "They will say: 'Our Lord, we have brought out those whom You commanded us to, and no one remains in the Fire in whom there is any good.'" He said: "Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'The angels have interceded, the prophets have interceded, and the believers have interceded, and there remains the Most Merciful of the merciful.'" He said: "Then He will grasp a handful from the Fire, or he said: 'two handfuls,' of those who never did any good for Allah, Mighty and Majestic. They will have been burned until they became charcoal. He said: They will be brought to a water called the Water of Life, and it will be poured over them, and they will sprout just as a seed sprouts in the silt carried by a flood. They will come out, and their bodies [will be] like pearls, with seals upon their necks, (freed ones of Allah, Mighty and Majestic). It will be said to them: 'Enter Paradise. Whatever you wish for or see is yours, and it is better in My sight than this.'"

He said: "They will say: 'Our Lord, You have given us what You have not given anyone among the worlds!'" He said: "He will say: 'Indeed, I have something better than this for you.' They will say: 'Our Lord, and what is better than that?'" He said: "He will say: 'My good pleasure with you, so I will never be angry with you again.'" [Musnad Ahmad: 3/94.]

Others said: This is in a report from Ibn [...] [An illegible word.], from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will gather the first and the last. Then a caller from Allah will call out: "Whoever had a grievance against his brother, let him take it now." He said: By Allah, a man will be glad that he has a right over his father, his child, his wife, or his brother, and he takes it from him, even if it is small. The evidence for this in the Book of Allah, the Exalted, is His saying: ﴿So when the Horn is blown, there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask of one another﴾ [Surah al-Mu'minun 23:101]. Then the servant will be brought, and a caller will call out upon the heads of the witnesses: "The first and the last! This is so-and-so, son of so-and-so, whoever had a right against him, let him come to his side." Then it will be said to him: "Give these people their rights." He will say: "From where? The world has gone!" Allah, Exalted, will say to His angels: "Look at his good deeds and give them from them." If an atom's weight of good deed remains, the angels will say: "Our Lord, You know this better than them. We have given every person with a right his right, and there remains for him an atom's weight of good deed." Then He will say to the angels: "Double it for My servant, and admit him into Paradise by My bounty." The evidence for this in the Book of Allah is: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight; and if it is a good deed, He will double it and give from Himself a great reward﴾.

But if the servant is wretched, the angels will say: "Our God, his good deeds have perished and his evil deeds remain, and there remain many claimants." He, Mighty and Majestic, will say: "Take from their evil deeds and add them to his evil deeds, then write him a document (sakk) to the Fire."

So the meaning of the verse according to this interpretation is: ﴿He does not wrong an atom's weight﴾ against an adversary in favor of an adversary, but He rewards him for it and doubles it for him. This is His saying: ﴿and if it is a good deed, He will double it﴾. The reading of the general body of readers is ḥasanatan (حَسَنَةً) in the accusative, meaning: "if it is the weight of an atom." The people of the Hijaz read it in the nominative, in the sense of "if a good deed occurs or exists." Al-Mubarrad said: Its meaning is: ﴿and if there is a good deed remaining, He will double it.﴾

Al-Hasan read nudha'if'uha (نضاعفها) with a nun, while the rest read it with a ya'. The latter is the correct reading, because of His saying: ﴿and gives from Himself﴾. Abu Raja' and the people of Madina read yudha'ifha (يضعّفها) with tashdid, while the rest read yudha'ifha. Both are dialects, and their meaning is multiplication. Abu Ubayda said: yudha'ifha (يُضاعِفْها) means to make it into many multiples, and yudha''ifha (يضعّفها) with tashdid means to make it double.

﴿And gives from Himself (min ladunhu)﴾: that is, from His presence. Al-Kisa'i said: For ladun (لدن) there are four dialects: ladun, ladaa, lada, and ladun. When they attached it to themselves, they doubled the nun.

﴿A great reward﴾: and that is Paradise.

Abu Uthman reported: It reached me from Abu Hurayra that he said: "Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gives His believing servant for a single good deed a thousand thousand good deeds." Abu Hurayra said: "No, rather I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Indeed, Allah gives him two thousand thousand good deeds.'" [Kanz al-Ummal: 6/352, no. 16019, with variation.] Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight﴾ up to ﴿a great reward﴾. [320]

He also said: "When Allah says 'a great reward,' who after that knows its measure?"

﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness﴾: that is, how will they act when We bring from every nation a witness of truth from among them, who will testify against them concerning what they did? ﴿And We bring you, O Muhammad, as a witness against these?﴾ A parallel to it is in al-Baqara [Surah al-Baqara 2:143: "...and that the Messenger may be a witness over you"], in al-Nahl [Surah al-Nahl 16:89: "And We have brought you as a witness over these"], and in al-Hajj [Surah al-Hajj 22:78: "that the Messenger may be a witness over you"].

Asim reported from Zirr, from Abdullah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: "Recite." So I recited Surah al-Nisa', until when I reached ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness﴾, the eyes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) overflowed with tears, and he said: "Enough (hasbuna)." [Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 5/28.] [321]

﴿On that Day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth would be leveled over them﴾: The people of Madina and Syria read it with a fatha on the ta' and a tashdid on the sin, meaning "tatasawwa" (تتسوّى), so the ta' was assimilated into the sin. The people of Kufa, except Asim, read it with a fatha on the ta' and a takhfif (lightening) on the sin, by deleting the ta' of tafa''ala, as in His saying: ﴿No soul will speak except by His permission﴾ [Surah Hud 11:105]. The rest read it with a damma on the ta' and a lightening on the sin, in the passive voice (majhul). They said: "Sawwayta bihim al-ard" (the earth was leveled with them), and they and the earth become one thing. Qatada and Ubayda said: It means: if the earth were to move, they would walk upon it and return to it as they came out of it, and then it would be leveled over them until it covers them. Ibn Kaysan said: They wish they had not been raised at all, and that they had only been taken from the dust, and the earth had been level with them. Al-Kalbi said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to the beasts, the wild animals, the birds, and the predators: "Be dust," so that the earth may be leveled with them. At that point, the disbelievers wish they were dust walking over them, the people of the gathering. Its explanation is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿The disbeliever will say: "Would that I were dust!"﴾ [Surah al-Naba' 78:40].

Al-Tha'labi said: Our teacher Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn related that he heard someone interpret this verse as: "Nothing on earth would be accepted from them as ransom (fidya)." Its evidence is His saying: ﴿The criminal would wish to ransom himself from the punishment of that Day by his children﴾ [Surah al-Ma'arij 70:11], up to the end of the verse.

﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement?﴾ Qatada said: "They wish the earth would be leveled over them, and they had not concealed the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ) or his description." Others said: Rather, it is a new (independent) sentence, meaning: "And they will not conceal from Allah any statement, because what they did is not hidden from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and they cannot conceal it." Al-Kalbi and a group said: ﴿They will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾, because the guardians of Hell will testify against them.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said: "Things in the Qur'an differ for me. Is it doubt about it?" He said: "No, but it is a difference in verses that seem contradictory to you." He said: "Explain it." Ibn Abbas said: "Listen: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Then their trial will be only that they will say: 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists'﴾ [Surah al-An'am 6:23], and He says: ﴿They will not conceal from Allah any statement,﴾ yet they have concealed." Ibn Abbas said: "As for their saying ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾, when they saw on the Day of Resurrection that Allah forgives the people of Islam, they said: 'Come, let us testify.' So the polytheists denied, saying: 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists,' hoping that He would forgive them. Then their mouths will be sealed, and their hands and feet will speak of what they used to do. At that point, ﴿On that Day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth would be leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah any statement.﴾"

Al-Hasan said: These are occasions (mawatin). In one occasion they do not speak, and no one hears except a whisper. In other occasions they speak and lie, saying: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ and ﴿we did no evil.﴾ In another occasion they confess against themselves, as in His, Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿So they confessed their sin﴾ [Surah al-Mulk 67:11]. In another place they ask for mercy. The last of those occasions is when their mouths are sealed and their limbs speak, and that is His saying, Exalted: ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah any statement.﴾
