'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim narrated from al-Qasim, from 'A'ishah, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed while I was lying across in front of him like a girl (al-jariyah) [in Musnad Ahmad 6/260: "like a cushion (al-khabazah)", which is more fitting] until when he wanted to perform the witr, he touched me with his foot."

Al-A'raj narrated from Abu Hurayrah, from 'A'ishah, who said: "I lost the Prophet ﷺ one night, so I began searching for him with my hand, and my hand fell upon his feet, which were upright, while he was in prostration saying: 'I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your anger, and in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot enumerate Your praise; You are as You have praised Yourself.'" [Musnad Ahmad: 1/96; Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1263].

In some reports: when he finished his prayer, he said to me: "O 'A'ishah, did your devil come to you?" [al-Mustadrak: 1/228; al-Sunan al-Kubra: 2/116] [329]. They said: 'A'ishah touched him while he was praying, and he continued the prayer.

Because of these reports, those who mentioned them restricted the nullification of wudu' to touching with desire.

Abu Rawq narrated from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from 'A'ishah, that the Prophet ﷺ used to kiss some of his wives and then pray without performing wudu'.

As for the washing and the manner of touching according to the school of al-Shafi'i, it has three categories: a touch that nullifies wudu' by agreement; a touch that does not nullify wudu'; and a touch on which there is disagreement. What nullifies wudu' is a man touching a young woman deliberately, whether she is alive or dead. What does not nullify it is touching hair, teeth, or nails. What is disputed is touching a young girl, an adult woman, or one of his close relatives whom he may not marry. [Regarding this there are two opinions:] one is that it nullifies wudu', because it is a deliberate touch [....]; the other is that it does not nullify, because desire does not enter into these. What supports the latter is what is reported from Abu Qatadah al-Salami al-Ansari, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray while carrying Umamah, daughter of Zaynab, daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the child of Abu al-'As ibn Rabi'ah ibn 'Abd Shams. When he prostrated, he would put her down, and when he stood, he would lift her up.

This is the ruling of touching when there is no barrier [so in the manuscript; the apparent reading is: when there is a barrier]. As for touching without a barrier, it nullifies purity, whether the barrier is thick or thin. This is the view of the majority.

Malik said: it nullifies if the barrier is thin, and does not nullify if it is thick. Al-Layth and Rabi'ah said: it nullifies whether the barrier is thick or thin. The evidence that touching does not nullify wudu' when there is no barrier is the apparent meaning of the verse ﴿or you have contacted women﴾. So if he touches her with a barrier, he has not touched her; he has touched the barrier. Accordingly, if a man swears not to touch her and touches her through a barrier, he does not break his oath.

This is all the ruling for the one who touches. As for the one who is touched, does his purity nullify because of it or not? There are two opinions of al-Shafi'i: One: it nullifies, because both share in the enjoyment. The second: it does not nullify, based on the report of 'A'ishah: "My hand fell upon the sole of the foot of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

And Allah knows best.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿and you find no water, then perform tayammum﴾. Know that tayammum is one of the distinctive features of this community, based on what Rab'i ibn Khirash narrated from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "We were given preference over the people in three ways: our rows were made like the rows of the angels; the earth was made a mosque for us; and its dust was made a means of purification for us when we do not find water." [Kanz al-'Ummal: 11/409, no. 31912] [330].

As for the beginning of tayammum: Malik reported from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from 'A'ishah, and Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Abwa' [in Sahih al-Bukhari 4/195 (on some of his journeys); similarly in Sunan al-Nasa'i 1/163], until when we were at al-Bayda' or Dhat al-Jaysh, my necklace broke. I had borrowed it from Asma'. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that it be searched for, and it was searched for but not found. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made his camel kneel, and they spent that night, and they stayed on that impurity [without water], and they had no water with them. The people came to Abu Bakr and said: 'Do you not see what 'A'ishah has done? She has detained the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the people without water.' So Abu Bakr came while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had placed his head on my thigh and was sleeping. He rebuked me and said: 'Ma sha' Allah!' and said: 'May Allah disgrace her necklace! It has detained the people without water while the prayer has come.' Then he jabbed me in the side with his hand, but what prevented me from moving was that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was resting his head on my thigh. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose and remained until morning without water. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the verse of tayammum."

She said: "Then they sent the camel I had been riding, and we found the necklace beneath it." Usayd ibn Hudayr said: "This is not the first of your blessings, O family of Abu Bakr; may Allah reward you with good. By Allah, no matter ever befell you that you disliked, except that Allah made in it good for you and for the Muslims."

Allah, the Exalted, permitted tayammum under five conditions:

The first: the entry of the time of prayer. It is not permitted to perform tayammum except after the time of prayer has entered, and it may be used to combine two obligatory prayers. This is the view of 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Hamzah, and the school of Malik, al-Shafi'i, al-Layth ibn Sa'd and Ahmad ibn Hanbal. They said: "Because it is a purification of necessity, so we analogize it to the case of the mustahadah (woman with continuous bleeding), and because the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Wherever the prayer overtakes you, perform tayammum and pray.'" [331].

Abu Ishaq narrated from al-Huraith, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Perform tayammum for every prayer." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/160, where it reads "tayammum"] [332].

Ibn al-Mahdi narrated from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from 'Amr ibn Qays [an illegible word in the manuscript; the apparent reading is what we have written], who said: "Rather, one performs tayammum for every prayer even if one has not broken wudu'."

Another group held that tayammum, like purification with water, may be performed before the time of prayer, and one may pray with it from major impurity to minor impurity, both obligatory and voluntary prayers. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Hasan, al-Thawri and Abu 'Ubaydah, and they argued by the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Clean earth is the wudu' of the Muslim, even if he does not find water for ten years." [Sunan al-Daraqutni: 1/196, with slight variation] [333].

The second condition among the conditions that permit tayammum: seeking water. The manner of seeking is that one searches for it in one's belongings. If he does not find it, he asks his companions. If he does not find it with them, he searches to the right and left, behind and in front. If there is a hill there, he climbs it and looks. If he sees a person approaching, he should ask him. If he performs tayammum before searching, it is not valid according to most jurists.

Abu Hanifah said: seeking water is not a condition for the permissibility of tayammum, but a recommended act. So if he performs tayammum before it, it suffices, because if it were a condition for it, it would be a condition for voluntary prayers when water is absent. Since tayammum for voluntary prayers is permitted without seeking water, it is also permitted for obligatory prayers without it. Its evidence is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿and you find no water, then perform tayammum with clean earth﴾. And it cannot be said that it is permitted only for one who has sought water. The evidence against this is that if a man appoints an agent to buy something for him, and the agent does not find it, and then he buys the second item before first seeking the original, he is liable.

The third condition is the inability to find water after searching for it. If there is an obstacle between him and the water, such as a thief, an enemy, a predator, a rampaging camel, a fire or the like, then he is without water. Likewise, if reaching it would cause him harm, such as fearing for his belongings if he leaves them, or if the water is in a well and he cannot reach it.

The fourth condition is an excuse, either illness or travel, based on His saying: ﴿And if you are sick or on a journey﴾.

Illness is of three kinds. An illness with which using water does no harm does not permit tayammum (dry ablution with clean earth) with it. A second kind is one in which using water may cause death, so tayammum is permitted. Likewise, if there is blood on a wound and washing it may cause death, he performs tayammum, and he repeats the prayer if he is able to wash off the blood later. The third kind is one in which using water would increase the illness or delay healing. Regarding this kind there are several opinions:
The first is that tayammum is permitted, and this is the view of Abu Hanifa.
The second is that it is not permitted. If the wound is on part of his body and not the rest, he washes the part where there is no harm and performs tayammum for the injured part, and neither of the two suffices without the other. Abu Hanifa said: if most of his body is affected, he is obliged to perform wudu' (ablution) and use water, and tayammum does not suffice for him, either with it or without it. If most of his body is wounded, the obligation of wudu' and ghusl (full washing) falls from him, and tayammum suffices for everything.

He said: (It is not permitted to combine using water on some limbs with tayammum on others.) Likewise, if a junub (one in a state of major ritual impurity) or a muhdith (one in a state of minor impurity) finds only an amount of water that is not enough for the muhdith's wudu' or the junub's full washing, al-Shafi'i has two opinions on this:
One is that the obligation to use the water falls from him and tayammum suffices for him. This is the view of Abu Hanifa, Malik and al-Muzani.
The second opinion is that he must use the amount of water he found, and then perform tayammum as I related [[as is in the manuscript.]]. If he is junub, he washes with it whichever of his limbs he wishes, then performs tayammum for the face and hands. If he is muhdith, he washes his face, then his hands, in order, then performs tayammum for the limbs of wudu' he did not wash. So if he washes all the limbs of his wudu' but a patch on his foot remains that water did not reach, he performs tayammum for that patch.

If some of his limbs are broken and he sets them, he should not go beyond the place of the break with the splints, and he should only put them on while in a state of wudu', like khuffs (leather socks). If he put them on while in a state of purity, he may wipe over the splint for as long as the excuse remains. Then, is he obliged to repeat the prayers he performed while wiping over the splints or not? There are two opinions on this:
One: he must repeat them.
The second: he does not have to repeat them. This is the choice of al-Muzani, and the evidence for it is what Zayd ibn Ali related from his father, from his grandfather, that Hazm had one of his forearms broken, and the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) commanded him to wipe over the splints.
Al-Shafi'i said: If the hadith of Ali is authentic, I follow it; but this is a matter on which I seek Allah's guidance.
If he put the splints on while not in a state of purity and they extended beyond the place of the break, then: if he does not fear for the loss of his hand or any other limb, he removes them; but if he fears that loss, he does not remove them, rather he washes what he is able to wash, and he repeats the prayer when he is able to remove them.

As for travel, it is the minimum that is called travel, whether long or short, because Allah the Exalted did not distinguish between them. The evidence for this is what al-Shafi'i reported from Ibn 'Uyayna, from Ibn 'Ajlan, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar: that he came from al-Jurf, and when he was in Medina he performed tayammum, wiped his face and hands, and prayed 'Asr. Then he entered Medina while the sun was still high, and did not repeat the prayer. Al-Jurf is near Medina.

The fifth condition is the concealed intention.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿then seek clean earth﴾ means: intend clean earth. The scholars differed about what is wiped with in tayammum, in four positions:
Abu Hanifa said: tayammum is permitted with the earth and whatever is of its kind, even if nothing from it sticks to the hand. He permitted kohl, orpiment, lime from plaster, crushed stone, and even dust, and even if he struck his hand on a smooth rock and wiped, it suffices. But if he performs tayammum with filings of gold, silver, brass, lead or copper, it does not suffice, because it is not of the kind of earth.
Malik said: it is permitted with earth and everything that is connected to it. He permitted tayammum with kinds of earth and trees, and said: if he struck his hand on something else and then wiped with it, it suffices.
Al-Awza'i and al-Thawri said: it is permitted with the earth and everything on it, of trees, stones, clods and others, to the extent that they said: if he struck his hands on hard ice or snow, it suffices. They argued with what 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmuz related from 'Umayr, the freedman of Ibn 'Abbas, that he heard him say: I and 'Abd Allah ibn Yasar, freedman of Maymuna, came until we entered upon Abu Juhaym al-Harith ibn al-Samma al-Ansari. Abu Juhaym said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) came from the direction of the Well of the Camel, and a man met him and greeted him, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) did not return the greeting until he turned to the wall, wiped his face and hands, and then returned the greeting to him.

Al-Shafi'i held that what is wiped with is clean dust that has powder which sticks to the hand, and this is the preferred view, because Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿then seek clean earth﴾. Sa'id is the name of dust, and tayyib is the name of what grows. As for what does not grow from the earth, it is not tayyib. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿And the good land, its vegetation comes forth by the permission of its Lord﴾, and the saying of the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ): "The earth has been made for me a place of prostration and its dust a purifier," so he specified dust for this. And Allah knows best.

﴿Then wipe your faces and your hands; indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.﴾ The discussion of what is wiped with has passed. As for the amount to be wiped and the manner of tayammum, people differed on it in five positions:
Al-Zuhri said: you wipe the face and hands up to the armpits and shoulders, and he argued with what 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utba related from Ibn 'Abbas, from 'Ammar ibn Yasir, from the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ), that he was on a journey with 'A'isha, and her necklace was lost, so they were detained in searching for it for a day. He said: then the verse of tayammum was revealed, and they struck their hands on the earth, then raised their hands without taking any dust, and wiped their faces and hands up to the shoulders, then the insides of their hands up to the armpits.
Ibn Sirin said: three strikes: one strike for the face, one strike for the hands, and one strike for the elbows. This was also the view of the Companions 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar and Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, and among the Successors al-Hasan al-Basri and al-Sha'bi, and among the jurists Abu Hanifa, Hanbal, Malik and al-Layth, may Allah be pleased with them. They argued with what al-A'raj related from Abu al-Samma, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) performed tayammum and wiped his face and forearms.
Abu Umama and Ibn 'Umar related that the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) said: "Tayammum is two strikes: one strike for the face, and one strike for the hands up to the elbows" [[al-Mustadrak: 1/179.]] [335].
Rabi' ibn Sabra related from his father, from his grandfather, from Aslaʿ, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) said to me: "Walk with us, O Aslaʿ." I said: "I am junub." He was silent, until we reached Mecca, then the verse of tayammum was revealed, and he said: "This suffices you."
He struck his palms on the earth, then shook them off, then wiped his forearms, their outer and inner sides.
Ali, may Allah honour his face, said: "It is two strikes: one strike for the face and one strike for the palms" [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 1/212.]] [337].
A group held that it is one strike for the face and palms. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Awza'i, Ahmad and Ishaq, and they argued with the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and your hands﴾ [[Surat al-Nisa': 43.]]. They said: the word "hand" without qualification includes the palm up to the wrist, as evidence that a thief's hand is cut up to the wrist, and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands﴾ [[Surat al-Ma'ida: 38.]]. They argued with what Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Rahman related from his father, from 'Ammar ibn Yasir, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) said concerning tayammum: "One strike for the face and palms, and tayammum from major impurity is like tayammum from minor impurity."

If the junub lacks water, he performs tayammum just as the muhdith does, without any disagreement, except what is reported from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, that they said: the junub has no right to tayammum, but he should wait until he finds water and performs ghusl. He explained His saying, exalted is He: ﴿or you have touched women﴾ as meaning touching with the hand, not intercourse.

Al-A'mash related from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, that a man asked 'Umar about a junub who finds no water. He said: he should not pray until he finds water. 'Ammar ibn Yasir said: Do you not remember when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) sent us, you and I, and I became junub, so I rolled in the dust, then I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) and told him of that, and he said: "It would have sufficed you to do such and such" [[Similar to it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 1: 6.]] [339]. And he struck his hand on the earth and wiped his face and body [[Sahih Muslim: 1/193.]]? 'Umar said: Fear Allah, O 'Ammar. He said: If you wish, I will never mention it again.
'Ammar ibn Yasir related from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, who said: I was with 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, when a Bedouin asked him: "We stay a month or two without finding water." 'Umar said: "As for me, if I were in that state, I would not pray." 'Ammar ibn Yasir said: "Do you not remember, O Commander of the Faithful, that you and I were with the camels?"
He said: "Yes." He said: "You became junub, so you rolled in the dust, and came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) and told him of that, and he laughed and said: 'It would have sufficed you thus.'" 'Ammar spread his palms, placed them on the earth, then shook one against the other, and wiped with them his face, and joined the palms with a little of the forearms. 'Umar said: Fear Allah, O 'Ammar. He said: O Commander of the Faithful, if you wish, I will never utter it again. He said: No, rather we will leave you to what you have taken on.
Al-A'mash related from Shaqiq, who said: I was sitting with 'Abd Allah and Abu Musa. Abu Musa said: O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, a man is junub and finds no water, should he pray? He said: No. He said: Do you not remember the saying of 'Ammar to 'Umar: "The Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) sent us, you and I, I became junub and rolled in the dust, then I came to the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) and told him of that, and he said: 'It would have sufficed him thus'"? And he struck his hands on the earth and wiped his face and hands? He said: I did not see 'Umar satisfied with that. He said: Then what will be done with this verse: ﴿and you find no water, so perform tayammum with clean earth﴾? He said: As for us, if we had permitted them this, then whenever one of them found the coolness of water he would perform tayammum with the earth [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/265.]]. Al-A'mash said: I said to Shaqiq: This was only out of his love for him.
He said: What indicates that the prayer of the junub with tayammum is permitted is what Ibn 'Awf related from Abu Raja', who said: I heard 'Imran ibn Husayn say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) saw a man separated from the people and not praying with them, and he said: "O so-and-so, what prevented you from praying with the people?" He said: O Messenger of Allah, I am junub and have no water. He said: "Use the clean earth, for it will suffice you" [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/434.]] [341].
Muslim related from Abu Raja' from 'Imran ibn Husayn, who said: I prayed behind the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ), and there was a man who was junub, so the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) commanded him to perform tayammum and pray. When he found water, the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) commanded him to perform ghusl and did not command him to repeat the prayer.
From Abu Dharr, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) said: "Clean earth is the wudu' of the Muslim, even if he does not find water for ten years" [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/155.]] [342].

His saying, exalted and majestic: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture?﴾ It means the Jews of Medina.
Ibn 'Abbas said: it was revealed concerning Rifa'a ibn Zayd ibn al-Sa'ib and Malik ibn Dukhshum. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) spoke, they twisted their tongues and reviled him, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.
﴿They buy error﴾: an abridgement; its full sense is: they buy error in exchange for guidance. ﴿And they wish that you would go astray﴾, O assembly of believers. Al-Hasan read ﴿tudilluu﴾ [you would be led astray]. ﴿From the way﴾, meaning: away from the way.
﴿And Allah knows your enemies﴾: among you, so do not seek their counsel, for they are your enemies. It may be that "a'lam" means "knowing", [like His saying: ﴿And it is easier for Him﴾ [[A blank in the photographed manuscript; what we have written is from Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/242.]], ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a Protector, and sufficient is Allah as a Helper﴾.
﴿Of those who are Jews﴾: if you wish, make it connected to His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture ... of those who are Jews﴾; and if you wish, make it disconnected from it and a new beginning, and the meaning will be: among those who are Jews are those who distort, like His saying: ﴿And there is none of us but has a known station﴾ [[Surat al-Saffat: 164.]], i.e., there is among us one who has a known station. Dhu al-Rumma said:
"So they remained, and among them his tear was flowing, and another pouring out a tear of the eye over the dregs."
He means: and among them is one whose tear.
﴿They distort﴾: they change. ﴿The words﴾.
Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The words from their places," meaning the description of Muhammad ﷺ (ﷺ), and the verse of stoning.
Ibn 'Abbas said: the Jews used to come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) and ask him about a matter, and he would inform them, thinking that they would take his words, but when they left his presence they would distort his words.
﴿And they say: We have heard, and we disobey, and hear without being heard﴾, i.e., not accepted from you. It was said: it is like their saying: "Hear, may you not hear."
﴿Ra'ina﴾ means: look upon us. The story has passed in Surat al-Baqara. ﴿Twisting their tongues and reviling the religion﴾, a slander against the religion. ﴿And if they had said: We have heard and obeyed, and hear, and look upon us, instead of ra'ina, it would have been better for them and more upright﴾, more correct and more just. ﴿But Allah cursed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except a little.﴾
﴿O you who were given the Scripture﴾: specifically the Jews. ﴿Believe in what We have sent down﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿confirming what is with you﴾.
Ibn 'Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) spoke to leaders of the Jewish rabbis, among them 'Abd Allah ibn Suriya and Ka'b ibn Asad, and said to them: "O assembly of Jews, fear Allah and submit, for by Allah, you know that what I have brought you is true" [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 4/260, with variation.]] [343]. They said: We do not know that, O Muhammad, and they denied it and persisted in disbelief. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿O you who were given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you.﴾
﴿Before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their backs﴾. The common reading is with the "mim" kasra; Abu Raja' read it with damma, and they are two dialects. Ibn 'Abbas said: He will make them like the hoof of a camel or the hoof of an animal. Qatada and al-Dahhak said: "We will blind them." The face is mentioned while the meaning is the eye. ﴿And turn them back on their backs﴾: i.e., We will turn their faces to their backs, and make their eyes be behind their necks. This is the report of 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Farra': the faces are places where hair grows, like the faces of monkeys, because the places where human hair grows are the backs of their faces. Al-Qutaybi: We will erase their traces and features of eye, eyebrow, nose and mouth; ﴿and turn them back on their backs﴾, i.e., like the napes.
If it is said: how could He threaten them with obliterating their faces if they do not believe, and then they did not believe and He did not do that to them?
The answer is: some said that this threat remains pending, and they said: there must be an obliteration of the faces of the Jews, that is by transformation, before the Hour. This is the view of al-Mubarrad. Others said: this was a threat conditional on something, and when 'Abd Allah ibn Salam and his companions embraced Islam, the rest were spared.
It was also said: when this verse was revealed, 'Abd Allah ibn Salam came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) before going to his family, and embraced Islam, and said: O Messenger of Allah, I did not think I would reach you until my face was turned to my back.
Al-Nakha'i said: 'Umar recited this verse to Ka'b al-Ahbar, and Ka'b said: O Lord, I have submitted, O Lord, I have submitted, for fear that the threat of this verse would include him.
Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The obliteration means that they apostatize as disbelievers and are never guided. Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: "Before We blind a people from the path and from the insights of guidance," ﴿and turn them back on their backs﴾, until they return to the place from which they first came, which is Syria. The root of ṭams is erasure, destruction and transformation; from it one says: "a effaced trace" (rasm ṭāsim), meaning effaced, and the wind obliterates the trace, i.e., erases and wipes it out.
﴿Or We curse them as We cursed the people of the Sabbath﴾, so We make them apes and swine. ﴿And the command of Allah is ever executed.﴾
﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾, the verse,

Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning the polytheists, Wahshi ibn Harb and his companions. He said: When he killed Hamza, he had been promised freedom in return for killing him, but this was not fulfilled for him. When he came to Makkah, he and his companions regretted what they had done. They wrote to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "We have regretted what we did, and nothing prevents us from embracing Islam except that we heard you say while you were in Makkah: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾ [Al-Furqan: 68]. We have invoked another deity with Allah, we have killed the soul which Allah forbade, and we have committed unlawful sexual intercourse. Had it not been for this verse, we would have followed you." Then ﴿Except for those who repent and believe﴾ [Al-Furqan: 70] and the verse after it were revealed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent these two verses to Wahshi and his companions. When they read them, they wrote back: "This is a severe condition. We fear that we will not do righteous deeds and so will not be among the people of this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾." He sent this to them, and they read it and wrote back: "We fear that we will not be among those whom He wills to forgive." Then it was revealed: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves...﴾ [Az-Zumar: 53]. He sent it to them, and when they read it, he and his companions entered Islam and returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who accepted them. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Wahshi: "Tell me how you killed Hamza." When he told him, he said: "Woe to you! Hide your face from me." [Al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 2/222, and al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 4/21.] [344] So Wahshi went to Syria and remained there until he died.

Muqatil said: This verse, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾, was revealed concerning the Jews, and His will applies to the people of monotheism.

Abu Mijlaz, from Ibn Umar: It was revealed concerning the believers. That is because when the verse ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves...﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood on the pulpit and recited it to the people. A man stood up and said: "And what about associating partners with Allah?" He remained silent. Then the man stood up to him two or three times, and then ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him...﴾ was revealed. So this verse is recorded in az-Zumar and this one in an-Nisa.

Al-Musayyib ibn Sharik, from Mutarrif ibn al-Shikhkhir, who said: Ibn Umar said: "In the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when one of us died in a state of a major sin, we testified that he was among the people of the Fire, until this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾, and we refrained from such testimonies."

From Jabir ibn Abdullah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Forgiveness [continues to] descend upon the servant as long as he does not raise the veil." It was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the raising of the veil?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah." [345] Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him...﴾ the verse. [The hadith is in Husn al-Zann bi-Allah by Ibn Abi al-Dunya: 65, no. 56.]

From Masruq, from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever meets Allah without associating anything with Him enters Paradise, and no sin will harm him with it, just as whoever meets Him while associating something with Him enters the Fire, and no good deed will benefit him." [Kanz al-Ummal: 1/81, no. 328.] [346]

And from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "In the Qur'an there is no verse more hopeful to me than this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/314, where it says "ahabb" instead of "arja".] [347]

﴿And whoever associates partners with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin.﴾ ﴿Have you not seen those who attribute purity to themselves...﴾ the verse.

Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning men of the Jews who brought their children to the Prophet (ﷺ), among them Adi ibn Amr, al-Nu'man ibn Awfa, and Suhayb ibn Zayd. They said: "O Muhammad, is there any sin upon these?" He said: "No." They said: "By Allah, we are only like them. What we do by day is expiated for us at night, and what we do by night is expiated for us by day." So Allah forgave them, and this verse was revealed.

Al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Sufyan and al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning the Jews and Christians who said: ﴿We are the children of Allah and His beloved﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 18], and who said: ﴿None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 111].

Mujahid and Ikrimah said: The "purification" means that they used to put their children forward in prayer, claiming that they had no sin, and that is the "purification." Atiyyah, from Ibn Abbas: The Jews said: "Our fathers and our sons have died, and they will intercede for us and purify us." So Allah revealed this verse. Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) said: It is the purification of one another by one another. From Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: I heard Ibn Mas'ud say: "A man may leave his house with his religion, and then meet a man who owns neither benefit nor harm for himself or for anyone else, and he says: 'By Allah, you are so-and-so, so-and-so,' perhaps praising him for something that is not in him. Then he returns to his house with nothing of his religion left." Then Abdullah recited: ﴿Have you not seen those who attribute purity to themselves?﴾

﴿Rather, Allah purifies whom He wills﴾, that is, cleanses from sins, ﴿whom He wills [...]﴾ [There is a blank in the manuscript photograph.] therefore ﴿and they will not be wronged a fatilah﴾. A fatil is what is in the cleft of a date pit. It was also said: it is what you twist between your two fingers of dirt, so it is fa'il in the sense of maf'ul. The poet said:

He gathers an army of thousands, then raids,
Then does not harm the enemy the slightest fatil.
[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/171, where it says "al-a'adi" instead of "al-aduww"; Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/103.]

Look, O Muhammad, ﴿how they invent lies against Allah﴾, that is, they fabricate upon Allah the lie in their interpretation of His Book. ﴿And sufficient is that as a clear sin.﴾

﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book?﴾ As-Sulami recited "alam tarah" (Have you not seen him) throughout the Qur'an. This is the dialect of a people who do not content themselves with dropping the letter in the jussive, but also elide its vowel, like the poet's words:

Whomever Allah guides is guided, and he has no misguider,
and whomever He misguides, no guide will guide him.

﴿They believe in al-Jibt and al-Taghut﴾. Scholars differed about these two. Ikrimah said: They are two idols that the polytheists worshipped besides Allah. Abu Ubaydah said: They are every object of worship, whether of stone, clay, an image, or a devil. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿Worship Allah and avoid al-Taghut﴾ [An-Nahl: 36], and His saying: ﴿Those who avoided al-Taghut, that they should not worship it﴾ [Az-Zumar: 17].

Atiyyah, from Ibn Abbas: al-Jibt means the idols, and al-Taghut means the interpreters of the idols who stand before them and invent lies about them to mislead people. It was also said: al-Jibt means the idols, and al-Taghut means the devils of the idols; each idol has a devil who speaks through it, and people are deceived by it. Abu Amr al-Shaʿbi and Mujahid: al-Jibt is magic, and al-Taghut is the devil. Zayd ibn Arqam: al-Jibt is the sorcerer, and it is also called al-Jibs (the sin changed into a ta'), and al-Taghut is the devil. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve, their protectors are al-Taghut﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 257].

Muhammad ibn Sirin and Makhul said: al-Jibt is the soothsayer, and al-Taghut is the magician; this is also a narration of al-Walibi from Ibn Abbas. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Abu al-Aliyah said: al-Jibt is a poet in the Abyssinian language, and al-Taghut is the soothsayer. Ikrimah said: Abu Hurayrah was a soothsayer in the pre-Islamic era, to whom some people who had embraced Islam used to resort, so this verse was revealed. Al-Dahhak, al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: al-Jibt is Huyayy ibn Akhtab, and al-Taghut is Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, and the evidence for this is His saying: ﴿They desire to seek judgment before al-Taghut﴾ [An-Nisa: 60].

Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn related, from some scholars, that al-Jibt is Iblis and al-Taghut is his allies.

From Qatar ibn Qabisah, from Makhariq, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Taraq (sorcery by drawing lines), tiyarah (omens) and 'iyafah (augury) are from al-Jibt. [Musnad Ahmad: 3/477; al-Musannaf of Abd al-Razzaq: 10/403; al-Sunan al-Kubra: 6/324; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/249. 'Iyafah is the scaring away of birds and the seeking of omens by their names; tarq is drawing a line on the ground, and it was said it is drawing in sand, and it was said it is striking with pebbles.] And al-Jibt is everything that Allah has forbidden, and al-Taghut is whatever makes a person transgress." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/249.] [348]

﴿And they say to those who disbelieved: "These are better guided than those who believed in the way."﴾ The commentators said: After the Battle of Uhud, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf went out with seventy riders of the Jews to Makkah, to form an alliance with Quraysh against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to break the covenant that existed between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Ka'b stayed with Abu Sufyan, who honored his lodging, and the Jews stayed in the houses of Quraysh. The people of Makkah said: "You are people of a Book, and Muhammad is a man of a Book, while we are unlettered. We do not feel safe that this may be a trick from you. If you want us to go out with you, prostrate to these two idols and believe in them." He did so, and this is His saying: ﴿They believe in al-Jibt and al-Taghut.﴾ Then Ka'b said to the people of Makkah: "Let thirty from you and thirty from us come and press our livers against the Ka'bah, and let us make a covenant with the Lord of the House that we will strive hard to fight Muhammad." They did so. When they had finished, Abu Sufyan said: "You are a man who reads the Book and knows, and we are unlettered and do not know. Which of us is better guided on the way and nearer to the truth? Are we, or Muhammad?"

Ka'b said: "Present your religion to me." Abu Sufyan said: "We slaughter camels for the generous pilgrims, we give them water, we host the guest, we free the captive, we uphold the ties of kinship, we maintain the House of our Lord and circumambulate it, and we are the people of the sanctuary. Muhammad has abandoned the religion of his fathers, severed kinship, and left the sanctuary. Our religion is ancient, and Muhammad's religion is new." Ka'b said: "By Allah, you are better guided on the way than what Muhammad is upon." So Allah revealed the verse: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book?﴾ [Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi: 104.] That means Ka'b and his companions. ﴿They believe in al-Jibt and al-Taghut﴾ means the two idols. ﴿They say to those who disbelieved﴾ means Abu Sufyan and his companions: ﴿These are better guided than those who believed﴾ means Muhammad and his companions, ﴿in the way﴾, that is, in religion.

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, and whomever Allah curses, you will not find for him a helper.﴾ ﴿Or do they have a share of the dominion?﴾ That is, "do they have" (the meem is a connecting letter), ﴿a share﴾ meaning a portion, ﴿of the dominion?﴾ This is in the form of denial, meaning they have no share of dominion at all. Even if they had dominion, ﴿then they would not give the people﴾, meaning Muhammad and his companions, ﴿the speck﴾ out of their envy, stinginess and hatred. The word ﴿yu'tuna﴾ is in the nominative case [...] [Unreadable words in the manuscript.]

In the recitation of Abdullah it is: "fa-idhan la yu'tu al-nas" (in the subjunctive) [...] [Unreadable words in the manuscript.]

They differed about the naqir. Ibn Abbas said: It is the spot on the back of the date pit, and from it [...] [Unreadable words in the manuscript.]

Mujahid: It is the seed-kernel in the middle of the date pit. [See Zad al-Masir: 2/140, and Lisan al-Arab: 5/228.]

Al-Dahhak: It means the white part of the date pit that is in its middle. Abu al-Aliyah: It is the flicking of a thing by a man with the tip of his finger, as one flicks a dirham. He said: I asked Ibn Abbas about it, and he placed the tip of his thumb on the inside of his index finger, then raised it and said: "This is the naqir." [See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/250.]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verses 43–53 (part 1 of 3):

﴿O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾. It was revealed concerning some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who used to drink wine and attend the prayer while they were intoxicated, so they did not know how many units they were praying and did not know what they were saying in their prayers. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾, "intoxicated" (sukara, plural of sakran) meaning drunk from wine. Al-Nakha'i recited (junuban), and both are dialectal forms.

﴿until you know what you are saying﴾ and what you recite in your prayer. After the revelation of this verse, they would avoid intoxication at the times of prayer, until the prohibition of wine was revealed in Surah al-Ma'idah.

Salamah ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding ﴿do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾, said: It does not mean intoxication from wine; it means the intoxication of sleep.

Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If one of you feels drowsy while in prayer, let him sleep until the sleep leaves him, for if he prays while drowsy, he may go to seek forgiveness and end up cursing himself." [Musnad Ahmad: 6/56] [322].

Hisham ibn 'Urwah also, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If a man feels drowsy while praying, let him leave, for perhaps he will invoke curse upon himself without realizing it." [al-Sunan al-Kubra: 1/97] [323].

Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If one of you rises at night and the Qur'an becomes confused on his tongue, so that he does not know what he is saying, let him lie down." [Kanz al-'Ummal: 7/789, no. 21420] [324].

It is narrated from 'Ubaydah al-Salmani concerning this verse that he said: It refers to one who is holding in urine (al-haqin). His evidence is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "None of you should pray while holding back the two impurities." [In all sources: "holding back urine and excrement."] [Kanz al-'Ummal: 8/179, no. 22464] [325].

﴿Nor [do not approach prayer] while in a state of major impurity (junuban)﴾ is an accusative of circumstance (hal), meaning: do not approach prayer while you are in a state of janabah (major impurity). Ibrahim al-Nakha'i recited (junbun) with a sukun on the nun. It is said: a man is junub, two men and two women are junub, and men and women together are junub. The verb from it is ajnaba, yujnibu. The root meaning of janabah is distance, and he is called junub because he keeps away (yajtanib) until he purifies himself. Then Allah made an exception, saying: ﴿except as travellers (ʿabiri sabil)﴾. The scholars differed on its meaning.

Some said: it means, "except if you are travellers and do not find water, so that you perform tayammum (dry ablution)." This is the view of 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, Ibn Zayd, Mujahid, al-Hakam, al-Hasan ibn Muslim and Ibn Kathir.

Others said: its meaning is "except those passing through it (the mosque) in order to leave it, such as one who sleeps in the mosque and then becomes junub, or who has water in it, or whose path passes through it. He is permitted to pass through it without remaining." According to this view, "prayer" (salah) means the place of prayer and the mosque, as in the verse ﴿ṣalawat﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 157], meaning the places of prayer. This is the view of 'Abd Allah, Ibn al-Musayyib, Ibn Yasar, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, 'Ikrimah, Ibrahim, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, al-Nakha'i and al-Zaydi. What supports it is what al-Layth narrated from Yazid ibn Abi Habib: that some men from the Ansar had their doors opening into the mosque, so they would become junub and have no water with them. They wanted water but could find no way to reach it except through the mosque, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse.

The root of ʿubur is crossing. It is said: ʿabara al-tariq and al-nahr, meaning he crossed them and moved through them. [So in the manuscript.]

﴿And if you are ill (marda)﴾, plural of mari (sick).

Isma'il, from his father, from al-Husayn, from Umm Salamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed my mosque is forbidden to every menstruating woman and every man in a state of janabah, except for Muhammad and his household: 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, peace be upon them." [al-Sunan al-Kubra: 7/65] [326].

By this is meant an illness in which contact with water would harm him, such as smallpox, wounds, and sores, or a fracture on which splints have been placed. He is granted a concession to perform tayammum. This is the view of a group of jurists, except for what 'Ata' and al-Hasan held: that one does not perform tayammum while water is available, and they argued with the verse ﴿and you find no water, then perform tayammum﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 43], and this person has water.

This is an error, because of what 'Ata' narrated from Jabir, who said: We went out on a journey, and a stone struck a man among us and wounded his head. Then he had a wet dream, so he asked his companions, "Do you find any concession for me?" They said, "We do not find a concession for you while you are able to use water." So he bathed, and he died. When we arrived before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he was informed of this, and he said: "They killed him; may Allah kill them! Why did they not ask when they did not know? The cure for ignorance is asking. It would have sufficed him to perform tayammum, bind a cloth over his wound, wipe over it, and wash the rest of his body." [Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/85] [327].

﴿or on a journey﴾, whether long or short. For him there is tayammum when water is unavailable. If there is neither illness nor journey, but water is absent in a place where water is normally not absent, such as being in a city where the water has completely run out, or in a village whose water has dried up, then there are three positions. Al-Shafi'i and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan held that he must perform tayammum and pray, and he must repeat the prayer. Malik, al-Awza'i and Abu Yusuf held that he performs tayammum and prays, with no need to repeat. Abu Hanifah held that he neither performs tayammum nor prays, but rather waits until he finds water, then performs wudu' and prays.

﴿or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself (al-ghaʾit)﴾. Al-Zuhri recited (min al-ghaytu). Al-ghayt, al-ghawt and al-ghaʾit all have one meaning, which is a low, sunken part of the ground. Mujahid said: it is a valley. Al-Hasan said: a depression among valleys. [The word is] "tasawwaba" [so in the manuscript]. Al-Mu'arrikh [said]: a hollow in the land surrounded and covered by trees. Its plural is ghaytan. The verb is (ghaṭa yaghuṭu), like (ʿada yaʿudu). Taghawwata yataghawwatu means he went to the ghaʾit. They used to relieve themselves there, so the place was used as a euphemism for the act, as with ʿadhirah and hadath. Here it is a metaphor for the needs of the belly.

﴿or you have contacted women (lamastum al-nisa')﴾. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited (lamastum) without alif here, and in al-Ma'idah [the verse: ﴿or you have contacted women﴾, Surah al-Ma'idah: 6]. This is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd. The others recited with the alif in both places, which is the choice of Abu Hatim.

The exegetes differed about the meaning of contact (lams) and touching (mulamasah). Some said: it means intercourse; this is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid and Qatadah. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When the matter of lams was mentioned, some of the mawali (non-Arab clients) said: "It is not intercourse," and some of the Arabs said: "It is intercourse." So I went to Ibn 'Abbas and told him. He said: "Which of the two groups were you with?" I said: "With the mawali." He said: "The group of the mawali has prevailed. Indeed lams, mass, and mubashara mean intercourse, but Allah uses euphemism for what He wills by what He wills." According to this view, contact was used as an euphemism for intercourse, because contact leads to it, just as the word "sky" (sama') is used for cloud, for rain, and for pasture, since through the cloud one reaches rain, and through rain one reaches pasture. The poet said:

"When the sky falls upon the land of a people, we graze upon it, even if they are angry." [al-Sihah: 6/2382]

Others said: it is the meeting of the two skins, whether it is with intercourse or without it. This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Umar, Abu 'Ubaydah, Mansur, 'Ubaydah, al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i, Hammad and al-Hakam.

The scholars differed on the ruling of the verse in five positions. Al-Shafi'i said: If a man's body makes contact with any part of a woman's body, whether with the hand or with another part of the body, the nullification of purity is connected to it. This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Umar, al-Zuhri and Rabi'ah.

Al-Awza'i said: If the touching is with the hand, it nullifies purity, but if it is with something other than the hand, it does not nullify it; he treated it as the touching of the private part.

Malik, al-Layth ibn Sa'd, Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh said: If the touching is for desire, it nullifies; if it is not for desire, it does not nullify. Abu Hanifah and Abu Yusuf said: If it is a gross touching (mulamasah fahishah), it nullifies; otherwise it does not. The gross touching is that which causes ejaculation (al-ifsad).

A group held that touching never nullifies purity under any circumstances. Among the Companions, Ibn 'Abbas held this view, and among the Successors, al-Hasan al-Basri, and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn also went to this position.

From al-Thawri there are two reports: one is this view just mentioned [i.e., the view stated above], and the other is like the view of Malik, according to the evidence of al-Shafi'i from the verse, that touching with the hand is what is reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he forbade the sale of mulamasah (a type of sale). The word lams is most often used for touching with the hand. Al-Shafi'i recited:

"I touched with my palm the palm of one seeking wealth, and I did not know that generosity flows from his hand. So I did not gain from his wealth what the wealthy gained, and I was spent, and what I had was squandered." [In the source: "I took" instead of "I touched"; "I seek" instead of "seeking"; "I squandered" instead of "I was spent."] [Al-Ansab, al-Sam'ani: 1/236; al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah: 10/166].

Al-Zuhri narrated from Salim, from his father, who said: "He felt her with his hand," which is from mulamasah. This is supported by what 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla narrated from Mu'adh, that a man asked the Prophet ﷺ about a man who obtains from a woman who is not lawful to him what a husband obtains from his wife, short of intercourse. He said: "Let him perform wudu' thoroughly." [al-Mustadrak 'ala al-Sahihayn: 1/35] [328]. Thus it is established that touching nullifies wudu'.

Those who did not require wudu' because of mulamasah itself argued from what Malik narrated from Abu al-Nadr, from Abu Salamah, from 'A'ishah, who said: "I used to sleep in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with my legs toward his qiblah. When he prostrated, he would nudge me, and I would withdraw my legs; when he stood, I would stretch them out. The houses at that time had no lamps."

'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim narrated from al-Qasim, from 'A'ishah, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed while I was lying across in front of him like a girl (al-jariyah) [in Musnad Ahmad 6/260: "like a cushion (al-khabazah)", which is more fitting] until when he wanted to perform the witr, he touched me with his foot."

Al-A'raj narrated from Abu Hurayrah, from 'A'ishah, who said: "I lost the Prophet ﷺ one night, so I began searching for him with my hand, and my hand fell upon his feet, which were upright, while he was in prostration saying: 'I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your anger, and in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot enumerate Your praise; You are as You have praised Yourself.'" [Musnad Ahmad: 1/96; Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1263].

In some reports: when he finished his prayer, he said to me: "O 'A'ishah, did your devil come to you?" [al-Mustadrak: 1/228; al-Sunan al-Kubra: 2/116] [329]. They said: 'A'ishah touched him while he was praying, and he continued the prayer.

Because of these reports, those who mentioned them restricted the nullification of wudu' to touching with desire.

Abu Rawq narrated from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from 'A'ishah, that the Prophet ﷺ used to kiss some of his wives and then pray without performing wudu'.

As for the washing and the manner of touching according to the school of al-Shafi'i, it has three categories: a touch that nullifies wudu' by agreement; a touch that does not nullify wudu'; and a touch on which there is disagreement. What nullifies wudu' is a man touching a young woman deliberately, whether she is alive or dead. What does not nullify it is touching hair, teeth, or nails. What is disputed is touching a young girl, an adult woman, or one of his close relatives whom he may not marry. [Regarding this there are two opinions:] one is that it nullifies wudu', because it is a deliberate touch [....]; the other is that it does not nullify, because desire does not enter into these. What supports the latter is what is reported from Abu Qatadah al-Salami al-Ansari, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray while carrying Umamah, daughter of Zaynab, daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the child of Abu al-'As ibn Rabi'ah ibn 'Abd Shams. When he prostrated, he would put her down, and when he stood, he would lift her up.

This is the ruling of touching when there is no barrier [so in the manuscript; the apparent reading is: when there is a barrier]. As for touching without a barrier, it nullifies purity, whether the barrier is thick or thin. This is the view of the majority.

Malik said: it nullifies if the barrier is thin, and does not nullify if it is thick. Al-Layth and Rabi'ah said: it nullifies whether the barrier is thick or thin. The evidence that touching does not nullify wudu' when there is no barrier is the apparent meaning of the verse ﴿or you have contacted women﴾. So if he touches her with a barrier, he has not touched her; he has touched the barrier. Accordingly, if a man swears not to touch her and touches her through a barrier, he does not break his oath.

This is all the ruling for the one who touches. As for the one who is touched, does his purity nullify because of it or not? There are two opinions of al-Shafi'i: One: it nullifies, because both share in the enjoyment. The second: it does not nullify, based on the report of 'A'ishah: "My hand fell upon the sole of the foot of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

And Allah knows best.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿and you find no water, then perform tayammum﴾. Know that tayammum is one of the distinctive features of this community, based on what Rab'i ibn Khirash narrated from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "We were given preference over the people in three ways: our rows were made like the rows of the angels; the earth was made a mosque for us; and its dust was made a means of purification for us when we do not find water." [Kanz al-'Ummal: 11/409, no. 31912] [330].

As for the beginning of tayammum: Malik reported from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from 'A'ishah, and Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Abwa' [in Sahih al-Bukhari 4/195 (on some of his journeys); similarly in Sunan al-Nasa'i 1/163], until when we were at al-Bayda' or Dhat al-Jaysh, my necklace broke. I had borrowed it from Asma'. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that it be searched for, and it was searched for but not found. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made his camel kneel, and they spent that night, and they stayed on that impurity [without water], and they had no water with them. The people came to Abu Bakr and said: 'Do you not see what 'A'ishah has done? She has detained the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the people without water.' So Abu Bakr came while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had placed his head on my thigh and was sleeping. He rebuked me and said: 'Ma sha' Allah!' and said: 'May Allah disgrace her necklace! It has detained the people without water while the prayer has come.' Then he jabbed me in the side with his hand, but what prevented me from moving was that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was resting his head on my thigh. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose and remained until morning without water. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the verse of tayammum."

She said: "Then they sent the camel I had been riding, and we found the necklace beneath it." Usayd ibn Hudayr said: "This is not the first of your blessings, O family of Abu Bakr; may Allah reward you with good. By Allah, no matter ever befell you that you disliked, except that Allah made in it good for you and for the Muslims."

Allah, the Exalted, permitted tayammum under five conditions:

The first: the entry of the time of prayer. It is not permitted to perform tayammum except after the time of prayer has entered, and it may be used to combine two obligatory prayers. This is the view of 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Hamzah, and the school of Malik, al-Shafi'i, al-Layth ibn Sa'd and Ahmad ibn Hanbal. They said: "Because it is a purification of necessity, so we analogize it to the case of the mustahadah (woman with continuous bleeding), and because the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Wherever the prayer overtakes you, perform tayammum and pray.'" [331].

Abu Ishaq narrated from al-Huraith, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Perform tayammum for every prayer." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/160, where it reads "tayammum"] [332].

Ibn al-Mahdi narrated from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from 'Amr ibn Qays [an illegible word in the manuscript; the apparent reading is what we have written], who said: "Rather, one performs tayammum for every prayer even if one has not broken wudu'."

Another group held that tayammum, like purification with water, may be performed before the time of prayer, and one may pray with it from major impurity to minor impurity, both obligatory and voluntary prayers. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Hasan, al-Thawri and Abu 'Ubaydah, and they argued by the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Clean earth is the wudu' of the Muslim, even if he does not find water for ten years." [Sunan al-Daraqutni: 1/196, with slight variation] [333].

The second condition among the conditions that permit tayammum: seeking water. The manner of seeking is that one searches for it in one's belongings. If he does not find it, he asks his companions. If he does not find it with them, he searches to the right and left, behind and in front. If there is a hill there, he climbs it and looks. If he sees a person approaching, he should ask him. If he performs tayammum before searching, it is not valid according to most jurists.

Abu Hanifah said: seeking water is not a condition for the permissibility of tayammum, but a recommended act. So if he performs tayammum before it, it suffices, because if it were a condition for it, it would be a condition for voluntary prayers when water is absent. Since tayammum for voluntary prayers is permitted without seeking water, it is also permitted for obligatory prayers without it. Its evidence is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿and you find no water, then perform tayammum with clean earth﴾. And it cannot be said that it is permitted only for one who has sought water. The evidence against this is that if a man appoints an agent to buy something for him, and the agent does not find it, and then he buys the second item before first seeking the original, he is liable.

The third condition is the inability to find water after searching for it. If there is an obstacle between him and the water, such as a thief, an enemy, a predator, a rampaging camel, a fire or the like, then he is without water. Likewise, if reaching it would cause him harm, such as fearing for his belongings if he leaves them, or if the water is in a well and he cannot reach it.

The fourth condition is an excuse, either illness or travel, based on His saying: ﴿And if you are sick or on a journey﴾.

Illness is of three kinds. An illness with which using water does no harm does not permit tayammum (dry ablution with clean earth) with it. A second kind is one in which using water may cause death, so tayammum is permitted. Likewise, if there is blood on a wound and washing it may cause death, he performs tayammum, and he repeats the prayer if he is able to wash off the blood later. The third kind is one in which using water would increase the illness or delay healing. Regarding this kind there are several opinions:
The first is that tayammum is permitted, and this is the view of Abu Hanifa.
The second is that it is not permitted. If the wound is on part of his body and not the rest, he washes the part where there is no harm and performs tayammum for the injured part, and neither of the two suffices without the other. Abu Hanifa said: if most of his body is affected, he is obliged to perform wudu' (ablution) and use water, and tayammum does not suffice for him, either with it or without it. If most of his body is wounded, the obligation of wudu' and ghusl (full washing) falls from him, and tayammum suffices for everything.

He said: (It is not permitted to combine using water on some limbs with tayammum on others.) Likewise, if a junub (one in a state of major ritual impurity) or a muhdith (one in a state of minor impurity) finds only an amount of water that is not enough for the muhdith's wudu' or the junub's full washing, al-Shafi'i has two opinions on this:
One is that the obligation to use the water falls from him and tayammum suffices for him. This is the view of Abu Hanifa, Malik and al-Muzani.
The second opinion is that he must use the amount of water he found, and then perform tayammum as I related [[as is in the manuscript.]]. If he is junub, he washes with it whichever of his limbs he wishes, then performs tayammum for the face and hands. If he is muhdith, he washes his face, then his hands, in order, then performs tayammum for the limbs of wudu' he did not wash. So if he washes all the limbs of his wudu' but a patch on his foot remains that water did not reach, he performs tayammum for that patch.

If some of his limbs are broken and he sets them, he should not go beyond the place of the break with the splints, and he should only put them on while in a state of wudu', like khuffs (leather socks). If he put them on while in a state of purity, he may wipe over the splint for as long as the excuse remains. Then, is he obliged to repeat the prayers he performed while wiping over the splints or not? There are two opinions on this:
One: he must repeat them.
The second: he does not have to repeat them. This is the choice of al-Muzani, and the evidence for it is what Zayd ibn Ali related from his father, from his grandfather, that Hazm had one of his forearms broken, and the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) commanded him to wipe over the splints.
Al-Shafi'i said: If the hadith of Ali is authentic, I follow it; but this is a matter on which I seek Allah's guidance.
If he put the splints on while not in a state of purity and they extended beyond the place of the break, then: if he does not fear for the loss of his hand or any other limb, he removes them; but if he fears that loss, he does not remove them, rather he washes what he is able to wash, and he repeats the prayer when he is able to remove them.

As for travel, it is the minimum that is called travel, whether long or short, because Allah the Exalted did not distinguish between them. The evidence for this is what al-Shafi'i reported from Ibn 'Uyayna, from Ibn 'Ajlan, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar: that he came from al-Jurf, and when he was in Medina he performed tayammum, wiped his face and hands, and prayed 'Asr. Then he entered Medina while the sun was still high, and did not repeat the prayer. Al-Jurf is near Medina.

The fifth condition is the concealed intention.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿then seek clean earth﴾ means: intend clean earth. The scholars differed about what is wiped with in tayammum, in four positions:
Abu Hanifa said: tayammum is permitted with the earth and whatever is of its kind, even if nothing from it sticks to the hand. He permitted kohl, orpiment, lime from plaster, crushed stone, and even dust, and even if he struck his hand on a smooth rock and wiped, it suffices. But if he performs tayammum with filings of gold, silver, brass, lead or copper, it does not suffice, because it is not of the kind of earth.
Malik said: it is permitted with earth and everything that is connected to it. He permitted tayammum with kinds of earth and trees, and said: if he struck his hand on something else and then wiped with it, it suffices.
Al-Awza'i and al-Thawri said: it is permitted with the earth and everything on it, of trees, stones, clods and others, to the extent that they said: if he struck his hands on hard ice or snow, it suffices. They argued with what 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmuz related from 'Umayr, the freedman of Ibn 'Abbas, that he heard him say: I and 'Abd Allah ibn Yasar, freedman of Maymuna, came until we entered upon Abu Juhaym al-Harith ibn al-Samma al-Ansari. Abu Juhaym said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) came from the direction of the Well of the Camel, and a man met him and greeted him, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) did not return the greeting until he turned to the wall, wiped his face and hands, and then returned the greeting to him.

Al-Shafi'i held that what is wiped with is clean dust that has powder which sticks to the hand, and this is the preferred view, because Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿then seek clean earth﴾. Sa'id is the name of dust, and tayyib is the name of what grows. As for what does not grow from the earth, it is not tayyib. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿And the good land, its vegetation comes forth by the permission of its Lord﴾, and the saying of the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ): "The earth has been made for me a place of prostration and its dust a purifier," so he specified dust for this. And Allah knows best.

﴿Then wipe your faces and your hands; indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.﴾ The discussion of what is wiped with has passed. As for the amount to be wiped and the manner of tayammum, people differed on it in five positions:
Al-Zuhri said: you wipe the face and hands up to the armpits and shoulders, and he argued with what 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utba related from Ibn 'Abbas, from 'Ammar ibn Yasir, from the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ), that he was on a journey with 'A'isha, and her necklace was lost, so they were detained in searching for it for a day. He said: then the verse of tayammum was revealed, and they struck their hands on the earth, then raised their hands without taking any dust, and wiped their faces and hands up to the shoulders, then the insides of their hands up to the armpits.
Ibn Sirin said: three strikes: one strike for the face, one strike for the hands, and one strike for the elbows. This was also the view of the Companions 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar and Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, and among the Successors al-Hasan al-Basri and al-Sha'bi, and among the jurists Abu Hanifa, Hanbal, Malik and al-Layth, may Allah be pleased with them. They argued with what al-A'raj related from Abu al-Samma, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) performed tayammum and wiped his face and forearms.
Abu Umama and Ibn 'Umar related that the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) said: "Tayammum is two strikes: one strike for the face, and one strike for the hands up to the elbows" [[al-Mustadrak: 1/179.]] [335].
Rabi' ibn Sabra related from his father, from his grandfather, from Aslaʿ, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) said to me: "Walk with us, O Aslaʿ." I said: "I am junub." He was silent, until we reached Mecca, then the verse of tayammum was revealed, and he said: "This suffices you."
He struck his palms on the earth, then shook them off, then wiped his forearms, their outer and inner sides.
Ali, may Allah honour his face, said: "It is two strikes: one strike for the face and one strike for the palms" [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 1/212.]] [337].
A group held that it is one strike for the face and palms. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Awza'i, Ahmad and Ishaq, and they argued with the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and your hands﴾ [[Surat al-Nisa': 43.]]. They said: the word "hand" without qualification includes the palm up to the wrist, as evidence that a thief's hand is cut up to the wrist, and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands﴾ [[Surat al-Ma'ida: 38.]]. They argued with what Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Rahman related from his father, from 'Ammar ibn Yasir, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) said concerning tayammum: "One strike for the face and palms, and tayammum from major impurity is like tayammum from minor impurity."

If the junub lacks water, he performs tayammum just as the muhdith does, without any disagreement, except what is reported from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, that they said: the junub has no right to tayammum, but he should wait until he finds water and performs ghusl. He explained His saying, exalted is He: ﴿or you have touched women﴾ as meaning touching with the hand, not intercourse.

Al-A'mash related from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, that a man asked 'Umar about a junub who finds no water. He said: he should not pray until he finds water. 'Ammar ibn Yasir said: Do you not remember when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) sent us, you and I, and I became junub, so I rolled in the dust, then I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) and told him of that, and he said: "It would have sufficed you to do such and such" [[Similar to it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 1: 6.]] [339]. And he struck his hand on the earth and wiped his face and body [[Sahih Muslim: 1/193.]]? 'Umar said: Fear Allah, O 'Ammar. He said: If you wish, I will never mention it again.
'Ammar ibn Yasir related from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, who said: I was with 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, when a Bedouin asked him: "We stay a month or two without finding water." 'Umar said: "As for me, if I were in that state, I would not pray." 'Ammar ibn Yasir said: "Do you not remember, O Commander of the Faithful, that you and I were with the camels?"
He said: "Yes." He said: "You became junub, so you rolled in the dust, and came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) and told him of that, and he laughed and said: 'It would have sufficed you thus.'" 'Ammar spread his palms, placed them on the earth, then shook one against the other, and wiped with them his face, and joined the palms with a little of the forearms. 'Umar said: Fear Allah, O 'Ammar. He said: O Commander of the Faithful, if you wish, I will never utter it again. He said: No, rather we will leave you to what you have taken on.
Al-A'mash related from Shaqiq, who said: I was sitting with 'Abd Allah and Abu Musa. Abu Musa said: O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, a man is junub and finds no water, should he pray? He said: No. He said: Do you not remember the saying of 'Ammar to 'Umar: "The Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) sent us, you and I, I became junub and rolled in the dust, then I came to the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) and told him of that, and he said: 'It would have sufficed him thus'"? And he struck his hands on the earth and wiped his face and hands? He said: I did not see 'Umar satisfied with that. He said: Then what will be done with this verse: ﴿and you find no water, so perform tayammum with clean earth﴾? He said: As for us, if we had permitted them this, then whenever one of them found the coolness of water he would perform tayammum with the earth [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/265.]]. Al-A'mash said: I said to Shaqiq: This was only out of his love for him.
He said: What indicates that the prayer of the junub with tayammum is permitted is what Ibn 'Awf related from Abu Raja', who said: I heard 'Imran ibn Husayn say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) saw a man separated from the people and not praying with them, and he said: "O so-and-so, what prevented you from praying with the people?" He said: O Messenger of Allah, I am junub and have no water. He said: "Use the clean earth, for it will suffice you" [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/434.]] [341].
Muslim related from Abu Raja' from 'Imran ibn Husayn, who said: I prayed behind the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ), and there was a man who was junub, so the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) commanded him to perform tayammum and pray. When he found water, the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) commanded him to perform ghusl and did not command him to repeat the prayer.
From Abu Dharr, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) said: "Clean earth is the wudu' of the Muslim, even if he does not find water for ten years" [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/155.]] [342].

His saying, exalted and majestic: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture?﴾ It means the Jews of Medina.
Ibn 'Abbas said: it was revealed concerning Rifa'a ibn Zayd ibn al-Sa'ib and Malik ibn Dukhshum. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) spoke, they twisted their tongues and reviled him, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.
﴿They buy error﴾: an abridgement; its full sense is: they buy error in exchange for guidance. ﴿And they wish that you would go astray﴾, O assembly of believers. Al-Hasan read ﴿tudilluu﴾ [you would be led astray]. ﴿From the way﴾, meaning: away from the way.
﴿And Allah knows your enemies﴾: among you, so do not seek their counsel, for they are your enemies. It may be that "a'lam" means "knowing", [like His saying: ﴿And it is easier for Him﴾ [[A blank in the photographed manuscript; what we have written is from Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/242.]], ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a Protector, and sufficient is Allah as a Helper﴾.
﴿Of those who are Jews﴾: if you wish, make it connected to His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture ... of those who are Jews﴾; and if you wish, make it disconnected from it and a new beginning, and the meaning will be: among those who are Jews are those who distort, like His saying: ﴿And there is none of us but has a known station﴾ [[Surat al-Saffat: 164.]], i.e., there is among us one who has a known station. Dhu al-Rumma said:
"So they remained, and among them his tear was flowing, and another pouring out a tear of the eye over the dregs."
He means: and among them is one whose tear.
﴿They distort﴾: they change. ﴿The words﴾.
Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The words from their places," meaning the description of Muhammad ﷺ (ﷺ), and the verse of stoning.
Ibn 'Abbas said: the Jews used to come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) and ask him about a matter, and he would inform them, thinking that they would take his words, but when they left his presence they would distort his words.
﴿And they say: We have heard, and we disobey, and hear without being heard﴾, i.e., not accepted from you. It was said: it is like their saying: "Hear, may you not hear."
﴿Ra'ina﴾ means: look upon us. The story has passed in Surat al-Baqara. ﴿Twisting their tongues and reviling the religion﴾, a slander against the religion. ﴿And if they had said: We have heard and obeyed, and hear, and look upon us, instead of ra'ina, it would have been better for them and more upright﴾, more correct and more just. ﴿But Allah cursed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except a little.﴾
﴿O you who were given the Scripture﴾: specifically the Jews. ﴿Believe in what We have sent down﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿confirming what is with you﴾.
Ibn 'Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) spoke to leaders of the Jewish rabbis, among them 'Abd Allah ibn Suriya and Ka'b ibn Asad, and said to them: "O assembly of Jews, fear Allah and submit, for by Allah, you know that what I have brought you is true" [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 4/260, with variation.]] [343]. They said: We do not know that, O Muhammad, and they denied it and persisted in disbelief. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿O you who were given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you.﴾
﴿Before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their backs﴾. The common reading is with the "mim" kasra; Abu Raja' read it with damma, and they are two dialects. Ibn 'Abbas said: He will make them like the hoof of a camel or the hoof of an animal. Qatada and al-Dahhak said: "We will blind them." The face is mentioned while the meaning is the eye. ﴿And turn them back on their backs﴾: i.e., We will turn their faces to their backs, and make their eyes be behind their necks. This is the report of 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Farra': the faces are places where hair grows, like the faces of monkeys, because the places where human hair grows are the backs of their faces. Al-Qutaybi: We will erase their traces and features of eye, eyebrow, nose and mouth; ﴿and turn them back on their backs﴾, i.e., like the napes.
If it is said: how could He threaten them with obliterating their faces if they do not believe, and then they did not believe and He did not do that to them?
The answer is: some said that this threat remains pending, and they said: there must be an obliteration of the faces of the Jews, that is by transformation, before the Hour. This is the view of al-Mubarrad. Others said: this was a threat conditional on something, and when 'Abd Allah ibn Salam and his companions embraced Islam, the rest were spared.
It was also said: when this verse was revealed, 'Abd Allah ibn Salam came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (ﷺ) before going to his family, and embraced Islam, and said: O Messenger of Allah, I did not think I would reach you until my face was turned to my back.
Al-Nakha'i said: 'Umar recited this verse to Ka'b al-Ahbar, and Ka'b said: O Lord, I have submitted, O Lord, I have submitted, for fear that the threat of this verse would include him.
Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The obliteration means that they apostatize as disbelievers and are never guided. Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: "Before We blind a people from the path and from the insights of guidance," ﴿and turn them back on their backs﴾, until they return to the place from which they first came, which is Syria. The root of ṭams is erasure, destruction and transformation; from it one says: "a effaced trace" (rasm ṭāsim), meaning effaced, and the wind obliterates the trace, i.e., erases and wipes it out.
﴿Or We curse them as We cursed the people of the Sabbath﴾, so We make them apes and swine. ﴿And the command of Allah is ever executed.﴾
﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾, the verse,

Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning the polytheists, Wahshi ibn Harb and his companions. He said: When he killed Hamza, he had been promised freedom in return for killing him, but this was not fulfilled for him. When he came to Makkah, he and his companions regretted what they had done.
