Someone asked him: "Which part of the Qur'an?" He said: "Umar ibn al-Khattab freed them. Did you not hear the words of God Most High, ﴿and those in authority among you﴾? Umar was among those in authority!" And he said: "Let her be freed, even if her child is a miscarriage."

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Aʿraj, Hammam ibn Munabbih, and Abu Salih all narrate from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever obeys me has obeyed God, and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed God. Whoever obeys the commander has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys the commander has disobeyed me." [[Riyad al-Salihin: 338, and Musnad al-Shamiyyin: 4/272, with the end of the hadith added in the second source.]] [357].

And from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The Children of Israel were governed by prophets; whenever one prophet died, another prophet would succeed him. Indeed, there will be no prophet after me."

A man said: "What will there be after you?" He said: "There will be caliphs, and they will be many."

They said: "What should we do?" He said: "Fulfil the pledge of allegiance to the first, then the first, and give them their due, for God will question them about what is entrusted to them." [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 10/419.]] [359].

ʿAlqama ibn Wa'il narrates from his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) while a man was asking him: "What do you think if there are commanders over us who withhold our rights from us and demand their rights from us?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Listen and obey, for upon them is what they are charged with, and upon you is what you are charged with." [[Nazarat fi al-Kutub al-Khalida: 95.]] [360].

From Abu Umama, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, while he was upon al-Jad'a, meaning his she-camel, and he called out in the saddle, stretching himself up: [361].

He said, so that the people would hear, and then said: "Do you not hear?" – raising his voice with it – and a speaker from among the groups of people said: "What do you charge us with, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Worship your Lord, pray your five prayers, fast your month, pay the zakat of your wealth, and obey those in authority, and you will enter the Garden of your Lord." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 5/294, with slight variation.]] [362].

Makhul narrates from Muʿadh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "O Muʿadh, obey every commander, pray behind every imam, and do not revile any of my Companions." [363].

Hisham narrates from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "After me there will be rulers who will govern you; the righteous will govern with their righteousness and the wicked with their wickedness. So listen to them and obey them in everything that accords with the truth, pray behind them. If they do good, it is for you and for them; if they do evil, it is for you and against them." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 6/237.]] [364].

﴿And if you dispute﴾ – i.e., differ – ﴿about anything﴾ of your religious affairs, differing in opinions, so that each one pursues what he sees, contrary to the opinion of his companion. Its root is from *al-naz'* (pulling), as when the disputants draw apart from one another and become opposed. From it is the saying:
*munawa'a*: contention (*munaza'a*).
Al-A'sha said:
*Nazaʿtum qudub al-rayhan mutaki'an... wa qahwatan murran rawuquha khadil*
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/261; *al-rawuq* means the strainer.]]

﴿then refer it to God﴾ – meaning to the Book of God – ﴿and the Messenger﴾ while he was alive; after his death, to his sunna. His saying ﴿that is better﴾ means that this referral is better for you, ﴿and better in outcome﴾, in recompense and consequence. *Ta'wil* is what a matter returns to.

Abu al-Malih al-Hudhali narrates from Maʿqil ibn Yasar, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Act upon the Qur'an: make lawful what it makes lawful, make unlawful what it makes unlawful, believe in it, and do not disbelieve in any part of it. What is unclear to you, refer it to God and to those of knowledge after me, that they may inform you. Believe in it, and believe in the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms, and in ﴿what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾. Let the Qur'an suffice you, with the clarity it contains, for it is an intercessor whose intercession is accepted, an advocate whose testimony is believed, and for every letter of it there is a light on the Day of Resurrection." [[Tafsir al-Tha'alibi: 1/177; and al-Mustadrak: 1/568.]] [365].

﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you?﴾ – the verse.

Al-Hasan said: A man went to the Prophet (ﷺ) to have another man judged, and the other said: "No, rather let us go to the idol of so-and-so's house." So God revealed this verse.

Al-Sha'bi said: There was a dispute between a Jew and a hypocrite. The Jew said: "Let us have him judge us, Muhammad." The hypocrite said: "No." The Jew kept calling to the Muslims, because he knew they would not accept bribes nor deviate in judgment, while the hypocrite kept calling to the Jews, because he knew they accepted bribes and inclined in judgment. They disagreed, then agreed to go to a soothsayer in Juhayna to have him judge between them. So God revealed this verse.

Al-Kalbi narrates from Abu Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: It was revealed concerning a hypocrite called Bishr, who had a dispute with a Jew. He said: "Come, let us go to Muhammad." The hypocrite said: "No, rather to Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf," whom God called *al-taghut*. The Jew refused to dispute with him except before the Messenger of God (ﷺ). When the hypocrite saw that, he went with him to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and they disputed before him. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) judged in favour of the Jew. When they left his presence, the hypocrite clung to him and said: "Come, let us go to Umar (may God be pleased with him)." They went to Umar, and the Jew said: "I and this man disputed before Muhammad, and he judged in my favour, but he was not satisfied with his judgment and claimed that he would dispute before you, and he clung to me, so I came with him." Umar said to the hypocrite: "Is that so?" He said: "Yes."

He said to them both: "Wait for me until I come out to you." Umar entered the house, took his sword, then came out to them and struck the hypocrite with it until he died, and said: "This is how I judge between one who is not satisfied with the judgment of God and the judgment of His Messenger (ﷺ)." The Jew fled, and this verse was revealed.

Jibril said: "Umar distinguished between truth and falsehood," so he was named *al-Faruq*.

Al-Suddi said: Some Jews had embraced Islam and some refused. In the Jahiliyya, when a man of Qurayza killed a man of al-Nadir, he was killed for him and his blood-money was taken: one hundred wasq of dates. When a man of al-Nadir killed a man of Qurayza, he was not killed for him, and he gave sixty wasq of dates as blood-money. al-Nadir, who were allies of the Aws, were more numerous and more honourable than Qurayza, who were allies of the Khazraj.

When God brought Islam and the Prophet (ﷺ) emigrated to Madina, a man of al-Nadir killed a man of Qurayza, and they disputed over it.

The Banu al-Nadir said: "In the Jahiliyya we and you agreed that we would kill from among you but you would not kill from among us, and that your blood-money is sixty wasq, the wasq being sixty sa', and our blood-money is one hundred wasq. So we will give you that."

The Khazraj said: "This is something you said in the Jahiliyya because you were numerous and we were few, so you dominated us. Today we and you are brothers, our religion and yours is one, and you have no superiority over us." The Banu al-Nadir said: "No, rather we remain as we were."

The hypocrites among them said: "Let us go to Abu Burda the soothsayer of Aslam and Malik ibn Khuzayma." The Muslims of both groups said: "No, rather to the Prophet (ﷺ)." The hypocrites refused, so they went to Abu Burda to judge between them.

He said: "Enlarge the bribe" – meaning the bribe. They said: "We will give you ten wasq." He said: "No, rather one hundred wasq as my blood-money, for I fear that if I support the Nadiri, Qurayza will kill me, or if I support Qurayza, al-Nadir will kill me." They refused to give him more than ten wasq, and he refused to judge between them. So God revealed this verse, and He revealed His words: ﴿O you who believe, retaliation is prescribed for you concerning the slain﴾ [[Surat al-Baqara: 178.]] and His words ﴿and We prescribed for them therein that a life is for a life﴾ [[Surat al-Ma'ida: 45.]], the verse. The Prophet (ﷺ) summoned the soothsayer of Aslam to Islam; he came, then turned away. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his two sons: "Go after your father, for if he passes such-and-such a pass he will never embrace Islam." They caught up with him and kept at him until he turned back and embraced Islam. The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded a herald to proclaim: "That soothsayer has embraced Islam." [[Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi: 109.]] This is His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you, desiring to refer their judgment to the taghut﴾ – meaning the idol. It is also said: the soothsayer; it is also said: Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf; it is also said: Huyayy ibn Akhtab.

﴿And they had been commanded to reject it﴾ – to His saying ﴿who turn away from you with aversion﴾ – i.e., turning away. The verb is governed by its verbal noun, as in His saying ﴿And God spoke to Musa with speech﴾ and His saying ﴿and submit with full submission﴾.

﴿So how is it, when disaster strikes them﴾ – meaning: how will they act when disaster strikes them ﴿for what their hands have sent forth﴾ – meaning as punishment for their aversion. This is a threat and warning, and the statement is complete. Then the report about their deed begins: they seek judgment from the taghut while they disbelieve in God. The meaning of His saying ﴿then they come to you﴾ is: they swear to you.

It is also said: by the disaster is meant the killing of their companion, for when Umar (may God be pleased with him) killed the hypocrite, they came to his people seeking blood-money, swearing ﴿we intended only good and reconciliation﴾. "We intended" – i.e., "we did not intend" – with *in* meaning *idh* and also meaning *ma*: we did not intend by referring to Umar ﴿except good and reconciliation﴾.

Al-Kalbi said: ﴿except good﴾ in speech, and ﴿reconciliation﴾, correctness.

Ibn Kaysan: truth and justice, similar to it.

﴿And they will swear, "If we intended only good..." – those are they whom God knows what is in their hearts of hypocrisy. So turn away from them, admonish them, and speak to them in their souls a far-reaching word.﴾ It is also said: ﴿turn away from them, and admonish them﴾ with the tongue and do not punish them. It is also said: threaten them with killing if they do not repent of shirk. ﴿Turn away from them and admonish them﴾ – i.e., in public. ﴿And speak to them a far-reaching word﴾ – in private and in public. It is also said: this was abrogated by the verse of fighting.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verse 54–63 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾ "The people" here means the Jews, said Qatadah. He said: It means the Arabs; they envied them for prophethood and for what Allah had honoured Muhammad (ﷺ) with.

It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi who said: I heard 'Ali (peace be upon him) on the pulpit, concerning His words ﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾, say: "They are the Messenger of Allah, Abu Bakr and 'Umar (peace be upon them)."

Others said: By "the people" here is meant the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whom they envied for what Allah had made lawful to him of women. This is what 'Ali ibn 'Ali narrated from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali concerning His words ﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾: "By 'the people' in this verse is meant the Prophet of Allah. The Jews said: Look at this Prophet! By Allah, he is never satisfied with food, and by Allah his only concern is women. If he were a prophet, the matter of prophethood would have occupied him away from women." So they envied him for the multitude of his wives and reproached him for it, saying: "If he were a prophet, he would not desire many women." So Allah refuted them, saying: ﴿We had already given the family of Abraham the Book and wisdom﴾, meaning by wisdom, prophethood. ﴿And We gave them a great kingdom﴾. Then He informed them of what David and Solomon had of wives, and rebuked them for it. The Jews then acknowledged to the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him) that Solomon had gathered a thousand wives, three hundred free wives and seven hundred concubines, and David had a hundred wives. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "A thousand wives for one man, and a hundred wives for another man, or nine wives?" At that time the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had nine wives. So they fell silent.¹

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Among them were those who believed in him﴾, meaning in Muhammad (ﷺ), namely 'Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions; ﴿and among them were those who turned away from him﴾, meaning turned aside from him and did not believe in him; ﴿and Hell is sufficient as a blazing flame﴾, as fuel.

Al-Suddi said: The two verses refer back to Abraham (peace be upon him). He sowed a crop one year, and the people sowed too, but the people's crops were destroyed while Abraham's crop flourished, and the people came to need it. They would come to Abraham (peace be upon him) asking him, and he would say to them: "Whoever believes in Allah, I will give him; whoever refuses, I will withhold from him." So whoever believed in him, the crop came to him, and whoever refused did not receive it.²

It is narrated from 'Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi who said: When Moses (peace be upon him) hastened to his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, he passed by a man whom he envied for his nearness to the Throne. He asked about him, saying: "O Lord, who is this?" It was said to him: "He will not tell you his name, but he will inform you of his deed: he did not walk about with tale-bearing, did not envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty, and did not disobey his parents."

Abu Ziyad narrated from Anas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Envy devours good deeds as fire devours wood."³

It is narrated from Yusuf ibn al-Husayn al-Razi who said: I heard Dhu al-Nun say: "The envious one does not lead."

Al-Asma'i said: Sufyan said to a singer: Allah says: "The envious one is an enemy of My blessing, dissatisfied with My allotment among My servants."

Al-Tha'labi said: I was recited, by Mansur al-Faqih, verses on this meaning:
"Tell whoever has been envious of me: do you know whom you have wronged in manners?
You have wronged Allah in His doing, when you are not pleased with what He has decreed for me.
Your recompense from Him is increases for me, and that you will not attain what you seek."⁴

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our signs – We will surely burn them in a Fire.﴾ "We will cause them to enter a Fire." Hamid ibn Qays recited "nusliyhim" with a fatha on the nun, meaning "We will make them level/equal," and it was said its meaning is "We will burn them." In this reading, "nāran" is in the accusative by removal of the preposition, its implied sense being "with a Fire."

﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins﴾, other than the burned skins. Ibn 'Abbas said: They will be replaced with white skins like sheets of paper. Nafi' narrated from Ibn 'Umar who said: A man recited before 'Umar "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins." 'Umar said: "Repeat it." He repeated it. Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: "I have its explanation: they are replaced a hundred times in one hour." 'Umar said: "Thus I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say."

Hisham narrated from al-Hasan concerning His words: "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins." He said: "It (the fire) consumes them every day seventy thousand times; every time it consumes them and roasts them, it is said to them: 'Return,' and they return as they were."

Al-Musayyib narrated from al-A'mash from Mujahid who said: Between their skin, their flesh and their blood there are worms, and their skin is renewed like the skin of wild donkeys.

Al-A'mash narrated from Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The skin of the disbeliever is forty-two cubits thick, and his molar is like Uhud."⁵

If it is said: How could a skin be punished when it did not disobey? We say: Sin and pain fall upon the self, not the skin, for skins only feel pain through the spirits. And the proof that the punishment targets the bodies, and does not punish the skins, is His saying: ﴿so that they may taste the punishment﴾,⁶ and He did not say "so that it may taste the punishment."

It was also said: The meaning is: He replaces skins which are those same burned skins. This is because "other" (ghayr) is of two kinds: other in the sense of contrast, other in the sense of difference, and other in the sense of transformation. "Other" of contrast is like your saying to the goldsmith: "Make for me from this ring another ring," and he breaks it and forges you a ring; the forged ring is the first, but the workmanship has changed, while the silver is the same.

This is like your recollection of a brother of yours who was healthy, then you see him afterwards sick and wasted, and you say: "How are you?" He says: "I am not as you knew me." He is the same, but his condition has changed. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿On the day when the earth will be changed to a different earth﴾,⁷ and it is that same earth, except that its mountains, hills, rivers and trees have been changed. And a poet recited:
"The people are not the people you knew, nor is the dwelling the dwelling you used to know."

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Nasir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Muzahim say: I heard Muzahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sharidah al-Kishi say: I heard Jabir ibn Zayd say: I heard Waki' ibn al-Jarrah say: I heard Isra'il say: I heard al-Sha'bi say: A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "Do you not see what 'A'ishah has done? She has disparaged her age," for she recited the two verses of Labid:
"Gone are those in whose shelter one lived; and I remain in a later generation like the skin of a mangy camel.
They take their pleasure in licentiousness and abasement, and whoever speaks is reproached, even if he does not make trouble."
Then she said: "May Allah have mercy on Labid. How would he be if he had lived in our time?"
Ibn 'Abbas said to him: "If 'A'ishah disparaged her age, then 'Ad disparaged its age. For a arrow as long as the longest spear was found in the treasury of 'Ad after they had perished, with written on it:
'Is there any way for me to return to the sands of Dhu al-Liwa... the Liwa of the sand, before the death of the hearts?
Lands in which we dwelt, and we were of its people, when the people were people and the lands were lands.'"
The lands remain as they are, except that their conditions and the conditions of their people have changed.⁸

The wise said: Just as the skin is renewed before resurrection, so it is changed in this way.

Al-Suddi said: The skins are only replaced by other skins, from the flesh of the disbeliever: the skin returns to flesh, and from the flesh another skin emerges, which is not a replacement for a skin that committed no sin.

It was also said: By "skins" is meant their garments of tar, so called because they cling to their skins; just as one says of a thing that belongs to a person, "it is the skin between his bone and his face." So whenever the garments burn, he is punished.

The poet said:
"Meanness clothed Taym in green skins; so woe to Taym because of their green garments."
Thus he referred to their skins by the garments.

'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya said: Allah the Exalted replaces the people of the Fire with skins that do not feel pain, and their ash becomes a punishment for them; so whenever their skin is burned, Allah replaces it with another. This is a punishment for them, as He said: ﴿Their garments are of tar﴾,⁹ so the garments cause them pain while they do not feel pain.

﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds...﴾ up to His saying ﴿shade, dense shade﴾: dense, which the sun does not heat.

﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners.﴾ It was revealed concerning 'Uthman ibn Talhah al-Hajabi of the Banu 'Abd al-Dar, who was the custodian of the Ka'bah. When the Prophet (ﷺ) entered Makkah on the day of the Conquest, 'Uthman closed the door of the House and climbed onto the roof. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked for the key, and it was said that it was with 'Uthman. 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) asked him for it, and he replied: "If I had known that he was the Messenger of Allah, I would not have withheld the key from him." 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) twisted his arm, took the key from him, and opened the door. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered and prayed two rak'ahs within it. When he came out, al-'Abbas asked him to give him the key and to combine for him the watering of the pilgrims with the custodianship; then Allah revealed this verse. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded 'Ali to return the key to 'Uthman, and 'Ali did so, (may Allah be pleased with him).

'Uthman said to him: "O 'Ali, you disliked and harmed me, then you came gently." He said to him: "Because of what Allah revealed concerning you," and he recited this verse to him.

'Uthman said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," and he embraced Islam. Then Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "As long as this House has a first brick standing, the key and the custodianship will be with the sons of 'Uthman," and it is today in their hands.

﴿And when you judge between people, to judge with justice. Excellent is that which Allah instructs you. Indeed, Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing.﴾ "O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you."

They differed concerning them. 'Ikrimah said: "Those in authority among you are Abu Bakr and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them)." What supports this is what Malik ibn Anas narrated from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqbari from Abu Shurayh al-Ka'bi that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Follow the two after me, Abu Bakr and 'Umar. Indeed, I have two ministers in heaven and two ministers on earth. In heaven they are Jibril and Mika'il; on earth they are Abu Bakr and 'Umar." And they are to me like the head to the body! Their likeness in this world, in kindness, is that Abu Bakr is like Abraham and Jesus. Abraham said: ﴿Whoever follows me is of me﴾,¹⁰ and Jesus said: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants﴾,¹¹ and so on. And 'Umar is like Moses and Noah. Moses said: ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth﴾,¹² and Noah said: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant﴾.¹³

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: They are the rightly-guided caliphs: Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Ali (peace be upon them). What supports this is what Hushaym narrated from Ibn Bashir from Abu al-Zubayr from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The caliphate after me among my community is in four: in Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Ali."

Sa'id ibn Jumhan narrated from Safinah, freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) built the mosque, Abu Bakr came with a stone and placed it; then 'Umar came with a stone and placed it; then 'Uthman came with a stone and placed it. He said: "These are the rulers after me."

'Ata': They are the Muhajirun and the Ansar and the Successors in excellence, as evidence for His saying: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Muhajirun and the Ansar...﴾ the verse.

Bakr ibn 'Abdullah al-Muzani: They are the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). What supports this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "My Companions are like stars; whichever of them you follow, you will be guided."

It is narrated from al-Hasan that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of my Companions among people is like salt in food; when salt is gone, the food is spoiled."

Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Mujahid, al-Mubarak ibn Fudalah and Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid: They are the jurists and scholars, the people of religion and virtue, who teach people the landmarks of their religion and command you to good and forbid you from evil; Allah made obedience to them obligatory upon the servants.

This is the report of 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn 'Abbas, which is the evidence for this interpretation.

His saying: ﴿But if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them...﴾ the verse.

Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali said: Nothing is more honourable than knowledge: kings rule over people, and scholars rule over kings.

Ibn Kaysan: They are the people of intellect and opinion who concern themselves with the affairs of people.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The foundation of religion is built upon the intellect, the obligations were imposed upon the intellect, our Lord is known by the intellect and approached by the intellect; the intellectual person is nearer to his Lord than all the diligent ones without intellect, and the weight of an atom of an intellectual person's righteousness is better than the struggle of an ignorant one for a thousand years.

It is narrated from Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Malik who said: al-Thawri said: Allah revealed to one of the prophets: "When you see an intelligent person, be a servant to him."

Maymun ibn Mihran, Muqatil and al-Suddi and al-Sha'bi: They are the commanders of the expeditions.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Khalid ibn al-Walid in a expedition against a tribe of the Arabs, and 'Ammar ibn Yasir was with him. Khalid marched until, when he approached the people, he camped so as to advise them; then a warner came to them and they fled, except one man who had embraced Islam. He ordered his companions to prepare for departure, then went off until he came to Khalid's army and entered upon 'Ammar, and said: "O Abu al-Yaqzan, I am a Muslim, and when my people heard of you they fled; I stayed behind, and my word and my benefit to you is that I stay, or I flee as my people fled."

He said: "Remain, for that will benefit you." The man returned to his family and ordered them to stay. Khalid rose in the morning and came upon the people, and found none but that man; he seized him and seized his property. 'Ammar came to him and said: "Release the man, for he is a Muslim, and I had granted him protection and ordered him to remain."

Khalid said: "You grant protection against me, and I am the commander." He said: "Yes, I grant protection against you, and I am the commander." There was an argument between them, and they went back to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him of the man's affair. The Prophet (ﷺ) granted the man safety, and approved 'Ammar's protection, and afterwards forbade him to command anyone without his permission.

He said: Then 'Ammar and Khalid quarrelled in front of the Prophet (ﷺ); 'Ammar spoke harshly to Khalid, and Khalid became angry and said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you leave this slave to revile me? By Allah, if it were not for you, 'Ammar would not have reviled me." 'Ammar was a freedman of Hashim ibn al-Mughirah.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Khalid, leave 'Ammar alone, for whoever reviles 'Ammar, Allah reviles him, and whoever hates 'Ammar, Allah hates him." Then 'Ammar stood up and Khalid followed him, took hold of his garment and asked him to be pleased with him, and he was pleased with him.

Then Allah revealed this verse and commanded obedience to those in authority.

Abu Hurayrah and Ibn Zayd said: They are the commanders and rulers, since they were commanded to render trusts to the subjects; by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners﴾, the subjects are commanded to show good obedience to them.

'Ali, may Allah honour his face, said: "It is incumbent upon the imam to judge by what Allah has revealed and to render the trust; when he does so, it is incumbent upon the subjects to listen to him, obey him, and respond when called."

Al-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Those Arabs around Makkah did not know of rulers, and they would disdain to give obedience to one another's rulership. When they submitted to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in obedience, they did not think it proper for anyone other than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so they were commanded to obey those in authority.

'Ikrimah said: The mothers of children are free by the Qur'an.

Someone asked him: "Which part of the Qur'an?" He said: "Umar ibn al-Khattab freed them. Did you not hear the words of God Most High, ﴿and those in authority among you﴾? Umar was among those in authority!" And he said: "Let her be freed, even if her child is a miscarriage."

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Aʿraj, Hammam ibn Munabbih, and Abu Salih all narrate from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever obeys me has obeyed God, and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed God. Whoever obeys the commander has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys the commander has disobeyed me." [[Riyad al-Salihin: 338, and Musnad al-Shamiyyin: 4/272, with the end of the hadith added in the second source.]] [357].

And from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The Children of Israel were governed by prophets; whenever one prophet died, another prophet would succeed him. Indeed, there will be no prophet after me."

A man said: "What will there be after you?" He said: "There will be caliphs, and they will be many."

They said: "What should we do?" He said: "Fulfil the pledge of allegiance to the first, then the first, and give them their due, for God will question them about what is entrusted to them." [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 10/419.]] [359].

ʿAlqama ibn Wa'il narrates from his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) while a man was asking him: "What do you think if there are commanders over us who withhold our rights from us and demand their rights from us?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Listen and obey, for upon them is what they are charged with, and upon you is what you are charged with." [[Nazarat fi al-Kutub al-Khalida: 95.]] [360].

From Abu Umama, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, while he was upon al-Jad'a, meaning his she-camel, and he called out in the saddle, stretching himself up: [361].

He said, so that the people would hear, and then said: "Do you not hear?" – raising his voice with it – and a speaker from among the groups of people said: "What do you charge us with, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Worship your Lord, pray your five prayers, fast your month, pay the zakat of your wealth, and obey those in authority, and you will enter the Garden of your Lord." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 5/294, with slight variation.]] [362].

Makhul narrates from Muʿadh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "O Muʿadh, obey every commander, pray behind every imam, and do not revile any of my Companions." [363].

Hisham narrates from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "After me there will be rulers who will govern you; the righteous will govern with their righteousness and the wicked with their wickedness. So listen to them and obey them in everything that accords with the truth, pray behind them. If they do good, it is for you and for them; if they do evil, it is for you and against them." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 6/237.]] [364].

﴿And if you dispute﴾ – i.e., differ – ﴿about anything﴾ of your religious affairs, differing in opinions, so that each one pursues what he sees, contrary to the opinion of his companion. Its root is from *al-naz'* (pulling), as when the disputants draw apart from one another and become opposed. From it is the saying:
*munawa'a*: contention (*munaza'a*).
Al-A'sha said:
*Nazaʿtum qudub al-rayhan mutaki'an... wa qahwatan murran rawuquha khadil*
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/261; *al-rawuq* means the strainer.]]

﴿then refer it to God﴾ – meaning to the Book of God – ﴿and the Messenger﴾ while he was alive; after his death, to his sunna. His saying ﴿that is better﴾ means that this referral is better for you, ﴿and better in outcome﴾, in recompense and consequence. *Ta'wil* is what a matter returns to.

Abu al-Malih al-Hudhali narrates from Maʿqil ibn Yasar, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Act upon the Qur'an: make lawful what it makes lawful, make unlawful what it makes unlawful, believe in it, and do not disbelieve in any part of it. What is unclear to you, refer it to God and to those of knowledge after me, that they may inform you. Believe in it, and believe in the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms, and in ﴿what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾. Let the Qur'an suffice you, with the clarity it contains, for it is an intercessor whose intercession is accepted, an advocate whose testimony is believed, and for every letter of it there is a light on the Day of Resurrection." [[Tafsir al-Tha'alibi: 1/177; and al-Mustadrak: 1/568.]] [365].

﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you?﴾ – the verse.

Al-Hasan said: A man went to the Prophet (ﷺ) to have another man judged, and the other said: "No, rather let us go to the idol of so-and-so's house." So God revealed this verse.

Al-Sha'bi said: There was a dispute between a Jew and a hypocrite. The Jew said: "Let us have him judge us, Muhammad." The hypocrite said: "No." The Jew kept calling to the Muslims, because he knew they would not accept bribes nor deviate in judgment, while the hypocrite kept calling to the Jews, because he knew they accepted bribes and inclined in judgment. They disagreed, then agreed to go to a soothsayer in Juhayna to have him judge between them. So God revealed this verse.

Al-Kalbi narrates from Abu Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: It was revealed concerning a hypocrite called Bishr, who had a dispute with a Jew. He said: "Come, let us go to Muhammad." The hypocrite said: "No, rather to Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf," whom God called *al-taghut*. The Jew refused to dispute with him except before the Messenger of God (ﷺ). When the hypocrite saw that, he went with him to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and they disputed before him. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) judged in favour of the Jew. When they left his presence, the hypocrite clung to him and said: "Come, let us go to Umar (may God be pleased with him)." They went to Umar, and the Jew said: "I and this man disputed before Muhammad, and he judged in my favour, but he was not satisfied with his judgment and claimed that he would dispute before you, and he clung to me, so I came with him." Umar said to the hypocrite: "Is that so?" He said: "Yes."

He said to them both: "Wait for me until I come out to you." Umar entered the house, took his sword, then came out to them and struck the hypocrite with it until he died, and said: "This is how I judge between one who is not satisfied with the judgment of God and the judgment of His Messenger (ﷺ)." The Jew fled, and this verse was revealed.

Jibril said: "Umar distinguished between truth and falsehood," so he was named *al-Faruq*.

Al-Suddi said: Some Jews had embraced Islam and some refused. In the Jahiliyya, when a man of Qurayza killed a man of al-Nadir, he was killed for him and his blood-money was taken: one hundred wasq of dates. When a man of al-Nadir killed a man of Qurayza, he was not killed for him, and he gave sixty wasq of dates as blood-money. al-Nadir, who were allies of the Aws, were more numerous and more honourable than Qurayza, who were allies of the Khazraj.

When God brought Islam and the Prophet (ﷺ) emigrated to Madina, a man of al-Nadir killed a man of Qurayza, and they disputed over it.

The Banu al-Nadir said: "In the Jahiliyya we and you agreed that we would kill from among you but you would not kill from among us, and that your blood-money is sixty wasq, the wasq being sixty sa', and our blood-money is one hundred wasq. So we will give you that."

The Khazraj said: "This is something you said in the Jahiliyya because you were numerous and we were few, so you dominated us. Today we and you are brothers, our religion and yours is one, and you have no superiority over us." The Banu al-Nadir said: "No, rather we remain as we were."

The hypocrites among them said: "Let us go to Abu Burda the soothsayer of Aslam and Malik ibn Khuzayma." The Muslims of both groups said: "No, rather to the Prophet (ﷺ)." The hypocrites refused, so they went to Abu Burda to judge between them.

He said: "Enlarge the bribe" – meaning the bribe. They said: "We will give you ten wasq." He said: "No, rather one hundred wasq as my blood-money, for I fear that if I support the Nadiri, Qurayza will kill me, or if I support Qurayza, al-Nadir will kill me." They refused to give him more than ten wasq, and he refused to judge between them. So God revealed this verse, and He revealed His words: ﴿O you who believe, retaliation is prescribed for you concerning the slain﴾ [[Surat al-Baqara: 178.]] and His words ﴿and We prescribed for them therein that a life is for a life﴾ [[Surat al-Ma'ida: 45.]], the verse. The Prophet (ﷺ) summoned the soothsayer of Aslam to Islam; he came, then turned away. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his two sons: "Go after your father, for if he passes such-and-such a pass he will never embrace Islam." They caught up with him and kept at him until he turned back and embraced Islam. The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded a herald to proclaim: "That soothsayer has embraced Islam." [[Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi: 109.]] This is His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you, desiring to refer their judgment to the taghut﴾ – meaning the idol. It is also said: the soothsayer; it is also said: Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf; it is also said: Huyayy ibn Akhtab.

﴿And they had been commanded to reject it﴾ – to His saying ﴿who turn away from you with aversion﴾ – i.e., turning away. The verb is governed by its verbal noun, as in His saying ﴿And God spoke to Musa with speech﴾ and His saying ﴿and submit with full submission﴾.

﴿So how is it, when disaster strikes them﴾ – meaning: how will they act when disaster strikes them ﴿for what their hands have sent forth﴾ – meaning as punishment for their aversion. This is a threat and warning, and the statement is complete. Then the report about their deed begins: they seek judgment from the taghut while they disbelieve in God. The meaning of His saying ﴿then they come to you﴾ is: they swear to you.

It is also said: by the disaster is meant the killing of their companion, for when Umar (may God be pleased with him) killed the hypocrite, they came to his people seeking blood-money, swearing ﴿we intended only good and reconciliation﴾. "We intended" – i.e., "we did not intend" – with *in* meaning *idh* and also meaning *ma*: we did not intend by referring to Umar ﴿except good and reconciliation﴾.

Al-Kalbi said: ﴿except good﴾ in speech, and ﴿reconciliation﴾, correctness.

Ibn Kaysan: truth and justice, similar to it.

﴿And they will swear, "If we intended only good..." – those are they whom God knows what is in their hearts of hypocrisy. So turn away from them, admonish them, and speak to them in their souls a far-reaching word.﴾ It is also said: ﴿turn away from them, and admonish them﴾ with the tongue and do not punish them. It is also said: threaten them with killing if they do not repent of shirk. ﴿Turn away from them and admonish them﴾ – i.e., in public. ﴿And speak to them a far-reaching word﴾ – in private and in public. It is also said: this was abrogated by the verse of fighting.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verse 54–63 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾ "The people" here means the Jews, said Qatadah. He said: It means the Arabs; they envied them for prophethood and for what Allah had honoured Muhammad (ﷺ) with.

It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi who said: I heard 'Ali (peace be upon him) on the pulpit, concerning His words ﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾, say: "They are the Messenger of Allah, Abu Bakr and 'Umar (peace be upon them)."

Others said: By "the people" here is meant the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whom they envied for what Allah had made lawful to him of women. This is what 'Ali ibn 'Ali narrated from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali concerning His words ﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾: "By 'the people' in this verse is meant the Prophet of Allah. The Jews said: Look at this Prophet! By Allah, he is never satisfied with food, and by Allah his only concern is women. If he were a prophet, the matter of prophethood would have occupied him away from women." So they envied him for the multitude of his wives and reproached him for it, saying: "If he were a prophet, he would not desire many women." So Allah refuted them, saying: ﴿We had already given the family of Abraham the Book and wisdom﴾, meaning by wisdom, prophethood. ﴿And We gave them a great kingdom﴾. Then He informed them of what David and Solomon had of wives, and rebuked them for it. The Jews then acknowledged to the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him) that Solomon had gathered a thousand wives, three hundred free wives and seven hundred concubines, and David had a hundred wives. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "A thousand wives for one man, and a hundred wives for another man, or nine wives?" At that time the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had nine wives. So they fell silent.¹

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Among them were those who believed in him﴾, meaning in Muhammad (ﷺ), namely 'Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions; ﴿and among them were those who turned away from him﴾, meaning turned aside from him and did not believe in him; ﴿and Hell is sufficient as a blazing flame﴾, as fuel.

Al-Suddi said: The two verses refer back to Abraham (peace be upon him). He sowed a crop one year, and the people sowed too, but the people's crops were destroyed while Abraham's crop flourished, and the people came to need it. They would come to Abraham (peace be upon him) asking him, and he would say to them: "Whoever believes in Allah, I will give him; whoever refuses, I will withhold from him." So whoever believed in him, the crop came to him, and whoever refused did not receive it.²

It is narrated from 'Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi who said: When Moses (peace be upon him) hastened to his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, he passed by a man whom he envied for his nearness to the Throne. He asked about him, saying: "O Lord, who is this?" It was said to him: "He will not tell you his name, but he will inform you of his deed: he did not walk about with tale-bearing, did not envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty, and did not disobey his parents."

Abu Ziyad narrated from Anas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Envy devours good deeds as fire devours wood."³

It is narrated from Yusuf ibn al-Husayn al-Razi who said: I heard Dhu al-Nun say: "The envious one does not lead."

Al-Asma'i said: Sufyan said to a singer: Allah says: "The envious one is an enemy of My blessing, dissatisfied with My allotment among My servants."

Al-Tha'labi said: I was recited, by Mansur al-Faqih, verses on this meaning:
"Tell whoever has been envious of me: do you know whom you have wronged in manners?
You have wronged Allah in His doing, when you are not pleased with what He has decreed for me.
Your recompense from Him is increases for me, and that you will not attain what you seek."⁴

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our signs – We will surely burn them in a Fire.﴾ "We will cause them to enter a Fire." Hamid ibn Qays recited "nusliyhim" with a fatha on the nun, meaning "We will make them level/equal," and it was said its meaning is "We will burn them." In this reading, "nāran" is in the accusative by removal of the preposition, its implied sense being "with a Fire."

﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins﴾, other than the burned skins. Ibn 'Abbas said: They will be replaced with white skins like sheets of paper. Nafi' narrated from Ibn 'Umar who said: A man recited before 'Umar "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins." 'Umar said: "Repeat it." He repeated it. Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: "I have its explanation: they are replaced a hundred times in one hour." 'Umar said: "Thus I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say."

Hisham narrated from al-Hasan concerning His words: "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins." He said: "It (the fire) consumes them every day seventy thousand times; every time it consumes them and roasts them, it is said to them: 'Return,' and they return as they were."

Al-Musayyib narrated from al-A'mash from Mujahid who said: Between their skin, their flesh and their blood there are worms, and their skin is renewed like the skin of wild donkeys.

Al-A'mash narrated from Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The skin of the disbeliever is forty-two cubits thick, and his molar is like Uhud."⁵

If it is said: How could a skin be punished when it did not disobey? We say: Sin and pain fall upon the self, not the skin, for skins only feel pain through the spirits. And the proof that the punishment targets the bodies, and does not punish the skins, is His saying: ﴿so that they may taste the punishment﴾,⁶ and He did not say "so that it may taste the punishment."

It was also said: The meaning is: He replaces skins which are those same burned skins. This is because "other" (ghayr) is of two kinds: other in the sense of contrast, other in the sense of difference, and other in the sense of transformation. "Other" of contrast is like your saying to the goldsmith: "Make for me from this ring another ring," and he breaks it and forges you a ring; the forged ring is the first, but the workmanship has changed, while the silver is the same.

This is like your recollection of a brother of yours who was healthy, then you see him afterwards sick and wasted, and you say: "How are you?" He says: "I am not as you knew me." He is the same, but his condition has changed. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿On the day when the earth will be changed to a different earth﴾,⁷ and it is that same earth, except that its mountains, hills, rivers and trees have been changed. And a poet recited:
"The people are not the people you knew, nor is the dwelling the dwelling you used to know."

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Nasir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Muzahim say: I heard Muzahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sharidah al-Kishi say: I heard Jabir ibn Zayd say: I heard Waki' ibn al-Jarrah say: I heard Isra'il say: I heard al-Sha'bi say: A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "Do you not see what 'A'ishah has done? She has disparaged her age," for she recited the two verses of Labid:
"Gone are those in whose shelter one lived; and I remain in a later generation like the skin of a mangy camel.
They take their pleasure in licentiousness and abasement, and whoever speaks is reproached, even if he does not make trouble."
Then she said: "May Allah have mercy on Labid. How would he be if he had lived in our time?"
Ibn 'Abbas said to him: "If 'A'ishah disparaged her age, then 'Ad disparaged its age. For a arrow as long as the longest spear was found in the treasury of 'Ad after they had perished, with written on it:
'Is there any way for me to return to the sands of Dhu al-Liwa... the Liwa of the sand, before the death of the hearts?
Lands in which we dwelt, and we were of its people, when the people were people and the lands were lands.'"
The lands remain as they are, except that their conditions and the conditions of their people have changed.⁸

The wise said: Just as the skin is renewed before resurrection, so it is changed in this way.

Al-Suddi said: The skins are only replaced by other skins, from the flesh of the disbeliever: the skin returns to flesh, and from the flesh another skin emerges, which is not a replacement for a skin that committed no sin.

It was also said: By "skins" is meant their garments of tar, so called because they cling to their skins; just as one says of a thing that belongs to a person, "it is the skin between his bone and his face." So whenever the garments burn, he is punished.

The poet said:
"Meanness clothed Taym in green skins; so woe to Taym because of their green garments."
Thus he referred to their skins by the garments.

'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya said: Allah the Exalted replaces the people of the Fire with skins that do not feel pain, and their ash becomes a punishment for them; so whenever their skin is burned, Allah replaces it with another. This is a punishment for them, as He said: ﴿Their garments are of tar﴾,⁹ so the garments cause them pain while they do not feel pain.

﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds...﴾ up to His saying ﴿shade, dense shade﴾: dense, which the sun does not heat.

﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners.﴾ It was revealed concerning 'Uthman ibn Talhah al-Hajabi of the Banu 'Abd al-Dar, who was the custodian of the Ka'bah. When the Prophet (ﷺ) entered Makkah on the day of the Conquest, 'Uthman closed the door of the House and climbed onto the roof. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked for the key, and it was said that it was with 'Uthman. 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) asked him for it, and he replied: "If I had known that he was the Messenger of Allah, I would not have withheld the key from him." 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) twisted his arm, took the key from him, and opened the door. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered and prayed two rak'ahs within it. When he came out, al-'Abbas asked him to give him the key and to combine for him the watering of the pilgrims with the custodianship; then Allah revealed this verse. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded 'Ali to return the key to 'Uthman, and 'Ali did so, (may Allah be pleased with him).

'Uthman said to him: "O 'Ali, you disliked and harmed me, then you came gently." He said to him: "Because of what Allah revealed concerning you," and he recited this verse to him.

'Uthman said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," and he embraced Islam. Then Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "As long as this House has a first brick standing, the key and the custodianship will be with the sons of 'Uthman," and it is today in their hands.

﴿And when you judge between people, to judge with justice. Excellent is that which Allah instructs you. Indeed, Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing.﴾ "O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you."

They differed concerning them. 'Ikrimah said: "Those in authority among you are Abu Bakr and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them)." What supports this is what Malik ibn Anas narrated from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqbari from Abu Shurayh al-Ka'bi that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Follow the two after me, Abu Bakr and 'Umar. Indeed, I have two ministers in heaven and two ministers on earth. In heaven they are Jibril and Mika'il; on earth they are Abu Bakr and 'Umar." And they are to me like the head to the body! Their likeness in this world, in kindness, is that Abu Bakr is like Abraham and Jesus. Abraham said: ﴿Whoever follows me is of me﴾,¹⁰ and Jesus said: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants﴾,¹¹ and so on. And 'Umar is like Moses and Noah. Moses said: ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth﴾,¹² and Noah said: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant﴾.¹³

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: They are the rightly-guided caliphs: Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Ali (peace be upon them). What supports this is what Hushaym narrated from Ibn Bashir from Abu al-Zubayr from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The caliphate after me among my community is in four: in Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Ali."

Sa'id ibn Jumhan narrated from Safinah, freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) built the mosque, Abu Bakr came with a stone and placed it; then 'Umar came with a stone and placed it; then 'Uthman came with a stone and placed it. He said: "These are the rulers after me."

'Ata': They are the Muhajirun and the Ansar and the Successors in excellence, as evidence for His saying: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Muhajirun and the Ansar...﴾ the verse.

Bakr ibn 'Abdullah al-Muzani: They are the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). What supports this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "My Companions are like stars; whichever of them you follow, you will be guided."

It is narrated from al-Hasan that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of my Companions among people is like salt in food; when salt is gone, the food is spoiled."

Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Mujahid, al-Mubarak ibn Fudalah and Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid: They are the jurists and scholars, the people of religion and virtue, who teach people the landmarks of their religion and command you to good and forbid you from evil; Allah made obedience to them obligatory upon the servants.

This is the report of 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn 'Abbas, which is the evidence for this interpretation.

His saying: ﴿But if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them...﴾ the verse.

Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali said: Nothing is more honourable than knowledge: kings rule over people, and scholars rule over kings.

Ibn Kaysan: They are the people of intellect and opinion who concern themselves with the affairs of people.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The foundation of religion is built upon the intellect, the obligations were imposed upon the intellect, our Lord is known by the intellect and approached by the intellect; the intellectual person is nearer to his Lord than all the diligent ones without intellect, and the weight of an atom of an intellectual person's righteousness is better than the struggle of an ignorant one for a thousand years.

It is narrated from Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Malik who said: al-Thawri said: Allah revealed to one of the prophets: "When you see an intelligent person, be a servant to him."

Maymun ibn Mihran, Muqatil and al-Suddi and al-Sha'bi: They are the commanders of the expeditions.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Khalid ibn al-Walid in a expedition against a tribe of the Arabs, and 'Ammar ibn Yasir was with him. Khalid marched until, when he approached the people, he camped so as to advise them; then a warner came to them and they fled, except one man who had embraced Islam. He ordered his companions to prepare for departure, then went off until he came to Khalid's army and entered upon 'Ammar, and said: "O Abu al-Yaqzan, I am a Muslim, and when my people heard of you they fled; I stayed behind, and my word and my benefit to you is that I stay, or I flee as my people fled."

He said: "Remain, for that will benefit you." The man returned to his family and ordered them to stay. Khalid rose in the morning and came upon the people, and found none but that man; he seized him and seized his property. 'Ammar came to him and said: "Release the man, for he is a Muslim, and I had granted him protection and ordered him to remain."

Khalid said: "You grant protection against me, and I am the commander." He said: "Yes, I grant protection against you, and I am the commander." There was an argument between them, and they went back to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him of the man's affair. The Prophet (ﷺ) granted the man safety, and approved 'Ammar's protection, and afterwards forbade him to command anyone without his permission.

He said: Then 'Ammar and Khalid quarrelled in front of the Prophet (ﷺ); 'Ammar spoke harshly to Khalid, and Khalid became angry and said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you leave this slave to revile me? By Allah, if it were not for you, 'Ammar would not have reviled me." 'Ammar was a freedman of Hashim ibn al-Mughirah.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Khalid, leave 'Ammar alone, for whoever reviles 'Ammar, Allah reviles him, and whoever hates 'Ammar, Allah hates him." Then 'Ammar stood up and Khalid followed him, took hold of his garment and asked him to be pleased with him, and he was pleased with him.

Then Allah revealed this verse and commanded obedience to those in authority.

Abu Hurayrah and Ibn Zayd said: They are the commanders and rulers, since they were commanded to render trusts to the subjects; by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners﴾, the subjects are commanded to show good obedience to them.

'Ali, may Allah honour his face, said: "It is incumbent upon the imam to judge by what Allah has revealed and to render the trust; when he does so, it is incumbent upon the subjects to listen to him, obey him, and respond when called."

Al-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Those Arabs around Makkah did not know of rulers, and they would disdain to give obedience to one another's rulership. When they submitted to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in obedience, they did not think it proper for anyone other than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so they were commanded to obey those in authority.

'Ikrimah said: The mothers of children are free by the Qur'an.
