When *ahl* returns to *al-qarya* (القرية, "the town"), the act attributed to it becomes equivalent to its own act, as in the saying: *marartu bi-l-rajuli al-wāsi'atin dāruhu* (مررت بالرجل الواسعة داره), "I passed by the man whose house is spacious," and *marartu bi-rajulin ḥasanatin 'aynuhu* (مررت برجل حسنة عينه), "I passed by a man whose eye is beautiful."

﴿And appoint for us from Yourself a protector, and appoint for us from Yourself a helper﴾, one who will protect us from the polytheists. So God answered their supplication.

When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) conquered Mecca, God made the Prophet a protector for them, and he appointed 'Attab ibn Asid over it. God made him a helper for them, and he would give the weak their due from the strong, so God granted them victory through him and aided them, and they became more honored there than the oppressors had been before.

In this verse there is evidence refuting the view of one who claims that the servant gains nothing by supplication, because God, exalted is He, related that they supplicated Him, and He answered them and gave them what they asked. Had He not answered their supplication, there would be no point in mentioning their supplication. And God knows best.

﴿Those who believe fight in the way of God﴾, that is, in His obedience; ﴿and those who disbelieve fight in the way of the Taghut﴾, that is, in the obedience of Satan. ﴿So fight, O believers, against the allies of Satan﴾, that is, his party and his soldiers. ﴿Indeed, the plot of Satan is ever weak﴾, meaning his scheme, his deception, his handiwork, and the deception of those who follow him, just as He forsook them on the Day of Badr.

﴿Have you not seen those to whom it was said: "Restrain your hands"﴾.

Al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf al-Zuhri, al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad al-Kindi, Qudama ibn Maz'un al-Jumahi, and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas al-Zuhri. They were suffering great harm from the polytheists while they were in Mecca, before they migrated to Medina. They complained to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, permit us to fight these people, for they have harmed us." He would say to them: "Restrain your hands [from them]" [[Added in the source.]] "for I have not been commanded to fight them." [[Asbab al-Nuzul al-Ayat: 111.]] [371]

When they migrated to Medina, God commanded them to fight the polytheists, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) commanded them to march to Badr. When they realized it was fighting, some of them disliked it and it was hard on them. So God, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those to whom it was said: "Restrain your hands [from fighting]" [in Mecca], and establish prayer and give zakat? But when fighting was prescribed for them [in Medina] [behold], a party of them fear men as they fear God or with greater fear.﴾ That is, greater in fear. Those men are the polytheists of Mecca.

It was also said: "or [with] a greater fear," like His saying in another verse: ﴿And they say, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? Why did You not delay us to a near term?"﴾ That is, why did You make fighting obligatory for us? "Why did You not delay us to a near term," meaning death: why did You not leave us until we die at our appointed times?

They differed concerning His saying, exalted is He, ﴿when a party of them﴾. Some people said: it was revealed concerning the hypocrites, because their saying ﴿why have You prescribed fighting for us?﴾, meaning why You made it obligatory, does not befit the believers, and likewise fear of other than God.

Some of them said: rather it was revealed concerning a group of believers who were not firmly rooted in knowledge, and the people of faith differ in their degrees of faith: among them is the perfect one whose faith does not free him from the dominance of his natural disposition; and among them is one who falls short of that state, so he shrinks from what he is commanded to do when hardship befalls him in it.

It was also said: it was revealed concerning a people who were believers, but when jihad was made obligatory upon them, they became hypocrites regarding jihad out of cowardice, and they stayed behind from jihad.

What supports this is that God does not require the disbeliever and the hypocrite to observe the laws; rather He requires them first to have faith, and then the laws. So when they became hypocrites, God drew attention to their conditions.

God has indeed spoken, informing about the hypocrites: ﴿that they believed, then they disbelieved﴾.

Say, O Muhammad, to them: ﴿The enjoyment of this world is little﴾, that is, its benefit and the enjoyment of it; ﴿and the Hereafter﴾, meaning the reward of the Hereafter, ﴿is better﴾, more excellent, ﴿for those who fear God﴾, who avoid associating partners with God and rejecting the Messenger's prophethood; ﴿and you will not be wronged [even as much as] a fatil﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ali ibn al-Hakam said: the *fatīl* (فتيل) is the thread that is in the cleft of a date stone.

﴿Wherever you are, death will overtake you﴾, that is, it will descend upon you. It was revealed concerning the saying of the hypocrites when the people of Uhud were struck: ﴿If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed.﴾ So God refuted them with His saying: ﴿Wherever you are, death will overtake you, even if you should be within towers well-constructed.﴾

Qatada said: in fortified palaces. 'Ikrima said: plastered and decorated. Al-Qutabi said: lofty.

Al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: *al-burūj* (البروج) are the fortresses, the strongholds, and the citadels.

In this verse there is a refutation of the people of *qadar* (أهل القدر, i.e., those who deny or limit divine decree), because God related that the disbelievers said: ﴿If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed﴾ [[Surat Al 'Imran: 156.]] and said: ﴿God has bestowed favor upon me since I was not with them as a witness.﴾ He refuted both groups with His saying: ﴿Wherever you are, death will overtake you﴾, thereby making them know that when the appointed terms come to an end, the departure of the soul from the bodies is inevitable.

If that happens through killing, then it is so; otherwise it is through death. This is contrary to what the Mu'tazila (المعتزلة, a rationalist theological school) claimed: that this slain person, had this killer not killed him, would have lived. Thus their view agreed with that of the disbelievers, and God refuted them all together.

﴿If good befalls them﴾ [to the end of the verse]. It was revealed concerning the hypocrites and the Jews, because they said when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) arrived in Medina: "We have continued to notice a decrease in our fruits and our fields since this man and his companions came to us." So God, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And if good befalls them﴾, meaning the Jews and the hypocrites, that is, fertility [and abundance] [[Thus in the manuscript.]] and cheapness of prices, ﴿they say, "This is from God"﴾; ﴿and if evil befalls them﴾, meaning drought, high prices, and failure of rain, ﴿they say, "This is from you [Muhammad]"﴾, that is, from the people of Muhammad and his companions.

Some of them said: its meaning is: ﴿If good befalls them﴾, meaning victory and booty, ﴿they say, "This is from God"﴾; and ﴿if evil befalls them﴾, meaning by killing and defeat, ﴿they say, "This is from you"﴾, [it was] revealed: "This is what you, O Muhammad, have brought upon us." Say: ﴿Each is from God﴾, that is, good and evil are all from God.

Then He reproached them for their ignorance, saying: ﴿So what is [the matter] with these people that they can hardly understand any statement?﴾ That is, the hypocrites and the Jews do not understand any speech except denial of the blessing.

Al-Farra' said: the saying ﴿fa-mā li-hā'ulā'i l-qawmi﴾ (فمال هؤلاء القوم) has been mispronounced in speech, so that they thought the *lām* (اللام) is connected to it and that they are one letter. So in some copies of the Qur'an they separated the *lām* in *hā'ulā'* (هؤلاء), and in some they joined it. The connection is in the recitation, and it is not permissible to pause on the *lām*, because it is a *lām* of genitive (*lām khāfiḍa*, the preposition "li-").

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verse 79–84:

﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾ — i.e., whatever good, favour and blessing (ni'mah) reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil, affliction and matter you dislike befalls you is from yourself, i.e., from you; and it is I who decreed them upon you. The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), but what is meant is others, the like of it.

His saying: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned﴾.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: «There is no scratch from a stick, nor twitching of a vein, nor stumble of a foot, except that it is due to a sin, and what Allah forgives is more.» [[Kanz al-Ummal: 3/341, no. 6849, with transposition of phrases; in full in Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/138.]] [372].

Al-Harawi related from Sufyan ibn Sa'id, from one who heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say: A man does not memorise the Qur'an and then forget it except because of a sin. Then he recited ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾, and said: So forgetting the Qur'an is the greatest of afflictions.

Some said: This verse is connected to what precedes it, and its sense is: What is wrong with these people that they do not understand any statement, so that they say: ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾? The people of qadar (divine decree) clung to this verse and said: Allah negated evil from Himself by His saying ﴿and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾, and attributed it to the servant. It is said to them: What Allah related to His Prophet of the words of the hypocrites, that when a good befell them they said, "This is from Allah," and if an evil befell them they said, "This is from you" — it did not refer to the good and evil of acquisition (kasb), nor their evils, because what is from you is the action of another upon you, not your own action; for that reason it is attributed to someone other than you.

As He said: ﴿If good touches you, it grieves them; and if an evil befalls you, they rejoice at it﴾ [[Surah Al 'Imran: 120.]] ... ﴿And if an evil befalls them, they attribute it omen to Musa and those with him﴾ [[al-A'raf: 131.]]. All of these are causes from among the causes, not from acquisition. Do you not see that He attributed them to others, and did not mention reward or punishment with them? When He mentioned the good deeds and evil deeds of acquisition, He attributed them to you and mentioned reward and punishment in them.

Like His saying: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like, and whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like﴾ [[Surah al-An'am: 160.]]. And what Allah related of the hypocrites' saying about the good and evil was not the good and evil of acquisition; then His statement following it, ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah﴾, was joined to ﴿from yourself﴾ — so by His saying ﴿from yourself﴾ He did not affirm what He had negated, nor negate what He had affirmed, because that is not permissible for the Wise, exalted is His majesty. Rather, it is from the cause that made this affliction deserved, and that was from his acquisition. From this is His saying: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned﴾, where He made this affliction a recompense for the act; and when a recompense is applied, it is applied only to what He attributed to the servants, like His saying: ﴿a reward for what they used to do﴾, ﴿a reward for what they used to earn﴾ [[Surah al-Tawbah: 82.]]. As for His saying: ﴿And whatever evil befalls you, it is from yourself﴾, there is no evidence in it that He does not will the evil or does not do it; rather, it is what was a recompense, so it is attributed to the servant by way of recompense.

﴿And We have sent you to mankind as a Messenger﴾ — O Muhammad — ﴿and Allah suffices as a witness﴾ that you are a truthful Messenger.

It has also been said regarding it: ﴿And Allah suffices as a witness﴾ that good and evil are all from Allah. ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾.

That is because the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: «Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever loves me [Allah loves him]» [[In the source: "then he has loved Allah."]] [[Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 2/158.]] [373]. Then some of the hypocrites said: This man only wants us to take him as a lord, as in the case of the Christians with 'Isa. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger in what he commands, has obeyed Allah; and whoever turns away — We have not sent you as a guardian over them﴾, i.e., a protector and a watcher.

al-Qutabi said: a reckoner (muhasib). Then Allah abrogated this noble verse and commanded him to fight whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger.

﴿And they say, "Obedience"﴾ — meaning the hypocrites; that is because they used to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "We have believed in you, so command us, (our) obedience," while they disbelieved in him in secret. His saying ﴿ṭā'ah﴾ (obedience) is in the nominative, in the sense of "ours is obedience" and "your command is obedience"; likewise His saying ﴿Do not swear, obedience﴾ is in the nominative, i.e., say: "We hear and obey." Likewise His saying ﴿So for them is obedience and a known word﴾ [Surah Muhammad: 21]; it is not raised to them, but from Me it is raised in the manner I have mentioned.

﴿So when they go out from your presence﴾, i.e., they depart, ﴿a party of them plots a course other than what you say﴾, i.e., they falsify and embellish; and it has been said here:

Qatadah and al-Kalbi said: ﴿bayyata﴾ means they changed and altered what the Prophet (ﷺ) had enjoined upon them, and the cause is the meaning of alteration.

The poet said:

"They altered my words concerning 'Abd al-Malik — may Allah curse him, a disbelieving servant."  [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/289; Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/368, where it reads: "may Allah curse you, a rebellious servant."]]

Al-Qutabi and Abu 'Ubaydah said: ﴿A party of them plotted﴾ means they said and planned by night what they had given you assurance of by day; and every matter planned at night with evil is called tabyit (plotting by night).

'Ubayd ibn al-Hammam said:

"They came to me, but I was not pleased with what they plotted, and they had come to me with a shameful matter,
To marry their unmarried woman to a warner — and does a free man marry a slave to a free woman?" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/289; Lisan al-'Arab: 5/234.]]

Al-Nimr ibn Tawlab said:

"Be silent, you who blame me by night, listen;
Let your blame keep you wakeful — so sleep."

Abu al-Hasan Sa'id ibn Mas'adah al-Akhfash said: The Arabs say of a thing once it has been planned that it has been plotted (bayyata), likening its planning to the arranging of houses (buyut) [the poetry].

﴿And Allah records what they plot﴾, i.e., what they alter, falsify and plan.

Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas: it means what they conceal of hypocrisy. ﴿So turn away from them﴾, O Muhammad, and do not punish them; ﴿and put your trust in Allah; and Allah suffices as a trustee﴾, i.e., a guarantor, a reliance, and a helper in avenging you upon them. Then Allah abrogated His saying ﴿so turn away from them﴾ with His saying: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers﴾ [[Surah al-Tawbah: 73.]] with the sword, ﴿and the hypocrites﴾ with harsh speech.

If it is said: What is the wisdom in [the change of] the address? He mentioned their group, then said ﴿a party of them plotted﴾, turning the address from the whole of them to some of them.

It is said: It is only that He spoke of the condition of one whom Allah knew remained upon his disbelief and hypocrisy; as for one whom He knew would return from that, He pardoned mention of him. And it has been said: He spoke of a condition of theirs that was concealed in its matter; as for one who heard and remained silent, He did not mention him.

His saying ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ is evidence refuting the view of one who claims that the Sunnah is presented to the Book and, if it is not acted upon, is not followed. For everything Allah the Mighty and Majestic has stated explicitly becomes an obligation through the Book; when the explicit text is absent from the Book and the Sunnah has come with it, then following it is obligatory; whoever opposes it has opposed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and whoever opposes the Messenger has opposed Allah, because in obeying the Messenger is obeying Allah. So whoever claims that he will not accept his report unless it is first presented to the Book of Allah has nullified every ruling that came from him that the Book did not explicitly state.

As for His saying ﴿And they say, "Obedience"﴾, it contains evidence that whoever does not believe in obedience is not truly obedient; for Allah the Exalted has taken their obedience as established by what they displayed, saying "they say that," because if obedience had a reality only by belief, He would not have judged them by it. Thus it is established that one is not obedient except by belief in obedience together with its existence.

﴿Do they not ponder the Qur'an?﴾ — i.e., do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, so that they see part of it resembles part, and part confirms part, and that no creature could have produced it? They will then know by that that it is from Allah: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy﴾, i.e., much variation and contradiction. This is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas.

Some said: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it﴾, i.e., in the reports of what is hidden from them of what has been and what will be, ﴿much discrepancy﴾, meaning clear variation. Since the unseen is known only to Allah, they will know by that that it is the speech of Allah and that Muhammad is the truthful Messenger of Allah. In this verse there is evidence that the Qur'an is not created, since it is free of defects from every aspect; and if it were created, it would not be free of discrepancy and variation.

﴿And when there comes to them a matter of security or fear﴾ — the verse. This is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to dispatch expeditions (sariyyah); when they prevailed or were overcome, the hypocrites would hasten to inquire about the condition of the expeditions, and they would spread it and speak of it before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) related it. So Allah revealed: ﴿And when there comes to them﴾, i.e., the hypocrites, ﴿a matter of security﴾ [such as the victory of the Muslims and the killing of their enemy] ﴿or fear﴾ such as defeat and killing, ﴿they spread it﴾, i.e., they publicised and disseminated it. ﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them﴾, i.e., even if they had not related it or spread it, until the Prophet (ﷺ) himself would relate it and disseminate it. And "those of authority" (ulu al-amr) are the people of opinion among the Companions, such as Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them.

﴿Would have known it, those who draw it out﴾.

Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih and Ibn 'Abbas, and 'Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Dahhak: ﴿yastanbitunahu﴾ means they follow it.

'Ikrimah said: they are eager for it and ask about it. Ibn 'Ubaydah and al-Qutabi said: they bring it out; it is said: "istanbata" (he extracted) the water when he brought it out.

Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying ﴿And when there comes to them a matter of security or fear, they spread it﴾: the hypocrites, when commanded to fight, did not obey Allah in what He commanded them; and if He forbade them His prohibitions, they did not refrain; and if the Messenger confided to them in secret, they spread it to the enemy by night, with concealment. So Allah the Exalted revealed in reply to them: ﴿And if they had referred it﴾, i.e., their matters concerning the lawful and unlawful, ﴿to the Messenger﴾ in confirming it and accepting it, ﴿and to those of authority among them﴾, i.e., the bearers of jurisprudence and wisdom, ﴿would have known it, those among them who draw it out﴾, i.e., those who investigate knowledge. Then He said: ﴿And were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except a few﴾, i.e., its meaning is: you would all have followed Satan.

Al-Dahhak said: they are the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), whom he would command with a matter of the affairs of Satan.

Ibn 'Abbas said: the bounty of Allah is Islam, and His mercy is the Qur'an. ﴿You would have followed Satan, except a few﴾ — by the few whom Allah tested their hearts. In accordance with this view, His saying ﴿except a few﴾ is an exception from His saying ﴿you would have followed Satan﴾.

Some said: there is inversion and reordering in the verse; its meaning is: ﴿would have known it, those who draw it out, except a few﴾.

Some said: its meaning is: if they spread a little of it, it was not spread or disseminated; this is what al-Kalbi said, and al-Farra' also chose this view, saying: because the knowledge of Allah encompasses both those who draw it out and others, and dissemination may occur in some of them and not others; therefore he preferred the exception to refer to the dissemination. In this verse there is evidence for those who hold the view of ijtihad (independent reasoning) in the absence of an explicit text.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them, those among them who draw it out would have known it.﴾ So knowledge encompasses extraction (istinbat), not recitation.

And if its apprehension is by extraction, this shows that some knowledge is apprehended by recitation and transmission, which is the explicit text; and some of it is apprehended from both the text and its meaning. The reality of consideration (i'tibar) and extraction is analogy (qiyas) for deriving a ruling from the meanings deposited in the texts, which is other than deriving a ruling from the texts themselves.

﴿So fight in the way of Allah; you are not burdened except with yourself﴾. That was because when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Sufyan ibn Harb met at the Battle of Uhud, and their flight was what it was, Abu Sufyan returned to Mecca and promised the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) an encounter at the Lesser Badr in Dhu al-Qa'dah. When the appointed time arrived, the people said: "Go out to the enemy."

They disliked that greatly, or some of them did, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿So fight in the way of Allah; you are not burdened except with yourself﴾, i.e., do not abandon jihad against the enemy and the defence of the oppressed believers, even if you are alone.

It has been said: its meaning is: you are not obliged to the deeds of others, nor held accountable for them; and by "burdening" He did not mean command, because on this view it would imply that others are not commanded to fight.

The fa' in His saying ﴿fa-qatil﴾ is a response to His saying ﴿And whoever fights in the way of Allah and is killed or overcomes, We will give him a great reward﴾. So fight, ﴿and urge the believers﴾ to fight, i.e., urge them to jihad and encourage them to it.

They were slow to it and did not go out with him to fight. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out with seventy riders until he reached the appointed place at Badr; Allah restrained the enemy's might from them, and Abu Sufyan did not meet them, nor was he able to; so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions returned.

That is His saying: ﴿It may be that Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve﴾, i.e., the fighting of the polytheists and their assault, ﴿when you turned away﴾; and it is from Allah a binding promise wherever it is, and it has come in the speech of the Arabs with the meaning of certainty.

Ibn Muqbil said:

"My assumption that they are like 'asā (perhaps), and they are leaping from the earth, vying for the prizes of the tales."  [[Here the text reads thus in the original and in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/294 and the source. "Tanufah" is leaping from the ground; see Lisan al-'Arab: 5/327, where the verse appears.]]

﴿And Allah is mightier in might﴾, i.e., greater in assault, greater in authority, and more capable of what He wills, ﴿and mightier in punishment﴾ or retribution.

If it is said: If, as you say, "perhaps" (asā) from Allah is binding, then He said ﴿It may be that Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve﴾, and we see them in might and hardship — where is that promise? It is said to them: It has been said that it refers to the disbelievers whose might was restrained at the Lesser Badr and at Hudaybiyyah, by His saying ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you﴾ [Surah al-Fath: 24] — the verse. If its apparent meaning is generality, then what is meant by it is particularity.

It has also been said: He meant by it the period in which Allah commanded fighting until disbelief disappears, by His saying ﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah and religion is entirely for Allah﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 39]. Then at that time the might of those who disbelieve will be restrained, and that is the time in which al-Mahdi will descend, so he will be a just ruler, and Islam will prevail over all religion.

It has also been said: that refers to the people upon whom Allah cast terror into their hearts and expelled them from their homes and wealth without fighting by the believers against them; and this is a might which Allah has restrained from the believers.

It has also been said: He meant by it the Jews and Christians, who pay the jizyah and have abandoned fighting; their might has been restrained from the believers when they pay the jizyah in humiliation.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verse 79–84:

﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾ — i.e., whatever good, favour and blessing (ni'mah) reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil, affliction and matter you dislike befalls you is from yourself, i.e., from you; and it is I who decreed them upon you. The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), but what is meant is others, the like of it.

His saying: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned﴾.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: «There is no scratch from a stick, nor twitching of a vein, nor stumble of a foot, except that it is due to a sin, and what Allah forgives is more.» [[Kanz al-Ummal: 3/341, no. 6849, with transposition of phrases; in full in Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/138.]] [372].

Al-Harawi related from Sufyan ibn Sa'id, from one who heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say: A man does not memorise the Qur'an and then forget it except because of a sin. Then he recited ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾, and said: So forgetting the Qur'an is the greatest of afflictions.

Some said: This verse is connected to what precedes it, and its sense is: What is wrong with these people that they do not understand any statement, so that they say: ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾? The people of qadar (divine decree) clung to this verse and said: Allah negated evil from Himself by His saying ﴿and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾, and attributed it to the servant. It is said to them: What Allah related to His Prophet of the words of the hypocrites, that when a good befell them they said, "This is from Allah," and if an evil befell them they said, "This is from you" — it did not refer to the good and evil of acquisition (kasb), nor their evils, because what is from you is the action of another upon you, not your own action; for that reason it is attributed to someone other than you.

As He said: ﴿If good touches you, it grieves them; and if an evil befalls you, they rejoice at it﴾ [[Surah Al 'Imran: 120.]] ... ﴿And if an evil befalls them, they attribute it omen to Musa and those with him﴾ [[al-A'raf: 131.]]. All of these are causes from among the causes, not from acquisition. Do you not see that He attributed them to others, and did not mention reward or punishment with them? When He mentioned the good deeds and evil deeds of acquisition, He attributed them to you and mentioned reward and punishment in them.

Like His saying: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like, and whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like﴾ [[Surah al-An'am: 160.]]. And what Allah related of the hypocrites' saying about the good and evil was not the good and evil of acquisition; then His statement following it, ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah﴾, was joined to ﴿from yourself﴾ — so by His saying ﴿from yourself﴾ He did not affirm what He had negated, nor negate what He had affirmed, because that is not permissible for the Wise, exalted is His majesty. Rather, it is from the cause that made this affliction deserved, and that was from his acquisition. From this is His saying: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned﴾, where He made this affliction a recompense for the act; and when a recompense is applied, it is applied only to what He attributed to the servants, like His saying: ﴿a reward for what they used to do﴾, ﴿a reward for what they used to earn﴾ [[Surah al-Tawbah: 82.]]. As for His saying: ﴿And whatever evil befalls you, it is from yourself﴾, there is no evidence in it that He does not will the evil or does not do it; rather, it is what was a recompense, so it is attributed to the servant by way of recompense.

﴿And We have sent you to mankind as a Messenger﴾ — O Muhammad — ﴿and Allah suffices as a witness﴾ that you are a truthful Messenger.

It has also been said regarding it: ﴿And Allah suffices as a witness﴾ that good and evil are all from Allah. ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾.

That is because the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: «Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever loves me [Allah loves him]» [[In the source: "then he has loved Allah."]] [[Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 2/158.]] [373]. Then some of the hypocrites said: This man only wants us to take him as a lord, as in the case of the Christians with 'Isa. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger in what he commands, has obeyed Allah; and whoever turns away — We have not sent you as a guardian over them﴾, i.e., a protector and a watcher.

al-Qutabi said: a reckoner (muhasib). Then Allah abrogated this noble verse and commanded him to fight whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger.

﴿And they say, "Obedience"﴾ — meaning the hypocrites; that is because they used to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "We have believed in you, so command us, (our) obedience," while they disbelieved in him in secret. His saying ﴿ṭā'ah﴾ (obedience) is in the nominative, in the sense of "ours is obedience" and "your command is obedience"; likewise His saying ﴿Do not swear, obedience﴾ is in the nominative, i.e., say: "We hear and obey." Likewise His saying ﴿So for them is obedience and a known word﴾ [Surah Muhammad: 21]; it is not raised to them, but from Me it is raised in the manner I have mentioned.

﴿So when they go out from your presence﴾, i.e., they depart, ﴿a party of them plots a course other than what you say﴾, i.e., they falsify and embellish; and it has been said here:

Qatadah and al-Kalbi said: ﴿bayyata﴾ means they changed and altered what the Prophet (ﷺ) had enjoined upon them, and the cause is the meaning of alteration.

The poet said:

"They altered my words concerning 'Abd al-Malik — may Allah curse him, a disbelieving servant."  [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/289; Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/368, where it reads: "may Allah curse you, a rebellious servant."]]

Al-Qutabi and Abu 'Ubaydah said: ﴿A party of them plotted﴾ means they said and planned by night what they had given you assurance of by day; and every matter planned at night with evil is called tabyit (plotting by night).

'Ubayd ibn al-Hammam said:

"They came to me, but I was not pleased with what they plotted, and they had come to me with a shameful matter,
To marry their unmarried woman to a warner — and does a free man marry a slave to a free woman?" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/289; Lisan al-'Arab: 5/234.]]

Al-Nimr ibn Tawlab said:

"Be silent, you who blame me by night, listen;
Let your blame keep you wakeful — so sleep."

Abu al-Hasan Sa'id ibn Mas'adah al-Akhfash said: The Arabs say of a thing once it has been planned that it has been plotted (bayyata), likening its planning to the arranging of houses (buyut) [the poetry].

﴿And Allah records what they plot﴾, i.e., what they alter, falsify and plan.

Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas: it means what they conceal of hypocrisy. ﴿So turn away from them﴾, O Muhammad, and do not punish them; ﴿and put your trust in Allah; and Allah suffices as a trustee﴾, i.e., a guarantor, a reliance, and a helper in avenging you upon them. Then Allah abrogated His saying ﴿so turn away from them﴾ with His saying: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers﴾ [[Surah al-Tawbah: 73.]] with the sword, ﴿and the hypocrites﴾ with harsh speech.

If it is said: What is the wisdom in [the change of] the address? He mentioned their group, then said ﴿a party of them plotted﴾, turning the address from the whole of them to some of them.

It is said: It is only that He spoke of the condition of one whom Allah knew remained upon his disbelief and hypocrisy; as for one whom He knew would return from that, He pardoned mention of him. And it has been said: He spoke of a condition of theirs that was concealed in its matter; as for one who heard and remained silent, He did not mention him.

His saying ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ is evidence refuting the view of one who claims that the Sunnah is presented to the Book and, if it is not acted upon, is not followed. For everything Allah the Mighty and Majestic has stated explicitly becomes an obligation through the Book; when the explicit text is absent from the Book and the Sunnah has come with it, then following it is obligatory; whoever opposes it has opposed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and whoever opposes the Messenger has opposed Allah, because in obeying the Messenger is obeying Allah. So whoever claims that he will not accept his report unless it is first presented to the Book of Allah has nullified every ruling that came from him that the Book did not explicitly state.

As for His saying ﴿And they say, "Obedience"﴾, it contains evidence that whoever does not believe in obedience is not truly obedient; for Allah the Exalted has taken their obedience as established by what they displayed, saying "they say that," because if obedience had a reality only by belief, He would not have judged them by it. Thus it is established that one is not obedient except by belief in obedience together with its existence.

﴿Do they not ponder the Qur'an?﴾ — i.e., do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, so that they see part of it resembles part, and part confirms part, and that no creature could have produced it? They will then know by that that it is from Allah: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy﴾, i.e., much variation and contradiction. This is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas.

Some said: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it﴾, i.e., in the reports of what is hidden from them of what has been and what will be, ﴿much discrepancy﴾, meaning clear variation. Since the unseen is known only to Allah, they will know by that that it is the speech of Allah and that Muhammad is the truthful Messenger of Allah. In this verse there is evidence that the Qur'an is not created, since it is free of defects from every aspect; and if it were created, it would not be free of discrepancy and variation.

﴿And when there comes to them a matter of security or fear﴾ — the verse. This is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to dispatch expeditions (sariyyah); when they prevailed or were overcome, the hypocrites would hasten to inquire about the condition of the expeditions, and they would spread it and speak of it before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) related it. So Allah revealed: ﴿And when there comes to them﴾, i.e., the hypocrites, ﴿a matter of security﴾ [such as the victory of the Muslims and the killing of their enemy] ﴿or fear﴾ such as defeat and killing, ﴿they spread it﴾, i.e., they publicised and disseminated it. ﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them﴾, i.e., even if they had not related it or spread it, until the Prophet (ﷺ) himself would relate it and disseminate it. And "those of authority" (ulu al-amr) are the people of opinion among the Companions, such as Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them.

﴿Would have known it, those who draw it out﴾.

Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih and Ibn 'Abbas, and 'Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Dahhak: ﴿yastanbitunahu﴾ means they follow it.

'Ikrimah said: they are eager for it and ask about it. Ibn 'Ubaydah and al-Qutabi said: they bring it out; it is said: "istanbata" (he extracted) the water when he brought it out.

Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying ﴿And when there comes to them a matter of security or fear, they spread it﴾: the hypocrites, when commanded to fight, did not obey Allah in what He commanded them; and if He forbade them His prohibitions, they did not refrain; and if the Messenger confided to them in secret, they spread it to the enemy by night, with concealment. So Allah the Exalted revealed in reply to them: ﴿And if they had referred it﴾, i.e., their matters concerning the lawful and unlawful, ﴿to the Messenger﴾ in confirming it and accepting it, ﴿and to those of authority among them﴾, i.e., the bearers of jurisprudence and wisdom, ﴿would have known it, those among them who draw it out﴾, i.e., those who investigate knowledge. Then He said: ﴿And were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except a few﴾, i.e., its meaning is: you would all have followed Satan.

Al-Dahhak said: they are the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), whom he would command with a matter of the affairs of Satan.

Ibn 'Abbas said: the bounty of Allah is Islam, and His mercy is the Qur'an. ﴿You would have followed Satan, except a few﴾ — by the few whom Allah tested their hearts. In accordance with this view, His saying ﴿except a few﴾ is an exception from His saying ﴿you would have followed Satan﴾.

Some said: there is inversion and reordering in the verse; its meaning is: ﴿would have known it, those who draw it out, except a few﴾.

Some said: its meaning is: if they spread a little of it, it was not spread or disseminated; this is what al-Kalbi said, and al-Farra' also chose this view, saying: because the knowledge of Allah encompasses both those who draw it out and others, and dissemination may occur in some of them and not others; therefore he preferred the exception to refer to the dissemination. In this verse there is evidence for those who hold the view of ijtihad (independent reasoning) in the absence of an explicit text.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them, those among them who draw it out would have known it.﴾ So knowledge encompasses extraction (istinbat), not recitation.

And if its apprehension is by extraction, this shows that some knowledge is apprehended by recitation and transmission, which is the explicit text; and some of it is apprehended from both the text and its meaning. The reality of consideration (i'tibar) and extraction is analogy (qiyas) for deriving a ruling from the meanings deposited in the texts, which is other than deriving a ruling from the texts themselves.

﴿So fight in the way of Allah; you are not burdened except with yourself﴾. That was because when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Sufyan ibn Harb met at the Battle of Uhud, and their flight was what it was, Abu Sufyan returned to Mecca and promised the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) an encounter at the Lesser Badr in Dhu al-Qa'dah. When the appointed time arrived, the people said: "Go out to the enemy."

They disliked that greatly, or some of them did, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿So fight in the way of Allah; you are not burdened except with yourself﴾, i.e., do not abandon jihad against the enemy and the defence of the oppressed believers, even if you are alone.

It has been said: its meaning is: you are not obliged to the deeds of others, nor held accountable for them; and by "burdening" He did not mean command, because on this view it would imply that others are not commanded to fight.

The fa' in His saying ﴿fa-qatil﴾ is a response to His saying ﴿And whoever fights in the way of Allah and is killed or overcomes, We will give him a great reward﴾. So fight, ﴿and urge the believers﴾ to fight, i.e., urge them to jihad and encourage them to it.

They were slow to it and did not go out with him to fight. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out with seventy riders until he reached the appointed place at Badr; Allah restrained the enemy's might from them, and Abu Sufyan did not meet them, nor was he able to; so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions returned.

That is His saying: ﴿It may be that Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve﴾, i.e., the fighting of the polytheists and their assault, ﴿when you turned away﴾; and it is from Allah a binding promise wherever it is, and it has come in the speech of the Arabs with the meaning of certainty.

Ibn Muqbil said:

"My assumption that they are like 'asā (perhaps), and they are leaping from the earth, vying for the prizes of the tales."  [[Here the text reads thus in the original and in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/294 and the source. "Tanufah" is leaping from the ground; see Lisan al-'Arab: 5/327, where the verse appears.]]

﴿And Allah is mightier in might﴾, i.e., greater in assault, greater in authority, and more capable of what He wills, ﴿and mightier in punishment﴾ or retribution.

If it is said: If, as you say, "perhaps" (asā) from Allah is binding, then He said ﴿It may be that Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve﴾, and we see them in might and hardship — where is that promise? It is said to them: It has been said that it refers to the disbelievers whose might was restrained at the Lesser Badr and at Hudaybiyyah, by His saying ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you﴾ [Surah al-Fath: 24] — the verse. If its apparent meaning is generality, then what is meant by it is particularity.

It has also been said: He meant by it the period in which Allah commanded fighting until disbelief disappears, by His saying ﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah and religion is entirely for Allah﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 39]. Then at that time the might of those who disbelieve will be restrained, and that is the time in which al-Mahdi will descend, so he will be a just ruler, and Islam will prevail over all religion.

It has also been said: that refers to the people upon whom Allah cast terror into their hearts and expelled them from their homes and wealth without fighting by the believers against them; and this is a might which Allah has restrained from the believers.

It has also been said: He meant by it the Jews and Christians, who pay the jizyah and have abandoned fighting; their might has been restrained from the believers when they pay the jizyah in humiliation.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verse 79–84:

﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾ — i.e., whatever good, favour and blessing (ni'mah) reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil, affliction and matter you dislike befalls you is from yourself, i.e., from you; and it is I who decreed them upon you. The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), but what is meant is others, the like of it.

His saying: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned﴾.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: «There is no scratch from a stick, nor twitching of a vein, nor stumble of a foot, except that it is due to a sin, and what Allah forgives is more.» [[Kanz al-Ummal: 3/341, no. 6849, with transposition of phrases; in full in Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/138.]] [372].

Al-Harawi related from Sufyan ibn Sa'id, from one who heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say: A man does not memorise the Qur'an and then forget it except because of a sin. Then he recited ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾, and said: So forgetting the Qur'an is the greatest of afflictions.

Some said: This verse is connected to what precedes it, and its sense is: What is wrong with these people that they do not understand any statement, so that they say: ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾? The people of qadar (divine decree) clung to this verse and said: Allah negated evil from Himself by His saying ﴿and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾, and attributed it to the servant. It is said to them: What Allah related to His Prophet of the words of the hypocrites, that when a good befell them they said, "This is from Allah," and if an evil befell them they said, "This is from you" — it did not refer to the good and evil of acquisition (kasb), nor their evils, because what is from you is the action of another upon you, not your own action; for that reason it is attributed to someone other than you.

As He said: ﴿If good touches you, it grieves them; and if an evil befalls you, they rejoice at it﴾ [[Surah Al 'Imran: 120.]] ... ﴿And if an evil befalls them, they attribute it omen to Musa and those with him﴾ [[al-A'raf: 131.]]. All of these are causes from among the causes, not from acquisition. Do you not see that He attributed them to others, and did not mention reward or punishment with them? When He mentioned the good deeds and evil deeds of acquisition, He attributed them to you and mentioned reward and punishment in them.

Like His saying: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like, and whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like﴾ [[Surah al-An'am: 160.]]. And what Allah related of the hypocrites' saying about the good and evil was not the good and evil of acquisition; then His statement following it, ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah﴾, was joined to ﴿from yourself﴾ — so by His saying ﴿from yourself﴾ He did not affirm what He had negated, nor negate what He had affirmed, because that is not permissible for the Wise, exalted is His majesty. Rather, it is from the cause that made this affliction deserved, and that was from his acquisition. From this is His saying: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned﴾, where He made this affliction a recompense for the act; and when a recompense is applied, it is applied only to what He attributed to the servants, like His saying: ﴿a reward for what they used to do﴾, ﴿a reward for what they used to earn﴾ [[Surah al-Tawbah: 82.]]. As for His saying: ﴿And whatever evil befalls you, it is from yourself﴾, there is no evidence in it that He does not will the evil or does not do it; rather, it is what was a recompense, so it is attributed to the servant by way of recompense.

﴿And We have sent you to mankind as a Messenger﴾ — O Muhammad — ﴿and Allah suffices as a witness﴾ that you are a truthful Messenger.

It has also been said regarding it: ﴿And Allah suffices as a witness﴾ that good and evil are all from Allah. ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾.

That is because the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: «Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever loves me [Allah loves him]» [[In the source: "then he has loved Allah."]] [[Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 2/158.]] [373]. Then some of the hypocrites said: This man only wants us to take him as a lord, as in the case of the Christians with 'Isa. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger in what he commands, has obeyed Allah; and whoever turns away — We have not sent you as a guardian over them﴾, i.e., a protector and a watcher.

al-Qutabi said: a reckoner (muhasib). Then Allah abrogated this noble verse and commanded him to fight whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger.

﴿And they say, "Obedience"﴾ — meaning the hypocrites; that is because they used to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "We have believed in you, so command us, (our) obedience," while they disbelieved in him in secret. His saying ﴿ṭā'ah﴾ (obedience) is in the nominative, in the sense of "ours is obedience" and "your command is obedience"; likewise His saying ﴿Do not swear, obedience﴾ is in the nominative, i.e., say: "We hear and obey." Likewise His saying ﴿So for them is obedience and a known word﴾ [Surah Muhammad: 21]; it is not raised to them, but from Me it is raised in the manner I have mentioned.

﴿So when they go out from your presence﴾, i.e., they depart, ﴿a party of them plots a course other than what you say﴾, i.e., they falsify and embellish; and it has been said here:

Qatadah and al-Kalbi said: ﴿bayyata﴾ means they changed and altered what the Prophet (ﷺ) had enjoined upon them, and the cause is the meaning of alteration.

The poet said:

"They altered my words concerning 'Abd al-Malik — may Allah curse him, a disbelieving servant."  [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/289; Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/368, where it reads: "may Allah curse you, a rebellious servant."]]

Al-Qutabi and Abu 'Ubaydah said: ﴿A party of them plotted﴾ means they said and planned by night what they had given you assurance of by day; and every matter planned at night with evil is called tabyit (plotting by night).

'Ubayd ibn al-Hammam said:

"They came to me, but I was not pleased with what they plotted, and they had come to me with a shameful matter,
To marry their unmarried woman to a warner — and does a free man marry a slave to a free woman?" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/289; Lisan al-'Arab: 5/234.]]

Al-Nimr ibn Tawlab said:

"Be silent, you who blame me by night, listen;
Let your blame keep you wakeful — so sleep."

Abu al-Hasan Sa'id ibn Mas'adah al-Akhfash said: The Arabs say of a thing once it has been planned that it has been plotted (bayyata), likening its planning to the arranging of houses (buyut) [the poetry].

﴿And Allah records what they plot﴾, i.e., what they alter, falsify and plan.

Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas: it means what they conceal of hypocrisy. ﴿So turn away from them﴾, O Muhammad, and do not punish them; ﴿and put your trust in Allah; and Allah suffices as a trustee﴾, i.e., a guarantor, a reliance, and a helper in avenging you upon them. Then Allah abrogated His saying ﴿so turn away from them﴾ with His saying: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers﴾ [[Surah al-Tawbah: 73.]] with the sword, ﴿and the hypocrites﴾ with harsh speech.

If it is said: What is the wisdom in [the change of] the address? He mentioned their group, then said ﴿a party of them plotted﴾, turning the address from the whole of them to some of them.

It is said: It is only that He spoke of the condition of one whom Allah knew remained upon his disbelief and hypocrisy; as for one whom He knew would return from that, He pardoned mention of him. And it has been said: He spoke of a condition of theirs that was concealed in its matter; as for one who heard and remained silent, He did not mention him.

His saying ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ is evidence refuting the view of one who claims that the Sunnah is presented to the Book and, if it is not acted upon, is not followed. For everything Allah the Mighty and Majestic has stated explicitly becomes an obligation through the Book; when the explicit text is absent from the Book and the Sunnah has come with it, then following it is obligatory; whoever opposes it has opposed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and whoever opposes the Messenger has opposed Allah, because in obeying the Messenger is obeying Allah. So whoever claims that he will not accept his report unless it is first presented to the Book of Allah has nullified every ruling that came from him that the Book did not explicitly state.

As for His saying ﴿And they say, "Obedience"﴾, it contains evidence that whoever does not believe in obedience is not truly obedient; for Allah the Exalted has taken their obedience as established by what they displayed, saying "they say that," because if obedience had a reality only by belief, He would not have judged them by it. Thus it is established that one is not obedient except by belief in obedience together with its existence.

﴿Do they not ponder the Qur'an?﴾ — i.e., do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, so that they see part of it resembles part, and part confirms part, and that no creature could have produced it? They will then know by that that it is from Allah: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy﴾, i.e., much variation and contradiction. This is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas.

Some said: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it﴾, i.e., in the reports of what is hidden from them of what has been and what will be, ﴿much discrepancy﴾, meaning clear variation. Since the unseen is known only to Allah, they will know by that that it is the speech of Allah and that Muhammad is the truthful Messenger of Allah. In this verse there is evidence that the Qur'an is not created, since it is free of defects from every aspect; and if it were created, it would not be free of discrepancy and variation.

﴿And when there comes to them a matter of security or fear﴾ — the verse. This is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to dispatch expeditions (sariyyah); when they prevailed or were overcome, the hypocrites would hasten to inquire about the condition of the expeditions, and they would spread it and speak of it before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) related it. So Allah revealed: ﴿And when there comes to them﴾, i.e., the hypocrites, ﴿a matter of security﴾ [such as the victory of the Muslims and the killing of their enemy] ﴿or fear﴾ such as defeat and killing, ﴿they spread it﴾, i.e., they publicised and disseminated it. ﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them﴾, i.e., even if they had not related it or spread it, until the Prophet (ﷺ) himself would relate it and disseminate it. And "those of authority" (ulu al-amr) are the people of opinion among the Companions, such as Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them.

﴿Would have known it, those who draw it out﴾.

Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih and Ibn 'Abbas, and 'Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Dahhak: ﴿yastanbitunahu﴾ means they follow it.

'Ikrimah said: they are eager for it and ask about it. Ibn 'Ubaydah and al-Qutabi said: they bring it out; it is said: "istanbata" (he extracted) the water when he brought it out.

Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying ﴿And when there comes to them a matter of security or fear, they spread it﴾: the hypocrites, when commanded to fight, did not obey Allah in what He commanded them; and if He forbade them His prohibitions, they did not refrain; and if the Messenger confided to them in secret, they spread it to the enemy by night, with concealment. So Allah the Exalted revealed in reply to them: ﴿And if they had referred it﴾, i.e., their matters concerning the lawful and unlawful, ﴿to the Messenger﴾ in confirming it and accepting it, ﴿and to those of authority among them﴾, i.e., the bearers of jurisprudence and wisdom, ﴿would have known it, those among them who draw it out﴾, i.e., those who investigate knowledge. Then He said: ﴿And were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except a few﴾, i.e., its meaning is: you would all have followed Satan.

Al-Dahhak said: they are the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), whom he would command with a matter of the affairs of Satan.

Ibn 'Abbas said: the bounty of Allah is Islam, and His mercy is the Qur'an. ﴿You would have followed Satan, except a few﴾ — by the few whom Allah tested their hearts. In accordance with this view, His saying ﴿except a few﴾ is an exception from His saying ﴿you would have followed Satan﴾.

Some said: there is inversion and reordering in the verse; its meaning is: ﴿would have known it, those who draw it out, except a few﴾.

Some said: its meaning is: if they spread a little of it, it was not spread or disseminated; this is what al-Kalbi said, and al-Farra' also chose this view, saying: because the knowledge of Allah encompasses both those who draw it out and others, and dissemination may occur in some of them and not others; therefore he preferred the exception to refer to the dissemination. In this verse there is evidence for those who hold the view of ijtihad (independent reasoning) in the absence of an explicit text.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them, those among them who draw it out would have known it.﴾ So knowledge encompasses extraction (istinbat), not recitation.

And if its apprehension is by extraction, this shows that some knowledge is apprehended by recitation and transmission, which is the explicit text; and some of it is apprehended from both the text and its meaning. The reality of consideration (i'tibar) and extraction is analogy (qiyas) for deriving a ruling from the meanings deposited in the texts, which is other than deriving a ruling from the texts themselves.

﴿So fight in the way of Allah; you are not burdened except with yourself﴾. That was because when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Sufyan ibn Harb met at the Battle of Uhud, and their flight was what it was, Abu Sufyan returned to Mecca and promised the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) an encounter at the Lesser Badr in Dhu al-Qa'dah. When the appointed time arrived, the people said: "Go out to the enemy."

They disliked that greatly, or some of them did, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿So fight in the way of Allah; you are not burdened except with yourself﴾, i.e., do not abandon jihad against the enemy and the defence of the oppressed believers, even if you are alone.

It has been said: its meaning is: you are not obliged to the deeds of others, nor held accountable for them; and by "burdening" He did not mean command, because on this view it would imply that others are not commanded to fight.

The fa' in His saying ﴿fa-qatil﴾ is a response to His saying ﴿And whoever fights in the way of Allah and is killed or overcomes, We will give him a great reward﴾. So fight, ﴿and urge the believers﴾ to fight, i.e., urge them to jihad and encourage them to it.

They were slow to it and did not go out with him to fight. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out with seventy riders until he reached the appointed place at Badr; Allah restrained the enemy's might from them, and Abu Sufyan did not meet them, nor was he able to; so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions returned.

That is His saying: ﴿It may be that Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve﴾, i.e., the fighting of the polytheists and their assault, ﴿when you turned away﴾; and it is from Allah a binding promise wherever it is, and it has come in the speech of the Arabs with the meaning of certainty.

Ibn Muqbil said:

"My assumption that they are like 'asā (perhaps), and they are leaping from the earth, vying for the prizes of the tales."  [[Here the text reads thus in the original and in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/294 and the source. "Tanufah" is leaping from the ground; see Lisan al-'Arab: 5/327, where the verse appears.]]

﴿And Allah is mightier in might﴾, i.e., greater in assault, greater in authority, and more capable of what He wills, ﴿and mightier in punishment﴾ or retribution.

If it is said: If, as you say, "perhaps" (asā) from Allah is binding, then He said ﴿It may be that Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve﴾, and we see them in might and hardship — where is that promise? It is said to them: It has been said that it refers to the disbelievers whose might was restrained at the Lesser Badr and at Hudaybiyyah, by His saying ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you﴾ [Surah al-Fath: 24] — the verse. If its apparent meaning is generality, then what is meant by it is particularity.

It has also been said: He meant by it the period in which Allah commanded fighting until disbelief disappears, by His saying ﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah and religion is entirely for Allah﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 39]. Then at that time the might of those who disbelieve will be restrained, and that is the time in which al-Mahdi will descend, so he will be a just ruler, and Islam will prevail over all religion.

It has also been said: that refers to the people upon whom Allah cast terror into their hearts and expelled them from their homes and wealth without fighting by the believers against them; and this is a might which Allah has restrained from the believers.

It has also been said: He meant by it the Jews and Christians, who pay the jizyah and have abandoned fighting; their might has been restrained from the believers when they pay the jizyah in humiliation.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verse 79–84:

﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾ — i.e., whatever good, favour and blessing (ni'mah) reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil, affliction and matter you dislike befalls you is from yourself, i.e., from you; and it is I who decreed them upon you. The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), but what is meant is others, the like of it.

His saying: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned﴾.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: «There is no scratch from a stick, nor twitching of a vein, nor stumble of a foot, except that it is due to a sin, and what Allah forgives is more.» [[Kanz al-Ummal: 3/341, no. 6849, with transposition of phrases; in full in Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/138.]] [372].

Al-Harawi related from Sufyan ibn Sa'id, from one who heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say: A man does not memorise the Qur'an and then forget it except because of a sin. Then he recited ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾, and said: So forgetting the Qur'an is the greatest of afflictions.

Some said: This verse is connected to what precedes it, and its sense is: What is wrong with these people that they do not understand any statement, so that they say: ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾? The people of qadar (divine decree) clung to this verse and said: Allah negated evil from Himself by His saying ﴿and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾, and attributed it to the servant. It is said to them: What Allah related to His Prophet of the words of the hypocrites, that when a good befell them they said, "This is from Allah," and if an evil befell them they said, "This is from you" — it did not refer to the good and evil of acquisition (kasb), nor their evils, because what is from you is the action of another upon you, not your own action; for that reason it is attributed to someone other than you.

As He said: ﴿If good touches you, it grieves them; and if an evil befalls you, they rejoice at it﴾ [[Surah Al 'Imran: 120.]] ... ﴿And if an evil befalls them, they attribute it omen to Musa and those with him﴾ [[al-A'raf: 131.]]. All of these are causes from among the causes, not from acquisition. Do you not see that He attributed them to others, and did not mention reward or punishment with them? When He mentioned the good deeds and evil deeds of acquisition, He attributed them to you and mentioned reward and punishment in them.

Like His saying: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like, and whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like﴾ [[Surah al-An'am: 160.]]. And what Allah related of the hypocrites' saying about the good and evil was not the good and evil of acquisition; then His statement following it, ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah﴾, was joined to ﴿from yourself﴾ — so by His saying ﴿from yourself﴾ He did not affirm what He had negated, nor negate what He had affirmed, because that is not permissible for the Wise, exalted is His majesty. Rather, it is from the cause that made this affliction deserved, and that was from his acquisition. From this is His saying: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned﴾, where He made this affliction a recompense for the act; and when a recompense is applied, it is applied only to what He attributed to the servants, like His saying: ﴿a reward for what they used to do﴾, ﴿a reward for what they used to earn﴾ [[Surah al-Tawbah: 82.]]. As for His saying: ﴿And whatever evil befalls you, it is from yourself﴾, there is no evidence in it that He does not will the evil or does not do it; rather, it is what was a recompense, so it is attributed to the servant by way of recompense.

﴿And We have sent you to mankind as a Messenger﴾ — O Muhammad — ﴿and Allah suffices as a witness﴾ that you are a truthful Messenger.

It has also been said regarding it: ﴿And Allah suffices as a witness﴾ that good and evil are all from Allah. ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾.

That is because the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: «Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever loves me [Allah loves him]» [[In the source: "then he has loved Allah."]] [[Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 2/158.]] [373]. Then some of the hypocrites said: This man only wants us to take him as a lord, as in the case of the Christians with 'Isa. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger in what he commands, has obeyed Allah; and whoever turns away — We have not sent you as a guardian over them﴾, i.e., a protector and a watcher.

al-Qutabi said: a reckoner (muhasib). Then Allah abrogated this noble verse and commanded him to fight whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger.

﴿And they say, "Obedience"﴾ — meaning the hypocrites; that is because they used to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "We have believed in you, so command us, (our) obedience," while they disbelieved in him in secret. His saying ﴿ṭā'ah﴾ (obedience) is in the nominative, in the sense of "ours is obedience" and "your command is obedience"; likewise His saying ﴿Do not swear, obedience﴾ is in the nominative, i.e., say: "We hear and obey." Likewise His saying ﴿So for them is obedience and a known word﴾ [Surah Muhammad: 21]; it is not raised to them, but from Me it is raised in the manner I have mentioned.

﴿So when they go out from your presence﴾, i.e., they depart, ﴿a party of them plots a course other than what you say﴾, i.e., they falsify and embellish; and it has been said here:

Qatadah and al-Kalbi said: ﴿bayyata﴾ means they changed and altered what the Prophet (ﷺ) had enjoined upon them, and the cause is the meaning of alteration.

The poet said:

"They altered my words concerning 'Abd al-Malik — may Allah curse him, a disbelieving servant."  [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/289; Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/368, where it reads: "may Allah curse you, a rebellious servant."]]

Al-Qutabi and Abu 'Ubaydah said: ﴿A party of them plotted﴾ means they said and planned by night what they had given you assurance of by day; and every matter planned at night with evil is called tabyit (plotting by night).

'Ubayd ibn al-Hammam said:

"They came to me, but I was not pleased with what they plotted, and they had come to me with a shameful matter,
To marry their unmarried woman to a warner — and does a free man marry a slave to a free woman?" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/289; Lisan al-'Arab: 5/234.]]

Al-Nimr ibn Tawlab said:

"Be silent, you who blame me by night, listen;
Let your blame keep you wakeful — so sleep."

Abu al-Hasan Sa'id ibn Mas'adah al-Akhfash said: The Arabs say of a thing once it has been planned that it has been plotted (bayyata), likening its planning to the arranging of houses (buyut) [the poetry].

﴿And Allah records what they plot﴾, i.e., what they alter, falsify and plan.

Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas: it means what they conceal of hypocrisy. ﴿So turn away from them﴾, O Muhammad, and do not punish them; ﴿and put your trust in Allah; and Allah suffices as a trustee﴾, i.e., a guarantor, a reliance, and a helper in avenging you upon them. Then Allah abrogated His saying ﴿so turn away from them﴾ with His saying: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers﴾ [[Surah al-Tawbah: 73.]] with the sword, ﴿and the hypocrites﴾ with harsh speech.

If it is said: What is the wisdom in [the change of] the address? He mentioned their group, then said ﴿a party of them plotted﴾, turning the address from the whole of them to some of them.

It is said: It is only that He spoke of the condition of one whom Allah knew remained upon his disbelief and hypocrisy; as for one whom He knew would return from that, He pardoned mention of him. And it has been said: He spoke of a condition of theirs that was concealed in its matter; as for one who heard and remained silent, He did not mention him.

His saying ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ is evidence refuting the view of one who claims that the Sunnah is presented to the Book and, if it is not acted upon, is not followed. For everything Allah the Mighty and Majestic has stated explicitly becomes an obligation through the Book; when the explicit text is absent from the Book and the Sunnah has come with it, then following it is obligatory; whoever opposes it has opposed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and whoever opposes the Messenger has opposed Allah, because in obeying the Messenger is obeying Allah. So whoever claims that he will not accept his report unless it is first presented to the Book of Allah has nullified every ruling that came from him that the Book did not explicitly state.

As for His saying ﴿And they say, "Obedience"﴾, it contains evidence that whoever does not believe in obedience is not truly obedient; for Allah the Exalted has taken their obedience as established by what they displayed, saying "they say that," because if obedience had a reality only by belief, He would not have judged them by it. Thus it is established that one is not obedient except by belief in obedience together with its existence.

﴿Do they not ponder the Qur'an?﴾ — i.e., do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, so that they see part of it resembles part, and part confirms part, and that no creature could have produced it? They will then know by that that it is from Allah: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy﴾, i.e., much variation and contradiction. This is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas.

Some said: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it﴾, i.e., in the reports of what is hidden from them of what has been and what will be, ﴿much discrepancy﴾, meaning clear variation. Since the unseen is known only to Allah, they will know by that that it is the speech of Allah and that Muhammad is the truthful Messenger of Allah. In this verse there is evidence that the Qur'an is not created, since it is free of defects from every aspect; and if it were created, it would not be free of discrepancy and variation.

﴿And when there comes to them a matter of security or fear﴾ — the verse. This is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to dispatch expeditions (sariyyah); when they prevailed or were overcome, the hypocrites would hasten to inquire about the condition of the expeditions, and they would spread it and speak of it before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) related it. So Allah revealed: ﴿And when there comes to them﴾, i.e., the hypocrites, ﴿a matter of security﴾ [such as the victory of the Muslims and the killing of their enemy] ﴿or fear﴾ such as defeat and killing, ﴿they spread it﴾, i.e., they publicised and disseminated it. ﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them﴾, i.e., even if they had not related it or spread it, until the Prophet (ﷺ) himself would relate it and disseminate it. And "those of authority" (ulu al-amr) are the people of opinion among the Companions, such as Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them.

﴿Would have known it, those who draw it out﴾.

Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih and Ibn 'Abbas, and 'Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Dahhak: ﴿yastanbitunahu﴾ means they follow it.

'Ikrimah said: they are eager for it and ask about it. Ibn 'Ubaydah and al-Qutabi said: they bring it out; it is said: "istanbata" (he extracted) the water when he brought it out.

Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying ﴿And when there comes to them a matter of security or fear, they spread it﴾: the hypocrites, when commanded to fight, did not obey Allah in what He commanded them; and if He forbade them His prohibitions, they did not refrain; and if the Messenger confided to them in secret, they spread it to the enemy by night, with concealment. So Allah the Exalted revealed in reply to them: ﴿And if they had referred it﴾, i.e., their matters concerning the lawful and unlawful, ﴿to the Messenger﴾ in confirming it and accepting it, ﴿and to those of authority among them﴾, i.e., the bearers of jurisprudence and wisdom, ﴿would have known it, those among them who draw it out﴾, i.e., those who investigate knowledge. Then He said: ﴿And were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except a few﴾, i.e., its meaning is: you would all have followed Satan.

Al-Dahhak said: they are the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), whom he would command with a matter of the affairs of Satan.

Ibn 'Abbas said: the bounty of Allah is Islam, and His mercy is the Qur'an. ﴿You would have followed Satan, except a few﴾ — by the few whom Allah tested their hearts. In accordance with this view, His saying ﴿except a few﴾ is an exception from His saying ﴿you would have followed Satan﴾.

Some said: there is inversion and reordering in the verse; its meaning is: ﴿would have known it, those who draw it out, except a few﴾.

Some said: its meaning is: if they spread a little of it, it was not spread or disseminated; this is what al-Kalbi said, and al-Farra' also chose this view, saying: because the knowledge of Allah encompasses both those who draw it out and others, and dissemination may occur in some of them and not others; therefore he preferred the exception to refer to the dissemination. In this verse there is evidence for those who hold the view of ijtihad (independent reasoning) in the absence of an explicit text.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them, those among them who draw it out would have known it.﴾ So knowledge encompasses extraction (istinbat), not recitation.

And if its apprehension is by extraction, this shows that some knowledge is apprehended by recitation and transmission, which is the explicit text; and some of it is apprehended from both the text and its meaning. The reality of consideration (i'tibar) and extraction is analogy (qiyas) for deriving a ruling from the meanings deposited in the texts, which is other than deriving a ruling from the texts themselves.

﴿So fight in the way of Allah; you are not burdened except with yourself﴾. That was because when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Sufyan ibn Harb met at the Battle of Uhud, and their flight was what it was, Abu Sufyan returned to Mecca and promised the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) an encounter at the Lesser Badr in Dhu al-Qa'dah. When the appointed time arrived, the people said: "Go out to the enemy."

They disliked that greatly, or some of them did, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿So fight in the way of Allah; you are not burdened except with yourself﴾, i.e., do not abandon jihad against the enemy and the defence of the oppressed believers, even if you are alone.

It has been said: its meaning is: you are not obliged to the deeds of others, nor held accountable for them; and by "burdening" He did not mean command, because on this view it would imply that others are not commanded to fight.

The fa' in His saying ﴿fa-qatil﴾ is a response to His saying ﴿And whoever fights in the way of Allah and is killed or overcomes, We will give him a great reward﴾. So fight, ﴿and urge the believers﴾ to fight, i.e., urge them to jihad and encourage them to it.

They were slow to it and did not go out with him to fight. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out with seventy riders until he reached the appointed place at Badr; Allah restrained the enemy's might from them, and Abu Sufyan did not meet them, nor was he able to; so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions returned.

That is His saying: ﴿It may be that Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve﴾, i.e., the fighting of the polytheists and their assault, ﴿when you turned away﴾; and it is from Allah a binding promise wherever it is, and it has come in the speech of the Arabs with the meaning of certainty.

Ibn Muqbil said:

"My assumption that they are like 'asā (perhaps), and they are leaping from the earth, vying for the prizes of the tales."  [[Here the text reads thus in the original and in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/294 and the source. "Tanufah" is leaping from the ground; see Lisan al-'Arab: 5/327, where the verse appears.]]

﴿And Allah is mightier in might﴾, i.e., greater in assault, greater in authority, and more capable of what He wills, ﴿and mightier in punishment﴾ or retribution.

If it is said: If, as you say, "perhaps" (asā) from Allah is binding, then He said ﴿It may be that Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve﴾, and we see them in might and hardship — where is that promise? It is said to them: It has been said that it refers to the disbelievers whose might was restrained at the Lesser Badr and at Hudaybiyyah, by His saying ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you﴾ [Surah al-Fath: 24] — the verse. If its apparent meaning is generality, then what is meant by it is particularity.

It has also been said: He meant by it the period in which Allah commanded fighting until disbelief disappears, by His saying ﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah and religion is entirely for Allah﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 39]. Then at that time the might of those who disbelieve will be restrained, and that is the time in which al-Mahdi will descend, so he will be a just ruler, and Islam will prevail over all religion.

It has also been said: that refers to the people upon whom Allah cast terror into their hearts and expelled them from their homes and wealth without fighting by the believers against them; and this is a might which Allah has restrained from the believers.

It has also been said: He meant by it the Jews and Christians, who pay the jizyah and have abandoned fighting; their might has been restrained from the believers when they pay the jizyah in humiliation.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verse 79–84:
