All of these will happen in the future, yet they come in the past form. It may also come in the form of the future while the past is meant, as in His saying ﴿And they did not take revenge on them except that they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Surah al-Buruj: 8], meaning "except that they believed." There are many such examples.

It has been said in interpreting this verse that this threat ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ refers to one who considers his killing permissible. As for the one who claims that there is no repentance for him, he is outside the Book and the Sunnah.

Allah forgives them their sins, and He commanded repentance from them, saying ﴿And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you﴾ [Surah al-Nur: 31], and similar verses. He did not distinguish between one sin and another. If Allah accepts repentance from disbelief, then accepting repentance from killing is more fitting.

Allah said ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾ [Surah al-Furqan: 68] up to ﴿and does righteous work﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 62]. And the brothers of Joseph said ﴿Kill Joseph﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 9], then said ﴿and be after him a righteous people﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 9], meaning through repentance.

The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "Is repentance accepted for every sin?" He said: "Yes." If it is said: "Why do they say in the reports that have come that the murderer has no repentance?" It is answered: Their interpretation, if the report is authentic, is that this applies when he has not committed [another] sin and has not sought Allah's forgiveness for it.

What supports this is what was narrated:
Khalid ibn Dihqan narrated from Abu Zakariya, who said: I heard Umm al-Darda' say: I heard Abu al-Darda' say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Every sin, Allah may forgive, except one who dies as a polytheist or kills a believer intentionally." [Kanz al-Ummal: 15/20, no. 39889] [375]

Khalid ibn Dihqan said: Hani ibn Kulthum said: I heard Mahmud ibn Rabi' narrate from Ubada ibn al-Samit, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever kills a believer and then rejoices in his killing, Allah will not accept from him any exchange or ransom." [Musnad al-Shamiyyin: 2/266] [376]

Khalid said: I asked Yahya ibn Yahya al-Ghassani about His saying "rejoices in his killing," and he said: They are those who fight in civil strife, so one of them is killed, and he believes he is upon guidance and never seeks Allah's forgiveness for it.

Sufyan narrated from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I know of no repentance for the killer except that he seeks Allah's forgiveness."

Abu al-Ashhab narrated from Sulayman ibn Ali al-Kalbi, from al-Hasan, that he recited this verse ﴿Because of that, We prescribed for the Children of Israel﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 32] up to ﴿all of them﴾. Then he said: "Come on, O Abu Sa'id," meaning: upon us as it was upon the Children of Israel.

He said: "Yes, by Allah, besides whom there is no god, He did not make the blood of the Children of Israel more honorable than our blood."

If it is said: What do you say about what Sufyan narrated from al-Mughira ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 93]: He said: "Nothing has abrogated it [naskh]."

Al-Hajjaj narrated from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Qasim ibn Abi [Bazza], that he asked Sa'id: "Is there repentance for one who has killed a believer?" He said: "No." So the verse was revealed to him: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾ up to ﴿except those who repent﴾ [Surah al-Furqan: 68–70].

Sa'id said: Ibn Abbas recited it to me, as I recited it to him, and he said: "This is Meccan; the one in Surah al-Nisa', which is Medinan, has abrogated it."

Abu al-Zinad narrated from Kharija ibn Zayd, from his father Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: When this verse in al-Furqan was revealed ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾ up to ﴿except those who repent﴾ [Surah al-Furqan: 70], we were amazed at its gentleness. We remained for seven months, then ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 93] was revealed in Surah al-Nisa', and the harsh verse abrogated the gentle one. It is said that the harsh one was revealed six months after the gentle one.

We say, and from Allah is success: The statement of the exegetes and their disagreement regarding the two verses, which of them was revealed first, and their statement that one of them is abrogating and the other abrogated, is of no benefit, because the method of abrogation [naskh] is not sound here, since abrogation does not occur in reports; it occurs in rulings, and both verses are [reports about] a matter [of news].

If the verse revealed in al-Nisa' was first, then it is general and its ruling has not been fully specified by the text, and its ruling was explained in the verse in al-Furqan.

If the one in al-Furqan was revealed earlier, and then the one in al-Nisa' was revealed, then the explanation of what is in the Qur'an dispensed with re-explaining it in al-Nisa'. And Allah knows best.

As for the statement of one who claims that whoever meets the Resurrection while committing major sins, but is a believer, that will not harm him, he has rejected the Book of Allah, the Exalted, because Allah the Exalted said ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 48]. He did not make forgiveness absolute for what is below polytheism; rather He referred it to His will, so that it is known that among it is what is forgiven, meaning that its doer is excused, then he comes out of the Fire and is not eternal in it. This is supported by the matter of intercession and other things.

These proofs establish the falsity of the view of the Wa'idiyya [the Mu'tazila who hold the threat of eternal punishment] and the Murji'a [who hold that sin does not harm faith], and the soundness of our view. This is the ruling of the verse.

﴿O you who believe, when you go forth in the cause of Allah﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 94], the verse.

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas: This verse was revealed concerning a man from the Banu Murrah ibn Awf ibn Sa'd [ibn Dhubyan], called Mirdas ibn Nahik, who was from the people of Fadak. He was a Muslim, and no one from his people had become Muslim except him. They heard of a detachment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heading toward them, and the commander of that detachment that day was a man called Ghalib ibn Fadala al-Laythi. So they fled, but the man remained, because he was upon the religion of the Muslims.

When he saw the horsemen, he feared they might be from other than the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he drove his sheep into a sandy ridge in the mountain and climbed the mountain himself. When the horsemen caught up, he heard them glorifying Allah [takbir], and when he heard the takbir he knew they were Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he too made takbir, came down, and said: "There is no god but Allah; Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; peace be upon you." Then Usama ibn Zayd ibn Haritha overtook him and killed him, and they took his sheep. They returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and told him the news, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was greatly grieved by that.

The news had preceded them before that.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You killed him in pursuit of what he had [of property]." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse to Usama ibn Zayd. Usama said: "O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness for me." He said: "How about 'there is no god but Allah'?" He said it three times.

[Sharh Sahih Muslim by al-Nawawi: 2/101]

Usama said: After that, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not look at me again until I wished I had not become Muslim except on that day. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked forgiveness for me three times afterward, and he said: "Free a slave."

Qatada said something similar.

Sammak ibn Harb narrated from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A man from the Banu Sulaym passed by a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), with a flock of sheep. He greeted them with salam, and they said: "He only greeted us to seek refuge," so they went to him and killed him and took his sheep, and brought them to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then Allah revealed ﴿O you who believe, when you go forth in the cause of Allah﴾.

Al-Mubarak narrated from al-Hasan that some Muslims met some polytheists and attacked them, and defeated them. He said: A man from among them charged, and a man pursued him and wanted his goods. When he reached him with the sword, the man said: "I am a Muslim, I am a Muslim," but he denied him, then thrust the spear into him, killed him, and took his goods.

He said: By Allah, the goods were little and meagre.

He said: This was reported to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Did you kill him after he claimed he was a Muslim?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, he only said it to seek refuge." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Why did you not split open his heart?" [Mustadrak al-Sahihayn: 3/116] [378]

He said: "Why, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "So that you may see whether he was truthful or lying." He said: "Could I have known that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Only his tongue reveals about him." [378]

He said: The killer did not remain long before he died and was buried, and in the morning he was found placed beside his grave. Then they returned, dug for him, and made room, and buried him, and in the morning he was found placed beside his grave, twice or three times. When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw that the earth would not accept him, they took his leg and threw him into one of those ravines. He said: So Allah revealed ﴿O you who believe, when you go forth in the cause of Allah﴾, the verse.

Al-Hasan said: As for that, it was not that the earth would hold back someone worse than him; rather it was an admonition for a people not to return to the like of his deed.

﴿O you who believe, when you go forth in the cause of Allah﴾, meaning: when you travel through the earth as fighters in the cause of Allah, ﴿then verify [fa-tabayyanu]﴾, meaning distinguish the believer from the disbeliever. As for one who recites it with the tā' and the thā' [fa-tathabbatu, "be steadfast/be sure"], it means: stop until you know the believer from the disbeliever. ﴿And do not say to one who offers you peace, "You are not a believer"﴾, because the greeting of the believer is salam, by which they recognize one another and greet one another.

Ibn Sirin said: He said ﴿to you﴾ because a man greeted them and they killed him. As for one who reads "al-salam," its meaning is "submission" [al-maqadah], meaning they seek by that the sheep and the spoils and the goods and the benefits and possessions of this world. It is said: "al-ard" [goods] is whatever is other than dirhams and dinars. ﴿With Allah are abundant spoils﴾, meaning abundant reward for whoever refrains from killing a believer. ﴿Thus you were before, [and Allah conferred favor upon you]﴾, meaning you were secure among your people, among the believers, by saying "there is no god but Allah" before the Hijra, so do not frighten anyone who says it. He forbade them to frighten anyone with a matter by which they themselves had been safe while among their own people. ﴿So Allah conferred favor upon you﴾ through the Hijra. ﴿So verify [tabayyanu]﴾ lest you kill a believer. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾, of good and evil.

Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And do not say to one who offers you peace, "You are not a believer"﴾. He said: Allah forbade the believer to say to one who professes that there is no god but Allah: "You are not a believer," just as He forbade them carrion. He is safe regarding his wealth and his blood, so they should not reject his words that he is a believer.

Ibn [Sirin] held this view based on this verse.

They said: When Allah said ﴿And do not say to one who offers you peace, "You are not a believer"﴾, He forbade them from those who came before them, after their manifesting Islam, and that was only their saying. Were it not that faith is speech — since these people, when they doubted the state of his origin, this statement of his was a refuge, so they killed him, and Allah the Exalted did not make it for His servant except to judge by the apparent.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, 'There is no god but Allah.'" [Musnad Ahmad: 1/11] [379]

It does not follow from this that faith is merely the declaration. Do you not see that the hypocrites used to say this saying, yet that was not faith from them?

It has become clear from the meaning of this verse that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Why did you not split open his heart?" [Kanz al-Ummal: 10/389, no. 29928] [380]. So it is established that faith is the declaration and other than it, and that the reality of affirmation is by speech, but the servant has no ruling except upon what is heard from him only.

In this verse there is also a refutation of the Qadariyya [those who deny predestination in the sense of divine decree of human acts], namely that Allah the Exalted informed that He bestowed favor upon the believers from among all creation, singling them out for success, so they became specified with faith. And if Allah had created all creatures for faith, as the Qadariyya claim, then what is the meaning of their being singled out for favor from among all creation, and of the distinction between them and one who says that the one who is blessed in faith in Allah — since they would be equal to others in all meanings — then they affirmed and did not oppose, as the others opposed? Their equality with them in all meanings is denied.

﴿Not equal are those believers who sit [at home] other than those with a disability﴾, the verse.

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas: When Allah mentioned the superiority of the fighters over those who stay behind from others in the jihad, Abd Allah ibn Umm Maktum and Abd Allah ibn Jahsh al-Asadi came — not al-Azdi — and both were blind. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah mentioned the superiority of the fighters over those who stay behind, and commanded jihad, and our state is as you see, and we answer the call to jihad; so is there any concession for us?" Then ﴿other than those with a disability﴾ was revealed concerning blindness of sight. They were among those who fought with the fighters because of their affliction.

Mujahid narrated from Thabit, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, who said: When this verse was revealed ﴿Not equal are those believers who sit [at home] other than those with a disability, and those who strive in the cause of Allah﴾, Ibn Umm Maktum said: "O Allah, reveal my excuse." Then ﴿other than those with a disability﴾ was revealed, and it was placed between them. After that he would go out to fight and say: "Hand me the banner," and say: "Set me between the two lines, for I cannot [am not able to] flee."

Ma'mar narrated from Ibn Shihab, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: I was sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his thigh upon my thigh, and he was dictating to me ﴿Not equal are those believers who sit﴾. Then Ibn Umm Maktum came. He said: "The thigh of the Messenger of Allah remained upon my thigh until it nearly broke, and ﴿other than those with a disability﴾ was revealed to him."

The rest of the verse ﴿Not equal are those believers who sit [at home]﴾ means: from the expedition or the jihad; ﴿other than those with a disability﴾ are those with an affliction and weakness in religion, and in sight. "Al-darar" is a verbal noun; it is said: "a man [rajul] darir" from "al-darar."

Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas: "Ulii al-darar" [those with a disability].

﴿And those who strive in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives﴾, meaning: not equal are the believers who stay behind from jihad, other than those with disability, and the believers who strive, since those with disability would be equal to the fighters, for the disability kept them from it. The word "al-darar" is in the nominative as a description of "the ones who sit," and in the accusative as an exception. ﴿Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit [at home] by a degree﴾, meaning a virtue. ﴿And to each Allah has promised the best﴾, meaning the fighter and the one who sits. And whoever strives [receives] Paradise; and He increased the excellence of the fighters, so He said ﴿And Allah has preferred those who strive over those who sit [at home] with a great reward, [degrees from Him and forgiveness and mercy. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful]﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 95–96]. He said: It used to be said:
Islam is a degree, the Hijra in the way of Allah is a degree, jihad within the Hijra is a degree, and being killed in jihad is a degree.

Ibn [Muhayriz] said regarding this verse: it is seventy degrees, between each two degrees is the distance of seventy autumns for a swift, trained horse.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verse 92–96 (part 1 of 2):

﴿It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake...﴾ (the verse)

It was revealed concerning ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿah al-Makhzumi. He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Makkah before the Messenger of Allah migrated to Madinah, and he embraced Islam with him. Then he feared that his Islam would become known to his family, and that the people of Makkah would learn of his Islam, so he fled from Makkah to Madinah. He arrived there and took refuge in one of its fortified towers (ʾatam), and shut himself in it. His mother was greatly distressed when news reached her of his Islam and his departure to Madinah. She said to her sons, al-Harith and Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, who were her sons from another father, "By Allah, I will not be shaded by any roof, nor will I taste food or drink, until you bring him back to me." So they set out in pursuit of him, and al-Harith ibn Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah went out with them from the Kaʿbah toward Madinah. They came to Madinah and found ʿAyyash in the tower (meaning, the mountain). They said to him, "Come down, for your mother has not had a roof over her head since you left, and she has sworn that she will not eat food or drink until you return to her. This is a covenant of Allah upon us that we will not coerce you in anything, nor come between you and your religion." When they mentioned this to him, he came down to them, and they swore by Allah. Then they took him out of Madinah, bound him with a rope (nisʿ), and each man among them flogged him one hundred lashes. Then they brought him to his mother, whose name was Asma bint Makhramah. When he entered, she said, "By Allah, I will not release you from your bonds until you disbelieve in what you have believed in."

Then they left him bound in the sun for as long as Allah willed, until he gave them what they wanted. Al-Harith ibn Zayd came to him and said, "O ʿAyyash, this is the state you were in. By Allah, if it was guidance, then you have abandoned guidance, and if it was misguidance, then you were upon it." ʿAyyash grew angry at his words and said, "By Allah, I will not meet you alone ever again without killing you." Then after that al-Harith embraced Islam and migrated to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah, while ʿAyyash was present at that time, and he was not aware of al-Harith's Islam. While ʿAyyash was present, he met al-Harith ibn Zayd, and when he saw him he attacked him and killed him. The people said, "What have you done? He had embraced Islam." So ʿAyyash returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, my affair and al-Harith's affair was as you know, and I was not aware of his Islam until I killed him." So there was revealed to him the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿It is not for a believer...﴾ — meaning, it is not befitting for a believer ﴿to kill a believer except by mistake﴾.

The meaning of His saying ﴿It is not for a believer﴾ is not a statement of negation; rather, it is a prohibition and a forbidding, like His saying: ﴿It is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab: 53].

Had it been a negation, you would never find a believer killing a believer, because what Allah negates cannot come into existence.

Like His saying: ﴿It is not for you to cause its trees to grow﴾ [Surah al-Naml: 60], and the servants are absolutely unable to cause its trees to grow.

As for His saying ﴿except by mistake﴾, in our view it is not part of the first meaning. ﴿It is not for a believer to kill a believer﴾ absolutely, except that a believer may err in killing, and the expiation for his error is what is mentioned after it.

Abu ʿUbaydah said: The Arabs make an exception of a thing from a thing, though it is not from it, by way of abbreviation and implication, meaning: he is not a believer in any state, except that he kills by mistake; then if he kills a believer, upon him is such-and-such. Similar to this is His saying: ﴿Those who avoid the major sins and the indecencies, except for minor lapses﴾ [Surah al-Najm: 32], and "lamam" (minor lapses) is not among the major sins; its meaning is "except that he draws near to them," i.e., comes close to them.

Similar to this is the verse of Jarir:
"Of the white ones who did not wander far, nor tread upon the earth except the trailing hem of a striped cloak."
So it is as if he said: she did not tread upon the earth except that she trod on the hem of the cloak, so it is not from the earth.

And Abu Kharrash al-Hudhali said:
"Sumaqam has become a desolate waste, with no companion in it,
except the beasts of prey and the wind passing over the sand-dunes."
The "ghuraf" is a place where they work sieves; Sumaqam is a valley of Hudhayl, and Abu ʿAmr al-Hudhali used to pasture there. Similar to this is the saying of the poet:
"And a land with no companion in it, except the young gazelles and except the camels,"
he means: except that there were in it the young gazelles and the camels.

Some of them said: "Illa" here has the meaning of "but" (lakin), so it is as if He said: ﴿It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake﴾ and not intentionally, except in a case; but if he kills him by mistake, then such-and-such. This is like His saying: ﴿Do not consume your wealth among yourselves in falsehood, except that it be trade﴾ [Surah al-Nisa: 29], meaning: but it be trade by mutual consent from you.

As for His saying ﴿And whoever kills a believer by mistake, then the freeing of a believing slave﴾, meaning: upon him is the freeing (taḥrir), i.e., the manumission of a believing slave.

The exegetes said: "Believing" (muminah) means one who prays and is mature, who has attained faith. If the believing slave is not available, then a child born (mawlud) or older, who has no infirmity, is acceptable. ﴿And a compensation (diyah) paid in full﴾, meaning complete, to the family of the slain who inherit from him and whom he inherits from. ﴿Unless they remit it﴾, meaning they give it as charity, forgoing and dropping the compensation.

﴿But if he was from a people hostile to you and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave﴾ — the verse — is upon the killer, and there is no compensation for the family of the slain, because they are disbelieving combatants, their property is not protected among the Muslims, and there is no covenant or pact between them and Allah. That is because a man would embrace Islam and not migrate, and his people, who were at war with the Muslims, would then strike him when he was encountered.

Hammad narrated from ʿAta ibn al-Sa'ib from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: A man would embrace Islam, then go to his people who were polytheists, and a detachment of the Prophet's army would pass by them, [and among those killed he is killed, and his killer frees a slave, and there is no compensation for him] (addition from Tafsir al-Tabari 5/281). Then this verse was revealed: ﴿But if he was from a people hostile to you and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave﴾, and there is no compensation for him. Al-Harith ibn Zayd had killed a believer from a people who were at war with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); in that case there was the freeing of a slave, and there was no compensation, because there was no covenant between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his people.

Then He said: ﴿But if he was from a people between you and whom there is a covenant (mithaq)﴾, meaning a pact, ﴿and you strike a man from them, then a compensation paid to his family and the freeing of a believing slave﴾ — upon the perpetrator. ﴿But whoever does not find [a slave], then fasting for two consecutive months﴾, without interruption in his fasting, ﴿as a repentance from Allah﴾, and Allah made this a repentance for the killer by mistake. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of whoever killed by mistake, All-Wise regarding whom He judges.﴾

The compensation for manslaughter by mistake is one hundred camels: twenty bint makhad, twenty bint labun, twenty hiqqah, and twenty jadha'ah. It is imposed upon the ʿaqilah (paternal kin who bear the blood-money) other than his own camels, and it is divided among them. If there are no camels in his city, the camels of the nearest city to him are imposed. If camels are unavailable, then their value in dinars or dirhams, as ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) assessed them, when he imposed gold and silver upon a Bedouin because he did not find camels; and this is taken from the town-dweller because camels are unavailable.

Al-Shafiʿi said in the old (qadim) position: upon the people of gold, a thousand dinars; and upon the people of silver, twelve thousand dirhams.

As for the ages of the aggravated compensation in quasi-intentional and intentional killing, when it is returned to the diyah (the camels), they tie behind him... [....] [an illegible word] his due, and thirty jadha'ah.

﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ — the verse.

It was revealed concerning Muʿayyin ibn Dababah al-Kinani. He found his brother Hisham ibn Dababah slain among the Banu al-Najjar, and he had been a Muslim. He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent with him a man from the Banu Fihr, and said to him: "Go to the Banu al-Najjar and greet them, and say: The Messenger of Allah commands you: if you know the killer of Hisham ibn Dababah, then he shall be retaliated against; and if you do not know a killer, then you must pay his compensation." The Fihri conveyed this to them from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They said: "We hear and obey Allah and His Messenger. By Allah, we do not know a killer for him, but we will pay his compensation." He said: So they gave him one hundred camels. Then the two returned toward Madinah, and between them and Madinah was a short distance. Satan deceived him and whispered to him, saying: "What have you done? You accept the compensation of your brother, and it will be a disgrace upon you. Kill the one who is with you, so that one soul will be in place of one soul, and you will have the compensation."

He said: Muʿayyin then caught the Fihri off guard and struck him with a rock, crushing his head. Then he mounted one of the camels and drove the rest back toward Makkah as an unbeliever. He began to say in his poetry:
"I killed for his sake a man of Fihr, and carried his blood-money,
the chiefs of the Banu al-Najjar, lords of Fari'."
"And I obtained my vengeance, and I lay down reclining,
and I went back to the idols, the first to return."

The statement concerning it is: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein﴾ — because of his disbelief and his apostasy from Islam.

The ruling of this verse:
The Kharijites and the Mu'tazilah said: it was revealed concerning a believer who kills a believer, and this threat applies to him.

The Murji'ah said: it was revealed concerning a disbeliever who kills a believer; as for a believer who kills a believer, he does not enter the Fire.

A group among the Ahl al-Hadith said: it was revealed concerning a believer who kills a believer, and it is a threat for him as long as he remains, unless he repents or seeks forgiveness.

Another group among them said: every believer who kills a believer is abiding in the Fire, not eternally, and he will come out of it by intercession and reward; and they claimed that there is no repentance for one who kills a believer intentionally.

Our view is that when a believer kills a believer intentionally, he does not become a disbeliever by his act, nor does he leave faith, unless he does that out of considering it lawful and as a religious conviction (istihlal wa diyanah).

But if he does not do it out of considering it lawful and as a religious conviction, then his blood-money is due from the one who killed him, and that is an expiation for him. If he repents from that and was not subject to retaliation, then repentance for this is an expiation for him.

If he leaves this world without repentance and without retaliation [qawd] (so in the manuscript), then his affair is with Allah: if He wills, He forgives him and satisfies his opponent with what He wills; and if He wills, He punishes him for his act, and then brings him out afterward to the Garden which He promised, if Allah wills, for He does not break His promise. Abandoning punishment by threat is a favor, and abandoning reward by promise would be a failure to fulfill; Allah is exalted above that, most high.

The evidence that the believer does not become a disbeliever or leave faith by killing a believer is that when Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the prescription of retaliation, He named the killer a believer by His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, retaliation is prescribed for you concerning the slain﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 178].

Retaliation applies only in intentional killing, and He called them believers and made them brothers, like His saying: ﴿But whoever is pardoned by his brother in any part...﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 178]. He meant by it only brotherhood of faith, and a disbeliever cannot be a brother to a believer.

Then He said: ﴿That is a lightening from your Lord and a mercy﴾, and that does not apply to disbelievers. Then He made a painful punishment obligatory upon transgressors after that by His saying: ﴿So whoever transgresses after that, for him is a painful punishment﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 178].

With such a verse, wrath is not mentioned, nor eternal abiding in the Fire, and this punishment is not called "fire." Punishment may be fire and may be other than fire in this world. Do you not see His saying: ﴿Allah will punish them by your hands﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 14], meaning killing and captivity? The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer...﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 6], addressing the fighters, so He addressed the worshippers with it. Had killing removed them from faith, it would not be permissible to address them with that. Thus Allah said: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight one another...﴾ [Surah al-Hujurat: 9], and the fighting of the two groups was either intentional or by mistake.

Also, the evidence for this is what is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he would convey to his companions that they should not associate anything with Allah, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and for what is in the Qur'an, whoever did any of that and was thereby recompensed, then it is an expiation for him; and whoever disbelieved in Allah, his affair is with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: if He wills, He forgives him, and if He wills, He punishes him. Had the killer been outside Islam, the Prophet's statement would have had no meaning.

And it is narrated that a believer killed a believer intentionally in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he did not command the killer to believe as a result of his act, though he would have been [a disbeliever] or outside faith; he would have commanded him first to believe.

He said to the claimant of blood: "Will you pardon?" He said: "No." He said: "Will you take the compensation?" He said: "No." So he commanded him to kill him, then repeated it to him two or three times until he accepted the compensation, and he did not judge the killer to be a disbeliever.

Had that been disbelief, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would have made it clear, because by it his family would have become unlawful to him, and it would not be permissible for the Messenger to neglect it, for he was the sincere adviser, the compassionate one, sent to discipline and teach.

It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Three are from the people of Islam: refraining from one who says 'There is no god but Allah' — we do not declare him a disbeliever for a sin, nor remove him from Islam by an act; jihad continues since Allah sent me until the Hour is established; and belief in the decrees." (Kanz al-ʿUmmal 15/811, no. 43226; al-Jami' al-Saghir 1/527, with variation.)

Another evidence that the killer does not become a disbeliever by killing is that disbelief is denial, and also shirk is ascribing partners; and the killer did not deny nor reject the obligations, nor ascribe partners to Allah. If one who did not commit disbelief could be a disbeliever, then one who did not commit belief could be a believer [....] [an illegible word].

The Kharijites and the Mu'tazilah have strained over this verse.

It has been said: a believer who kills a believer intentionally enters the Fire eternally, because Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿abiding therein﴾.

It is said to them: this verse was revealed concerning a disbeliever who killed a believer intentionally. We have mentioned the story concerning it, the context of the verse, and the narrations of the exegetes [about it]. Yet even if we grant that it was revealed concerning a believer who killed a believer intentionally, we would say to them: why do you say that "abiding" means perpetual? Inform us about the saying of Allah: ﴿And We did not make eternity (al-khuld) for any human before you﴾ [Surah al-Anbiya: 34]. What then is the meaning of "khuld" here in the Fire? They say: it means perpetuity in this world.

But this world passes away and perishes.

Similar to it is His saying: ﴿So if you die, will they be the everlasting (al-khalidun)?﴾ [Surah al-Anbiya: 34], and likewise His saying: ﴿He thinks his wealth will make him immortal (akhladahu)﴾ [Surah al-Humazah: 3], meaning only in this world. Do you say that He meant perpetuity?

If they say: No, and it must be so, then it is said to them: it is established that the meaning of "khulud" is the meaning of "ta'bid" (perpetuity). Likewise the Arabs say: "I will surely deposit so-and-so in prison." Do you say he meant perpetuity, when the prison ends and perishes?

And likewise the one imprisoned enters and exits from it.

If they say: when Allah said, ﴿And Allah became angry with him and cursed him﴾, this indicates his disbelief, because Allah does not become angry except with one who is a disbeliever or outside faith.

We reply: this verse does not necessitate anger upon him, because its meaning is ﴿his recompense is Hell﴾ — that He may become angry with him and curse him. Whatever Allah mentions as a thing and makes as a recompense for something, that does not make it obligatory; like His saying: ﴿The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger is only...﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 33]. How many who wage war against Allah and His Messenger have had none of these meanings befall them until they departed this world. And ﴿The recompense of an evil deed is an evil deed like it﴾ [Surah al-Shura: 40].

He did not say, "I will recompense every evil deed with an evil deed like it."

Had the two meanings been equal in this, then His saying ﴿and He pardons much﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 15] would have had no meaning; so likewise here.

Had it been in the sense of obligation, then His saying ﴿And whoever among them says, "Indeed I am a god besides Him," that We will recompense with Hell﴾ would have... and we find in the language of the Arabs that when a speaker says, "His recompense is such-and-such," and then does not recompense him, he is not a liar; but if he says, "I will recompense him," and does not do it, he is a liar. Thus it is known that there is a clear distinction between them, which indicates the soundness of this interpretation.

What Ibn al-Musayyib narrated from ʿAsim ibn Abi al-Najud from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿Then his recompense is Hell﴾ [Surah al-Nisa: 93]: that is, concerning his recompense — if He wills, He punishes him, and if He wills, He forgives him.

And Shu'bah narrated from Yasar from Abu Salih, who said: ﴿Then it is his recompense﴾ — if He recompenses him, then it is his recompense.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verses 92–96 (part 2 of 2):

Al-Hajjaj ibn al-Aswad narrated from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His saying ﴿But his recompense is Hell﴾: "His recompense is, if He recompenses him." [He said: "So is not"] His saying ﴿And Allah is angry with him and has cursed him﴾ among the past-tense verbs?

If you say that what is meant is "His recompense is that, if He recompenses him," is this among the future-tense verbs? It is said to them: The address may come in the form of the past tense while the future is meant. Such is His saying ﴿And the Trumpet is blown﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 99], ﴿And We shall gather them﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 47], and ﴿His companion will say﴾ [Surah Qaf: 23]. All of these will happen in the future, yet they come in the past form. It may also come in the form of the future while the past is meant, as in His saying ﴿And they did not take revenge on them except that they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Surah al-Buruj: 8], meaning "except that they believed." There are many such examples.

It has been said in interpreting this verse that this threat ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ refers to one who considers his killing permissible. As for the one who claims that there is no repentance for him, he is outside the Book and the Sunnah.

Allah forgives them their sins, and He commanded repentance from them, saying ﴿And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you﴾ [Surah al-Nur: 31], and similar verses. He did not distinguish between one sin and another. If Allah accepts repentance from disbelief, then accepting repentance from killing is more fitting.

Allah said ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾ [Surah al-Furqan: 68] up to ﴿and does righteous work﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 62]. And the brothers of Joseph said ﴿Kill Joseph﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 9], then said ﴿and be after him a righteous people﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 9], meaning through repentance.

The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "Is repentance accepted for every sin?" He said: "Yes." If it is said: "Why do they say in the reports that have come that the murderer has no repentance?" It is answered: Their interpretation, if the report is authentic, is that this applies when he has not committed [another] sin and has not sought Allah's forgiveness for it.

What supports this is what was narrated:
Khalid ibn Dihqan narrated from Abu Zakariya, who said: I heard Umm al-Darda' say: I heard Abu al-Darda' say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Every sin, Allah may forgive, except one who dies as a polytheist or kills a believer intentionally." [Kanz al-Ummal: 15/20, no. 39889] [375]

Khalid ibn Dihqan said: Hani ibn Kulthum said: I heard Mahmud ibn Rabi' narrate from Ubada ibn al-Samit, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever kills a believer and then rejoices in his killing, Allah will not accept from him any exchange or ransom." [Musnad al-Shamiyyin: 2/266] [376]

Khalid said: I asked Yahya ibn Yahya al-Ghassani about His saying "rejoices in his killing," and he said: They are those who fight in civil strife, so one of them is killed, and he believes he is upon guidance and never seeks Allah's forgiveness for it.

Sufyan narrated from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I know of no repentance for the killer except that he seeks Allah's forgiveness."

Abu al-Ashhab narrated from Sulayman ibn Ali al-Kalbi, from al-Hasan, that he recited this verse ﴿Because of that, We prescribed for the Children of Israel﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 32] up to ﴿all of them﴾. Then he said: "Come on, O Abu Sa'id," meaning: upon us as it was upon the Children of Israel.

He said: "Yes, by Allah, besides whom there is no god, He did not make the blood of the Children of Israel more honorable than our blood."

If it is said: What do you say about what Sufyan narrated from al-Mughira ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 93]: He said: "Nothing has abrogated it [naskh]."

Al-Hajjaj narrated from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Qasim ibn Abi [Bazza], that he asked Sa'id: "Is there repentance for one who has killed a believer?" He said: "No." So the verse was revealed to him: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾ up to ﴿except those who repent﴾ [Surah al-Furqan: 68–70].

Sa'id said: Ibn Abbas recited it to me, as I recited it to him, and he said: "This is Meccan; the one in Surah al-Nisa', which is Medinan, has abrogated it."

Abu al-Zinad narrated from Kharija ibn Zayd, from his father Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: When this verse in al-Furqan was revealed ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾ up to ﴿except those who repent﴾ [Surah al-Furqan: 70], we were amazed at its gentleness. We remained for seven months, then ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 93] was revealed in Surah al-Nisa', and the harsh verse abrogated the gentle one. It is said that the harsh one was revealed six months after the gentle one.

We say, and from Allah is success: The statement of the exegetes and their disagreement regarding the two verses, which of them was revealed first, and their statement that one of them is abrogating and the other abrogated, is of no benefit, because the method of abrogation [naskh] is not sound here, since abrogation does not occur in reports; it occurs in rulings, and both verses are [reports about] a matter [of news].

If the verse revealed in al-Nisa' was first, then it is general and its ruling has not been fully specified by the text, and its ruling was explained in the verse in al-Furqan.

If the one in al-Furqan was revealed earlier, and then the one in al-Nisa' was revealed, then the explanation of what is in the Qur'an dispensed with re-explaining it in al-Nisa'. And Allah knows best.

As for the statement of one who claims that whoever meets the Resurrection while committing major sins, but is a believer, that will not harm him, he has rejected the Book of Allah, the Exalted, because Allah the Exalted said ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 48]. He did not make forgiveness absolute for what is below polytheism; rather He referred it to His will, so that it is known that among it is what is forgiven, meaning that its doer is excused, then he comes out of the Fire and is not eternal in it. This is supported by the matter of intercession and other things.

These proofs establish the falsity of the view of the Wa'idiyya [the Mu'tazila who hold the threat of eternal punishment] and the Murji'a [who hold that sin does not harm faith], and the soundness of our view. This is the ruling of the verse.

﴿O you who believe, when you go forth in the cause of Allah﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 94], the verse.

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas: This verse was revealed concerning a man from the Banu Murrah ibn Awf ibn Sa'd [ibn Dhubyan], called Mirdas ibn Nahik, who was from the people of Fadak. He was a Muslim, and no one from his people had become Muslim except him. They heard of a detachment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heading toward them, and the commander of that detachment that day was a man called Ghalib ibn Fadala al-Laythi. So they fled, but the man remained, because he was upon the religion of the Muslims.

When he saw the horsemen, he feared they might be from other than the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he drove his sheep into a sandy ridge in the mountain and climbed the mountain himself. When the horsemen caught up, he heard them glorifying Allah [takbir], and when he heard the takbir he knew they were Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he too made takbir, came down, and said: "There is no god but Allah; Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; peace be upon you." Then Usama ibn Zayd ibn Haritha overtook him and killed him, and they took his sheep. They returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and told him the news, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was greatly grieved by that.

The news had preceded them before that.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You killed him in pursuit of what he had [of property]." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse to Usama ibn Zayd. Usama said: "O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness for me." He said: "How about 'there is no god but Allah'?" He said it three times.

[Sharh Sahih Muslim by al-Nawawi: 2/101]

Usama said: After that, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not look at me again until I wished I had not become Muslim except on that day. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked forgiveness for me three times afterward, and he said: "Free a slave."

Qatada said something similar.

Sammak ibn Harb narrated from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A man from the Banu Sulaym passed by a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), with a flock of sheep. He greeted them with salam, and they said: "He only greeted us to seek refuge," so they went to him and killed him and took his sheep, and brought them to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then Allah revealed ﴿O you who believe, when you go forth in the cause of Allah﴾.

Al-Mubarak narrated from al-Hasan that some Muslims met some polytheists and attacked them, and defeated them. He said: A man from among them charged, and a man pursued him and wanted his goods. When he reached him with the sword, the man said: "I am a Muslim, I am a Muslim," but he denied him, then thrust the spear into him, killed him, and took his goods.

He said: By Allah, the goods were little and meagre.

He said: This was reported to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Did you kill him after he claimed he was a Muslim?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, he only said it to seek refuge." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Why did you not split open his heart?" [Mustadrak al-Sahihayn: 3/116] [378]

He said: "Why, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "So that you may see whether he was truthful or lying." He said: "Could I have known that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Only his tongue reveals about him." [378]

He said: The killer did not remain long before he died and was buried, and in the morning he was found placed beside his grave. Then they returned, dug for him, and made room, and buried him, and in the morning he was found placed beside his grave, twice or three times. When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw that the earth would not accept him, they took his leg and threw him into one of those ravines. He said: So Allah revealed ﴿O you who believe, when you go forth in the cause of Allah﴾, the verse.

Al-Hasan said: As for that, it was not that the earth would hold back someone worse than him; rather it was an admonition for a people not to return to the like of his deed.

﴿O you who believe, when you go forth in the cause of Allah﴾, meaning: when you travel through the earth as fighters in the cause of Allah, ﴿then verify [fa-tabayyanu]﴾, meaning distinguish the believer from the disbeliever. As for one who recites it with the tā' and the thā' [fa-tathabbatu, "be steadfast/be sure"], it means: stop until you know the believer from the disbeliever. ﴿And do not say to one who offers you peace, "You are not a believer"﴾, because the greeting of the believer is salam, by which they recognize one another and greet one another.

Ibn Sirin said: He said ﴿to you﴾ because a man greeted them and they killed him. As for one who reads "al-salam," its meaning is "submission" [al-maqadah], meaning they seek by that the sheep and the spoils and the goods and the benefits and possessions of this world. It is said: "al-ard" [goods] is whatever is other than dirhams and dinars. ﴿With Allah are abundant spoils﴾, meaning abundant reward for whoever refrains from killing a believer. ﴿Thus you were before, [and Allah conferred favor upon you]﴾, meaning you were secure among your people, among the believers, by saying "there is no god but Allah" before the Hijra, so do not frighten anyone who says it. He forbade them to frighten anyone with a matter by which they themselves had been safe while among their own people. ﴿So Allah conferred favor upon you﴾ through the Hijra. ﴿So verify [tabayyanu]﴾ lest you kill a believer. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾, of good and evil.

Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And do not say to one who offers you peace, "You are not a believer"﴾. He said: Allah forbade the believer to say to one who professes that there is no god but Allah: "You are not a believer," just as He forbade them carrion. He is safe regarding his wealth and his blood, so they should not reject his words that he is a believer.

Ibn [Sirin] held this view based on this verse.

They said: When Allah said ﴿And do not say to one who offers you peace, "You are not a believer"﴾, He forbade them from those who came before them, after their manifesting Islam, and that was only their saying. Were it not that faith is speech — since these people, when they doubted the state of his origin, this statement of his was a refuge, so they killed him, and Allah the Exalted did not make it for His servant except to judge by the apparent.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, 'There is no god but Allah.'" [Musnad Ahmad: 1/11] [379]

It does not follow from this that faith is merely the declaration. Do you not see that the hypocrites used to say this saying, yet that was not faith from them?

It has become clear from the meaning of this verse that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Why did you not split open his heart?" [Kanz al-Ummal: 10/389, no. 29928] [380]. So it is established that faith is the declaration and other than it, and that the reality of affirmation is by speech, but the servant has no ruling except upon what is heard from him only.

In this verse there is also a refutation of the Qadariyya [those who deny predestination in the sense of divine decree of human acts], namely that Allah the Exalted informed that He bestowed favor upon the believers from among all creation, singling them out for success, so they became specified with faith. And if Allah had created all creatures for faith, as the Qadariyya claim, then what is the meaning of their being singled out for favor from among all creation, and of the distinction between them and one who says that the one who is blessed in faith in Allah — since they would be equal to others in all meanings — then they affirmed and did not oppose, as the others opposed? Their equality with them in all meanings is denied.

﴿Not equal are those believers who sit [at home] other than those with a disability﴾, the verse.

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas: When Allah mentioned the superiority of the fighters over those who stay behind from others in the jihad, Abd Allah ibn Umm Maktum and Abd Allah ibn Jahsh al-Asadi came — not al-Azdi — and both were blind. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah mentioned the superiority of the fighters over those who stay behind, and commanded jihad, and our state is as you see, and we answer the call to jihad; so is there any concession for us?" Then ﴿other than those with a disability﴾ was revealed concerning blindness of sight. They were among those who fought with the fighters because of their affliction.

Mujahid narrated from Thabit, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, who said: When this verse was revealed ﴿Not equal are those believers who sit [at home] other than those with a disability, and those who strive in the cause of Allah﴾, Ibn Umm Maktum said: "O Allah, reveal my excuse." Then ﴿other than those with a disability﴾ was revealed, and it was placed between them. After that he would go out to fight and say: "Hand me the banner," and say: "Set me between the two lines, for I cannot [am not able to] flee."

Ma'mar narrated from Ibn Shihab, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: I was sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his thigh upon my thigh, and he was dictating to me ﴿Not equal are those believers who sit﴾. Then Ibn Umm Maktum came. He said: "The thigh of the Messenger of Allah remained upon my thigh until it nearly broke, and ﴿other than those with a disability﴾ was revealed to him."

The rest of the verse ﴿Not equal are those believers who sit [at home]﴾ means: from the expedition or the jihad; ﴿other than those with a disability﴾ are those with an affliction and weakness in religion, and in sight. "Al-darar" is a verbal noun; it is said: "a man [rajul] darir" from "al-darar."

Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas: "Ulii al-darar" [those with a disability].

﴿And those who strive in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives﴾, meaning: not equal are the believers who stay behind from jihad, other than those with disability, and the believers who strive, since those with disability would be equal to the fighters, for the disability kept them from it. The word "al-darar" is in the nominative as a description of "the ones who sit," and in the accusative as an exception. ﴿Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit [at home] by a degree﴾, meaning a virtue. ﴿And to each Allah has promised the best﴾, meaning the fighter and the one who sits. And whoever strives [receives] Paradise; and He increased the excellence of the fighters, so He said ﴿And Allah has preferred those who strive over those who sit [at home] with a great reward, [degrees from Him and forgiveness and mercy. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful]﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 95–96]. He said: It used to be said:
Islam is a degree, the Hijra in the way of Allah is a degree, jihad within the Hijra is a degree, and being killed in jihad is a degree.

Ibn [Muhayriz] said regarding this verse: it is seventy degrees, between each two degrees is the distance of seventy autumns for a swift, trained horse.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verse 92–96 (part 1 of 2):

﴿It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake...﴾ (the verse)

It was revealed concerning ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿah al-Makhzumi. He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Makkah before the Messenger of Allah migrated to Madinah, and he embraced Islam with him. Then he feared that his Islam would become known to his family, and that the people of Makkah would learn of his Islam, so he fled from Makkah to Madinah. He arrived there and took refuge in one of its fortified towers (ʾatam), and shut himself in it. His mother was greatly distressed when news reached her of his Islam and his departure to Madinah. She said to her sons, al-Harith and Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, who were her sons from another father, "By Allah, I will not be shaded by any roof, nor will I taste food or drink, until you bring him back to me." So they set out in pursuit of him, and al-Harith ibn Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah went out with them from the Kaʿbah toward Madinah. They came to Madinah and found ʿAyyash in the tower (meaning, the mountain). They said to him, "Come down, for your mother has not had a roof over her head since you left, and she has sworn that she will not eat food or drink until you return to her. This is a covenant of Allah upon us that we will not coerce you in anything, nor come between you and your religion." When they mentioned this to him, he came down to them, and they swore by Allah. Then they took him out of Madinah, bound him with a rope (nisʿ), and each man among them flogged him one hundred lashes. Then they brought him to his mother, whose name was Asma bint Makhramah. When he entered, she said, "By Allah, I will not release you from your bonds until you disbelieve in what you have believed in."

Then they left him bound in the sun for as long as Allah willed, until he gave them what they wanted. Al-Harith ibn Zayd came to him and said, "O ʿAyyash, this is the state you were in. By Allah, if it was guidance, then you have abandoned guidance, and if it was misguidance, then you were upon it." ʿAyyash grew angry at his words and said, "By Allah, I will not meet you alone ever again without killing you." Then after that al-Harith embraced Islam and migrated to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah, while ʿAyyash was present at that time, and he was not aware of al-Harith's Islam. While ʿAyyash was present, he met al-Harith ibn Zayd, and when he saw him he attacked him and killed him. The people said, "What have you done? He had embraced Islam." So ʿAyyash returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, my affair and al-Harith's affair was as you know, and I was not aware of his Islam until I killed him." So there was revealed to him the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿It is not for a believer...﴾ — meaning, it is not befitting for a believer ﴿to kill a believer except by mistake﴾.

The meaning of His saying ﴿It is not for a believer﴾ is not a statement of negation; rather, it is a prohibition and a forbidding, like His saying: ﴿It is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab: 53].

Had it been a negation, you would never find a believer killing a believer, because what Allah negates cannot come into existence.

Like His saying: ﴿It is not for you to cause its trees to grow﴾ [Surah al-Naml: 60], and the servants are absolutely unable to cause its trees to grow.

As for His saying ﴿except by mistake﴾, in our view it is not part of the first meaning. ﴿It is not for a believer to kill a believer﴾ absolutely, except that a believer may err in killing, and the expiation for his error is what is mentioned after it.

Abu ʿUbaydah said: The Arabs make an exception of a thing from a thing, though it is not from it, by way of abbreviation and implication, meaning: he is not a believer in any state, except that he kills by mistake; then if he kills a believer, upon him is such-and-such. Similar to this is His saying: ﴿Those who avoid the major sins and the indecencies, except for minor lapses﴾ [Surah al-Najm: 32], and "lamam" (minor lapses) is not among the major sins; its meaning is "except that he draws near to them," i.e., comes close to them.

Similar to this is the verse of Jarir:
"Of the white ones who did not wander far, nor tread upon the earth except the trailing hem of a striped cloak."
So it is as if he said: she did not tread upon the earth except that she trod on the hem of the cloak, so it is not from the earth.

And Abu Kharrash al-Hudhali said:
"Sumaqam has become a desolate waste, with no companion in it,
except the beasts of prey and the wind passing over the sand-dunes."
The "ghuraf" is a place where they work sieves; Sumaqam is a valley of Hudhayl, and Abu ʿAmr al-Hudhali used to pasture there. Similar to this is the saying of the poet:
"And a land with no companion in it, except the young gazelles and except the camels,"
he means: except that there were in it the young gazelles and the camels.

Some of them said: "Illa" here has the meaning of "but" (lakin), so it is as if He said: ﴿It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake﴾ and not intentionally, except in a case; but if he kills him by mistake, then such-and-such. This is like His saying: ﴿Do not consume your wealth among yourselves in falsehood, except that it be trade﴾ [Surah al-Nisa: 29], meaning: but it be trade by mutual consent from you.

As for His saying ﴿And whoever kills a believer by mistake, then the freeing of a believing slave﴾, meaning: upon him is the freeing (taḥrir), i.e., the manumission of a believing slave.

The exegetes said: "Believing" (muminah) means one who prays and is mature, who has attained faith. If the believing slave is not available, then a child born (mawlud) or older, who has no infirmity, is acceptable. ﴿And a compensation (diyah) paid in full﴾, meaning complete, to the family of the slain who inherit from him and whom he inherits from. ﴿Unless they remit it﴾, meaning they give it as charity, forgoing and dropping the compensation.

﴿But if he was from a people hostile to you and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave﴾ — the verse — is upon the killer, and there is no compensation for the family of the slain, because they are disbelieving combatants, their property is not protected among the Muslims, and there is no covenant or pact between them and Allah. That is because a man would embrace Islam and not migrate, and his people, who were at war with the Muslims, would then strike him when he was encountered.

Hammad narrated from ʿAta ibn al-Sa'ib from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: A man would embrace Islam, then go to his people who were polytheists, and a detachment of the Prophet's army would pass by them, [and among those killed he is killed, and his killer frees a slave, and there is no compensation for him] (addition from Tafsir al-Tabari 5/281). Then this verse was revealed: ﴿But if he was from a people hostile to you and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave﴾, and there is no compensation for him. Al-Harith ibn Zayd had killed a believer from a people who were at war with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); in that case there was the freeing of a slave, and there was no compensation, because there was no covenant between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his people.

Then He said: ﴿But if he was from a people between you and whom there is a covenant (mithaq)﴾, meaning a pact, ﴿and you strike a man from them, then a compensation paid to his family and the freeing of a believing slave﴾ — upon the perpetrator. ﴿But whoever does not find [a slave], then fasting for two consecutive months﴾, without interruption in his fasting, ﴿as a repentance from Allah﴾, and Allah made this a repentance for the killer by mistake. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of whoever killed by mistake, All-Wise regarding whom He judges.﴾

The compensation for manslaughter by mistake is one hundred camels: twenty bint makhad, twenty bint labun, twenty hiqqah, and twenty jadha'ah. It is imposed upon the ʿaqilah (paternal kin who bear the blood-money) other than his own camels, and it is divided among them. If there are no camels in his city, the camels of the nearest city to him are imposed. If camels are unavailable, then their value in dinars or dirhams, as ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) assessed them, when he imposed gold and silver upon a Bedouin because he did not find camels; and this is taken from the town-dweller because camels are unavailable.

Al-Shafiʿi said in the old (qadim) position: upon the people of gold, a thousand dinars; and upon the people of silver, twelve thousand dirhams.

As for the ages of the aggravated compensation in quasi-intentional and intentional killing, when it is returned to the diyah (the camels), they tie behind him... [....] [an illegible word] his due, and thirty jadha'ah.

﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ — the verse.

It was revealed concerning Muʿayyin ibn Dababah al-Kinani. He found his brother Hisham ibn Dababah slain among the Banu al-Najjar, and he had been a Muslim. He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent with him a man from the Banu Fihr, and said to him: "Go to the Banu al-Najjar and greet them, and say: The Messenger of Allah commands you: if you know the killer of Hisham ibn Dababah, then he shall be retaliated against; and if you do not know a killer, then you must pay his compensation." The Fihri conveyed this to them from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They said: "We hear and obey Allah and His Messenger. By Allah, we do not know a killer for him, but we will pay his compensation." He said: So they gave him one hundred camels. Then the two returned toward Madinah, and between them and Madinah was a short distance. Satan deceived him and whispered to him, saying: "What have you done? You accept the compensation of your brother, and it will be a disgrace upon you. Kill the one who is with you, so that one soul will be in place of one soul, and you will have the compensation."

He said: Muʿayyin then caught the Fihri off guard and struck him with a rock, crushing his head. Then he mounted one of the camels and drove the rest back toward Makkah as an unbeliever. He began to say in his poetry:
"I killed for his sake a man of Fihr, and carried his blood-money,
the chiefs of the Banu al-Najjar, lords of Fari'."
"And I obtained my vengeance, and I lay down reclining,
and I went back to the idols, the first to return."

The statement concerning it is: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein﴾ — because of his disbelief and his apostasy from Islam.

The ruling of this verse:
The Kharijites and the Mu'tazilah said: it was revealed concerning a believer who kills a believer, and this threat applies to him.

The Murji'ah said: it was revealed concerning a disbeliever who kills a believer; as for a believer who kills a believer, he does not enter the Fire.

A group among the Ahl al-Hadith said: it was revealed concerning a believer who kills a believer, and it is a threat for him as long as he remains, unless he repents or seeks forgiveness.

Another group among them said: every believer who kills a believer is abiding in the Fire, not eternally, and he will come out of it by intercession and reward; and they claimed that there is no repentance for one who kills a believer intentionally.

Our view is that when a believer kills a believer intentionally, he does not become a disbeliever by his act, nor does he leave faith, unless he does that out of considering it lawful and as a religious conviction (istihlal wa diyanah).

But if he does not do it out of considering it lawful and as a religious conviction, then his blood-money is due from the one who killed him, and that is an expiation for him. If he repents from that and was not subject to retaliation, then repentance for this is an expiation for him.

If he leaves this world without repentance and without retaliation [qawd] (so in the manuscript), then his affair is with Allah: if He wills, He forgives him and satisfies his opponent with what He wills; and if He wills, He punishes him for his act, and then brings him out afterward to the Garden which He promised, if Allah wills, for He does not break His promise. Abandoning punishment by threat is a favor, and abandoning reward by promise would be a failure to fulfill; Allah is exalted above that, most high.

The evidence that the believer does not become a disbeliever or leave faith by killing a believer is that when Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the prescription of retaliation, He named the killer a believer by His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, retaliation is prescribed for you concerning the slain﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 178].

Retaliation applies only in intentional killing, and He called them believers and made them brothers, like His saying: ﴿But whoever is pardoned by his brother in any part...﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 178]. He meant by it only brotherhood of faith, and a disbeliever cannot be a brother to a believer.

Then He said: ﴿That is a lightening from your Lord and a mercy﴾, and that does not apply to disbelievers. Then He made a painful punishment obligatory upon transgressors after that by His saying: ﴿So whoever transgresses after that, for him is a painful punishment﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 178].

With such a verse, wrath is not mentioned, nor eternal abiding in the Fire, and this punishment is not called "fire." Punishment may be fire and may be other than fire in this world. Do you not see His saying: ﴿Allah will punish them by your hands﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 14], meaning killing and captivity? The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer...﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 6], addressing the fighters, so He addressed the worshippers with it. Had killing removed them from faith, it would not be permissible to address them with that. Thus Allah said: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight one another...﴾ [Surah al-Hujurat: 9], and the fighting of the two groups was either intentional or by mistake.

Also, the evidence for this is what is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he would convey to his companions that they should not associate anything with Allah, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and for what is in the Qur'an, whoever did any of that and was thereby recompensed, then it is an expiation for him; and whoever disbelieved in Allah, his affair is with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: if He wills, He forgives him, and if He wills, He punishes him. Had the killer been outside Islam, the Prophet's statement would have had no meaning.

And it is narrated that a believer killed a believer intentionally in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he did not command the killer to believe as a result of his act, though he would have been [a disbeliever] or outside faith; he would have commanded him first to believe.

He said to the claimant of blood: "Will you pardon?" He said: "No." He said: "Will you take the compensation?" He said: "No." So he commanded him to kill him, then repeated it to him two or three times until he accepted the compensation, and he did not judge the killer to be a disbeliever.

Had that been disbelief, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would have made it clear, because by it his family would have become unlawful to him, and it would not be permissible for the Messenger to neglect it, for he was the sincere adviser, the compassionate one, sent to discipline and teach.

It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Three are from the people of Islam: refraining from one who says 'There is no god but Allah' — we do not declare him a disbeliever for a sin, nor remove him from Islam by an act; jihad continues since Allah sent me until the Hour is established; and belief in the decrees." (Kanz al-ʿUmmal 15/811, no. 43226; al-Jami' al-Saghir 1/527, with variation.)

Another evidence that the killer does not become a disbeliever by killing is that disbelief is denial, and also shirk is ascribing partners; and the killer did not deny nor reject the obligations, nor ascribe partners to Allah. If one who did not commit disbelief could be a disbeliever, then one who did not commit belief could be a believer [....] [an illegible word].

The Kharijites and the Mu'tazilah have strained over this verse.

It has been said: a believer who kills a believer intentionally enters the Fire eternally, because Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿abiding therein﴾.

It is said to them: this verse was revealed concerning a disbeliever who killed a believer intentionally. We have mentioned the story concerning it, the context of the verse, and the narrations of the exegetes [about it]. Yet even if we grant that it was revealed concerning a believer who killed a believer intentionally, we would say to them: why do you say that "abiding" means perpetual? Inform us about the saying of Allah: ﴿And We did not make eternity (al-khuld) for any human before you﴾ [Surah al-Anbiya: 34]. What then is the meaning of "khuld" here in the Fire? They say: it means perpetuity in this world.

But this world passes away and perishes.

Similar to it is His saying: ﴿So if you die, will they be the everlasting (al-khalidun)?﴾ [Surah al-Anbiya: 34], and likewise His saying: ﴿He thinks his wealth will make him immortal (akhladahu)﴾ [Surah al-Humazah: 3], meaning only in this world. Do you say that He meant perpetuity?

If they say: No, and it must be so, then it is said to them: it is established that the meaning of "khulud" is the meaning of "ta'bid" (perpetuity). Likewise the Arabs say: "I will surely deposit so-and-so in prison." Do you say he meant perpetuity, when the prison ends and perishes?

And likewise the one imprisoned enters and exits from it.

If they say: when Allah said, ﴿And Allah became angry with him and cursed him﴾, this indicates his disbelief, because Allah does not become angry except with one who is a disbeliever or outside faith.

We reply: this verse does not necessitate anger upon him, because its meaning is ﴿his recompense is Hell﴾ — that He may become angry with him and curse him. Whatever Allah mentions as a thing and makes as a recompense for something, that does not make it obligatory; like His saying: ﴿The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger is only...﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 33]. How many who wage war against Allah and His Messenger have had none of these meanings befall them until they departed this world. And ﴿The recompense of an evil deed is an evil deed like it﴾ [Surah al-Shura: 40].

He did not say, "I will recompense every evil deed with an evil deed like it."

Had the two meanings been equal in this, then His saying ﴿and He pardons much﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 15] would have had no meaning; so likewise here.

Had it been in the sense of obligation, then His saying ﴿And whoever among them says, "Indeed I am a god besides Him," that We will recompense with Hell﴾ would have... and we find in the language of the Arabs that when a speaker says, "His recompense is such-and-such," and then does not recompense him, he is not a liar; but if he says, "I will recompense him," and does not do it, he is a liar. Thus it is known that there is a clear distinction between them, which indicates the soundness of this interpretation.

What Ibn al-Musayyib narrated from ʿAsim ibn Abi al-Najud from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿Then his recompense is Hell﴾ [Surah al-Nisa: 93]: that is, concerning his recompense — if He wills, He punishes him, and if He wills, He forgives him.

And Shu'bah narrated from Yasar from Abu Salih, who said: ﴿Then it is his recompense﴾ — if He recompenses him, then it is his recompense.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verses 92–96 (part 2 of 2):

Al-Hajjaj ibn al-Aswad narrated from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His saying ﴿But his recompense is Hell﴾: "His recompense is, if He recompenses him." [He said: "So is not"] His saying ﴿And Allah is angry with him and has cursed him﴾ among the past-tense verbs?

If you say that what is meant is "His recompense is that, if He recompenses him," is this among the future-tense verbs? It is said to them: The address may come in the form of the past tense while the future is meant. Such is His saying ﴿And the Trumpet is blown﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 99], ﴿And We shall gather them﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 47], and ﴿His companion will say﴾ [Surah Qaf: 23]. All of these will happen in the future, yet they come in the past form. It may also come in the form of the future while the past is meant, as in His saying ﴿And they did not take revenge on them except that they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Surah al-Buruj: 8], meaning "except that they believed." There are many such examples.

It has been said in interpreting this verse that this threat ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ refers to one who considers his killing permissible. As for the one who claims that there is no repentance for him, he is outside the Book and the Sunnah.

Allah forgives them their sins, and He commanded repentance from them, saying ﴿And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you﴾ [Surah al-Nur: 31], and similar verses. He did not distinguish between one sin and another. If Allah accepts repentance from disbelief, then accepting repentance from killing is more fitting.

Allah said ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾ [Surah al-Furqan: 68] up to ﴿and does righteous work﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 62]. And the brothers of Joseph said ﴿Kill Joseph﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 9], then said ﴿and be after him a righteous people﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 9], meaning through repentance.

The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "Is repentance accepted for every sin?" He said: "Yes." If it is said: "Why do they say in the reports that have come that the murderer has no repentance?" It is answered: Their interpretation, if the report is authentic, is that this applies when he has not committed [another] sin and has not sought Allah's forgiveness for it.

What supports this is what was narrated:
Khalid ibn Dihqan narrated from Abu Zakariya, who said: I heard Umm al-Darda' say: I heard Abu al-Darda' say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Every sin, Allah may forgive, except one who dies as a polytheist or kills a believer intentionally." [Kanz al-Ummal: 15/20, no. 39889] [375]

Khalid ibn Dihqan said: Hani ibn Kulthum said: I heard Mahmud ibn Rabi' narrate from Ubada ibn al-Samit, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever kills a believer and then rejoices in his killing, Allah will not accept from him any exchange or ransom." [Musnad al-Shamiyyin: 2/266] [376]

Khalid said: I asked Yahya ibn Yahya al-Ghassani about His saying "rejoices in his killing," and he said: They are those who fight in civil strife, so one of them is killed, and he believes he is upon guidance and never seeks Allah's forgiveness for it.

Sufyan narrated from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I know of no repentance for the killer except that he seeks Allah's forgiveness."

Abu al-Ashhab narrated from Sulayman ibn Ali al-Kalbi, from al-Hasan, that he recited this verse ﴿Because of that, We prescribed for the Children of Israel﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 32] up to ﴿all of them﴾. Then he said: "Come on, O Abu Sa'id," meaning: upon us as it was upon the Children of Israel.

He said: "Yes, by Allah, besides whom there is no god, He did not make the blood of the Children of Israel more honorable than our blood."

If it is said: What do you say about what Sufyan narrated from al-Mughira ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 93]: He said: "Nothing has abrogated it [naskh]."

Al-Hajjaj narrated from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Qasim ibn Abi [Bazza], that he asked Sa'id: "Is there repentance for one who has killed a believer?" He said: "No." So the verse was revealed to him: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾ up to ﴿except those who repent﴾ [Surah al-Furqan: 68–70].

Sa'id said: Ibn Abbas recited it to me, as I recited it to him, and he said: "This is Meccan; the one in Surah al-Nisa', which is Medinan, has abrogated it."
