Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, and Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Dahhak: "al-murāghim" means the wide plains of the earth, from one land to another.
As for "al-sa'a" (abundance), it is abundance of provision, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said likewise.

Abu Ubayda said: "al-murāghim" and "al-muhājir" are one and the same. It is said: "I opposed my people (rāghamtu qawmī) and emigrated from them," and it is the place of movement and the path on earth.

Al-Nabigha al-Ja'di said:
"Like a mountain that is sought for refuge at its corners, mighty in its opposition and its refuge."

And a poet said:
"To a land whose dwelling is not near, far in its opposition and its place of movement."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 12/247.]]

Al-Qaysi said: Its origin is that a man, when he became Muslim, would leave his people as a murāghim, meaning one who angers them, and as a muhājir, meaning one who cuts off from their religion. It is said that "murāghim" also refers to the destination, and the Prophet's (ﷺ) migration is called hijrah because it was the migration of a man from his people.

It is also said: its origin is from al-righām, which is dust, meaning "I rubbed him in the dust (raghamtuhu)," that is, I emigrated from him and did not care even if his nose was rubbed in the dirt.

When these verses were revealed, a man from the Banu Layth, an old man of noble bearing [and handsome], called Jundaʿ [[In Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/324: Damra.]], heard them and said: "By Allah, I am not among those whom Allah excepted, and I can devise a plan, and I have enough wealth to bring me to Madinah and beyond. By Allah, I will not spend the night in Makkah. Take me out!" So they carried him out on a litter until they brought him to al-Tan'im, where death overtook him. He struck his right hand upon his left and said: "This is for You, and this is for Your Messenger. I pledge allegiance to You upon what Your Messenger pledged to You." Then he died as a martyr. The news reached the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they said: "If he had reached Madinah, he would have been a muhājir." The polytheists also said, laughing at him: "He did not attain what he sought." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And whoever leaves his house as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him﴾ before he reaches his destination of emigration, ﴿his reward has become due from Allah﴾, that is, its reward has become obligatory, ﴿by His obligating it upon Himself﴾, ﴿and Allah is ever Forgiving﴾, of what was from him in the state of polytheism, ﴿Merciful﴾, toward what was from him in Islam.

﴿And when you travel through the earth﴾, that is, when you emigrate through it, ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, that is, no sin or wrong, ﴿in shortening the prayer﴾, meaning from four rak'ahs to two rak'ahs, ﴿if you fear that those who disbelieve will harm you﴾, that is, if you know that they will ﴿afflict you﴾ in the prayer, ﴿indeed the disbelievers are ever to you an open enemy﴾, openly displaying their hostility. And he said: "'Aduwwan' means 'a'dā' (enemies)," and Allah knows best.

His words ﴿When you travel through the earth, there is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer﴾: the complete statement ends here. Then the conjunction clause follows: "﴿if you fear that those who disbelieve will afflict you﴾", meaning "if you fear", and "in" is a conditional particle. The Qur'an has many such instances, where the statement is completed, and then a particle separated from it in meaning, but connected in appearance, is attached to it, as in His words, ﴿Now the truth has become evident. I sought to seduce him, and indeed he is of the truthful﴾ [[Surat Yusuf: 51.]], and so on. This is the confession of the wife of al-Aziz. Then another narrative about Yusuf is attached to it, namely His words: ﴿That he may know that I did not betray him in secret﴾, because after the admission of sin there is no meaning to her saying "I did not betray him in secret."

In the exegesis: when Yusuf said this statement, Jibril (peace be upon him) said to him: "Nor when you were inclined?" Then Yusuf said: ﴿Nor do I absolve myself﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/4.]]. A similar usage is His words, Exalted, ﴿Your Lord creates what He wills and chooses﴾, and ﴿It is not for them to choose﴾ [[Surat al-Qasas: 68.]], which is the beginning of another statement intended as negation; for if it were connected to the first part of the speech, its meaning would be [....] [[Unreadable text.]].

He said: Placing the verse in the manner of arrangement we have indicated gives an additional meaning, which is the obligation of shortening the prayer during travel without fear, because the text of the verse, when you separate His words ﴿that those who disbelieve will afflict you﴾ from the mention of shortening the prayer, would require you to say that shortening the prayer during travel without fear is by the Sunnah (prophetic practice), and that the Sunnah abrogates (nāsikhah, naskh) the Book. It was said: giving the additional meaning while keeping the construction sound is preferable to interpreting it otherwise.

Ruling of the verse:
The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and those after them differed on completing the prayer in four rak'ahs during travel, but shortening was permitted for ease toward him. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, though he preferred that it is obligatory.

Talha ibn Amr narrated from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did all of that at Usfan, during the expedition of Banu Lihyan" [[See Ahkam al-Quran of al-Jassas: 2/331.]].

﴿And when you are among them and lead them in prayer...﴾ (the verse).

Al-Kalbi narrated from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas and Jabir, who both said: When the polytheists saw that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions were praying the noon prayer together with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) leading them, they regretted leaving them, and it seemed too great to them. Some of them said to others: "Leave them, for they have another prayer after this which is dearer to them than their fathers and their sons," meaning the afternoon prayer. "When you see them standing in it, then attack them and kill them."

When they stood for the afternoon prayer, Jibril (peace be upon him) descended and said: "O Muhammad, this is the prayer of fear, for Allah says: ﴿And when you are among them, being present with them, and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand with you and let them take their arms, and when they have prostrated...﴾" to the end of the verse. He said: So Jibril taught him another prayer.

When the Prophet (ﷺ) stood for prayer, his Companions stood in two rows. Then he said the takbir, and they all said the takbir together. Then the second row faced the enemy with their faces, protecting the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed one rak'ah and two prostrations with the row that was with him. Then they stood and said the takbir behind them, without speaking, to the position of their companions. Others held back until they stood behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he prayed with them one rak'ah and two prostrations, then he recited the tashahhud and gave the salam. Then the row behind him stood, and they went to the position of their companions. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had two rak'ahs and four prostrations, and the people had one rak'ah and two prostrations, and each person among them prayed one rak'ah and two prostrations for himself.

The method of the prayer of fear:
The scholars differed on the manner of the prayer of fear.

Al-Shafi'i said: If one prays the prayer of fear during travel from an enemy who is not safe, the imam prays with one group one rak'ah, and the other group stands guard, facing the enemy. When the first group has finished, they stand and wait, standing and lengthening, and the group completes the rak'ah that remains for them, reciting Umm al-Qur'an and a surah, shortening it, and gives the salam and departs, standing guard facing the enemy. Then the other group comes, and the imam prays with them the second rak'ah that remains for him, and after they come, he recites Umm al-Qur'an and a short surah, and he remains seated. The group stands and completes for itself the rak'ah that remains for them, with Umm al-Qur'an and a short surah. Then each of the two groups sits with its imam in what the other has not yet done.

He argued with the words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand...﴾ (the verse).

He also argued:
that the Prophet (ﷺ) did this on the day of Dhat al-Riqa'.

Mu'awiya narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿And when you are among them and lead them in prayer﴾, he said: "This is in the prayer during fear. The imam stands, and a group stands with him, and a group takes their weapons and stands facing the enemy. The imam prays with those who are with him one rak'ah, then he remains standing, and the people stand and pray the second rak'ah for themselves, then they depart until they come to their companions and stand in their place. Then the others come, and the imam prays with them the second rak'ah. Then the imam sits and waits for them, and the people stand and pray the second rak'ah for themselves and recite the tashahhud, then the imam gives the salam to them. This is how the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed on the day of Dhat al-Riqa'."

The soundness of this interpretation is also supported by the hadith of Sahl ibn Abi Khaythama concerning the prayer of fear, and he was one of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "In the prayer of fear, the imam stands, and one row stands behind him and another row faces the enemy. He prays with these one rak'ah. When he has prayed with them one rak'ah, they stand in their place while the imam is standing, and they complete one rak'ah. Then these go to the position of those, and those come, and he prays with them one rak'ah. Then they stand in their place and pray one rak'ah."

Al-Shafi'i said: If it is the maghrib prayer, then if he prays two rak'ahs with the first group, he remains standing, and they complete for themselves, which is good. If he remains seated, and they complete for themselves, it is permissible. Then he comes to the other group and prays with them what remains for him, then he remains seated until he finishes what remains for them, then he gives the salam to them.

He said: If it is a resident's prayer, then he waits seated in the second rak'ah or standing in the third rak'ah until the group with him completes. Then the other group comes, and he prays with them as the first was described.

He said: If the enemy is few on the side of the qiblah and the Muslims are many, and they are safe in a level place where nothing shelters them, if they attack them, then the imam prays with them all, and he bows and prostrates with them all, except for a row or part of a row behind him. When they stand after the two prostrations, those who were guarding prostrate.

When he bows, he bows with them all, and when he prostrates, those who were guarding prostrate with him, except a row or part of a row guarding them among them. When they have prostrated twice and sit, those who were guarding them prostrate. Then he recites the tashahhud, and they recite the tashahhud, then he gives the salam to them all together. He said: and this is a delay on their part, as they guard them up to the second row, and the second row advances and guards, and there is no harm in this. This is similar to the prayer of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Usfan.

Shibl narrated from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿there is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer﴾, he said: "Some people said: The Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions were at Usfan, and the polytheists were at Dajnan [[A mountain in the region of Makkah on the road to Madinah.]]. They met, and the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed the noon prayer with his Companions four rak'ahs, their bowing, prostrating and standing all together. The polytheists intended to attack their rows and their baggage. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Let a group of them stand with you﴾. So he prayed the afternoon prayer, and his Companions formed two rows. Then he said the takbir with them all, then the first row prostrated one prostration, and the others [after], then they prostrated when the Prophet (ﷺ) and the smaller row stood. Then he said the takbir with them, and they bowed with them all. The rear row advanced, and the front row retreated, and they prayed together as they did the first time, and the afternoon prayer was shortened to two rak'ahs, and he recited the tashahhud."

This is the hadith of Jabir concerning the prayer of fear.

Ata' narrated from Jabir, who said: "We prayed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the prayer of fear, and the enemy was between us and the qiblah. The prayer was called, and we formed two rows behind him. He said the takbir, and we said the takbir with him all together. Then he bowed, and we bowed with him. Then he raised his head and prostrated. When he prostrated, and the row that was next to him, the rear row stood facing the enemy. When the Prophet (ﷺ) finished the prostration, he and the row next to him, the rear row prostrated in their place with the prostration, and then the front row retreated, and the rear row advanced. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said the takbir, then bowed, and we bowed all together. Then he raised his head and stood upright. Then he and the row next to him, which had been in the rear, prostrated in the first rak'ah. When the Prophet (ﷺ) finished the prostration, he and the row next to him, the rear row prostrated with the prostration, then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave the salam, and they all gave the salam together, as we do, and these gave the salam to their companions."

Al-Shafi'i said: If he prayed with the rear group [....] [[An unreadable word.]].

If he prays with the other group two rak'ahs and then gives the salam, it is permissible, and thus was the prayer of the Prophet (ﷺ) at Batn al-Mahall.

Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated from Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who informed him that he prayed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the prayer of fear. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed with one of the two groups two rak'ahs, and he prayed with the other group two rak'ahs. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed four rak'ahs, and each group prayed two rak'ahs.

Al-Muzani said: This indicates to me the obligation of a fard (obligatory prayer) behind one who is praying a nafl (voluntary prayer), because the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed with the second group what was obligatory for them and voluntary for him (ﷺ). This is the position of al-Shafi'i concerning the prayer of fear.

Abu Hanifa said: The Sunna is that the imam divides the Muslims into two groups. He prays one rak'a with one group, while the other group faces the enemy. Then he stands up for the second rak'a, and that group completes its prayer alone and goes to face the enemy, while the other group comes and prays the other rak'a with the imam. Then the second group departs, and the first group returns and completes its prayer, and then they return to face the enemy, and the other group departs and completes its prayer.

Abu Hanifa followed in this the hadith of Ibn Umar regarding the prayer of fear.

It is what Ibn Shihab narrated from Salim ibn Abd Allah that Abd Allah ibn Umar used to relate that he prayed it with the Prophet ﷺ. A group lined up behind him and another group faced the enemy. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led them in one rak'a and two prostrations, [prostrating] like half of the Subh prayer. Then they departed and faced the enemy, and the other group came and prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, and he did the same. Then the Prophet ﷺ gave the salam, and each man from the two groups stood and prayed one rak'a and two prostrations for himself. [Musnad Ahmad: 2/150.]

Nafi said, quoting Ibn Umar: If the fear is more severe than that, they should pray standing or riding, facing whichever direction they are in. This was his prayer at Dhat Qarad.

It is also narrated from Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Jahm, from Ubayd Allah ibn Utba, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the prayer of fear at Dhat Qarad, arranging a row facing the enemy.

He said: He prayed one rak'a with the row that was with him. Then those went to the position of these, and these came to the position of those, and they prayed one rak'a. Then he gave the salam to all of them and departed. The Prophet ﷺ had prayed two rak'as, and each of the two groups had one rak'a.

The hadith of Abu Hurayra on the prayer of fear:

Urwa ibn al-Zubayr narrated from Marwan ibn al-Hakam that he asked Abu Hurayra: Did you pray the prayer of fear with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Abu Hurayra said: Yes. Marwan said: When? He said: In the year of the expedition to Najd. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood for the Asr prayer, and one group stood with him while another group faced the enemy. Their faces were toward the qibla. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said takbir, and those with him said takbir, as did those fighting the enemy, all together. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bowed one rak'a, and the group nearest to him bowed with him. Then he prostrated, and the group nearest to him prostrated. The others stood facing the people. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood, and the group with him stood and went to the enemy and fought them. The group that had been facing the enemy came and bowed while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained standing as he was. Then they stood, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bowed a second rak'a and they bowed with him, and he prostrated and they prostrated. Then the group that had been facing the enemy came, bowed and prostrated, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained seated as he was. Then he gave the salam and they all gave the salam together. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had prayed two rak'as, and each man of the two groups had two rak'as.

Know that the prayer of fear is permissible after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ without disagreement among the scholars, except what is reported from Abu Yusuf and al-Muzani, that they said: the prayer of fear is not to be prayed after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. This is not the place for discussion, and seeking their evidence to the extent I have mentioned here will, God willing, be beneficial.

﴿There is no blame upon you if you put down your weapons because of rain or if you are ill.﴾ This verse was revealed specifically concerning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ raided Muharib and Banu Anmar. [Allah defeated them, and they secured the captives and the wealth.] The Messenger of Allah and the Muslims with him halted, and they saw none of the enemy. The people set down their weapons and belongings in one place, and the Messenger of Allah went out, walking for some needs, with his sword laid aside, until he crossed the valley, [and the water was flowing]. The valley came between the Messenger of Allah and his companions. The Messenger of Allah sat down, and Ghawrath ibn al-Harith al-Muharibi, then al-Hadrami, swooped down with a rock to strike him. His companions said: "O Ghawrath, this is Muhammad, cut off from his companions." He said: "May God kill me if I leave him." Then he descended from the mountain with his sword, and the Messenger of Allah did not notice him until he was standing over his head with the sword drawn from its sheath. He said: "O Muhammad, who will protect you from me now?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah." Then he supplicated: "O Allah, suffice me against Ghawrath ibn al-Harith however You wish." Then he swung the sword at the Messenger of Allah to strike him, but he fell on his face from a push that struck him between his shoulders, and his sword slipped away. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose, took it, and said: "Who will protect you from me now, O Ghawrath?" He said: "No one."

He said: "Testify that there is no god but Allah and that I am His servant and Messenger." He said: "No, but I testify that I will never fight you nor assist anyone against you." The Messenger of Allah gave him his sword. Ghawrath said to the Prophet ﷺ: "You are better than me." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, I have more right to you than you have to yourself." Then Ghawrath returned to his companions. They said: "Woe to you! We saw you swinging the sword while standing over his head. What prevented you from him?" He said: "By God, I swung the sword at him, but I do not know who pushed me from my shoulder, so I fell on my face, and my sword fell from before me, and he got ahead of me and took it and said: 'O Ghawrath, who will protect you from me now?' I said: 'No one.' Then he said: 'Testify that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah, and I will give you your sword.' I said: 'No, but I give you my pledge that I will never fight you nor assist an enemy against you.' So he returned the sword to me."

He said: The valley became calm, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ crossed it to his companions and informed them of the news, and recited to them this verse: ﴿There is no blame upon you if you put down your weapons because of rain or if you are ill; and take your precautions against your enemy. Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.﴾ (Lā junāḥ: "no harm," i.e., no injury.) The people who are humiliated therein.

Al-Zajjaj said: al-junāḥ (blame, sin) is from "janahtu" when one deviates from a place and turns aside from the right course. Then He said: ﴿There is no blame upon you﴾, meaning you do not deviate from the truth if you put down your weapons. Adha (harm) is with a short vowel, as one says adha yadhá adhan, like far'a yaf'a far'an. ﴿So when you have finished the prayer﴾, meaning the prayer of fear, that is, when you have completed it, ﴿then remember Allah﴾, meaning pray to Allah, ﴿standing﴾ for the healthy, ﴿sitting﴾ for the sick, ﴿and on your sides﴾ for the wounded and the ill who cannot sit. It is also said: its meaning is remember Allah by His oneness, glorification, and thanks in every state. ﴿When you are secure﴾, meaning in the prayer of fear, sickness, and fighting, and you have returned to your homes, ﴿then establish the prayer﴾, that is, complete the prayer in its four rak'as. ﴿Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers as a decree of specified times﴾, that is, an obligation prescribed in both residence and travel: two rak'as on a journey and four at home. Allah prescribed it for them and set its times, that is, appointed times for it. From this is His saying: ﴿And when the messengers are brought to their appointed time﴾ (wuqqitat, with a light doubling).

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verses 97–103 (part 1 of 2):

Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves... (the verse). It was revealed concerning some people of Makkah who entered Islam but did not emigrate, among them Qays ibn al-Fakih ibn al-Mughira, and Qays ibn al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. They displayed faith and concealed hypocrisy. When the day of Badr came, they went out with the polytheists to fight the Muslims. When the two sides met and they saw the small number of the believers, they said: "These people's religion has deluded them." They were killed on the day of Badr, and the angels struck their faces and their backs and defeated them. Allah the Exalted mentioned this in His words, ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death﴾, meaning, the Angel of Death takes their souls.

As for His words ﴿taking them in death (tawaffahum)﴾: if you read the verb with a fatha on the ta' (tawaffāhumu, as a past tense), then it is in the past, and its position is accusative. If you read it as an imperfect (tatawaffāhum), its meaning is the present/future, and the verb is ﴿tatawaffāhum﴾. By "the angels" He means the Angel of Death, because Allah the Exalted sometimes addresses a matter in general terms and explains it in another place, so the explained text governs. The verse ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death﴾ may mean the Angel of Death, and may mean others. But when He explained it in another place, saying, ﴿Say: The Angel of Death who has been entrusted with you will take you in death﴾ [[Surat al-Sajda: 11.]], it became known that the intended meaning of ﴿the angels take them in death﴾ is the Angel of Death, and Allah knows best.

If it is asked: why did He express it in the plural form? It is answered: the address may come in the plural form while the intended meaning is the singular, as in His words, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿Indeed, We, We...﴾, and in ﴿Do not be concerned, for Allah is One.﴾ Similar usages are abundant in the Qur'an.

As for His words ﴿wronging themselves (zālimī anfusihim)﴾, this means by shirk (polytheism) and hypocrisy. The word ﴿zālimī﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from ﴿the angels take them in death﴾, meaning "in the state of their being upon shirk." ﴿They will say﴾, meaning the angels:

﴿In what were you?﴾ That is, "in what state were you?" It is a question of rebuke and reproach. It is also permissible that its meaning be: "among whom were you? Were you among the polytheists or among the Muslims?"

﴿They will say: We were oppressed (mustaḍʿafīn) on earth﴾, that is, subdued and powerless, ﴿on earth﴾, meaning the land of Makkah, ﴿so they took us along with them unwillingly.﴾ ﴿They will say﴾, meaning the angels: ﴿Was not the earth of Allah spacious, so that you could have emigrated therein?﴾ That is, the land of Madinah, ﴿spacious﴾, meaning safe, ﴿so that you could have emigrated therein﴾, so that you could have gone astray there and left from among the midst of Makkah.

Sulayman ibn Amr narrated from Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His words ﴿Was not the earth of Allah spacious, so that you could have emigrated therein?﴾ that he said: "When sins are committed in a land, one should leave it."

Sulayman ibn Amr narrated from Abbad ibn Mansur ibn al-Nājī, from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever flees with his religion from a land, even if it is a span of land, has earned Paradise by it, and he will be the companion of his father Ibrahim and his Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ)" [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/172, and Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/347.]] [381].

Allah the Mighty and Majestic refuted them, for they were able to emigrate. So He said: ﴿Those, their refuge is Hell, and it is an evil destination.﴾ That is, their dwelling is Jahannam, and evil is the destination to Jahannam.

Then He excepted from them the people of Makkah, saying: ﴿Except the oppressed (al-mustaḍʿafīn)﴾, meaning the sincere believers who were subdued in Makkah, unable to emigrate and prevented from joining the Prophet (ﷺ), and preparing to join him, ﴿among men, women and children﴾. The word ﴿al-mustaḍʿafīn﴾ is in the accusative as an exception from ﴿their refuge﴾. ﴿Who cannot devise a plan﴾, meaning who are unable to devise any plan, nor have any strength or provision to leave it, ﴿nor are they guided to a way﴾, meaning they do not know a path out of it. He said: "That is, the way to Madinah." Ibn Abbas said: "I and my mother were among those who ﴿cannot devise a plan nor are guided to a way﴾, and I was a young boy." ﴿Those who are of this description, perhaps Allah will pardon them﴾, that is, He will overlook them, ﴿and Allah is ever Pardoning, Forgiving.﴾

In this verse there is evidence for the possibility of the view of those who say that faith is merely verbal affirmation (al-iqrār). These people had concealed their affirmation, and it did not benefit them, since their inner states did not agree with their statements.

﴿And whoever emigrates in the way of Allah﴾, that is, in obedience to Allah, ﴿will find on earth many a refuge and abundance.﴾

Mujahid: ﴿muraghaman kathīran﴾: "moving away despite dislike."
Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, and Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Dahhak: "al-murāghim" means the wide plains of the earth, from one land to another.
As for "al-sa'a" (abundance), it is abundance of provision, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said likewise.

Abu Ubayda said: "al-murāghim" and "al-muhājir" are one and the same. It is said: "I opposed my people (rāghamtu qawmī) and emigrated from them," and it is the place of movement and the path on earth.

Al-Nabigha al-Ja'di said:
"Like a mountain that is sought for refuge at its corners, mighty in its opposition and its refuge."

And a poet said:
"To a land whose dwelling is not near, far in its opposition and its place of movement."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 12/247.]]

Al-Qaysi said: Its origin is that a man, when he became Muslim, would leave his people as a murāghim, meaning one who angers them, and as a muhājir, meaning one who cuts off from their religion. It is said that "murāghim" also refers to the destination, and the Prophet's (ﷺ) migration is called hijrah because it was the migration of a man from his people.

It is also said: its origin is from al-righām, which is dust, meaning "I rubbed him in the dust (raghamtuhu)," that is, I emigrated from him and did not care even if his nose was rubbed in the dirt.

When these verses were revealed, a man from the Banu Layth, an old man of noble bearing [and handsome], called Jundaʿ [[In Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/324: Damra.]], heard them and said: "By Allah, I am not among those whom Allah excepted, and I can devise a plan, and I have enough wealth to bring me to Madinah and beyond. By Allah, I will not spend the night in Makkah. Take me out!" So they carried him out on a litter until they brought him to al-Tan'im, where death overtook him. He struck his right hand upon his left and said: "This is for You, and this is for Your Messenger. I pledge allegiance to You upon what Your Messenger pledged to You." Then he died as a martyr. The news reached the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they said: "If he had reached Madinah, he would have been a muhājir." The polytheists also said, laughing at him: "He did not attain what he sought." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And whoever leaves his house as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him﴾ before he reaches his destination of emigration, ﴿his reward has become due from Allah﴾, that is, its reward has become obligatory, ﴿by His obligating it upon Himself﴾, ﴿and Allah is ever Forgiving﴾, of what was from him in the state of polytheism, ﴿Merciful﴾, toward what was from him in Islam.

﴿And when you travel through the earth﴾, that is, when you emigrate through it, ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, that is, no sin or wrong, ﴿in shortening the prayer﴾, meaning from four rak'ahs to two rak'ahs, ﴿if you fear that those who disbelieve will harm you﴾, that is, if you know that they will ﴿afflict you﴾ in the prayer, ﴿indeed the disbelievers are ever to you an open enemy﴾, openly displaying their hostility. And he said: "'Aduwwan' means 'a'dā' (enemies)," and Allah knows best.

His words ﴿When you travel through the earth, there is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer﴾: the complete statement ends here. Then the conjunction clause follows: "﴿if you fear that those who disbelieve will afflict you﴾", meaning "if you fear", and "in" is a conditional particle. The Qur'an has many such instances, where the statement is completed, and then a particle separated from it in meaning, but connected in appearance, is attached to it, as in His words, ﴿Now the truth has become evident. I sought to seduce him, and indeed he is of the truthful﴾ [[Surat Yusuf: 51.]], and so on. This is the confession of the wife of al-Aziz. Then another narrative about Yusuf is attached to it, namely His words: ﴿That he may know that I did not betray him in secret﴾, because after the admission of sin there is no meaning to her saying "I did not betray him in secret."

In the exegesis: when Yusuf said this statement, Jibril (peace be upon him) said to him: "Nor when you were inclined?" Then Yusuf said: ﴿Nor do I absolve myself﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/4.]]. A similar usage is His words, Exalted, ﴿Your Lord creates what He wills and chooses﴾, and ﴿It is not for them to choose﴾ [[Surat al-Qasas: 68.]], which is the beginning of another statement intended as negation; for if it were connected to the first part of the speech, its meaning would be [....] [[Unreadable text.]].

He said: Placing the verse in the manner of arrangement we have indicated gives an additional meaning, which is the obligation of shortening the prayer during travel without fear, because the text of the verse, when you separate His words ﴿that those who disbelieve will afflict you﴾ from the mention of shortening the prayer, would require you to say that shortening the prayer during travel without fear is by the Sunnah (prophetic practice), and that the Sunnah abrogates (nāsikhah, naskh) the Book. It was said: giving the additional meaning while keeping the construction sound is preferable to interpreting it otherwise.

Ruling of the verse:
The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and those after them differed on completing the prayer in four rak'ahs during travel, but shortening was permitted for ease toward him. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, though he preferred that it is obligatory.

Talha ibn Amr narrated from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did all of that at Usfan, during the expedition of Banu Lihyan" [[See Ahkam al-Quran of al-Jassas: 2/331.]].

﴿And when you are among them and lead them in prayer...﴾ (the verse).

Al-Kalbi narrated from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas and Jabir, who both said: When the polytheists saw that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions were praying the noon prayer together with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) leading them, they regretted leaving them, and it seemed too great to them. Some of them said to others: "Leave them, for they have another prayer after this which is dearer to them than their fathers and their sons," meaning the afternoon prayer. "When you see them standing in it, then attack them and kill them."

When they stood for the afternoon prayer, Jibril (peace be upon him) descended and said: "O Muhammad, this is the prayer of fear, for Allah says: ﴿And when you are among them, being present with them, and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand with you and let them take their arms, and when they have prostrated...﴾" to the end of the verse. He said: So Jibril taught him another prayer.

When the Prophet (ﷺ) stood for prayer, his Companions stood in two rows. Then he said the takbir, and they all said the takbir together. Then the second row faced the enemy with their faces, protecting the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed one rak'ah and two prostrations with the row that was with him. Then they stood and said the takbir behind them, without speaking, to the position of their companions. Others held back until they stood behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he prayed with them one rak'ah and two prostrations, then he recited the tashahhud and gave the salam. Then the row behind him stood, and they went to the position of their companions. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had two rak'ahs and four prostrations, and the people had one rak'ah and two prostrations, and each person among them prayed one rak'ah and two prostrations for himself.

The method of the prayer of fear:
The scholars differed on the manner of the prayer of fear.

Al-Shafi'i said: If one prays the prayer of fear during travel from an enemy who is not safe, the imam prays with one group one rak'ah, and the other group stands guard, facing the enemy. When the first group has finished, they stand and wait, standing and lengthening, and the group completes the rak'ah that remains for them, reciting Umm al-Qur'an and a surah, shortening it, and gives the salam and departs, standing guard facing the enemy. Then the other group comes, and the imam prays with them the second rak'ah that remains for him, and after they come, he recites Umm al-Qur'an and a short surah, and he remains seated. The group stands and completes for itself the rak'ah that remains for them, with Umm al-Qur'an and a short surah. Then each of the two groups sits with its imam in what the other has not yet done.

He argued with the words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand...﴾ (the verse).

He also argued:
that the Prophet (ﷺ) did this on the day of Dhat al-Riqa'.

Mu'awiya narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿And when you are among them and lead them in prayer﴾, he said: "This is in the prayer during fear. The imam stands, and a group stands with him, and a group takes their weapons and stands facing the enemy. The imam prays with those who are with him one rak'ah, then he remains standing, and the people stand and pray the second rak'ah for themselves, then they depart until they come to their companions and stand in their place. Then the others come, and the imam prays with them the second rak'ah. Then the imam sits and waits for them, and the people stand and pray the second rak'ah for themselves and recite the tashahhud, then the imam gives the salam to them. This is how the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed on the day of Dhat al-Riqa'."

The soundness of this interpretation is also supported by the hadith of Sahl ibn Abi Khaythama concerning the prayer of fear, and he was one of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "In the prayer of fear, the imam stands, and one row stands behind him and another row faces the enemy. He prays with these one rak'ah. When he has prayed with them one rak'ah, they stand in their place while the imam is standing, and they complete one rak'ah. Then these go to the position of those, and those come, and he prays with them one rak'ah. Then they stand in their place and pray one rak'ah."

Al-Shafi'i said: If it is the maghrib prayer, then if he prays two rak'ahs with the first group, he remains standing, and they complete for themselves, which is good. If he remains seated, and they complete for themselves, it is permissible. Then he comes to the other group and prays with them what remains for him, then he remains seated until he finishes what remains for them, then he gives the salam to them.

He said: If it is a resident's prayer, then he waits seated in the second rak'ah or standing in the third rak'ah until the group with him completes. Then the other group comes, and he prays with them as the first was described.

He said: If the enemy is few on the side of the qiblah and the Muslims are many, and they are safe in a level place where nothing shelters them, if they attack them, then the imam prays with them all, and he bows and prostrates with them all, except for a row or part of a row behind him. When they stand after the two prostrations, those who were guarding prostrate.

When he bows, he bows with them all, and when he prostrates, those who were guarding prostrate with him, except a row or part of a row guarding them among them. When they have prostrated twice and sit, those who were guarding them prostrate. Then he recites the tashahhud, and they recite the tashahhud, then he gives the salam to them all together. He said: and this is a delay on their part, as they guard them up to the second row, and the second row advances and guards, and there is no harm in this. This is similar to the prayer of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Usfan.

Shibl narrated from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿there is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer﴾, he said: "Some people said: The Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions were at Usfan, and the polytheists were at Dajnan [[A mountain in the region of Makkah on the road to Madinah.]]. They met, and the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed the noon prayer with his Companions four rak'ahs, their bowing, prostrating and standing all together. The polytheists intended to attack their rows and their baggage. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Let a group of them stand with you﴾. So he prayed the afternoon prayer, and his Companions formed two rows. Then he said the takbir with them all, then the first row prostrated one prostration, and the others [after], then they prostrated when the Prophet (ﷺ) and the smaller row stood. Then he said the takbir with them, and they bowed with them all. The rear row advanced, and the front row retreated, and they prayed together as they did the first time, and the afternoon prayer was shortened to two rak'ahs, and he recited the tashahhud."

This is the hadith of Jabir concerning the prayer of fear.

Ata' narrated from Jabir, who said: "We prayed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the prayer of fear, and the enemy was between us and the qiblah. The prayer was called, and we formed two rows behind him. He said the takbir, and we said the takbir with him all together. Then he bowed, and we bowed with him. Then he raised his head and prostrated. When he prostrated, and the row that was next to him, the rear row stood facing the enemy. When the Prophet (ﷺ) finished the prostration, he and the row next to him, the rear row prostrated in their place with the prostration, and then the front row retreated, and the rear row advanced. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said the takbir, then bowed, and we bowed all together. Then he raised his head and stood upright. Then he and the row next to him, which had been in the rear, prostrated in the first rak'ah. When the Prophet (ﷺ) finished the prostration, he and the row next to him, the rear row prostrated with the prostration, then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave the salam, and they all gave the salam together, as we do, and these gave the salam to their companions."

Al-Shafi'i said: If he prayed with the rear group [....] [[An unreadable word.]].

If he prays with the other group two rak'ahs and then gives the salam, it is permissible, and thus was the prayer of the Prophet (ﷺ) at Batn al-Mahall.

Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated from Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who informed him that he prayed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the prayer of fear. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed with one of the two groups two rak'ahs, and he prayed with the other group two rak'ahs. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed four rak'ahs, and each group prayed two rak'ahs.

Al-Muzani said: This indicates to me the obligation of a fard (obligatory prayer) behind one who is praying a nafl (voluntary prayer), because the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed with the second group what was obligatory for them and voluntary for him (ﷺ). This is the position of al-Shafi'i concerning the prayer of fear.

Abu Hanifa said: The Sunna is that the imam divides the Muslims into two groups. He prays one rak'a with one group, while the other group faces the enemy. Then he stands up for the second rak'a, and that group completes its prayer alone and goes to face the enemy, while the other group comes and prays the other rak'a with the imam. Then the second group departs, and the first group returns and completes its prayer, and then they return to face the enemy, and the other group departs and completes its prayer.

Abu Hanifa followed in this the hadith of Ibn Umar regarding the prayer of fear.

It is what Ibn Shihab narrated from Salim ibn Abd Allah that Abd Allah ibn Umar used to relate that he prayed it with the Prophet ﷺ. A group lined up behind him and another group faced the enemy. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led them in one rak'a and two prostrations, [prostrating] like half of the Subh prayer. Then they departed and faced the enemy, and the other group came and prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, and he did the same. Then the Prophet ﷺ gave the salam, and each man from the two groups stood and prayed one rak'a and two prostrations for himself. [Musnad Ahmad: 2/150.]

Nafi said, quoting Ibn Umar: If the fear is more severe than that, they should pray standing or riding, facing whichever direction they are in. This was his prayer at Dhat Qarad.

It is also narrated from Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Jahm, from Ubayd Allah ibn Utba, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the prayer of fear at Dhat Qarad, arranging a row facing the enemy.

He said: He prayed one rak'a with the row that was with him. Then those went to the position of these, and these came to the position of those, and they prayed one rak'a. Then he gave the salam to all of them and departed. The Prophet ﷺ had prayed two rak'as, and each of the two groups had one rak'a.

The hadith of Abu Hurayra on the prayer of fear:

Urwa ibn al-Zubayr narrated from Marwan ibn al-Hakam that he asked Abu Hurayra: Did you pray the prayer of fear with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Abu Hurayra said: Yes. Marwan said: When? He said: In the year of the expedition to Najd. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood for the Asr prayer, and one group stood with him while another group faced the enemy. Their faces were toward the qibla. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said takbir, and those with him said takbir, as did those fighting the enemy, all together. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bowed one rak'a, and the group nearest to him bowed with him. Then he prostrated, and the group nearest to him prostrated. The others stood facing the people. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood, and the group with him stood and went to the enemy and fought them. The group that had been facing the enemy came and bowed while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained standing as he was. Then they stood, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bowed a second rak'a and they bowed with him, and he prostrated and they prostrated. Then the group that had been facing the enemy came, bowed and prostrated, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained seated as he was. Then he gave the salam and they all gave the salam together. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had prayed two rak'as, and each man of the two groups had two rak'as.

Know that the prayer of fear is permissible after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ without disagreement among the scholars, except what is reported from Abu Yusuf and al-Muzani, that they said: the prayer of fear is not to be prayed after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. This is not the place for discussion, and seeking their evidence to the extent I have mentioned here will, God willing, be beneficial.

﴿There is no blame upon you if you put down your weapons because of rain or if you are ill.﴾ This verse was revealed specifically concerning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ raided Muharib and Banu Anmar. [Allah defeated them, and they secured the captives and the wealth.] The Messenger of Allah and the Muslims with him halted, and they saw none of the enemy. The people set down their weapons and belongings in one place, and the Messenger of Allah went out, walking for some needs, with his sword laid aside, until he crossed the valley, [and the water was flowing]. The valley came between the Messenger of Allah and his companions. The Messenger of Allah sat down, and Ghawrath ibn al-Harith al-Muharibi, then al-Hadrami, swooped down with a rock to strike him. His companions said: "O Ghawrath, this is Muhammad, cut off from his companions." He said: "May God kill me if I leave him." Then he descended from the mountain with his sword, and the Messenger of Allah did not notice him until he was standing over his head with the sword drawn from its sheath. He said: "O Muhammad, who will protect you from me now?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah." Then he supplicated: "O Allah, suffice me against Ghawrath ibn al-Harith however You wish." Then he swung the sword at the Messenger of Allah to strike him, but he fell on his face from a push that struck him between his shoulders, and his sword slipped away. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose, took it, and said: "Who will protect you from me now, O Ghawrath?" He said: "No one."

He said: "Testify that there is no god but Allah and that I am His servant and Messenger." He said: "No, but I testify that I will never fight you nor assist anyone against you." The Messenger of Allah gave him his sword. Ghawrath said to the Prophet ﷺ: "You are better than me." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, I have more right to you than you have to yourself." Then Ghawrath returned to his companions. They said: "Woe to you! We saw you swinging the sword while standing over his head. What prevented you from him?" He said: "By God, I swung the sword at him, but I do not know who pushed me from my shoulder, so I fell on my face, and my sword fell from before me, and he got ahead of me and took it and said: 'O Ghawrath, who will protect you from me now?' I said: 'No one.' Then he said: 'Testify that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah, and I will give you your sword.' I said: 'No, but I give you my pledge that I will never fight you nor assist an enemy against you.' So he returned the sword to me."

He said: The valley became calm, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ crossed it to his companions and informed them of the news, and recited to them this verse: ﴿There is no blame upon you if you put down your weapons because of rain or if you are ill; and take your precautions against your enemy. Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.﴾ (Lā junāḥ: "no harm," i.e., no injury.) The people who are humiliated therein.

Al-Zajjaj said: al-junāḥ (blame, sin) is from "janahtu" when one deviates from a place and turns aside from the right course. Then He said: ﴿There is no blame upon you﴾, meaning you do not deviate from the truth if you put down your weapons. Adha (harm) is with a short vowel, as one says adha yadhá adhan, like far'a yaf'a far'an. ﴿So when you have finished the prayer﴾, meaning the prayer of fear, that is, when you have completed it, ﴿then remember Allah﴾, meaning pray to Allah, ﴿standing﴾ for the healthy, ﴿sitting﴾ for the sick, ﴿and on your sides﴾ for the wounded and the ill who cannot sit. It is also said: its meaning is remember Allah by His oneness, glorification, and thanks in every state. ﴿When you are secure﴾, meaning in the prayer of fear, sickness, and fighting, and you have returned to your homes, ﴿then establish the prayer﴾, that is, complete the prayer in its four rak'as. ﴿Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers as a decree of specified times﴾, that is, an obligation prescribed in both residence and travel: two rak'as on a journey and four at home. Allah prescribed it for them and set its times, that is, appointed times for it. From this is His saying: ﴿And when the messengers are brought to their appointed time﴾ (wuqqitat, with a light doubling).

**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 4, verses 104–113:**

﴿And do not falter in pursuit of the people﴾: do not weaken in seeking the people, meaning Abu Sufyan and his companions, on the day of Uhud. This story has already passed in Surah Al 'Imran.

﴿If you suffer pain, indeed they suffer pain as you suffer pain﴾: i.e., you feel pain and complain of the wounds, and they feel pain and complain of the wounds, as you do, while you remain safe. ﴿And you hope from Allah for that which they do not hope﴾: i.e., reward, recompense, the victory Allah has promised you, and the manifestation of your religion over all other religions.

It is also said that the verse ﴿and you hope from Allah for that which they do not hope﴾ means: you fear from the punishment of Allah what they do not fear. Al-Farra' said: "Hope (*raja'*) does not mean fear (*khawf*) except with negation, like the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Say to those who believe that they should forgive those who do not hope for the days of Allah﴾, meaning who do not fear the days of Allah. Likewise His saying: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not hope for dignity from Allah?﴾, meaning you do not fear greatness from Allah. This is the Hijazi dialect (*lugha hijaziyya*)."

The poet said:

*"You do not hope when you meet the defender, whether seven met together or one."* [Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/358]

Al-Hudhali said, describing the honey-collector (*mu'tar al-'asal*) who has a woven/stitched (*nawb*) — meaning the bees:

*"And in the verse, 'a nawb that is 'awamil' ... when the bee stings him he does not hope for its sting."* It is narrated as *"nawb 'awamil"* in one verse, and in another verse it is *"nawb 'awamil"* with a variant (*'awasil*). [Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/358]

He said: It is not permissible to say "I hoped for you" while meaning "I feared you," nor "I feared you" while meaning "I hoped for you." [Lisan al-'Arab: 14/310]

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book with truth﴾

Al-Kalbi narrated from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: This verse was revealed concerning a man from the Ansar called Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq, of the Banu Zafar, a clan of Sulaym, who stole a coat of mail (*dir'*) from a neighbour of his called Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man. The coat of mail was in a sack containing flour, and the flour was scattering through a hole in the sack, until it reached the house, and there were traces of flour in it. Then he hid it with a Jewish man called Zayd ibn al-Samin. The coat of mail was searched for at Ta'mah's house but was not found there, and he swore to them, "By Allah, I did not take it and I have no knowledge of it." The owners of the coat of mail said, "Yes, by Allah, he entered our house, so bring it back to us," and they followed his trail, and they saw the scattered flour, until they reached the Jew's dwelling. Then they seized him, and the Jew said, "Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq gave it to me." Some Jews testified to this. The Banu Zafar, the people of Ta'mah, said: "Shall they take us to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) so that we may speak to him about our companion, and excuse him, and argue on his behalf? Our companion appears to be excused." So they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and spoke to him about it, asking him to argue on behalf of their companion, and they said: "If you do not do so, our companion will be destroyed and disgraced, and the Jew will be cleared." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended to do so and to punish the Jew, so Allah, the Exalted, revealed reproof to him: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book with truth﴾, the verses.

In another narration from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: Ta'mah stole a coat of mail from an Ansari man, and it was in a sack containing bran. He tore the sack so that the bran scattered from it all along the road. He came to the house of Zayd ibn al-Samin following the trail of the bran, [took it] and brought it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended to cut off the hand of the Jew Zayd, so Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse.

'Ali ibn al-Dahhak said: This verse was revealed concerning a man from the Ansar who was entrusted with a coat of mail, and its owner denied it. Some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accused him of betrayal. His people came and excused him and insisted upon him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) believed them, excused them, and rejected those who had said what they said about him. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse. When his treachery became clear, he apostatized from Islam and joined Makkah. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 110], the verse.

Muqatil said: Zayd al-Samin deposited a coat of mail with Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq, and Ta'mah denied it. When Zayd came seeking it, he closed the door, went up onto the roof, and threw the coat of mail into the house of his neighbour Abu Hilal. Then he opened the door, and they found nothing in it. He went up to the roof and said: "I see a coat of mail in the house of Abu Hilal; perhaps it is your coat of mail." They looked, and it was indeed that, and they took it up. Then Ta'mah gathered his people, and they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), complaining and saying: "They have disgraced us and accused us of theft." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reproached them, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book with truth﴾, meaning with the command, the prohibition, and the decisive judgment; ﴿so that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, meaning what Allah has taught you and revealed to you; ﴿and do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾, meaning a helper.

﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ for what you intended of cutting off the hand of Zayd.

Al-Kalbi: ﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾, O Muhammad, for your intention regarding the Jew, to strike him.

Muqatil: ﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ for your argument by which you argued on behalf of Ta'mah. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful.﴾

﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾

That is, who wrong themselves by treachery and theft, and cast it upon the Jew. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is treacherous and sinful﴾

That is, treacherous regarding the coat of mail. ﴿Sinful﴾

In his casting [of the accusation] upon the Jew and in His saying: ﴿And do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾. It has been said that the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ) while the intended meaning is someone else, like His saying: ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you﴾ [Surah Yunus: 94]. The Prophet (ﷺ) does not doubt what Allah has sent down. If it is said: he has been commanded to seek forgiveness, we say: this does not imply the existence of a sin, nor is it necessary that he seek forgiveness only for a sin, just as He commanded in Surah al-Fath to seek forgiveness without a preceding sin.

Know that seeking forgiveness (*istighfar*) in the case of all the prophets has several aspects. Among them, three aspects: it is for a preceding sin, such as [before] prophethood; it is for the sin of his community and relatives; and it is for leaving what is permissible (*al-mubah*) before the arrival of the restriction (*al-hadr*). Its meaning is by hearing and obedience to what he was commanded and forbidden, and by the bearing of divine success (*tawfiq*) upon it.

﴿They hide from the people﴾

That is, they conceal themselves and are ashamed before the people. ﴿And they do not hide from Allah﴾

That is, they do not conceal themselves nor feel shame before Allah. ﴿And He is with them﴾

That is, His knowledge.

﴿When they plot﴾

Al-Kalbi narrated from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, they say. From Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Abu Razin: they utter. ﴿What He does not approve of in speech﴾

That is, that the Jew stole it. ﴿And Allah is ever, of what they do, encompassing﴾

That is, Allah has encompassed their good deeds.

The Jahmiyya (followers of Jahm ibn Safwan) and the Mu'tazila (the rationalist school) clung to this verse. They used it as evidence that Allah is in every place. They said: when He said ﴿And He is with them﴾, this establishes that He is in every place, because He has affirmed His being with them. And as for His saying to them, in the sense of ﴿And He is with them﴾, that He knows what they say and that their deed is not hidden from Him, because He is the Knower of what creatures display and what they conceal. There is nothing in His saying ﴿And He is with them﴾ that necessitates that He is in every place, because He said: ﴿Are you secure from He who is in the heaven that He will cause the earth to swallow you?﴾ [Surah al-Mulk: 16], and His saying "He who is in the heaven" does not mean other than His essence, because the statement "Zayd is in such-and-such a place" without mention of any act or any other thing can only refer to his essence. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾ [Surah Fatir: 10], and He said: ﴿He arranges the affair from the heaven to the earth﴾ [Surah al-Sajdah: 5]. Thus He informed that [He] raises things from the heaven, and it is not permissible that He be with them in His essence and at the same time arrange the affair from the heaven and ascend to Him the good word. And if His saying ("And He is with them when they say what He does not approve of in speech") ...

Then he turned to the people of Ta'mah and said: ﴿Here you are﴾

That is, O people, [an exclamation] for alerting: ﴿you have argued﴾

That is, you have disputed on behalf of Abu Ta'mah, a man of the Banu Ubayriq. ﴿For them in this worldly life﴾

And the meaning of *jadal* in the language is with intense contention, and it derives from *jadal*, which is intense twisting. From this: "a man with a firmly twisted build (*majdul al-khalq*)", and "the *ajdal* for the falcon", because it is one of the strongest birds.

﴿Then who will argue with Allah on their behalf﴾

That is, on behalf of Ta'mah, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾

When Allah seizes him with His punishment and enters him into the Fire, ﴿or who will be their guardian?﴾

That is, a guarantor.

Then He resumed and said: ﴿And whoever does wrong﴾

That is, steals the coat of mail; ﴿or wrongs himself﴾

By casting the innocent man with the theft. It is said: ﴿And whoever does evil﴾

That is, associates a partner with Allah; ﴿or wrongs himself﴾

That is, by what is less than associating partners with Allah; ﴿then seeks forgiveness of Allah﴾

That is, repents to Allah; ﴿he will find Allah Forgiving﴾

Overlooking, ﴿Merciful﴾

To him, when He accepts his repentance. ﴿And whoever earns a sin﴾

That is, commits it by falsehood; ﴿then he earns it only against himself﴾

He says: he harms only himself, and none is taken for a sin except through the sin. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing﴾

Of the thief of the coat of mail; ﴿Wise﴾

In the judgment of cutting off the hand for Ta'mah for theft. ﴿And whoever earns an error﴾

That is, by his false oath; ﴿or a sin﴾

By his theft of the coat of mail and his casting of the Jew; ﴿then throws it upon an innocent person﴾

That is, he hurls what he committed away from its safe place; ﴿then he has borne a slander﴾

And *buhtan* means that he slanders a man with what he did not do.

Al-Zajjaj said: *al-buhtan* is the lie which is chosen from its magnitude. ﴿And a manifest sin﴾

A clear sin.

Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And whoever earns an error or a sin﴾.

'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul: ﴿then throws it upon an innocent person﴾

That is, concerning 'A'ishah, the Mother of the Believers, when he lied about her, and this was the case. His saying ﴿then throws it﴾ [uses the singular pronoun], and he did not say "them" in both cases, though he mentioned "error" and did not say "disbelief". It is permissible to refer by pronoun to the soul (*nafs*), and to three or more, while the singular of it is feminine but is used as masculine, and the singular is used because the souls take one act. This is permissible. And if you wish, you may join "error" and "sin" and treat them as one unit. And if you wish, you may make the pronoun refer to "sin" alone, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when they see a trade or amusement, they disperse to it﴾ [Surah al-Jumu'ah: 11], where He made it refer to the trade. And if he had used the masculine, treating them as one act, it would also be permissible.

Then He said to Muhammad: ﴿And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you﴾

By prophethood; ﴿and His mercy﴾

Your support by revelation; ﴿a group among them would have resolved﴾

He says: they had resolved, that is, they harboured [the intention] ﴿a faction﴾

That is, a group, ﴿among them﴾

That is, Ta'mah, ﴿to mislead you﴾

That is, to make you err. ﴿But they mislead none except themselves﴾

He says: they err only against themselves. ﴿And they do not harm you at all﴾

And their harm falls upon those who bore witness without right. ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom﴾

That is, the Qur'an and wisdom, meaning judgment by revelation. ﴿And taught you what you did not know﴾

Before revelation. ﴿And ever has the bounty of Allah upon you been great﴾

Allah's favour upon you ﴿great﴾

Through prophethood.

This is the saying of al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas.

Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: then he said: ﴿And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾

That is, Islam and the Qur'an. ﴿A group among them would have resolved﴾

That is, from Thaqif, ﴿to mislead you﴾

And that was because the delegation of Thaqif came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, we have come to you to pledge allegiance to you on condition that there be no gathering, no resurrection, and we will not break idols with our own hands, and that you let us enjoy al-'Uzza for a year." He did not agree to that, and Allah protected him by His favour, and informed him of His blessing upon him, that he was under His protection and guardianship, so that no matter that he disliked would reach him. Then He said: ﴿But they mislead none except themselves﴾

That is, the delegation of Thaqif. ﴿And they do not harm you at all﴾

That is, they cannot remove prophethood from you, since Allah has made you worthy of it. Then He said: ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom﴾

That is, the rulings. ﴿And taught you what you did not know﴾

Of the laws. ﴿And ever has the bounty of Allah been great﴾

That is, the favour of Allah upon you ﴿with faith, great.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 4, verses 104–113:**

﴿And do not falter in pursuit of the people﴾: do not weaken in seeking the people, meaning Abu Sufyan and his companions, on the day of Uhud. This story has already passed in Surah Al 'Imran.

﴿If you suffer pain, indeed they suffer pain as you suffer pain﴾: i.e., you feel pain and complain of the wounds, and they feel pain and complain of the wounds, as you do, while you remain safe. ﴿And you hope from Allah for that which they do not hope﴾: i.e., reward, recompense, the victory Allah has promised you, and the manifestation of your religion over all other religions.

It is also said that the verse ﴿and you hope from Allah for that which they do not hope﴾ means: you fear from the punishment of Allah what they do not fear. Al-Farra' said: "Hope (*raja'*) does not mean fear (*khawf*) except with negation, like the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Say to those who believe that they should forgive those who do not hope for the days of Allah﴾, meaning who do not fear the days of Allah. Likewise His saying: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not hope for dignity from Allah?﴾, meaning you do not fear greatness from Allah. This is the Hijazi dialect (*lugha hijaziyya*)."

The poet said:

*"You do not hope when you meet the defender, whether seven met together or one."* [Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/358]

Al-Hudhali said, describing the honey-collector (*mu'tar al-'asal*) who has a woven/stitched (*nawb*) — meaning the bees:

*"And in the verse, 'a nawb that is 'awamil' ... when the bee stings him he does not hope for its sting."* It is narrated as *"nawb 'awamil"* in one verse, and in another verse it is *"nawb 'awamil"* with a variant (*'awasil*). [Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/358]

He said: It is not permissible to say "I hoped for you" while meaning "I feared you," nor "I feared you" while meaning "I hoped for you." [Lisan al-'Arab: 14/310]

**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 4, verses 104–113:**

﴿And do not falter in pursuit of the people﴾: do not weaken in seeking the people, meaning Abu Sufyan and his companions, on the day of Uhud. This story has already passed in Surah Al 'Imran.

﴿If you suffer pain, indeed they suffer pain as you suffer pain﴾: i.e., you feel pain and complain of the wounds, and they feel pain and complain of the wounds, as you do, while you remain safe. ﴿And you hope from Allah for that which they do not hope﴾: i.e., reward, recompense, the victory Allah has promised you, and the manifestation of your religion over all other religions.

It is also said that the verse ﴿and you hope from Allah for that which they do not hope﴾ means: you fear from the punishment of Allah what they do not fear. Al-Farra' said: "Hope (*raja'*) does not mean fear (*khawf*) except with negation, like the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Say to those who believe that they should forgive those who do not hope for the days of Allah﴾, meaning who do not fear the days of Allah. Likewise His saying: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not hope for dignity from Allah?﴾, meaning you do not fear greatness from Allah. This is the Hijazi dialect (*lugha hijaziyya*)."

The poet said:

*"You do not hope when you meet the defender, whether seven met together or one."* [Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/358]

Al-Hudhali said, describing the honey-collector (*mu'tar al-'asal*) who has a woven/stitched (*nawb*) — meaning the bees:

*"And in the verse, 'a nawb that is 'awamil' ... when the bee stings him he does not hope for its sting."* It is narrated as *"nawb 'awamil"* in one verse, and in another verse it is *"nawb 'awamil"* with a variant (*'awasil*). [Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/358]

He said: It is not permissible to say "I hoped for you" while meaning "I feared you," nor "I feared you" while meaning "I hoped for you." [Lisan al-'Arab: 14/310]

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book with truth﴾

Al-Kalbi narrated from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: This verse was revealed concerning a man from the Ansar called Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq, of the Banu Zafar, a clan of Sulaym, who stole a coat of mail (*dir'*) from a neighbour of his called Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man. The coat of mail was in a sack containing flour, and the flour was scattering through a hole in the sack, until it reached the house, and there were traces of flour in it. Then he hid it with a Jewish man called Zayd ibn al-Samin. The coat of mail was searched for at Ta'mah's house but was not found there, and he swore to them, "By Allah, I did not take it and I have no knowledge of it." The owners of the coat of mail said, "Yes, by Allah, he entered our house, so bring it back to us," and they followed his trail, and they saw the scattered flour, until they reached the Jew's dwelling. Then they seized him, and the Jew said, "Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq gave it to me." Some Jews testified to this. The Banu Zafar, the people of Ta'mah, said: "Shall they take us to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) so that we may speak to him about our companion, and excuse him, and argue on his behalf? Our companion appears to be excused." So they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and spoke to him about it, asking him to argue on behalf of their companion, and they said: "If you do not do so, our companion will be destroyed and disgraced, and the Jew will be cleared." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended to do so and to punish the Jew, so Allah, the Exalted, revealed reproof to him: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book with truth﴾, the verses.

In another narration from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: Ta'mah stole a coat of mail from an Ansari man, and it was in a sack containing bran. He tore the sack so that the bran scattered from it all along the road. He came to the house of Zayd ibn al-Samin following the trail of the bran, [took it] and brought it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended to cut off the hand of the Jew Zayd, so Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse.

'Ali ibn al-Dahhak said: This verse was revealed concerning a man from the Ansar who was entrusted with a coat of mail, and its owner denied it. Some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accused him of betrayal. His people came and excused him and insisted upon him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) believed them, excused them, and rejected those who had said what they said about him. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse. When his treachery became clear, he apostatized from Islam and joined Makkah. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 110], the verse.

Muqatil said: Zayd al-Samin deposited a coat of mail with Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq, and Ta'mah denied it. When Zayd came seeking it, he closed the door, went up onto the roof, and threw the coat of mail into the house of his neighbour Abu Hilal. Then he opened the door, and they found nothing in it. He went up to the roof and said: "I see a coat of mail in the house of Abu Hilal; perhaps it is your coat of mail." They looked, and it was indeed that, and they took it up. Then Ta'mah gathered his people, and they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), complaining and saying: "They have disgraced us and accused us of theft." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reproached them, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book with truth﴾, meaning with the command, the prohibition, and the decisive judgment; ﴿so that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, meaning what Allah has taught you and revealed to you; ﴿and do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾, meaning a helper.

﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ for what you intended of cutting off the hand of Zayd.

Al-Kalbi: ﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾, O Muhammad, for your intention regarding the Jew, to strike him.

Muqatil: ﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ for your argument by which you argued on behalf of Ta'mah. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful.﴾

﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾

That is, who wrong themselves by treachery and theft, and cast it upon the Jew. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is treacherous and sinful﴾

That is, treacherous regarding the coat of mail. ﴿Sinful﴾

In his casting [of the accusation] upon the Jew and in His saying: ﴿And do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾. It has been said that the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ) while the intended meaning is someone else, like His saying: ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you﴾ [Surah Yunus: 94]. The Prophet (ﷺ) does not doubt what Allah has sent down. If it is said: he has been commanded to seek forgiveness, we say: this does not imply the existence of a sin, nor is it necessary that he seek forgiveness only for a sin, just as He commanded in Surah al-Fath to seek forgiveness without a preceding sin.

Know that seeking forgiveness (*istighfar*) in the case of all the prophets has several aspects. Among them, three aspects: it is for a preceding sin, such as [before] prophethood; it is for the sin of his community and relatives; and it is for leaving what is permissible (*al-mubah*) before the arrival of the restriction (*al-hadr*). Its meaning is by hearing and obedience to what he was commanded and forbidden, and by the bearing of divine success (*tawfiq*) upon it.

﴿They hide from the people﴾

That is, they conceal themselves and are ashamed before the people. ﴿And they do not hide from Allah﴾

That is, they do not conceal themselves nor feel shame before Allah. ﴿And He is with them﴾

That is, His knowledge.

﴿When they plot﴾

Al-Kalbi narrated from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, they say. From Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Abu Razin: they utter. ﴿What He does not approve of in speech﴾

That is, that the Jew stole it. ﴿And Allah is ever, of what they do, encompassing﴾

That is, Allah has encompassed their good deeds.

The Jahmiyya (followers of Jahm ibn Safwan) and the Mu'tazila (the rationalist school) clung to this verse. They used it as evidence that Allah is in every place. They said: when He said ﴿And He is with them﴾, this establishes that He is in every place, because He has affirmed His being with them. And as for His saying to them, in the sense of ﴿And He is with them﴾, that He knows what they say and that their deed is not hidden from Him, because He is the Knower of what creatures display and what they conceal. There is nothing in His saying ﴿And He is with them﴾ that necessitates that He is in every place, because He said: ﴿Are you secure from He who is in the heaven that He will cause the earth to swallow you?﴾ [Surah al-Mulk: 16], and His saying "He who is in the heaven" does not mean other than His essence, because the statement "Zayd is in such-and-such a place" without mention of any act or any other thing can only refer to his essence. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾ [Surah Fatir: 10], and He said: ﴿He arranges the affair from the heaven to the earth﴾ [Surah al-Sajdah: 5]. Thus He informed that [He] raises things from the heaven, and it is not permissible that He be with them in His essence and at the same time arrange the affair from the heaven and ascend to Him the good word.
