﴿There is no good in much of their secret talk.﴾

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: it refers to the people of Ta'mah. ﴿Except for one who enjoins charity﴾, i.e., urges it; ﴿or kindness﴾, i.e., helps someone by extending a loan; ﴿or reconciliation between people﴾, i.e., between Ta'mah and the Jew. ﴿And whoever does that﴾, i.e., the loan, by granting it or as a gift, ﴿seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾, i.e., seeking His approval, ﴿We shall give him﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿a great reward﴾, meaning Paradise.

From Ibn Sirin: the meaning of najwa (secret talk) in speech is that a group speaks privately, whether the person is in secret or in the open. The meaning of najwa in a specific usage comes from najawtu al-jild 'an al-ba'ir wa ghayrihi, meaning "I stripped the hide off the camel or other animal" (i.e., I removed it from it).

The poet said:

"I said, 'Strip it off, for the hide has been stripped; the hump and the wound will satisfy you both from it.'"

It is also said: najawtu fulanan, meaning "I smelled his breath" (istankahtuhu).

The poet said:

"I smelled Mujalid, and found from him
a smell like a dog's, that has died recently."

And najawtu al-watar wa-istanjaytuhu means "I cleared the string of a bow" when I purified it.

The poet said:

"He slumped, and slumped again, for her,
like the sitting of the left-handed man who cleans the bowstring."

All of this originates from najwa, which is a raised place on the ground.

The poet said:

"Like one who is on his high ground, like one in his shelter,
and the concealed one, like one walking in the open."

So the meaning of ﴿there is no good in much of their secret talk﴾ is what they recorded of their speech among themselves. ﴿Except for one who enjoins charity﴾ may be in the genitive, accusative, or nominative position. The genitive reading is as if you said: "There is no good in much of their secret talk, except in one who enjoins charity."

Here, najwa refers to the men who conspire together, as in His words: ﴿while they were in secret conference﴾.

Some scholars said: najwa is a noun, and ﴿except﴾ is an exception from a different category, so the accusative reading is clear, since the najwa is treated as a verb.

The poet Al-Nabigha said:

"Except the tethering posts, with their difficulty, how clearly they show,
and the trench like a pool at the hard ground."

The word may also be in the nominative position. The accusative is then treated as a definite term.

The poet said:

"A land where there is no companion,
except the gazelles, and except the camels."

﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him﴾ was also revealed concerning Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq. When the Qur'an was revealed about him and his people knew he was a wrongdoer, and he feared for himself from the amputation and disgrace, he fled to Mecca. So Allah revealed about him: ﴿whoever opposes the Messenger﴾, i.e., contradicts him, ﴿after guidance has become clear to him﴾, i.e., the Oneness of God with its limits, ﴿and follows other than the way of the believers﴾, i.e., the religion of the believers, which is the religion of the people of Mecca, the worship of idols. ﴿We shall turn him over to what he has turned to﴾, i.e., We shall leave him to what he chose, and what he stored up for himself in this world, ﴿and burn him in Hell, and evil is it as a destination.﴾

Ta'mah did not desist, did not reconsider, but deliberately went out at night toward a man from the Banu Sulaym from among the people of Mecca. The pilgrims said to him: "Stop, you mixture!" He then broke into the man's house, and a stone fell on him from the house, so he was injured by it and could not get in. He said: "Rajjihni" (i.e., return me) with the meaning "asbaha" (he became). He took [yatfulu] (so in the manuscript), and some of them said: "Leave him, for he has sought refuge with you." So they left him and expelled him from Mecca. He went out with merchants from Quda'a toward Syria, and at a stop he stole some of their goods and fled. They pursued him, caught him, and stoned him to death. His grave became those stones. It is also said that he boarded a ship toward Jeddah, and stole a purse of dinars from the ship. They seized him, and he was thrown into the sea. It is also said that he went down into the lava field of the Banu Sulaym and worshiped one of their idols until he died. So Allah revealed about him: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates partners with Allah has certainly strayed far astray.﴾ And there was revealed about him: ﴿As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands﴾ [Qur'an 5:38], and so on.

From Jawbar, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿whoever opposes the Messenger﴾: this verse was revealed concerning a group of Quraysh who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina and entered Islam. The Messenger of Allah gave them gifts, then they returned to Mecca as apostates and went back to worshiping idols. So Allah revealed about them this verse: ﴿whoever opposes the Messenger﴾, i.e., separates from the Messenger, opposes him, and wars against him, ﴿after guidance has become clear to him﴾, meaning after it had become clear to him that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, ﴿and follows other than the way of the believers﴾, i.e., other than the path of the Muslims. ﴿We shall turn him over to what he has turned to﴾, i.e., We shall leave him to the idols on the Day of Resurrection, though they own no harm or benefit and cannot save them from the punishment of Allah. ﴿And burn him in Hell﴾ for worshiping idols.

﴿And evil is it as a destination﴾, meaning: wretched is the abode they will settle in on the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: concerning His words Most High: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾, he said: an old man from the Bedouins came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Prophet of Allah, I am an old man who has indulged in sins and transgressions, but I have never associated anything with Allah since I came to know Him, and I believed in Him. I have not taken any protector besides Him, nor have I committed sins out of boldness toward Allah or arrogance toward Him, nor have I imagined it even for the blink of an eye. Indeed, I cannot escape Allah by fleeing, and I am regretful, repentant, and seeking forgiveness. What then is my state with Allah?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾, and shirk is a sin that is not forgiven for one who dies in it. ﴿But He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates partners with Allah has certainly strayed far astray﴾, meaning he has gone astray from the path and deprived himself of all good.

Know that in His words Most High, ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger﴾, there is evidence for the strength of the argument of the consensus (ijma', the agreement of scholars). And in His words:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾ there is evidence for the corruption of the view of the Khawarij (a sect that declared a grave sinner to be a disbeliever), when they claimed that the perpetrator of a major sin is a disbeliever. This is His statement, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.﴾ He distinguished between shirk and other sins, and made it definite for Himself that He would not forgive shirk.

If major sin were disbelief, His statement ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾ would be all-encompassing. Since He distinguished between shirk and other sins, the corruption of their view became clear. Allah has also explained at the end of the story what the shirk is, in His words: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [deities], and they invoke none but a rebellious devil.﴾ It is known that the one who commits a major sin without considering it lawful cannot be given the ruling of a disbeliever. This also shows the corruption of the view of the Mu'tazila concerning the intermediate position (manzila) between shirk and faith, since Allah has not placed any intermediate position between shirk and faith, and has not made sins the opposite of faith.

Also, the view of those who say major sin is disbelief is corrupt. So Allah revealed about him: ﴿whoever opposes the Messenger﴾, i.e., contradicts him, ﴿after guidance has become clear to him﴾, i.e., the Oneness of God with its limits, ﴿and follows other than the way of the believers﴾, i.e., the religion of the believers, which is the religion of the people of Mecca, the worship of idols. ﴿We shall turn him over to what he has turned to﴾, i.e., We shall leave him to what he chose, and what he stored up for himself in this world, ﴿and burn him in Hell, and evil is it as a destination.﴾

Ta'mah did not desist, did not reconsider, but deliberately went out at night toward a man from the Banu Sulaym from among the people of Mecca. The pilgrims said to him: "Stop, you mixture!" He then broke into the man's house, and a stone fell on him from the house, so he was injured by it and could not get in. He said: "Rajjihni" (i.e., return me) with the meaning "asbaha" (he became). He took [yatfulu] (so in the manuscript), and some of them said: "Leave him, for he has sought refuge with you." So they left him and expelled him from Mecca. He went out with merchants from Quda'a toward Syria, and at a stop he stole some of their goods and fled. They pursued him, caught him, and stoned him to death. His grave became those stones. It is also said that he boarded a ship toward Jeddah, and stole a purse of dinars from the ship. They seized him, and he was thrown into the sea. It is also said that he went down into the lava field of the Banu Sulaym and worshiped one of their idols until he died. So Allah revealed about him: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates partners with Allah has certainly strayed far astray.﴾ And there was revealed about him: ﴿As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands﴾ [Qur'an 5:38], and so on.

From Jawbar, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿whoever opposes the Messenger﴾: this verse was revealed concerning a group of Quraysh who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina and entered Islam. The Messenger of Allah gave them gifts, then they returned to Mecca as apostates and went back to worshiping idols. So Allah revealed about them this verse: ﴿whoever opposes the Messenger﴾, i.e., separates from the Messenger, opposes him, and wars against him, ﴿after guidance has become clear to him﴾, meaning after it had become clear to him that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, ﴿and follows other than the way of the believers﴾, i.e., other than the path of the Muslims. ﴿We shall turn him over to what he has turned to﴾, i.e., We shall leave him to the idols on the Day of Resurrection, though they own no harm or benefit and cannot save them from the punishment of Allah. ﴿And burn him in Hell﴾ for worshiping idols.

﴿And evil is it as a destination﴾, meaning: wretched is the abode they will settle in on the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: concerning His words Most High: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾, he said: an old man from the Bedouins came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Prophet of Allah, I am an old man who has indulged in sins and transgressions, but I have never associated anything with Allah since I came to know Him, and I believed in Him. I have not taken any protector besides Him, nor have I committed sins out of boldness toward Allah or arrogance toward Him, nor have I imagined it even for the blink of an eye. Indeed, I cannot escape Allah by fleeing, and I am regretful, repentant, and seeking forgiveness. What then is my state with Allah?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾, and shirk is a sin that is not forgiven for one who dies in it. ﴿But He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates partners with Allah has certainly strayed far astray﴾, meaning he has gone astray from the path and deprived himself of all good.

Know that in His words Most High, ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger﴾, there is evidence for the strength of the argument of the consensus (ijma', the agreement of scholars). And in His words:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾ there is evidence for the corruption of the view of the Khawarij (a sect that declared a grave sinner to be a disbeliever), when they claimed that the perpetrator of a major sin is a disbeliever. This is His statement, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.﴾ He distinguished between shirk and other sins, and made it definite for Himself that He would not forgive shirk.

If major sin were disbelief, His statement ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾ would be all-encompassing. Since He distinguished between shirk and other sins, the corruption of their view became clear. Allah has also explained at the end of the story what the shirk is, in His words: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [deities], and they invoke none but a rebellious devil.﴾ It is known that the one who commits a major sin without considering it lawful cannot be given the ruling of a disbeliever. This also shows the corruption of the view of the Mu'tazila concerning the intermediate position (manzila) between shirk and faith, since Allah has not placed any intermediate position between shirk and faith, and has not made sins the opposite of faith.

Also, the view of those who say major sin is disbelief is corrupt. There is evidence here for the corruption of the view of the Murji'a (those who postponed judgment on sinners), when they said: "The believer will not be punished, even if he commits sins." Because Allah removed the polytheist from the scope of forgiveness and made his ruling definite. If it were not permissible to punish the sinning believer, He would have removed him from the exception and stated the ruling about him absolutely, as He did with shirk. There is also evidence here for the corruption of the view of the Wa'idiyya (those who hold that the threat of punishment binds Allah absolutely), which we have mentioned before.

Then there was revealed concerning the people of Mecca: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [deities]﴾, like His words Most High: ﴿And your Lord says: Call upon Me; I will respond to you﴾ [Qur'an 40:60], i.e., worship Me and I will answer you. The phrase ﴿lakum﴾ (for you) is explained by His words after it: ﴿Indeed, those who are arrogant about My worship﴾.

﴿Besides Him﴾, i.e., besides Allah. Each of these idols had a devil within it, appearing to the custodians and soothsayers, speaking to them. This is His statement: ﴿and they invoke none but a rebellious devil﴾ [Qur'an 4:117]. The polytheists called their idols by name. This was the view of Mujahid, al-Kalbi, and most exegetes.

The correctness of this interpretation is supported by the recitation of Ibn 'Abbas: "in yad'una min dunihi illa awthanan" (they invoke besides Him none but idols), the plural of wathan (idol), where the waw is changed into a hamza, as in aqab and waqab. Its root is wathn. It was also recited as "inathan" (female), on the pattern of the plural of ina\u0101th (females), as in mithal, mathal, and thimar, thamar. Al-Hasan, Qatada, and Abu 'Ubayda said: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [deities]﴾ means lifeless things, with no spirit in them: wood, stone, clay, and the like.

This is because all inanimate things are referred to as feminine, as one refers to a feminine noun. From this, the idols are referred to with the statement: "in yad'un" (they invoke) and "wa ma ta'buduna" (and what you worship). ﴿But none but a rebellious devil﴾. The word marid means the one who rebels, and it is said it is in the sense of the active participle, like qadir and qadir (powerful). It means the fierce, stubborn one who has departed from obedience. It is said: marada al-rajul yamrudu murudan wa muradan, meaning he became defiant and departed from obedience. The root of marid comes from the Arab saying "hadathana mumarrid" (our narrator was smooth), meaning smooth.

It is also said: "shajara marda," meaning a tree whose leaves have shed. That is why one who has no beard is called amrad, meaning smooth where the beard would be.

Therefore, the meaning is: one who has departed from obedience and slipped out of it.

May Allah curse him. ﴿And he said﴾, meaning Iblis: ﴿"I will surely take from among Your servants a portion assigned."﴾ (Qur'an 4:118) "A portion assigned" means a known share. Whatever Iblis succeeds in misleading people into is "assigned" (mafrud). Al-Farra' said: "It means he has no authority over them, and it is like what is assigned. In some interpretations, 'all' refers to the sons of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the rest belong to Iblis."

The root meaning of *al-fard* (obligation, assignment) in the language is "severing." From it comes *al-fardah* in a river, which is a breach in it. It is said that its meaning is *bi-l-firad* and *al-fard*. *Al-fard* is the notch in a net where the thread is tied. *Al-farid* is the notch in a bow where the string is tied. *Al-fariḍah* (the obligation) refers to whatever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ordered His servants to do, making it a binding and definite command upon them. His words ﴿"And if you have already specified for them an obligation [a dowry]"﴾ (Qur'an 2:237) mean a portion of wealth for them.

It is said: "I assigned for the man," meaning I set aside for him a portion of wealth.

The poet said:

*"When I ate fish and fard,*
*I went long and I went wide."*

*Al-fard* here means dates, and dates were called *fard* because they are taken in the obligatory charity (fara'id al-sadaqah).

Then Iblis said: ﴿"And I will surely mislead them"﴾ [meaning these people], ﴿"and I will surely give them false hopes"﴾, that there is no Paradise, no Fire, and no resurrection.

Some of them said: ﴿"And I will surely give them false hopes"﴾ means I will cast into their hearts [*al-haymanah*, wishful deception]. ﴿"And I will surely command them, and they will slit the ears of cattle"﴾, meaning they will cut them and split them. This refers to the *bahirah* (the slit-eared she-camel). ﴿"And I will surely command them, and they will alter the creation of Allah."﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, reporting from al-Hasan, Qatadah, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, said: it means the religion of Allah, similar to His words: ﴿"There is no alteration to the creation of Allah"﴾ (Qur'an 30:30), meaning the religion of Allah.

'Ikrimah and a group of exegetes said: its meaning is "they will alter the creation of Allah" by dyeing [with henna], tattooing, cutting the ears, and gouging out the eyes.

The people of meanings (*ahl al-ma'ani*) said: the meaning of His words ﴿"and they will alter the creation of Allah"﴾ is that Allah created cattle for you to ride and eat, yet they forbade them to themselves. And He created the sun, moon, and stones subjected to people to benefit from, yet the polytheists worshipped them, thus altering the creation of Allah.

﴿"And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah"﴾, meaning as a lord, ﴿"and obeys him, has certainly suffered a clear loss."﴾ ﴿"He promises them"﴾ that they will not meet with good, ﴿"and gives them false hopes"﴾ of poverty, so that they do not spend in good or maintain kinship ties. ﴿"He gives them false hopes"﴾ that there is no resurrection, no Paradise, and no Fire. ﴿"And Satan promises them nothing but delusion"﴾, meaning falsehood. ﴿"Those, their refuge is Hell"﴾, meaning their destination is Hell, ﴿"and they will not find an escape from it"﴾, meaning no way of refuge.

'Awf said: "It has reached me that the believer, by his cunning against Satan, [achieves] more than Mudar [would achieve]. If Allah were to replace them for him, he would die."

If it is said: "Inform us about Iblis's words ﴿'I will surely take from among Your servants a portion assigned'﴾ [Qur'an 4:118]. How did he know that?"

It is said: There are several answers to this. One is that they say Allah, blessed and exalted, addressed him with His words ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with you and those who follow you, all together"﴾ (Qur'an 11:119). So Iblis knew that he would obtain from the offspring of Adam what he desires.

Another is that they say: when he whispered to Adam and obtained from him what he obtained, he hoped for his descendants, though he did not obtain from Adam all that he wished for in misguidance. So he hoped for some of his descendants and despaired of all of them.

Another is that they say: Iblis had witnessed Paradise and Hell and knew that Allah created them for people and jinn to dwell in. On this interpretation, he said ﴿"I will surely take from among Your servants a portion assigned."﴾

If it is said: "Inform us about the misguidance of Satan: Did his action succeed and his command take effect or not?"

It is said to him: the meaning of his misguiding is calling to error and adorning it for people. Had the error been up to him, he would have misguided all creation. That is why Allah bestowed favor upon their father (Adam) through ﴿"But those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is true, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement?"﴾ (Qur'an 4:122). That is, beneath the upper chambers and dwellings. Then He said: ﴿"It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book."﴾ (Qur'an 4:123)

Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: the Muslims and the People of the Book debated. The People of the Book said: "Our prophet came before your prophet, and our book before yours, and we are more deserving of Allah than you." The Muslims said: "We are more deserving of Allah than you, and our prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our book surpasses the books that came before it." So Allah, exalted, revealed ﴿"It is not by your wishful thinking..."﴾ the verse.

Mujahid said: the Quraysh said: "We will not be resurrected or held to account."

The People of the Book said: ﴿"The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days"﴾ (Qur'an 2:80). So Allah revealed: ﴿"It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book."﴾

The subject of *laysa* (it is not) is implied: "The reward of Allah is not by your wishful thinking..." ﴿"Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. He will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper."﴾ (Qur'an 4:123)

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: When this verse was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of us does not do evil apart from you? And what is the recompense?" He said: "Some of it occurs in this world. Whoever does a good deed will have ten good deeds [for it], and whoever is requited with an evil deed, one out of ten is subtracted, and nine good deeds remain for him. Woe to him whose ones outweigh his tens."

As for what is recompensed in the Hereafter, it is delayed until the Day of Resurrection, when his good and evil deeds are compared, and the surplus is examined. He is given his recompense in Paradise, and each person of deeds is given his surplus.

Isma'il narrated from Abu Khalid, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Zuhayr, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is righteousness after this verse?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Which verse?" He said: "Allah says ﴿'It is not by your wishful thinking...' ... 'Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.'﴾" He said: "We were not recompensed [for our deeds]." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "You have perished, O Abu Bakr. Do you not fall ill? Do you not become weary? Does not calamity befall you?" He said: "Yes." He said: "That is what they are recompensed for."

From 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, relating from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when this verse in Surah an-Nisa' was revealed: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper.﴾ The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Abu Bakr, shall I not recite to you a verse that was revealed to me?' I said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Recite it to me.' So I recited it, and I did not know that I had found a breaking in my back until I stretched out because of it. He said: 'What is wrong with you, O Abu Bakr?'

I said: 'May my father and mother be ransomed for you! Which of us does not do evil, and are we not recompensed for every evil we commit?' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'As for you, O Abu Bakr, and your fellow believers, you are recompensed for that in this world until you meet Allah with no sins.' As for the others, their sins are gathered until they are recompensed on the Day of Resurrection."

'Ata' said: When ﴿"It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book"﴾ was revealed, [Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, how severe this verse is!" He said: "O Abu Bakr, you fall ill, you grieve, and harm befalls you, and that is in return for that." And 'Ata' said:] Abu Bakr said: "The back-breaking verse has come, O Messenger of Allah." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is only the calamities of this world."

'Abdullah ibn Abi Mulaykah narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'A'ishah, who said: "I said: 'I know which verse of the Book of Allah was revealed concerning ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾.'" He said: "The believer is recompensed for his worst deed in this world." Then he mentioned things including illness and fatigue, and others mentioned the thorn that pricks him, all of which are recompense for his deed. O 'A'ishah, no one is held to account on the Day of Resurrection without being punished." She said: "I said: 'Did not Allah say ﴿He will be held to a light account﴾ (Qur'an 84:8)?'" He said: "That is not the reckoning [*al-'ard*]. Whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning is punished." He pointed with his hand: "For the calamity he was struck." [The text here is corrupt in the manuscript.]

Ibn Maytham ibn Yazid narrated from 'Abdullah ibn al-Arqam, who said, from Abu Hurayrah: "When ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book﴾ was revealed, we wept and grieved and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, this verse has left nothing [unaffected].' He said: 'As for the one who sins, [it is] from his own hand. But this was revealed to you. Rejoice and be moderate and seek to be upright. No one among you suffers a calamity in this world except that Allah expiates a sin for him through it, even the thorn that pricks one of you in his foot.'"

Al-Hasan said concerning His words ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾: "It refers to the disbeliever. Allah does not recompense the believer on the Day of Resurrection; rather, the believer is recompensed with the best of his deeds and his evil deeds are overlooked." Then he recited ﴿"That Allah may remove from them the worst of what they did"﴾ (Qur'an 39:35), and he also recited ﴿"And do We recompense any but the ungrateful?"﴾ (Qur'an 34:17).

Al-Tha'labi said: I say, were it not for the evil deed, the recompense would apply to the disbelievers, because of His words in the context of the verse: ﴿"He will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper."﴾ Whoever has no helper or protector on the Day of Resurrection is a disbeliever, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has guaranteed the victory of the believers in both abodes, by His words ﴿"Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe"﴾ (Qur'an 40:51).

But when a general address is revealed and the Messenger explains [that] upon his tongue, since the explanation belongs to him, Allah, exalted, said ﴿"that you may make clear to the people what was revealed to them"﴾ (Qur'an 16:44). Then Allah, exalted, explained the superiority of the believers over their opponents, saying ﴿"And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, even as much as the speck on a date seed"﴾ (Qur'an 4:124). It means that the speck is in the back of the date pit.

From Masruq, who said: When ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book; whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ was revealed, the People of the Book said: "We and you are equal," until ﴿"And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer"﴾ was revealed. And there was also revealed concerning them ﴿"And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah [and knows Allah]"﴾ (Qur'an 4:125).

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: it means one who makes his deed sincerely for Allah. It was also said: one who entrusts his affair to Allah. It was also said: a successful one. ﴿"While being a doer of good"﴾, meaning a monotheist. ﴿"And follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth [hanif]"﴾, meaning the religion of Abraham, hanif, a submitting and sincere one.

Ibn 'Abbas said: From the religion of Abraham are the Ka'bah, the prayer, circumambulating it and around it, the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah, the stoning of the jamarat, shaving the head, the two stations (of 'Arafah and Muzdalifah), and the rest of the rites. So whoever prays toward the qiblah and affirms this description has followed Abraham (peace be upon him). ﴿"And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend"﴾ (Qur'an 4:125).

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿"And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend"﴾: "a pure one and a close friend." It is from the expression "Abu al-Day'fan" (father of the guests), who hosts whoever passes by him. His dwelling was on the roadside. The people suffered a year of drought and hardship, and gathered at the door of his house seeking food. He used to receive grain every year from a friend of his in Egypt. He sent his servants with camels to that intimate friend to ask him for grain. That friend said to his servants: "If Abraham wanted it for himself, we would bear it for him, but the hardship has reached us as it has reached the people." So Abraham's messengers returned to him and passed through the sandy plain (al-Bathda', meaning the easy ground). They said: "If we load up from this sandy plain, so people will see that we have brought grain. We are ashamed to pass by them with empty camels." So they filled those sacks with sand. Then Abraham (peace be upon him) and Sarah were sleeping. They informed him of that. Abraham was worried about the people at his door, and his eyes overcame him, so he slept. Sarah woke up after the day had risen, and said: "Glory be to Allah! The servants have come." They said to her: "Yes." She said: "But they have brought nothing." They said: "Yes, they have." So she went to those sacks and opened them, and found in them the finest white flour. She ordered the bakers, and they baked and fed everyone. When Abraham awoke, he smelled the aroma of the food and said: "O Sarah, where is this food from?" She said: "From your Egyptian friend." He said: "This is from my friend Allah, not from my Egyptian friend." So on that day Allah took him as a sincere intimate friend.

Al-Zajjaj said: "The *khalil* is one whose love has no flaw." It is permissible that he was called the friend of Allah because He loved him and chose him with perfect Paradise. It is also permissible that he was called the friend of Allah, meaning one in need of Allah, because he placed his poverty and neediness only in Allah, sincerely in that. Allah said ﴿"You are the poor toward Allah"﴾ (Qur'an 35:15), since the meaning of *khalil* in the language has been said to be "the poor one."

Zuhayr said, praising Harim ibn Sinan:

*"If a friend in need comes to him on a day of request,*
*he says: 'Neither my wealth is absent nor Harim.'"*

*Al-khullah* means friendship, and *al-khullah* [in another sense] means need. If we derive *khalil* from *al-khullah* [need], it is the deficiency that befalls a person in what he needs. If we derive it from *al-khullah* [friendship], it is the root of friendship, and both meanings are one, because each of the two fills the other's deficiency in affection and need for him.

*Al-khalal* is every gap that occurs in a thing. *Al-khilal* is what one picks the teeth with, and it was called *khilal* because it removes the deficiency from between the teeth. *Al-khall* is a path in sand, meaning a gap opened in it, so it became a path on the ground. *Al-khall* that is eaten (vinegar) was called *khall* because it has lost [*akhalla*] the taste of sweetness. ﴿"And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever, of all things, Encompassing"﴾ (Qur'an 4:126), meaning: because of the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of all things.

May Allah curse him. ﴿And he said﴾, meaning Iblis: ﴿"I will surely take from among Your servants a portion assigned."﴾ (Qur'an 4:118) "A portion assigned" means a known share. Whatever Iblis succeeds in misleading people into is "assigned" (mafrud). Al-Farra' said: "It means he has no authority over them, and it is like what is assigned. In some interpretations, 'all' refers to the sons of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the rest belong to Iblis."

The root meaning of *al-fard* (obligation, assignment) in the language is "severing." From it comes *al-fardah* in a river, which is a breach in it. It is said that its meaning is *bi-l-firad* and *al-fard*. *Al-fard* is the notch in a net where the thread is tied. *Al-farid* is the notch in a bow where the string is tied. *Al-fariḍah* (the obligation) refers to whatever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ordered His servants to do, making it a binding and definite command upon them. His words ﴿"And if you have already specified for them an obligation [a dowry]"﴾ (Qur'an 2:237) mean a portion of wealth for them.

It is said: "I assigned for the man," meaning I set aside for him a portion of wealth.

The poet said:

*"When I ate fish and fard,*
*I went long and I went wide."*

*Al-fard* here means dates, and dates were called *fard* because they are taken in the obligatory charity (fara'id al-sadaqah).

Then Iblis said: ﴿"And I will surely mislead them"﴾ [meaning these people], ﴿"and I will surely give them false hopes"﴾, that there is no Paradise, no Fire, and no resurrection.

Some of them said: ﴿"And I will surely give them false hopes"﴾ means I will cast into their hearts [*al-haymanah*, wishful deception]. ﴿"And I will surely command them, and they will slit the ears of cattle"﴾, meaning they will cut them and split them. This refers to the *bahirah* (the slit-eared she-camel). ﴿"And I will surely command them, and they will alter the creation of Allah."﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, reporting from al-Hasan, Qatadah, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, said: it means the religion of Allah, similar to His words: ﴿"There is no alteration to the creation of Allah"﴾ (Qur'an 30:30), meaning the religion of Allah.

'Ikrimah and a group of exegetes said: its meaning is "they will alter the creation of Allah" by dyeing [with henna], tattooing, cutting the ears, and gouging out the eyes.

The people of meanings (*ahl al-ma'ani*) said: the meaning of His words ﴿"and they will alter the creation of Allah"﴾ is that Allah created cattle for you to ride and eat, yet they forbade them to themselves. And He created the sun, moon, and stones subjected to people to benefit from, yet the polytheists worshipped them, thus altering the creation of Allah.

﴿"And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah"﴾, meaning as a lord, ﴿"and obeys him, has certainly suffered a clear loss."﴾ ﴿"He promises them"﴾ that they will not meet with good, ﴿"and gives them false hopes"﴾ of poverty, so that they do not spend in good or maintain kinship ties. ﴿"He gives them false hopes"﴾ that there is no resurrection, no Paradise, and no Fire. ﴿"And Satan promises them nothing but delusion"﴾, meaning falsehood. ﴿"Those, their refuge is Hell"﴾, meaning their destination is Hell, ﴿"and they will not find an escape from it"﴾, meaning no way of refuge.

'Awf said: "It has reached me that the believer, by his cunning against Satan, [achieves] more than Mudar [would achieve]. If Allah were to replace them for him, he would die."

If it is said: "Inform us about Iblis's words ﴿'I will surely take from among Your servants a portion assigned'﴾ [Qur'an 4:118]. How did he know that?"

It is said: There are several answers to this. One is that they say Allah, blessed and exalted, addressed him with His words ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with you and those who follow you, all together"﴾ (Qur'an 11:119). So Iblis knew that he would obtain from the offspring of Adam what he desires.

Another is that they say: when he whispered to Adam and obtained from him what he obtained, he hoped for his descendants, though he did not obtain from Adam all that he wished for in misguidance. So he hoped for some of his descendants and despaired of all of them.

Another is that they say: Iblis had witnessed Paradise and Hell and knew that Allah created them for people and jinn to dwell in. On this interpretation, he said ﴿"I will surely take from among Your servants a portion assigned."﴾

If it is said: "Inform us about the misguidance of Satan: Did his action succeed and his command take effect or not?"

It is said to him: the meaning of his misguiding is calling to error and adorning it for people. Had the error been up to him, he would have misguided all creation. That is why Allah bestowed favor upon their father (Adam) through ﴿"But those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is true, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement?"﴾ (Qur'an 4:122). That is, beneath the upper chambers and dwellings. Then He said: ﴿"It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book."﴾ (Qur'an 4:123)

Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: the Muslims and the People of the Book debated. The People of the Book said: "Our prophet came before your prophet, and our book before yours, and we are more deserving of Allah than you." The Muslims said: "We are more deserving of Allah than you, and our prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our book surpasses the books that came before it." So Allah, exalted, revealed ﴿"It is not by your wishful thinking..."﴾ the verse.

Mujahid said: the Quraysh said: "We will not be resurrected or held to account."

The People of the Book said: ﴿"The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days"﴾ (Qur'an 2:80). So Allah revealed: ﴿"It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book."﴾

The subject of *laysa* (it is not) is implied: "The reward of Allah is not by your wishful thinking..." ﴿"Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. He will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper."﴾ (Qur'an 4:123)

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: When this verse was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of us does not do evil apart from you? And what is the recompense?" He said: "Some of it occurs in this world. Whoever does a good deed will have ten good deeds [for it], and whoever is requited with an evil deed, one out of ten is subtracted, and nine good deeds remain for him. Woe to him whose ones outweigh his tens."

As for what is recompensed in the Hereafter, it is delayed until the Day of Resurrection, when his good and evil deeds are compared, and the surplus is examined. He is given his recompense in Paradise, and each person of deeds is given his surplus.

Isma'il narrated from Abu Khalid, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Zuhayr, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is righteousness after this verse?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Which verse?" He said: "Allah says ﴿'It is not by your wishful thinking...' ... 'Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.'﴾" He said: "We were not recompensed [for our deeds]." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "You have perished, O Abu Bakr. Do you not fall ill? Do you not become weary? Does not calamity befall you?" He said: "Yes." He said: "That is what they are recompensed for."

I said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Recite it to me.' So I recited it, and I did not know that I had found a breaking in my back until I stretched out because of it. He said: 'What is wrong with you, O Abu Bakr?'

I said: 'May my father and mother be ransomed for you! Which of us does not do evil, and are we not recompensed for every evil we commit?' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'As for you, O Abu Bakr, and your fellow believers, you are recompensed for that in this world until you meet Allah with no sins.' As for the others, their sins are gathered until they are recompensed on the Day of Resurrection."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is only the calamities of this world."

O 'A'ishah, no one is held to account on the Day of Resurrection without being punished." She said: "I said: 'Did not Allah say ﴿He will be held to a light account﴾ (Qur'an 84:8)?'" He said: "That is not the reckoning [*al-'ard*]. Whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning is punished." He pointed with his hand: "For the calamity he was struck." [The text here is corrupt in the manuscript.]

It means that the speck is in the back of the date pit.

The people suffered a year of drought and hardship, and gathered at the door of his house seeking food. He used to receive grain every year from a friend of his in Egypt. He sent his servants with camels to that intimate friend to ask him for grain. That friend said to his servants: "If Abraham wanted it for himself, we would bear it for him, but the hardship has reached us as it has reached the people." So Abraham's messengers returned to him and passed through the sandy plain (al-Bathda', meaning the easy ground). They said: "If we load up from this sandy plain, so people will see that we have brought grain. We are ashamed to pass by them with empty camels." So they filled those sacks with sand. Then Abraham (peace be upon him) and Sarah were sleeping. They informed him of that. Abraham was worried about the people at his door, and his eyes overcame him, so he slept. Sarah woke up after the day had risen, and said: "Glory be to Allah! The servants have come." They said to her: "Yes." She said: "But they have brought nothing." They said: "Yes, they have." So she went to those sacks and opened them, and found in them the finest white flour. She ordered the bakers, and they baked and fed everyone. When Abraham awoke, he smelled the aroma of the food and said: "O Sarah, where is this food from?" She said: "From your Egyptian friend." He said: "This is from my friend Allah, not from my Egyptian friend." So on that day Allah took him as a sincere intimate friend.

Allah said ﴿"You are the poor toward Allah"﴾ (Qur'an 35:15), since the meaning of *khalil* in the language has been said to be "the poor one."

Zuhayr said, praising Harim ibn Sinan:

*"If a friend in need comes to him on a day of request,*
*he says: 'Neither my wealth is absent nor Harim.'"*

*Al-khullah* means friendship, and *al-khullah* [in another sense] means need. If we derive *khalil* from *al-khullah* [need], it is the deficiency that befalls a person in what he needs. If we derive it from *al-khullah* [friendship], it is the root of friendship, and both meanings are one, because each of the two fills the other's deficiency in affection and need for him.

*Al-khalal* is every gap that occurs in a thing. *Al-khilal* is what one picks the teeth with, and it was called *khilal* because it removes the deficiency from between the teeth. *Al-khall* is a path in sand, meaning a gap opened in it, so it became a path on the ground. *Al-khall* that is eaten (vinegar) was called *khall* because it has lost [*akhalla*] the taste of sweetness. ﴿"And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever, of all things, Encompassing"﴾ (Qur'an 4:126), meaning: because of the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of all things.

May Allah curse him. ﴿And he said﴾, meaning Iblis: ﴿"I will surely take from among Your servants a portion assigned."﴾ (Qur'an 4:118) "A portion assigned" means a known share. Whatever Iblis succeeds in misleading people into is "assigned" (mafrud). Al-Farra' said: "It means he has no authority over them, and it is like what is assigned. In some interpretations, 'all' refers to the sons of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the rest belong to Iblis."

The root meaning of *al-fard* (obligation, assignment) in the language is "severing." From it comes *al-fardah* in a river, which is a breach in it. It is said that its meaning is *bi-l-firad* and *al-fard*. *Al-fard* is the notch in a net where the thread is tied. *Al-farid* is the notch in a bow where the string is tied. *Al-fariḍah* (the obligation) refers to whatever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ordered His servants to do, making it a binding and definite command upon them. His words ﴿"And if you have already specified for them an obligation [a dowry]"﴾ (Qur'an 2:237) mean a portion of wealth for them.

It is said: "I assigned for the man," meaning I set aside for him a portion of wealth.

The poet said:

*"When I ate fish and fard,*
*I went long and I went wide."*

*Al-fard* here means dates, and dates were called *fard* because they are taken in the obligatory charity (fara'id al-sadaqah).

Al-Zajjaj said: "The *khalil* is one whose love has no flaw." It is permissible that he was called the friend of Allah because He loved him and chose him with perfect Paradise. It is also permissible that he was called the friend of Allah, meaning one in need of Allah, because he placed his poverty and neediness only in Allah, sincerely in that. Allah said ﴿"You are the poor toward Allah"﴾ (Qur'an 35:15), since the meaning of *khalil* in the language has been said to be "the poor one."

Zuhayr said, praising Harim ibn Sinan:

*he says: 'Neither my wealth is absent nor Harim.'"*

If we derive it from *al-khullah* [friendship], it is the root of friendship, and both meanings are one, because each of the two fills the other's deficiency in affection and need for him.

May Allah curse him. ﴿And he said﴾, meaning Iblis: ﴿"I will surely take from among Your servants a portion assigned."﴾ (Qur'an 4:118) "A portion assigned" means a known share. Another is that they say: Iblis had witnessed Paradise and Hell and knew that Allah created them for people and jinn to dwell in. On this interpretation, he said ﴿"I will surely take from among Your servants a portion assigned."﴾

As for what is recompensed in the Hereafter, it is delayed until the Day of Resurrection, when his good and evil deeds are compared, and the surplus is examined. He is given his recompense in Paradise, and each person of deeds is given his surplus.

It is said: There are several answers to this. One is that they say Allah, blessed and exalted, addressed him with His words ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with you and those who follow you, all together"﴾ (Qur'an 11:119). So Iblis knew that he would obtain from the offspring of Adam what he desires.

Another is that they say: when he whispered to Adam and obtained from him what he obtained, he hoped for his descendants, though he did not obtain from Adam all that he wished for in misguidance. So he hoped for some of his descendants and despaired of all of them.

Another is that they say: Iblis had witnessed Paradise and Hell and knew that Allah created them for people and jinn to dwell in. On this interpretation, he said ﴿"I will surely take from among Your servants a portion assigned."﴾

If it is said: "Inform us about the misguidance of Satan: Did his action succeed and his command take effect or not?"

It is said to him: the meaning of his misguiding is calling to error and adorning it for people. Had the error been up to him, he would have misguided all creation. That is why Allah bestowed favor upon their father (Adam) through ﴿"But those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is true, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement?"﴾ (Qur'an 4:122). That is, beneath the upper chambers and dwellings. Then He said: ﴿"It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book."﴾ (Qur'an 4:123)

Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: the Muslims and the People of the Book debated. The People of the Book said: "Our prophet came before your prophet, and our book before yours, and we are more deserving of Allah than you." The Muslims said: "We are more deserving of Allah than you, and our prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our book surpasses the books that came before it." So Allah, exalted, revealed ﴿"It is not by your wishful thinking..."﴾ the verse.

Mujahid said: the Quraysh said: "We will not be resurrected or held to account."

The People of the Book said: ﴿"The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days"﴾ (Qur'an 2:80). So Allah revealed: ﴿"It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book."﴾

The subject of *laysa* (it is not) is implied: "The reward of Allah is not by your wishful thinking..." ﴿"Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. He will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper."﴾ (Qur'an 4:123)

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: When this verse was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of us does not do evil apart from you? And what is the recompense?" He said: "Some of it occurs in this world. Whoever does a good deed will have ten good deeds [for it], and whoever is requited with an evil deed, one out of ten is subtracted, and nine good deeds remain for him. Woe to him whose ones outweigh his tens."

As for what is recompensed in the Hereafter, it is delayed until the Day of Resurrection, when his good and evil deeds are compared, and the surplus is examined. He is given his recompense in Paradise, and each person of deeds is given his surplus.

Isma'il narrated from Abu Khalid, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Zuhayr, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is righteousness after this verse?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Which verse?" He said: "Allah says ﴿'It is not by your wishful thinking...' ... Do you not become weary? Does not calamity befall you?" He said: "Yes." He said: "That is what they are recompensed for."

I said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Recite it to me.' So I recited it, and I did not know that I had found a breaking in my back until I stretched out because of it. He said: 'What is wrong with you, O Abu Bakr?'

I said: 'May my father and mother be ransomed for you! Which of us does not do evil, and are we not recompensed for every evil we commit?' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'As for you, O Abu Bakr, and your fellow believers, you are recompensed for that in this world until you meet Allah with no sins.' As for the others, their sins are gathered until they are recompensed on the Day of Resurrection."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is only the calamities of this world."

O 'A'ishah, no one is held to account on the Day of Resurrection without being punished." She said: "I said: 'Did not Allah say ﴿He will be held to a light account﴾ (Qur'an 84:8)?'" He said: "That is not the reckoning [*al-'ard*]. Whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning is punished." He pointed with his hand: "For the calamity he was struck." [The text here is corrupt in the manuscript.]

But when a general address is revealed and the Messenger explains [that] upon his tongue, since the explanation belongs to him, Allah, exalted, said ﴿"that you may make clear to the people what was revealed to them"﴾ (Qur'an 16:44). It means that the speck is in the back of the date pit.

The people suffered a year of drought and hardship, and gathered at the door of his house seeking food. He used to receive grain every year from a friend of his in Egypt. He sent his servants with camels to that intimate friend to ask him for grain. That friend said to his servants: "If Abraham wanted it for himself, we would bear it for him, but the hardship has reached us as it has reached the people." So Abraham's messengers returned to him and passed through the sandy plain (al-Bathda', meaning the easy ground). They said: "If we load up from this sandy plain, so people will see that we have brought grain. We are ashamed to pass by them with empty camels." So they filled those sacks with sand. Sarah woke up after the day had risen, and said: "Glory be to Allah! The servants have come." They said to her: "Yes." She said: "But they have brought nothing." They said: "Yes, they have." He said: "This is from my friend Allah, not from my Egyptian friend." So on that day Allah took him as a sincere intimate friend.

It is also permissible that he was called the friend of Allah, meaning one in need of Allah, because he placed his poverty and neediness only in Allah, sincerely in that. Allah said ﴿"You are the poor toward Allah"﴾ (Qur'an 35:15), since the meaning of *khalil* in the language has been said to be "the poor one."

Zuhayr said, praising Harim ibn Sinan:

*"If a friend in need comes to him on a day of request,*
*he says: 'Neither my wealth is absent nor Harim.'"*

*Al-khullah* means friendship, and *al-khullah* [in another sense] means need. If we derive *khalil* from *al-khullah* [need], it is the deficiency that befalls a person in what he needs. If we derive it from *al-khullah* [friendship], it is the root of friendship, and both meanings are one, because each of the two fills the other's deficiency in affection and need for him.

*Al-khalal* is every gap that occurs in a thing. *Al-khilal* is what one picks the teeth with, and it was called *khilal* because it removes the deficiency from between the teeth. *Al-khall* is a path in sand, meaning a gap opened in it, so it became a path on the ground. *Al-khall* that is eaten (vinegar) was called *khall* because it has lost [*akhalla*] the taste of sweetness. ﴿"And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever, of all things, Encompassing"﴾ (Qur'an 4:126), meaning: because of the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of all things.

May Allah curse him. ﴿And he said﴾, meaning Iblis: ﴿"I will surely take from among Your servants a portion assigned."﴾ (Qur'an 4:118) "A portion assigned" means a known share. Whatever Iblis succeeds in misleading people into is "assigned" (mafrud). Al-Farra' said: "It means he has no authority over them, and it is like what is assigned. In some interpretations, 'all' refers to the sons of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the rest belong to Iblis."

The root meaning of *al-fard* (obligation, assignment) in the language is "severing." From it comes *al-fardah* in a river, which is a breach in it. It is said that its meaning is *bi-l-firad* and *al-fard*. *Al-fard* is the notch in a net where the thread is tied. *Al-farid* is the notch in a bow where the string is tied. *Al-fariḍah* (the obligation) refers to whatever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ordered His servants to do, making it a binding and definite command upon them. His words ﴿"And if you have already specified for them an obligation [a dowry]"﴾ (Qur'an 2:237) mean a portion of wealth for them.

It is said: "I assigned for the man," meaning I set aside for him a portion of wealth.

The poet said:

*"When I ate fish and fard,*
*I went long and I went wide."*

*Al-fard* here means dates, and dates were called *fard* because they are taken in the obligatory charity (fara'id al-sadaqah).

Then Iblis said: ﴿"And I will surely mislead them"﴾ [meaning these people], ﴿"and I will surely give them false hopes"﴾, that there is no Paradise, no Fire, and no resurrection.

Some of them said: ﴿"And I will surely give them false hopes"﴾ means I will cast into their hearts [*al-haymanah*, wishful deception]. ﴿"And I will surely command them, and they will slit the ears of cattle"﴾, meaning they will cut them and split them. This refers to the *bahirah* (the slit-eared she-camel). ﴿"And I will surely command them, and they will alter the creation of Allah."﴾

'Ikrimah and a group of exegetes said: its meaning is "they will alter the creation of Allah" by dyeing [with henna], tattooing, cutting the ears, and gouging out the eyes.

The people of meanings (*ahl al-ma'ani*) said: the meaning of His words ﴿"and they will alter the creation of Allah"﴾ is that Allah created cattle for you to ride and eat, yet they forbade them to themselves. And He created the sun, moon, and stones subjected to people to benefit from, yet the polytheists worshipped them, thus altering the creation of Allah.
