He said: "This is from my friend Allah, not from my Egyptian friend." So on that day Allah took him as a sincere intimate friend.

Al-Zajjaj said: "The *khalil* is one whose love has no flaw." It is permissible that he was called the friend of Allah because He loved him and chose him with perfect Paradise. It is also permissible that he was called the friend of Allah, meaning one in need of Allah, because he placed his poverty and neediness only in Allah, sincerely in that. Allah said ﴿"You are the poor toward Allah"﴾ (Qur'an 35:15), since the meaning of *khalil* in the language has been said to be "the poor one."

Zuhayr said, praising Harim ibn Sinan:

*"If a friend in need comes to him on a day of request,*
*he says: 'Neither my wealth is absent nor Harim.'"*

*Al-khullah* means friendship, and *al-khullah* [in another sense] means need. If we derive *khalil* from *al-khullah* [need], it is the deficiency that befalls a person in what he needs. If we derive it from *al-khullah* [friendship], it is the root of friendship, and both meanings are one, because each of the two fills the other's deficiency in affection and need for him.

*Al-khalal* is every gap that occurs in a thing. *Al-khilal* is what one picks the teeth with, and it was called *khilal* because it removes the deficiency from between the teeth. *Al-khall* is a path in sand, meaning a gap opened in it, so it became a path on the ground. *Al-khall* that is eaten (vinegar) was called *khall* because it has lost [*akhalla*] the taste of sweetness. ﴿"And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever, of all things, Encompassing"﴾ (Qur'an 4:126), meaning: because of the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of all things.

May Allah curse him. ﴿And he said﴾, meaning Iblis: ﴿"I will surely take from among Your servants a portion assigned."﴾ (Qur'an 4:118) "A portion assigned" means a known share. Whatever Iblis succeeds in misleading people into is "assigned" (mafrud). Al-Farra' said: "It means he has no authority over them, and it is like what is assigned. In some interpretations, 'all' refers to the sons of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the rest belong to Iblis."

The root meaning of *al-fard* (obligation, assignment) in the language is "severing." From it comes *al-fardah* in a river, which is a breach in it. It is said that its meaning is *bi-l-firad* and *al-fard*. *Al-fard* is the notch in a net where the thread is tied. *Al-farid* is the notch in a bow where the string is tied. *Al-fariḍah* (the obligation) refers to whatever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ordered His servants to do, making it a binding and definite command upon them. His words ﴿"And if you have already specified for them an obligation [a dowry]"﴾ (Qur'an 2:237) mean a portion of wealth for them.

It is said: "I assigned for the man," meaning I set aside for him a portion of wealth.

The poet said:

*"When I ate fish and fard,*
*I went long and I went wide."*

*Al-fard* here means dates, and dates were called *fard* because they are taken in the obligatory charity (fara'id al-sadaqah).

Then Iblis said: ﴿"And I will surely mislead them"﴾ [meaning these people], ﴿"and I will surely give them false hopes"﴾, that there is no Paradise, no Fire, and no resurrection.

Some of them said: ﴿"And I will surely give them false hopes"﴾ means I will cast into their hearts [*al-haymanah*, wishful deception]. ﴿"And I will surely command them, and they will slit the ears of cattle"﴾, meaning they will cut them and split them. This refers to the *bahirah* (the slit-eared she-camel). ﴿"And I will surely command them, and they will alter the creation of Allah."﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, reporting from al-Hasan, Qatadah, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, said: it means the religion of Allah, similar to His words: ﴿"There is no alteration to the creation of Allah"﴾ (Qur'an 30:30), meaning the religion of Allah.

'Ikrimah and a group of exegetes said: its meaning is "they will alter the creation of Allah" by dyeing [with henna], tattooing, cutting the ears, and gouging out the eyes.

The people of meanings (*ahl al-ma'ani*) said: the meaning of His words ﴿"and they will alter the creation of Allah"﴾ is that Allah created cattle for you to ride and eat, yet they forbade them to themselves. And He created the sun, moon, and stones subjected to people to benefit from, yet the polytheists worshipped them, thus altering the creation of Allah.

﴿"And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah"﴾, meaning as a lord, ﴿"and obeys him, has certainly suffered a clear loss."﴾ ﴿"He promises them"﴾ that they will not meet with good, ﴿"and gives them false hopes"﴾ of poverty, so that they do not spend in good or maintain kinship ties. ﴿"He gives them false hopes"﴾ that there is no resurrection, no Paradise, and no Fire. ﴿"And Satan promises them nothing but delusion"﴾, meaning falsehood. ﴿"Those, their refuge is Hell"﴾, meaning their destination is Hell, ﴿"and they will not find an escape from it"﴾, meaning no way of refuge.

'Awf said: "It has reached me that the believer, by his cunning against Satan, [achieves] more than Mudar [would achieve]. If Allah were to replace them for him, he would die."

If it is said: "Inform us about Iblis's words ﴿'I will surely take from among Your servants a portion assigned'﴾ [Qur'an 4:118]. How did he know that?"

It is said: There are several answers to this. One is that they say Allah, blessed and exalted, addressed him with His words ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with you and those who follow you, all together"﴾ (Qur'an 11:119). So Iblis knew that he would obtain from the offspring of Adam what he desires.

Another is that they say: when he whispered to Adam and obtained from him what he obtained, he hoped for his descendants, though he did not obtain from Adam all that he wished for in misguidance. So he hoped for some of his descendants and despaired of all of them.

Another is that they say: Iblis had witnessed Paradise and Hell and knew that Allah created them for people and jinn to dwell in. On this interpretation, he said ﴿"I will surely take from among Your servants a portion assigned."﴾

If it is said: "Inform us about the misguidance of Satan: Did his action succeed and his command take effect or not?"

It is said to him: the meaning of his misguiding is calling to error and adorning it for people. Had the error been up to him, he would have misguided all creation. That is why Allah bestowed favor upon their father (Adam) through ﴿"But those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is true, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement?"﴾ (Qur'an 4:122). That is, beneath the upper chambers and dwellings. Then He said: ﴿"It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book."﴾ (Qur'an 4:123)

Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: the Muslims and the People of the Book debated. The People of the Book said: "Our prophet came before your prophet, and our book before yours, and we are more deserving of Allah than you." The Muslims said: "We are more deserving of Allah than you, and our prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our book surpasses the books that came before it." So Allah, exalted, revealed ﴿"It is not by your wishful thinking..."﴾ the verse.

Mujahid said: the Quraysh said: "We will not be resurrected or held to account."

The People of the Book said: ﴿"The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days"﴾ (Qur'an 2:80). So Allah revealed: ﴿"It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book."﴾

The subject of *laysa* (it is not) is implied: "The reward of Allah is not by your wishful thinking..." ﴿"Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. He will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper."﴾ (Qur'an 4:123)

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: When this verse was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of us does not do evil apart from you? And what is the recompense?" He said: "Some of it occurs in this world. Whoever does a good deed will have ten good deeds [for it], and whoever is requited with an evil deed, one out of ten is subtracted, and nine good deeds remain for him. Woe to him whose ones outweigh his tens."

As for what is recompensed in the Hereafter, it is delayed until the Day of Resurrection, when his good and evil deeds are compared, and the surplus is examined. He is given his recompense in Paradise, and each person of deeds is given his surplus.

Isma'il narrated from Abu Khalid, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Zuhayr, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is righteousness after this verse?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Which verse?" He said: "Allah says ﴿'It is not by your wishful thinking...' ... 'Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.'﴾" He said: "We were not recompensed [for our deeds]." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "You have perished, O Abu Bakr. Do you not fall ill? Do you not become weary? Does not calamity befall you?" He said: "Yes." He said: "That is what they are recompensed for."

From 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, relating from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when this verse in Surah an-Nisa' was revealed: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper.﴾ The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Abu Bakr, shall I not recite to you a verse that was revealed to me?' I said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Recite it to me.' So I recited it, and I did not know that I had found a breaking in my back until I stretched out because of it. He said: 'What is wrong with you, O Abu Bakr?'

I said: 'May my father and mother be ransomed for you! Which of us does not do evil, and are we not recompensed for every evil we commit?' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'As for you, O Abu Bakr, and your fellow believers, you are recompensed for that in this world until you meet Allah with no sins.' As for the others, their sins are gathered until they are recompensed on the Day of Resurrection."

'Ata' said: When ﴿"It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book"﴾ was revealed, [Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, how severe this verse is!" He said: "O Abu Bakr, you fall ill, you grieve, and harm befalls you, and that is in return for that." And 'Ata' said:] Abu Bakr said: "The back-breaking verse has come, O Messenger of Allah." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is only the calamities of this world."

'Abdullah ibn Abi Mulaykah narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'A'ishah, who said: "I said: 'I know which verse of the Book of Allah was revealed concerning ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾.'" He said: "The believer is recompensed for his worst deed in this world." Then he mentioned things including illness and fatigue, and others mentioned the thorn that pricks him, all of which are recompense for his deed. O 'A'ishah, no one is held to account on the Day of Resurrection without being punished." She said: "I said: 'Did not Allah say ﴿He will be held to a light account﴾ (Qur'an 84:8)?'" He said: "That is not the reckoning [*al-'ard*]. Whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning is punished." He pointed with his hand: "For the calamity he was struck." [The text here is corrupt in the manuscript.]

Ibn Maytham ibn Yazid narrated from 'Abdullah ibn al-Arqam, who said, from Abu Hurayrah: "When ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book﴾ was revealed, we wept and grieved and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, this verse has left nothing [unaffected].' He said: 'As for the one who sins, [it is] from his own hand. But this was revealed to you. Rejoice and be moderate and seek to be upright. No one among you suffers a calamity in this world except that Allah expiates a sin for him through it, even the thorn that pricks one of you in his foot.'"

Al-Hasan said concerning His words ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾: "It refers to the disbeliever. Allah does not recompense the believer on the Day of Resurrection; rather, the believer is recompensed with the best of his deeds and his evil deeds are overlooked." Then he recited ﴿"That Allah may remove from them the worst of what they did"﴾ (Qur'an 39:35), and he also recited ﴿"And do We recompense any but the ungrateful?"﴾ (Qur'an 34:17).

Al-Tha'labi said: I say, were it not for the evil deed, the recompense would apply to the disbelievers, because of His words in the context of the verse: ﴿"He will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper."﴾ Whoever has no helper or protector on the Day of Resurrection is a disbeliever, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has guaranteed the victory of the believers in both abodes, by His words ﴿"Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe"﴾ (Qur'an 40:51).

But when a general address is revealed and the Messenger explains [that] upon his tongue, since the explanation belongs to him, Allah, exalted, said ﴿"that you may make clear to the people what was revealed to them"﴾ (Qur'an 16:44). Then Allah, exalted, explained the superiority of the believers over their opponents, saying ﴿"And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, even as much as the speck on a date seed"﴾ (Qur'an 4:124). It means that the speck is in the back of the date pit.

From Masruq, who said: When ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book; whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ was revealed, the People of the Book said: "We and you are equal," until ﴿"And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer"﴾ was revealed. And there was also revealed concerning them ﴿"And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah [and knows Allah]"﴾ (Qur'an 4:125).

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: it means one who makes his deed sincerely for Allah. It was also said: one who entrusts his affair to Allah. It was also said: a successful one. ﴿"While being a doer of good"﴾, meaning a monotheist. ﴿"And follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth [hanif]"﴾, meaning the religion of Abraham, hanif, a submitting and sincere one.

Ibn 'Abbas said: From the religion of Abraham are the Ka'bah, the prayer, circumambulating it and around it, the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah, the stoning of the jamarat, shaving the head, the two stations (of 'Arafah and Muzdalifah), and the rest of the rites. So whoever prays toward the qiblah and affirms this description has followed Abraham (peace be upon him). ﴿"And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend"﴾ (Qur'an 4:125).

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿"And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend"﴾: "a pure one and a close friend." It is from the expression "Abu al-Day'fan" (father of the guests), who hosts whoever passes by him. His dwelling was on the roadside. The people suffered a year of drought and hardship, and gathered at the door of his house seeking food. He used to receive grain every year from a friend of his in Egypt. He sent his servants with camels to that intimate friend to ask him for grain. That friend said to his servants: "If Abraham wanted it for himself, we would bear it for him, but the hardship has reached us as it has reached the people." So Abraham's messengers returned to him and passed through the sandy plain (al-Bathda', meaning the easy ground). They said: "If we load up from this sandy plain, so people will see that we have brought grain. We are ashamed to pass by them with empty camels." So they filled those sacks with sand. Then Abraham (peace be upon him) and Sarah were sleeping. They informed him of that. Abraham was worried about the people at his door, and his eyes overcame him, so he slept. Sarah woke up after the day had risen, and said: "Glory be to Allah! The servants have come." They said to her: "Yes." She said: "But they have brought nothing." They said: "Yes, they have." So she went to those sacks and opened them, and found in them the finest white flour. She ordered the bakers, and they baked and fed everyone. When Abraham awoke, he smelled the aroma of the food and said: "O Sarah, where is this food from?" She said: "From your Egyptian friend." He said: "This is from my friend Allah, not from my Egyptian friend." So on that day Allah took him as a sincere intimate friend.

Al-Zajjaj said: "The *khalil* is one whose love has no flaw." It is permissible that he was called the friend of Allah because He loved him and chose him with perfect Paradise. It is also permissible that he was called the friend of Allah, meaning one in need of Allah, because he placed his poverty and neediness only in Allah, sincerely in that. Allah said ﴿"You are the poor toward Allah"﴾ (Qur'an 35:15), since the meaning of *khalil* in the language has been said to be "the poor one."

Zuhayr said, praising Harim ibn Sinan:

*"If a friend in need comes to him on a day of request,*
*he says: 'Neither my wealth is absent nor Harim.'"*

*Al-khullah* means friendship, and *al-khullah* [in another sense] means need. If we derive *khalil* from *al-khullah* [need], it is the deficiency that befalls a person in what he needs. If we derive it from *al-khullah* [friendship], it is the root of friendship, and both meanings are one, because each of the two fills the other's deficiency in affection and need for him.

*Al-khalal* is every gap that occurs in a thing. *Al-khilal* is what one picks the teeth with, and it was called *khilal* because it removes the deficiency from between the teeth. *Al-khall* is a path in sand, meaning a gap opened in it, so it became a path on the ground. *Al-khall* that is eaten (vinegar) was called *khall* because it has lost [*akhalla*] the taste of sweetness. ﴿"And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever, of all things, Encompassing"﴾ (Qur'an 4:126), meaning: because of the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of all things.

﴿وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ فِي النِّسَاءِ﴾.

al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: This verse was revealed concerning the daughters of Umm Kahha and their inheritance from their mother. This story has already been mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

Mu'awiya ibn Salih, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: In the Jahiliyya (the age of ignorance before Islam), a man would have an orphan girl in his care and would throw his garment over her. Once he had done this, no one could ever marry her. If she was beautiful and he desired her, he would marry her and consume her property. If she was ugly, the men would be prevented from marrying her until she died. Then he would inherit from her. So God forbade this, prohibited it, and revealed this verse.

Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatada and Ibrahim said: The people of the Jahiliyya did not give women and children any share of inheritance. A woman might be ugly in the Jahiliyya, yet possess wealth. Her guardian would dislike marrying her because of her ugliness, and would dislike that someone else marry her because of her wealth. So her guardian would not marry her, but would keep her confined with him until she died, and then he would inherit from her.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When the guardian of an orphan girl was someone who possessed wealth and beauty, he would desire her, marry her, and monopolize her. But if she had neither wealth nor beauty, he would neither marry her nor give her in marriage to another. So God revealed this verse.

It is also related from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayda, who said: A woman from the Ansar called Khawla bint Hakim came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, my brother has died and left daughters. They do not have the beauty that would make men desire them, and they are not given any share of their father's inheritance." So this verse was revealed concerning her.

﴿وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ﴾: that is, they ask you for a ruling (istikhbar, seeking information), ﴿فِي النِّسَاءِ﴾ concerning women. ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ﴾ Say: God gives you a ruling, informs you ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾ concerning them. ﴿وَمَا يُتْلَى﴾ and what is recited, that is, what is recited ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾ to you in the Book, that is, in the Qur'an. The place of "مَا" in the Arabic grammar (i'rab) is in the nominative (raf'), its meaning being: ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ وَمَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾, and [God] gives you a ruling concerning them, and [He also gives you a ruling concerning] what is recited to you in the Book. It is also permissible for it to be in the genitive (khafd) position, so that the meaning would be: "Say: God gives you a ruling concerning them and concerning what is recited among you." But this is remote, because the apparent (zahir) does not get conjoined to a pronoun (the pronoun in "فِيهِنَّ" being in the genitive without a preposition repeated). The nominative reading is clearer, because what is recited in the Book and what is recited among you is, in meaning, what they asked about.

﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ﴾ in His Book, He gives you a ruling concerning them, and this is His saying: ﴿وَآتُوا الْيَتَامَى أَمْوَالَهُمْ﴾ (And give the orphans their property) and the rest of the verse; and His saying: ﴿فِي يَتَامَى النِّسَاءِ اللَّاتِي لَا تُؤْتُونَهُنَّ مَا كُتِبَ لَهُنَّ﴾ concerning the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them, meaning, what has been ordained for them as a share of inheritance. ﴿وَتَرْغَبُونَ أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ﴾ and you desire to marry them, that is, and you turn away from marrying them because of their [lack of] property. It has also been said: "you desire to marry them for their wealth." ﴿وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الْوِلْدَانِ﴾ and the weak among the children, meaning the young children. It is in the genitive position, and the meaning is: "God gives you a ruling concerning them and concerning the weak among the children." ﴿وَأَنْ تَقُومُوا لِلْيَتَامَى بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ and that you stand for the orphans with justice, that is, with fairness. ﴿وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِهِ عَلِيمًا﴾ and whatever good you do, indeed God is ever Knowing of it.

Shu'ba related from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, that the last verse revealed was: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say: God gives you a ruling concerning them," and the last surah [revealed] was Bara'a (al-Tawba). [He also related:] ﴿وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ مِنْ بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزًا أَوْ إِعْرَاضًا﴾ And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband.

It was revealed concerning 'Umra, and it is said: Khuwayla bint Muhammad ibn Maslama, concerning her husband Rafi' ibn al-Rafi', and it is said: Rafi' ibn Khadij. He had married her when she was young. When she grew old (i.e., he married another young woman over her), he favored the other wife over her and neglected her son Muhammad ibn Maslama. She came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and complained to him, so this verse was revealed concerning her.

This is the view of al-Kalbi and a group of the exegetes (mufassirun).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: There was a man who had a wife who had grown old, and he had children by her. He wanted to divorce her and marry someone else. She said: "Do not divorce me. Let me look after my children, and you may share your nights with me once every two months, or more, if you wish; and if you wish, do not share with me." He said: "If that is what prevents you [from divorce], then it is more beloved to me." So he went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and told him about this. He said: "God has heard what you have said. If He wills, He will respond to you." Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ مِنْ بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزًا أَوْ إِعْرَاضًا﴾, that is, she knew from her husband ill-treatment (nushuz), meaning hatred.

al-Kalbi said: That means abandoning intercourse and lying with her, or aversion from living with her, from sitting with her and from conversing with her. ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا﴾ there is no blame upon them both, meaning upon the husband and the wife, ﴿أَنْ يُصْلِحَا بَيْنَهُمَا صُلْحًا﴾ if they make an arrangement between them, a settlement, that is, in the division [of nights] and in maintenance. This is that he says to her: "You are an ugly woman, and you have entered old age, and I want to marry a young, beautiful woman over you." He would then favor her in the division because of her youth. If she accepts this, she stays; and if she dislikes it, I release you. If she accepts that, then she is the one who does good, and that is not difficult for me. But if she does not accept, she is given her right. It is obligatory upon the husband to fulfil her right of residence and maintenance, or to release her with kindness, and not to keep her in humiliation. And if she remains with him, with his dislike for her companionship, and he fulfils her right, then he is the one who does good, whom God has praised, and He informs us that He knows his deed and will reward him for his action. A man cannot be compelled to have intercourse with one wife, because it is his own right and his share (hazz); and if he abandons it, he is not compelled to do it, and it is not like residence and maintenance.

His saying ﴿وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾ and settlement is better means: her remaining [with him] after he has given her the choice, and reconciling with her upon something known regarding residence and maintenance.

The Prophet (ﷺ) acted in this way with his wife, and she remained with him. That was because she was an elderly woman, and the Prophet (ﷺ) wanted to divorce her, but she asked him not to do so, saying: "I wish to be raised among your wives on the Day of Resurrection. So, my day and my night are for 'A'isha."

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said concerning His saying ﴿وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾: "It is when a woman is with a man, and she is either young or old, or her husband does not love her, so they come to an agreement upon a settlement."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It is that they both agree upon something known in itself and in property.

al-Dahhak said: The settlement is that he diminishes her share if he marries someone younger and more pleasing to him than her.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said concerning this verse: It is a man who has an elderly woman under him, and he marries a young woman over her. He says to the elderly woman: "I will give you a portion of my time, on condition that I share with this young woman more than I share with you, by night and by day." The other [wife] accepts what they have agreed upon. If she refuses to accept, then he must be just between them in the division.

Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Farwa related from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا أَنْ يُصْلِحَا بَيْنَهُمَا صُلْحًا وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾ [Qur'an 4:128]. He said: "It concerns an elderly, ugly woman who is with a man who wants to divorce her and replace her. [So he makes a settlement with her] concerning some of her right in the division and maintenance. That is permissible once she has consented. But if she denies it after the settlement, then that is her right, and she is entitled to her right, whether he keeps her or divorces her."

'Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn 'Abbas: It is a woman who is with a man who has another wife whom he loves more than her, so he favors her over her. God, when this occurs, commands that he say to her: "O such-and-such, if you wish to remain with me under these conditions that you see, I will shelter you and maintain you, so remain. And if you dislike it, I will release you." If she consents to remain after he has given her the choice, then there is no blame upon him; and this is His saying ﴿وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾, and this is the giving of choice.

Isra'il related from Simak ibn Harb, from Khalid ibn 'Ar'ara, who said: A man asked 'Ali about the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ مِنْ بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزًا أَوْ إِعْرَاضًا﴾ [the verse]. He said: "A woman is with a man, and his eye turns away from her because of ugliness or age, so she ransoms herself from him, [though] she dislikes separation. If she gives him some of her property, it is lawful for him; or if she gives him some of her household goods, it is lawful for him." ﴿وَأُحْضِرَتِ الْأَنْفُسُ الشُّحَّ﴾ [And souls are made to be prone to stinginess]: that is, the woman is stingy with her share from her husband, and the man is stingy with his share from the other [wife].

Ibn 'Abbas said: Shuhh (stinginess) is being greedy for something. ﴿وَإِنْ تُحْسِنُوا﴾ And if you do good, that is, you reconcile between them equitably, ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ and you guard against injustice and partiality.

It has also been said: this address is to the husband, meaning: ﴿وَإِنْ تُحْسِنُوا﴾ by remaining with her, despite your dislike of her companionship, ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ and you avoid wronging her. ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ indeed God is ever Aware of what you do, informing you of your deeds.

﴿وَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا بَيْنَ النِّسَاءِ﴾ And you will never be able to be just between wives. It means: you will not be able to make them equal in love. ﴿وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ﴾ even if you are eager [to do so]. ﴿فَلَا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ﴾ So do not incline completely [toward one], in maintenance, division and attention to her, ﴿وَتَذَرُوهَا كَالْمُعَلَّقَةِ﴾ and leave the other as one suspended, that is, as one hanging: neither married nor divorced, and without a [husband's] provision.

Qatada and al-Kalbi said: ﴿كَالْمُعَلَّقَةِ﴾ means "like one confined," and this was [said] concerning the wife of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, as if she were imprisoned.

Mujahid said: "You will not be able to be just between them, so do not deliberately [do that]."

It has been mentioned to us that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say: "O God, as for my heart, I do not control it; but as for what is other than that, I hope to be just."

﴿وَإِنْ تُصْلِحُوا﴾ And if you reconcile, by justice in the division among them, ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ and guard against injustice, ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا﴾ indeed God is ever Forgiving, Merciful, [forgiving] for what you have said [of inclination] toward the one you love in your heart, after justice in the division. ﴿وَإِنْ يَتَفَرَّقَا﴾ And if they separate, meaning the woman by divorce, ﴿يُغْنِ اللَّهُ كُلًّا مِنْ سَعَتِهِ﴾ God will enrich each of them from His abundance, that is, from provision: the woman with a husband, and the husband with a wife. ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ وَاسِعًا﴾ and God is ever All-Encompassing, [giving] them both [scope] in marriage, ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ All-Wise, [so that] it is possible for the husband to retain her with kindness or release her with goodness.

The ruling of the verse:

It is known that God, Mighty and Majestic, is compassionate toward His servants and aware of their conditions. So He alerted them to the rights of women that are obligatory upon them, and forbade them from inclining in their actions when they have no means to equalize between them in love. Whenever the servant gathers [his] action toward wealth and turns to one particular wife to the exclusion of others, that is injustice.

It has been related that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to divide [his time] and say: "O God, this is my division in what I possess, so do not blame me for what You possess and I do not" [388] [Tabari, 5/424, where it reads: "do not blame me for what You possess and I do not"]. He meant by this his heart. He used to go around with his wives during his illness until they permitted him [to stay in one place: "his wives" supplied from context], and he remained with 'A'isha.

The basis of the division is the night, because one rests in it. God the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَهُ مَا سَكَنَ فِي اللَّيْلِ﴾ [Qur'an 6:13]. So whenever a man has free Muslim women and dhimmi women, they are equal in division. He divides two nights for a free wife, and one night for a slave wife, if her master leaves him free with her during her night and day. A slave wife may release him from her turn without the master, because it is her right in her own person. He does not have intercourse with a woman on other than her day. And it is not permitted for a man to enter at night to the one for whom he has not been allotted a turn. There is no harm in his entering to her in the daytime for a need, or visiting her in her illness during another's night. If she becomes gravely ill, there is no harm in his remaining until she recovers or dies; then he must make up for the rest of his wives an amount equal to what he spent with her. If he wishes to divide [his time] as two nights or three nights for each, that is permitted for him [Ref.: Mukhtasar al-Muzani, p. 185].

Mention of how those who derive from this verse the imposition of what cannot be borne argue:

They say: God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا بَيْنَ النِّسَاءِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ فَلَا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ﴾. So He commanded them to be just, and informed that they are not able to be just. Thus He commanded them to do what they cannot do, and charged them with what they cannot bear.

If someone says: Did God impose upon the disbelievers what they cannot bear? It is said to him: If you mean that He imposed upon them what they cannot bear due to an incapacity that prevents them, then no, because He has made their bodies sound, perfected their speech, placed them [in the earth] [the text is "fi al-ard"; the apparent reading is as given], and removed from them illnesses and afflictions. And if you mean that He imposed upon them what they are unable to do by their leaving it and occupying themselves with its opposite, then indeed He has imposed that upon them.

If they say: Is it that the disbeliever is not able to occupy himself with disbelief? It is said to them: The meaning of "not occupied with disbelief" is that you believe; so it is as if you said: he is able to believe while remaining upon his disbelief. We have said that as long as he is occupied with disbelief he is not able to believe, in accordance with what the language permits, that a person is able to do something in the sense that if he does not neglect it, it takes effect upon him, as they say: "So-and-so is able over a man," meaning he is able over him if he attempts and intends to carry him, similar to their saying: "So-and-so understands," meaning he understands a thing when it is presented to him. Likewise they say: "The food satisfies (mushbi'),” and "the water quenches (marwi)," meaning that food satisfies when eaten, and water quenches when drunk.

What clarifies this is what people exchange among themselves: a man says: "Come with me at such-and-such a time," and the answer is: "I am not able to come with you because of what I am occupied with." God the Exalted said: ﴿مَا كَانُوا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ السَّمْعَ﴾ [Qur'an 11:20], meaning they could not accept it, because they found it burdensome. As for those who are confused and say: "Is the disbeliever able to believe?" — he says: "If he wills it, he is able to." When it is asked of him: "Is he able to will it?" he says: "If he dislikes disbelief." And when it is asked of him: "Is he able to disbelieve?" he says: "He is able to do that if he wills belief." So whenever the question is repeated to him, he repeats this answer.

﴿وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, [He being] its owner.

﴿وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ فِي النِّسَاءِ﴾.

al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: This verse was revealed concerning the daughters of Umm Kahha and their inheritance from their mother. This story has already been mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

Mu'awiya ibn Salih, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: In the Jahiliyya (the age of ignorance before Islam), a man would have an orphan girl in his care and would throw his garment over her. Once he had done this, no one could ever marry her. If she was beautiful and he desired her, he would marry her and consume her property. If she was ugly, the men would be prevented from marrying her until she died. Then he would inherit from her. So God forbade this, prohibited it, and revealed this verse.

Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatada and Ibrahim said: The people of the Jahiliyya did not give women and children any share of inheritance. A woman might be ugly in the Jahiliyya, yet possess wealth. Her guardian would dislike marrying her because of her ugliness, and would dislike that someone else marry her because of her wealth. So her guardian would not marry her, but would keep her confined with him until she died, and then he would inherit from her.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When the guardian of an orphan girl was someone who possessed wealth and beauty, he would desire her, marry her, and monopolize her. But if she had neither wealth nor beauty, he would neither marry her nor give her in marriage to another. So God revealed this verse.

It is also related from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayda, who said: A woman from the Ansar called Khawla bint Hakim came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, my brother has died and left daughters. They do not have the beauty that would make men desire them, and they are not given any share of their father's inheritance." So this verse was revealed concerning her.

﴿وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ﴾: that is, they ask you for a ruling (istikhbar, seeking information), ﴿فِي النِّسَاءِ﴾ concerning women. ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ﴾ Say: God gives you a ruling, informs you ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾ concerning them. ﴿وَمَا يُتْلَى﴾ and what is recited, that is, what is recited ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾ to you in the Book, that is, in the Qur'an. The place of "مَا" in the Arabic grammar (i'rab) is in the nominative (raf'), its meaning being: ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ وَمَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾, and [God] gives you a ruling concerning them, and [He also gives you a ruling concerning] what is recited to you in the Book. It is also permissible for it to be in the genitive (khafd) position, so that the meaning would be: "Say: God gives you a ruling concerning them and concerning what is recited among you." But this is remote, because the apparent (zahir) does not get conjoined to a pronoun (the pronoun in "فِيهِنَّ" being in the genitive without a preposition repeated). The nominative reading is clearer, because what is recited in the Book and what is recited among you is, in meaning, what they asked about.

﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ﴾ in His Book, He gives you a ruling concerning them, and this is His saying: ﴿وَآتُوا الْيَتَامَى أَمْوَالَهُمْ﴾ (And give the orphans their property) and the rest of the verse; and His saying: ﴿فِي يَتَامَى النِّسَاءِ اللَّاتِي لَا تُؤْتُونَهُنَّ مَا كُتِبَ لَهُنَّ﴾ concerning the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them, meaning, what has been ordained for them as a share of inheritance. ﴿وَتَرْغَبُونَ أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ﴾ and you desire to marry them, that is, and you turn away from marrying them because of their [lack of] property. It has also been said: "you desire to marry them for their wealth." ﴿وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الْوِلْدَانِ﴾ and the weak among the children, meaning the young children. It is in the genitive position, and the meaning is: "God gives you a ruling concerning them and concerning the weak among the children." ﴿وَأَنْ تَقُومُوا لِلْيَتَامَى بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ and that you stand for the orphans with justice, that is, with fairness. ﴿وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِهِ عَلِيمًا﴾ and whatever good you do, indeed God is ever Knowing of it.

Shu'ba related from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, that the last verse revealed was: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say: God gives you a ruling concerning them," and the last surah [revealed] was Bara'a (al-Tawba). [He also related:] ﴿وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ مِنْ بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزًا أَوْ إِعْرَاضًا﴾ And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband.

It was revealed concerning 'Umra, and it is said: Khuwayla bint Muhammad ibn Maslama, concerning her husband Rafi' ibn al-Rafi', and it is said: Rafi' ibn Khadij. He had married her when she was young. When she grew old (i.e., he married another young woman over her), he favored the other wife over her and neglected her son Muhammad ibn Maslama. She came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and complained to him, so this verse was revealed concerning her.

This is the view of al-Kalbi and a group of the exegetes (mufassirun).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: There was a man who had a wife who had grown old, and he had children by her. He wanted to divorce her and marry someone else. She said: "Do not divorce me. Let me look after my children, and you may share your nights with me once every two months, or more, if you wish; and if you wish, do not share with me." He said: "If that is what prevents you [from divorce], then it is more beloved to me." So he went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and told him about this. He said: "God has heard what you have said. If He wills, He will respond to you." Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ مِنْ بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزًا أَوْ إِعْرَاضًا﴾, that is, she knew from her husband ill-treatment (nushuz), meaning hatred.

al-Kalbi said: That means abandoning intercourse and lying with her, or aversion from living with her, from sitting with her and from conversing with her. ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا﴾ there is no blame upon them both, meaning upon the husband and the wife, ﴿أَنْ يُصْلِحَا بَيْنَهُمَا صُلْحًا﴾ if they make an arrangement between them, a settlement, that is, in the division [of nights] and in maintenance. This is that he says to her: "You are an ugly woman, and you have entered old age, and I want to marry a young, beautiful woman over you." He would then favor her in the division because of her youth. If she accepts this, she stays; and if she dislikes it, I release you. If she accepts that, then she is the one who does good, and that is not difficult for me. But if she does not accept, she is given her right. It is obligatory upon the husband to fulfil her right of residence and maintenance, or to release her with kindness, and not to keep her in humiliation. And if she remains with him, with his dislike for her companionship, and he fulfils her right, then he is the one who does good, whom God has praised, and He informs us that He knows his deed and will reward him for his action. A man cannot be compelled to have intercourse with one wife, because it is his own right and his share (hazz); and if he abandons it, he is not compelled to do it, and it is not like residence and maintenance.

His saying ﴿وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾ and settlement is better means: her remaining [with him] after he has given her the choice, and reconciling with her upon something known regarding residence and maintenance.

The Prophet (ﷺ) acted in this way with his wife, and she remained with him. That was because she was an elderly woman, and the Prophet (ﷺ) wanted to divorce her, but she asked him not to do so, saying: "I wish to be raised among your wives on the Day of Resurrection. So, my day and my night are for 'A'isha."

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said concerning His saying ﴿وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾: "It is when a woman is with a man, and she is either young or old, or her husband does not love her, so they come to an agreement upon a settlement."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It is that they both agree upon something known in itself and in property.

al-Dahhak said: The settlement is that he diminishes her share if he marries someone younger and more pleasing to him than her.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said concerning this verse: It is a man who has an elderly woman under him, and he marries a young woman over her. He says to the elderly woman: "I will give you a portion of my time, on condition that I share with this young woman more than I share with you, by night and by day." The other [wife] accepts what they have agreed upon. If she refuses to accept, then he must be just between them in the division.

Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Farwa related from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا أَنْ يُصْلِحَا بَيْنَهُمَا صُلْحًا وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾ [Qur'an 4:128]. He said: "It concerns an elderly, ugly woman who is with a man who wants to divorce her and replace her. [So he makes a settlement with her] concerning some of her right in the division and maintenance. That is permissible once she has consented. But if she denies it after the settlement, then that is her right, and she is entitled to her right, whether he keeps her or divorces her."

'Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn 'Abbas: It is a woman who is with a man who has another wife whom he loves more than her, so he favors her over her. God, when this occurs, commands that he say to her: "O such-and-such, if you wish to remain with me under these conditions that you see, I will shelter you and maintain you, so remain. And if you dislike it, I will release you." If she consents to remain after he has given her the choice, then there is no blame upon him; and this is His saying ﴿وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾, and this is the giving of choice.

Isra'il related from Simak ibn Harb, from Khalid ibn 'Ar'ara, who said: A man asked 'Ali about the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ مِنْ بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزًا أَوْ إِعْرَاضًا﴾ [the verse]. He said: "A woman is with a man, and his eye turns away from her because of ugliness or age, so she ransoms herself from him, [though] she dislikes separation. ﴿وَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا بَيْنَ النِّسَاءِ﴾ And you will never be able to be just between wives. ﴿وَإِنْ تُصْلِحُوا﴾ And if you reconcile, by justice in the division among them, ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ and guard against injustice, ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا﴾ indeed God is ever Forgiving, Merciful, [forgiving] for what you have said [of inclination] toward the one you love in your heart, after justice in the division. ﴿وَإِنْ يَتَفَرَّقَا﴾ And if they separate, meaning the woman by divorce, ﴿يُغْنِ اللَّهُ كُلًّا مِنْ سَعَتِهِ﴾ God will enrich each of them from His abundance, that is, from provision: the woman with a husband, and the husband with a wife. ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ وَاسِعًا﴾ and God is ever All-Encompassing, [giving] them both [scope] in marriage, ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ All-Wise, [so that] it is possible for the husband to retain her with kindness or release her with goodness.
