So He alerted them to the rights of women that are obligatory upon them, and forbade them from inclining in their actions when they have no means to equalize between them in love. Whenever the servant gathers [his] action toward wealth and turns to one particular wife to the exclusion of others, that is injustice.

It has been related that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to divide [his time] and say: "O God, this is my division in what I possess, so do not blame me for what You possess and I do not" [388] [Tabari, 5/424, where it reads: "do not blame me for what You possess and I do not"]. He meant by this his heart. He used to go around with his wives during his illness until they permitted him [to stay in one place: "his wives" supplied from context], and he remained with 'A'isha.

The basis of the division is the night, because one rests in it. God the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَهُ مَا سَكَنَ فِي اللَّيْلِ﴾ [Qur'an 6:13]. So whenever a man has free Muslim women and dhimmi women, they are equal in division. He divides two nights for a free wife, and one night for a slave wife, if her master leaves him free with her during her night and day. A slave wife may release him from her turn without the master, because it is her right in her own person. He does not have intercourse with a woman on other than her day. And it is not permitted for a man to enter at night to the one for whom he has not been allotted a turn. There is no harm in his entering to her in the daytime for a need, or visiting her in her illness during another's night. If she becomes gravely ill, there is no harm in his remaining until she recovers or dies; then he must make up for the rest of his wives an amount equal to what he spent with her. If he wishes to divide [his time] as two nights or three nights for each, that is permitted for him [Ref.: Mukhtasar al-Muzani, p. 185].

Mention of how those who derive from this verse the imposition of what cannot be borne argue:

They say: God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا بَيْنَ النِّسَاءِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ فَلَا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ﴾. So He commanded them to be just, and informed that they are not able to be just. Thus He commanded them to do what they cannot do, and charged them with what they cannot bear.

If someone says: Did God impose upon the disbelievers what they cannot bear? It is said to him: If you mean that He imposed upon them what they cannot bear due to an incapacity that prevents them, then no, because He has made their bodies sound, perfected their speech, placed them [in the earth] [the text is "fi al-ard"; the apparent reading is as given], and removed from them illnesses and afflictions. And if you mean that He imposed upon them what they are unable to do by their leaving it and occupying themselves with its opposite, then indeed He has imposed that upon them.

If they say: Is it that the disbeliever is not able to occupy himself with disbelief? It is said to them: The meaning of "not occupied with disbelief" is that you believe; so it is as if you said: he is able to believe while remaining upon his disbelief. We have said that as long as he is occupied with disbelief he is not able to believe, in accordance with what the language permits, that a person is able to do something in the sense that if he does not neglect it, it takes effect upon him, as they say: "So-and-so is able over a man," meaning he is able over him if he attempts and intends to carry him, similar to their saying: "So-and-so understands," meaning he understands a thing when it is presented to him. Likewise they say: "The food satisfies (mushbi'),” and "the water quenches (marwi)," meaning that food satisfies when eaten, and water quenches when drunk.

What clarifies this is what people exchange among themselves: a man says: "Come with me at such-and-such a time," and the answer is: "I am not able to come with you because of what I am occupied with." God the Exalted said: ﴿مَا كَانُوا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ السَّمْعَ﴾ [Qur'an 11:20], meaning they could not accept it, because they found it burdensome. As for those who are confused and say: "Is the disbeliever able to believe?" — he says: "If he wills it, he is able to." When it is asked of him: "Is he able to will it?" he says: "If he dislikes disbelief." And when it is asked of him: "Is he able to disbelieve?" he says: "He is able to do that if he wills belief." So whenever the question is repeated to him, he repeats this answer.

﴿وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, [He being] its owner.

﴿وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ فِي النِّسَاءِ﴾.

al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: This verse was revealed concerning the daughters of Umm Kahha and their inheritance from their mother. This story has already been mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

Mu'awiya ibn Salih, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: In the Jahiliyya (the age of ignorance before Islam), a man would have an orphan girl in his care and would throw his garment over her. Once he had done this, no one could ever marry her. If she was beautiful and he desired her, he would marry her and consume her property. If she was ugly, the men would be prevented from marrying her until she died. Then he would inherit from her. So God forbade this, prohibited it, and revealed this verse.

Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatada and Ibrahim said: The people of the Jahiliyya did not give women and children any share of inheritance. A woman might be ugly in the Jahiliyya, yet possess wealth. Her guardian would dislike marrying her because of her ugliness, and would dislike that someone else marry her because of her wealth. So her guardian would not marry her, but would keep her confined with him until she died, and then he would inherit from her.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When the guardian of an orphan girl was someone who possessed wealth and beauty, he would desire her, marry her, and monopolize her. But if she had neither wealth nor beauty, he would neither marry her nor give her in marriage to another. So God revealed this verse.

It is also related from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayda, who said: A woman from the Ansar called Khawla bint Hakim came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, my brother has died and left daughters. They do not have the beauty that would make men desire them, and they are not given any share of their father's inheritance." So this verse was revealed concerning her.

﴿وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ﴾: that is, they ask you for a ruling (istikhbar, seeking information), ﴿فِي النِّسَاءِ﴾ concerning women. ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ﴾ Say: God gives you a ruling, informs you ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾ concerning them. ﴿وَمَا يُتْلَى﴾ and what is recited, that is, what is recited ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾ to you in the Book, that is, in the Qur'an. The place of "مَا" in the Arabic grammar (i'rab) is in the nominative (raf'), its meaning being: ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ وَمَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾, and [God] gives you a ruling concerning them, and [He also gives you a ruling concerning] what is recited to you in the Book. It is also permissible for it to be in the genitive (khafd) position, so that the meaning would be: "Say: God gives you a ruling concerning them and concerning what is recited among you." But this is remote, because the apparent (zahir) does not get conjoined to a pronoun (the pronoun in "فِيهِنَّ" being in the genitive without a preposition repeated). The nominative reading is clearer, because what is recited in the Book and what is recited among you is, in meaning, what they asked about.

﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ﴾ in His Book, He gives you a ruling concerning them, and this is His saying: ﴿وَآتُوا الْيَتَامَى أَمْوَالَهُمْ﴾ (And give the orphans their property) and the rest of the verse; and His saying: ﴿فِي يَتَامَى النِّسَاءِ اللَّاتِي لَا تُؤْتُونَهُنَّ مَا كُتِبَ لَهُنَّ﴾ concerning the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them, meaning, what has been ordained for them as a share of inheritance. ﴿وَتَرْغَبُونَ أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ﴾ and you desire to marry them, that is, and you turn away from marrying them because of their [lack of] property. It has also been said: "you desire to marry them for their wealth." ﴿وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الْوِلْدَانِ﴾ and the weak among the children, meaning the young children. It is in the genitive position, and the meaning is: "God gives you a ruling concerning them and concerning the weak among the children." ﴿وَأَنْ تَقُومُوا لِلْيَتَامَى بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ and that you stand for the orphans with justice, that is, with fairness. ﴿وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِهِ عَلِيمًا﴾ and whatever good you do, indeed God is ever Knowing of it.

Shu'ba related from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, that the last verse revealed was: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say: God gives you a ruling concerning them," and the last surah [revealed] was Bara'a (al-Tawba). [He also related:] ﴿وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ مِنْ بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزًا أَوْ إِعْرَاضًا﴾ And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband.

It was revealed concerning 'Umra, and it is said: Khuwayla bint Muhammad ibn Maslama, concerning her husband Rafi' ibn al-Rafi', and it is said: Rafi' ibn Khadij. He had married her when she was young. When she grew old (i.e., he married another young woman over her), he favored the other wife over her and neglected her son Muhammad ibn Maslama. She came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and complained to him, so this verse was revealed concerning her.

This is the view of al-Kalbi and a group of the exegetes (mufassirun).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: There was a man who had a wife who had grown old, and he had children by her. He wanted to divorce her and marry someone else. She said: "Do not divorce me. Let me look after my children, and you may share your nights with me once every two months, or more, if you wish; and if you wish, do not share with me." He said: "If that is what prevents you [from divorce], then it is more beloved to me." So he went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and told him about this. He said: "God has heard what you have said. If He wills, He will respond to you." Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ مِنْ بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزًا أَوْ إِعْرَاضًا﴾, that is, she knew from her husband ill-treatment (nushuz), meaning hatred.

al-Kalbi said: That means abandoning intercourse and lying with her, or aversion from living with her, from sitting with her and from conversing with her. ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا﴾ there is no blame upon them both, meaning upon the husband and the wife, ﴿أَنْ يُصْلِحَا بَيْنَهُمَا صُلْحًا﴾ if they make an arrangement between them, a settlement, that is, in the division [of nights] and in maintenance. This is that he says to her: "You are an ugly woman, and you have entered old age, and I want to marry a young, beautiful woman over you." He would then favor her in the division because of her youth. If she accepts this, she stays; and if she dislikes it, I release you. If she accepts that, then she is the one who does good, and that is not difficult for me. But if she does not accept, she is given her right. It is obligatory upon the husband to fulfil her right of residence and maintenance, or to release her with kindness, and not to keep her in humiliation. And if she remains with him, with his dislike for her companionship, and he fulfils her right, then he is the one who does good, whom God has praised, and He informs us that He knows his deed and will reward him for his action. A man cannot be compelled to have intercourse with one wife, because it is his own right and his share (hazz); and if he abandons it, he is not compelled to do it, and it is not like residence and maintenance.

His saying ﴿وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾ and settlement is better means: her remaining [with him] after he has given her the choice, and reconciling with her upon something known regarding residence and maintenance.

The Prophet (ﷺ) acted in this way with his wife, and she remained with him. That was because she was an elderly woman, and the Prophet (ﷺ) wanted to divorce her, but she asked him not to do so, saying: "I wish to be raised among your wives on the Day of Resurrection. So, my day and my night are for 'A'isha."

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said concerning His saying ﴿وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾: "It is when a woman is with a man, and she is either young or old, or her husband does not love her, so they come to an agreement upon a settlement."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It is that they both agree upon something known in itself and in property.

al-Dahhak said: The settlement is that he diminishes her share if he marries someone younger and more pleasing to him than her.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said concerning this verse: It is a man who has an elderly woman under him, and he marries a young woman over her. He says to the elderly woman: "I will give you a portion of my time, on condition that I share with this young woman more than I share with you, by night and by day." The other [wife] accepts what they have agreed upon. If she refuses to accept, then he must be just between them in the division.

Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Farwa related from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا أَنْ يُصْلِحَا بَيْنَهُمَا صُلْحًا وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾ [Qur'an 4:128]. He said: "It concerns an elderly, ugly woman who is with a man who wants to divorce her and replace her. [So he makes a settlement with her] concerning some of her right in the division and maintenance. That is permissible once she has consented. But if she denies it after the settlement, then that is her right, and she is entitled to her right, whether he keeps her or divorces her."

'Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn 'Abbas: It is a woman who is with a man who has another wife whom he loves more than her, so he favors her over her. God, when this occurs, commands that he say to her: "O such-and-such, if you wish to remain with me under these conditions that you see, I will shelter you and maintain you, so remain. And if you dislike it, I will release you." If she consents to remain after he has given her the choice, then there is no blame upon him; and this is His saying ﴿وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾, and this is the giving of choice.

Isra'il related from Simak ibn Harb, from Khalid ibn 'Ar'ara, who said: A man asked 'Ali about the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ مِنْ بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزًا أَوْ إِعْرَاضًا﴾ [the verse]. He said: "A woman is with a man, and his eye turns away from her because of ugliness or age, so she ransoms herself from him, [though] she dislikes separation. If she gives him some of her property, it is lawful for him; or if she gives him some of her household goods, it is lawful for him." ﴿وَأُحْضِرَتِ الْأَنْفُسُ الشُّحَّ﴾ [And souls are made to be prone to stinginess]: that is, the woman is stingy with her share from her husband, and the man is stingy with his share from the other [wife].

Ibn 'Abbas said: Shuhh (stinginess) is being greedy for something. ﴿وَإِنْ تُحْسِنُوا﴾ And if you do good, that is, you reconcile between them equitably, ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ and you guard against injustice and partiality.

It has also been said: this address is to the husband, meaning: ﴿وَإِنْ تُحْسِنُوا﴾ by remaining with her, despite your dislike of her companionship, ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ and you avoid wronging her. ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ indeed God is ever Aware of what you do, informing you of your deeds.

﴿وَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا بَيْنَ النِّسَاءِ﴾ And you will never be able to be just between wives. It means: you will not be able to make them equal in love. ﴿وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ﴾ even if you are eager [to do so]. ﴿فَلَا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ﴾ So do not incline completely [toward one], in maintenance, division and attention to her, ﴿وَتَذَرُوهَا كَالْمُعَلَّقَةِ﴾ and leave the other as one suspended, that is, as one hanging: neither married nor divorced, and without a [husband's] provision.

Qatada and al-Kalbi said: ﴿كَالْمُعَلَّقَةِ﴾ means "like one confined," and this was [said] concerning the wife of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, as if she were imprisoned.

Mujahid said: "You will not be able to be just between them, so do not deliberately [do that]."

It has been mentioned to us that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say: "O God, as for my heart, I do not control it; but as for what is other than that, I hope to be just."

﴿وَإِنْ تُصْلِحُوا﴾ And if you reconcile, by justice in the division among them, ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ and guard against injustice, ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا﴾ indeed God is ever Forgiving, Merciful, [forgiving] for what you have said [of inclination] toward the one you love in your heart, after justice in the division. ﴿وَإِنْ يَتَفَرَّقَا﴾ And if they separate, meaning the woman by divorce, ﴿يُغْنِ اللَّهُ كُلًّا مِنْ سَعَتِهِ﴾ God will enrich each of them from His abundance, that is, from provision: the woman with a husband, and the husband with a wife. ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ وَاسِعًا﴾ and God is ever All-Encompassing, [giving] them both [scope] in marriage, ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ All-Wise, [so that] it is possible for the husband to retain her with kindness or release her with goodness.

The ruling of the verse:

It is known that God, Mighty and Majestic, is compassionate toward His servants and aware of their conditions. So He alerted them to the rights of women that are obligatory upon them, and forbade them from inclining in their actions when they have no means to equalize between them in love. Whenever the servant gathers [his] action toward wealth and turns to one particular wife to the exclusion of others, that is injustice.

It has been related that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to divide [his time] and say: "O God, this is my division in what I possess, so do not blame me for what You possess and I do not" [388] [Tabari, 5/424, where it reads: "do not blame me for what You possess and I do not"]. He meant by this his heart. He used to go around with his wives during his illness until they permitted him [to stay in one place: "his wives" supplied from context], and he remained with 'A'isha.

The basis of the division is the night, because one rests in it. God the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَهُ مَا سَكَنَ فِي اللَّيْلِ﴾ [Qur'an 6:13]. So whenever a man has free Muslim women and dhimmi women, they are equal in division. He divides two nights for a free wife, and one night for a slave wife, if her master leaves him free with her during her night and day. A slave wife may release him from her turn without the master, because it is her right in her own person. He does not have intercourse with a woman on other than her day. And it is not permitted for a man to enter at night to the one for whom he has not been allotted a turn. There is no harm in his entering to her in the daytime for a need, or visiting her in her illness during another's night. If she becomes gravely ill, there is no harm in his remaining until she recovers or dies; then he must make up for the rest of his wives an amount equal to what he spent with her. If he wishes to divide [his time] as two nights or three nights for each, that is permitted for him [Ref.: Mukhtasar al-Muzani, p. 185].

Mention of how those who derive from this verse the imposition of what cannot be borne argue:

They say: God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا بَيْنَ النِّسَاءِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ فَلَا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ﴾. So He commanded them to be just, and informed that they are not able to be just. Thus He commanded them to do what they cannot do, and charged them with what they cannot bear.

If someone says: Did God impose upon the disbelievers what they cannot bear? It is said to him: If you mean that He imposed upon them what they cannot bear due to an incapacity that prevents them, then no, because He has made their bodies sound, perfected their speech, placed them [in the earth] [the text is "fi al-ard"; the apparent reading is as given], and removed from them illnesses and afflictions. And if you mean that He imposed upon them what they are unable to do by their leaving it and occupying themselves with its opposite, then indeed He has imposed that upon them.

If they say: Is it that the disbeliever is not able to occupy himself with disbelief? It is said to them: The meaning of "not occupied with disbelief" is that you believe; so it is as if you said: he is able to believe while remaining upon his disbelief. We have said that as long as he is occupied with disbelief he is not able to believe, in accordance with what the language permits, that a person is able to do something in the sense that if he does not neglect it, it takes effect upon him, as they say: "So-and-so is able over a man," meaning he is able over him if he attempts and intends to carry him, similar to their saying: "So-and-so understands," meaning he understands a thing when it is presented to him. Likewise they say: "The food satisfies (mushbi'),” and "the water quenches (marwi)," meaning that food satisfies when eaten, and water quenches when drunk.

What clarifies this is what people exchange among themselves: a man says: "Come with me at such-and-such a time," and the answer is: "I am not able to come with you because of what I am occupied with." God the Exalted said: ﴿مَا كَانُوا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ السَّمْعَ﴾ [Qur'an 11:20], meaning they could not accept it, because they found it burdensome. As for those who are confused and say: "Is the disbeliever able to believe?" — he says: "If he wills it, he is able to." When it is asked of him: "Is he able to will it?" he says: "If he dislikes disbelief." And when it is asked of him: "Is he able to disbelieve?" he says: "He is able to do that if he wills belief." So whenever the question is repeated to him, he repeats this answer.

﴿وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, [He being] its owner.

﴿وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ فِي النِّسَاءِ﴾.

al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: This verse was revealed concerning the daughters of Umm Kahha and their inheritance from their mother. This story has already been mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

Mu'awiya ibn Salih, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: In the Jahiliyya (the age of ignorance before Islam), a man would have an orphan girl in his care and would throw his garment over her. Once he had done this, no one could ever marry her. If she was beautiful and he desired her, he would marry her and consume her property. If she was ugly, the men would be prevented from marrying her until she died. Then he would inherit from her. So God forbade this, prohibited it, and revealed this verse.

Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatada and Ibrahim said: The people of the Jahiliyya did not give women and children any share of inheritance. A woman might be ugly in the Jahiliyya, yet possess wealth. Her guardian would dislike marrying her because of her ugliness, and would dislike that someone else marry her because of her wealth. So her guardian would not marry her, but would keep her confined with him until she died, and then he would inherit from her.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When the guardian of an orphan girl was someone who possessed wealth and beauty, he would desire her, marry her, and monopolize her. But if she had neither wealth nor beauty, he would neither marry her nor give her in marriage to another. So God revealed this verse.

It is also related from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayda, who said: A woman from the Ansar called Khawla bint Hakim came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, my brother has died and left daughters. They do not have the beauty that would make men desire them, and they are not given any share of their father's inheritance." So this verse was revealed concerning her.

﴿وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ﴾: that is, they ask you for a ruling (istikhbar, seeking information), ﴿فِي النِّسَاءِ﴾ concerning women. ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ﴾ Say: God gives you a ruling, informs you ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾ concerning them. ﴿وَمَا يُتْلَى﴾ and what is recited, that is, what is recited ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾ to you in the Book, that is, in the Qur'an. The place of "مَا" in the Arabic grammar (i'rab) is in the nominative (raf'), its meaning being: ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ وَمَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾, and [God] gives you a ruling concerning them, and [He also gives you a ruling concerning] what is recited to you in the Book. It is also permissible for it to be in the genitive (khafd) position, so that the meaning would be: "Say: God gives you a ruling concerning them and concerning what is recited among you." But this is remote, because the apparent (zahir) does not get conjoined to a pronoun (the pronoun in "فِيهِنَّ" being in the genitive without a preposition repeated). The nominative reading is clearer, because what is recited in the Book and what is recited among you is, in meaning, what they asked about.

﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ﴾ in His Book, He gives you a ruling concerning them, and this is His saying: ﴿وَآتُوا الْيَتَامَى أَمْوَالَهُمْ﴾ (And give the orphans their property) and the rest of the verse; and His saying: ﴿فِي يَتَامَى النِّسَاءِ اللَّاتِي لَا تُؤْتُونَهُنَّ مَا كُتِبَ لَهُنَّ﴾ concerning the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them, meaning, what has been ordained for them as a share of inheritance. ﴿وَتَرْغَبُونَ أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ﴾ and you desire to marry them, that is, and you turn away from marrying them because of their [lack of] property. It has also been said: "you desire to marry them for their wealth." ﴿وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الْوِلْدَانِ﴾ and the weak among the children, meaning the young children. It is in the genitive position, and the meaning is: "God gives you a ruling concerning them and concerning the weak among the children." ﴿وَأَنْ تَقُومُوا لِلْيَتَامَى بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ and that you stand for the orphans with justice, that is, with fairness. ﴿وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِهِ عَلِيمًا﴾ and whatever good you do, indeed God is ever Knowing of it.

Shu'ba related from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, that the last verse revealed was: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say: God gives you a ruling concerning them," and the last surah [revealed] was Bara'a (al-Tawba). [He also related:] ﴿وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ مِنْ بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزًا أَوْ إِعْرَاضًا﴾ And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband.

It was revealed concerning 'Umra, and it is said: Khuwayla bint Muhammad ibn Maslama, concerning her husband Rafi' ibn al-Rafi', and it is said: Rafi' ibn Khadij. He had married her when she was young. When she grew old (i.e., he married another young woman over her), he favored the other wife over her and neglected her son Muhammad ibn Maslama. She came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and complained to him, so this verse was revealed concerning her.

This is the view of al-Kalbi and a group of the exegetes (mufassirun).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: There was a man who had a wife who had grown old, and he had children by her. He wanted to divorce her and marry someone else. She said: "Do not divorce me. Let me look after my children, and you may share your nights with me once every two months, or more, if you wish; and if you wish, do not share with me." He said: "If that is what prevents you [from divorce], then it is more beloved to me." So he went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and told him about this. He said: "God has heard what you have said. If He wills, He will respond to you." Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ مِنْ بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزًا أَوْ إِعْرَاضًا﴾, that is, she knew from her husband ill-treatment (nushuz), meaning hatred.

al-Kalbi said: That means abandoning intercourse and lying with her, or aversion from living with her, from sitting with her and from conversing with her. ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا﴾ there is no blame upon them both, meaning upon the husband and the wife, ﴿أَنْ يُصْلِحَا بَيْنَهُمَا صُلْحًا﴾ if they make an arrangement between them, a settlement, that is, in the division [of nights] and in maintenance. This is that he says to her: "You are an ugly woman, and you have entered old age, and I want to marry a young, beautiful woman over you." He would then favor her in the division because of her youth. If she accepts this, she stays; and if she dislikes it, I release you. If she accepts that, then she is the one who does good, and that is not difficult for me. But if she does not accept, she is given her right. It is obligatory upon the husband to fulfil her right of residence and maintenance, or to release her with kindness, and not to keep her in humiliation. And if she remains with him, with his dislike for her companionship, and he fulfils her right, then he is the one who does good, whom God has praised, and He informs us that He knows his deed and will reward him for his action. A man cannot be compelled to have intercourse with one wife, because it is his own right and his share (hazz); and if he abandons it, he is not compelled to do it, and it is not like residence and maintenance.

His saying ﴿وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾ and settlement is better means: her remaining [with him] after he has given her the choice, and reconciling with her upon something known regarding residence and maintenance.

The Prophet (ﷺ) acted in this way with his wife, and she remained with him. That was because she was an elderly woman, and the Prophet (ﷺ) wanted to divorce her, but she asked him not to do so, saying: "I wish to be raised among your wives on the Day of Resurrection. So, my day and my night are for 'A'isha."

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said concerning His saying ﴿وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾: "It is when a woman is with a man, and she is either young or old, or her husband does not love her, so they come to an agreement upon a settlement."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It is that they both agree upon something known in itself and in property.

al-Dahhak said: The settlement is that he diminishes her share if he marries someone younger and more pleasing to him than her.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said concerning this verse: It is a man who has an elderly woman under him, and he marries a young woman over her. He says to the elderly woman: "I will give you a portion of my time, on condition that I share with this young woman more than I share with you, by night and by day." The other [wife] accepts what they have agreed upon. If she refuses to accept, then he must be just between them in the division.

Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Farwa related from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا أَنْ يُصْلِحَا بَيْنَهُمَا صُلْحًا وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾ [Qur'an 4:128]. He said: "It concerns an elderly, ugly woman who is with a man who wants to divorce her and replace her. [So he makes a settlement with her] concerning some of her right in the division and maintenance. That is permissible once she has consented. But if she denies it after the settlement, then that is her right, and she is entitled to her right, whether he keeps her or divorces her."

'Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn 'Abbas: It is a woman who is with a man who has another wife whom he loves more than her, so he favors her over her. God, when this occurs, commands that he say to her: "O such-and-such, if you wish to remain with me under these conditions that you see, I will shelter you and maintain you, so remain. And if you dislike it, I will release you." If she consents to remain after he has given her the choice, then there is no blame upon him; and this is His saying ﴿وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾, and this is the giving of choice.

Isra'il related from Simak ibn Harb, from Khalid ibn 'Ar'ara, who said: A man asked 'Ali about the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ مِنْ بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزًا أَوْ إِعْرَاضًا﴾ [the verse]. He said: "A woman is with a man, and his eye turns away from her because of ugliness or age, so she ransoms herself from him, [though] she dislikes separation. If she gives him some of her property, it is lawful for him; or if she gives him some of her household goods, it is lawful for him." ﴿وَأُحْضِرَتِ الْأَنْفُسُ الشُّحَّ﴾ [And souls are made to be prone to stinginess]: that is, the woman is stingy with her share from her husband, and the man is stingy with his share from the other [wife].

Ibn 'Abbas said: Shuhh (stinginess) is being greedy for something. ﴿وَإِنْ تُحْسِنُوا﴾ And if you do good, that is, you reconcile between them equitably, ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ and you guard against injustice and partiality.

It has also been said: this address is to the husband, meaning: ﴿وَإِنْ تُحْسِنُوا﴾ by remaining with her, despite your dislike of her companionship, ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ and you avoid wronging her. ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ indeed God is ever Aware of what you do, informing you of your deeds.

﴿وَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا بَيْنَ النِّسَاءِ﴾ And you will never be able to be just between wives. It means: you will not be able to make them equal in love. ﴿وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ﴾ even if you are eager [to do so]. ﴿فَلَا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ﴾ So do not incline completely [toward one], in maintenance, division and attention to her, ﴿وَتَذَرُوهَا كَالْمُعَلَّقَةِ﴾ and leave the other as one suspended, that is, as one hanging: neither married nor divorced, and without a [husband's] provision.

Qatada and al-Kalbi said: ﴿كَالْمُعَلَّقَةِ﴾ means "like one confined," and this was [said] concerning the wife of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, as if she were imprisoned.

Mujahid said: "You will not be able to be just between them, so do not deliberately [do that]."

It has been mentioned to us that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say: "O God, as for my heart, I do not control it; but as for what is other than that, I hope to be just."

﴿وَإِنْ تُصْلِحُوا﴾ And if you reconcile, by justice in the division among them, ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ and guard against injustice, ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا﴾ indeed God is ever Forgiving, Merciful, [forgiving] for what you have said [of inclination] toward the one you love in your heart, after justice in the division. ﴿وَإِنْ يَتَفَرَّقَا﴾ And if they separate, meaning the woman by divorce, ﴿يُغْنِ اللَّهُ كُلًّا مِنْ سَعَتِهِ﴾ God will enrich each of them from His abundance, that is, from provision: the woman with a husband, and the husband with a wife. ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ وَاسِعًا﴾ and God is ever All-Encompassing, [giving] them both [scope] in marriage, ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ All-Wise, [so that] it is possible for the husband to retain her with kindness or release her with goodness.

The ruling of the verse:

It is known that God, Mighty and Majestic, is compassionate toward His servants and aware of their conditions. So He alerted them to the rights of women that are obligatory upon them, and forbade them from inclining in their actions when they have no means to equalize between them in love. Whenever the servant gathers [his] action toward wealth and turns to one particular wife to the exclusion of others, that is injustice.

It has been related that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to divide [his time] and say: "O God, this is my division in what I possess, so do not blame me for what You possess and I do not" [388] [Tabari, 5/424, where it reads: "do not blame me for what You possess and I do not"]. He meant by this his heart. He used to go around with his wives during his illness until they permitted him [to stay in one place: "his wives" supplied from context], and he remained with 'A'isha.

The basis of the division is the night, because one rests in it. God the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَهُ مَا سَكَنَ فِي اللَّيْلِ﴾ [Qur'an 6:13]. So whenever a man has free Muslim women and dhimmi women, they are equal in division. He divides two nights for a free wife, and one night for a slave wife, if her master leaves him free with her during her night and day. A slave wife may release him from her turn without the master, because it is her right in her own person. He does not have intercourse with a woman on other than her day. And it is not permitted for a man to enter at night to the one for whom he has not been allotted a turn. There is no harm in his entering to her in the daytime for a need, or visiting her in her illness during another's night. If she becomes gravely ill, there is no harm in his remaining until she recovers or dies; then he must make up for the rest of his wives an amount equal to what he spent with her. If he wishes to divide [his time] as two nights or three nights for each, that is permitted for him [Ref.: Mukhtasar al-Muzani, p. 185].

Mention of how those who derive from this verse the imposition of what cannot be borne argue:

They say: God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا بَيْنَ النِّسَاءِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ فَلَا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ﴾. So He commanded them to be just, and informed that they are not able to be just. Thus He commanded them to do what they cannot do, and charged them with what they cannot bear.

If someone says: Did God impose upon the disbelievers what they cannot bear? It is said to him: If you mean that He imposed upon them what they cannot bear due to an incapacity that prevents them, then no, because He has made their bodies sound, perfected their speech, placed them [in the earth] [the text is "fi al-ard"; the apparent reading is as given], and removed from them illnesses and afflictions. And if you mean that He imposed upon them what they are unable to do by their leaving it and occupying themselves with its opposite, then indeed He has imposed that upon them.

If they say: Is it that the disbeliever is not able to occupy himself with disbelief? It is said to them: The meaning of "not occupied with disbelief" is that you believe; so it is as if you said: he is able to believe while remaining upon his disbelief. We have said that as long as he is occupied with disbelief he is not able to believe, in accordance with what the language permits, that a person is able to do something in the sense that if he does not neglect it, it takes effect upon him, as they say: "So-and-so is able over a man," meaning he is able over him if he attempts and intends to carry him, similar to their saying: "So-and-so understands," meaning he understands a thing when it is presented to him. Likewise they say: "The food satisfies (mushbi'),” and "the water quenches (marwi)," meaning that food satisfies when eaten, and water quenches when drunk.

What clarifies this is what people exchange among themselves: a man says: "Come with me at such-and-such a time," and the answer is: "I am not able to come with you because of what I am occupied with." God the Exalted said: ﴿مَا كَانُوا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ السَّمْعَ﴾ [Qur'an 11:20], meaning they could not accept it, because they found it burdensome. As for those who are confused and say: "Is the disbeliever able to believe?" — he says: "If he wills it, he is able to." When it is asked of him: "Is he able to will it?" he says: "If he dislikes disbelief." And when it is asked of him: "Is he able to disbelieve?" he says: "He is able to do that if he wills belief." So whenever the question is repeated to him, he repeats this answer.

﴿وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, [He being] its owner.

And We have certainly enjoined those who were given the Book before you (meaning the People of the Torah and the Gospel, and the other earlier scriptures that preceded Islam), and you (O People of the Qur'an, in your Book): "Be mindful of God" (that is, affirm the oneness of God, obey Him, and do not associate anything with Him). But if you disbelieve, then to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth (meaning that God has angels who are more obedient to Him than you). And God is ever Self-sufficient (ghaniyy), free of need of all His creation, not needing anything that is in their hands.

The real meaning of al-Ghaniyy (the Self-Sufficient) according to the people of attributes (ashab al-sifat) is one who possesses ghina (sufficiency).

Ghina is the capacity to do what one wills, and al-ghaniyy is the one capable of what he wills. Then one considers: if he is capable of [describing] need in relation to him, we name him by that; and if the description of need cannot apply to him, he is not described by it. Poverty (faqr) is incapacity for that and its absence. This is the view taken by the [Mu'tazilah].

Al-Jubba'i said: The meaning of describing God as ghaniyy is that benefits and harms do not reach Him, and pleasures, joys and pains are not applicable to Him. The first view is more correct in this regard in the case of the witnessed and the unseen, and the Muslims' usage of describing one another as ghaniyy and faqir. And God knows best.

﴿And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and God is sufficient as Disposer of affairs (wakil).﴾

Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas: it means a protector, one who grants refuge.

'Ikrimah reported from Ibn 'Abbas: it means a witness.

﴿If He wills, He can take you away, O people, and bring others.﴾ That is, He causes you to die, meaning the disbelievers, ﴿and bring others﴾, meaning others besides you, better than you and more obedient. ﴿And God is ever Capable of that﴾, that is, able to do so.

The Capable (al-Qadir) and the Powerful (al-Qadir) according to the people of attributes is one who has a power subsisting in him, distinct from the incapable by it. The capable then differ after that: some have a power that inheres in a part of them, and others have a power not described as inherent. Power is that by which the act occurs, without dying with the death of the one who has it, and without its ceasing when incapacity sets in.

The Mu'tazilah said: The capable is the one from whom the act is possible. The proof of the correctness of what the people of attributes said is that we see the capable differing from the incapable in what he is able to do, and it has been shown that the difference is not due to his being an attribute of a described thing that differs from other described things, nor due to his being newly originated in a way that differs from the incapable. Since these divisions are not relevant, it is valid that he differs only because he has a power that the incapable lacks. Therefore we say that the Eternal, majestic is He, is capable through a power, not capable by His essence.

﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world, with God is the reward of this world and the Hereafter.﴾

He says: whoever intends by his deed, which God has made obligatory, a passing good of this world and does not intend God by it, God rewards him with what He loves of the goods of this world, or repels from him in it what He loves, but he has no reward in the Hereafter because he acted for other than God. And whoever intends by his deed, which God, Mighty and Majestic, has obligated upon him in this world, the reward of the Hereafter, God rewards him with what He loves of the goods of this world and repels from him what He loves, and recompenses him in the Hereafter with Paradise for his deed.

Sulayman ibn 'Amr reported from Abu Hazim from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: «The intention of the believer is better than his deed, and the deed of the hypocrite is better than his intention, and each acts according to his intention, and there is no believer who does a deed except that two images form in his heart» [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/61 and Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/419 no. 7237, with variation in the final part.]] [389].

If the first is for God, then He does not guide him to the Hereafter.

﴿O you who have believed, be steadfast in upholding justice, witnesses for God, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives…﴾ The verse means: be steadfast in bearing witness, and by justice is meant equity.

Ibn 'Abbas said: its meaning is: be steadfast in justice in testimony concerning whomever it is due, ﴿even against yourselves or parents and relatives﴾ within kinship; so establish it against them for the sake of God Exalted. Do not show favor to a rich man for his wealth, nor have mercy on a poor man for his poverty. This is His saying, ﴿If he is rich or poor, God is more entitled to them than you﴾, so He takes charge of that concerning them. ﴿So do not follow [your own] desire, lest you deviate﴾, meaning, lest you abandon the truth and disavow it.

Al-Farra' said: It is said the meaning is: do not follow sins in order to deviate, as one says: "Do not follow your desire so that He may be pleased with you," meaning: I forbid you from this so that your Lord may be pleased.

It is also said: ﴿do not follow desire﴾ out of fleeing from establishing testimony. ﴿And if you distort [it] or refuse [to give it], indeed God is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾: distortion by the tongue, altering testimony in order to nullify the truth, or refusal by withholding it and not establishing it before the judges. It is also said the meaning of ﴿if you distort﴾ is: you push back in establishing testimony. It is said: "I twisted his right," meaning I pushed it back and nullified it.

Ibn 'Abbas said: this verse concerns the judge who twists his cheek and turns away from one of the two litigants.

The Messenger of God ﷺ said upon the revelation of this verse: «Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him establish his testimony as it is; and whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him not deny a right he owes, and let him discharge it willingly, and not compel him to a ruler [to take] his right by it. As for a man who litigated before me, and I ruled for him against his brother in a right that was not his, let him not take it, for I am only cutting for him a piece of Hellfire» [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 23/382, abridged.]] [390].

A linguistic question

The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: the meaning of al-qist (justice) is equity. It is said: aqsata al-rajul yuqsitu iqsatan when he acted justly, and qasata yaqsutu qusutan when he acted unjustly.

God the Exalted said: ﴿And act justly; indeed God loves those who act justly﴾ [[Surah al-Hujurat: 9.]] and He said: ﴿As for the unjust, they will be fuel for Hell﴾.

It is also said: qasata al-ba'ir yaqsutu qasatan when its foreleg dried up, and yadun qasatan meaning a dry hand. So aqsata means to establish a thing in its true state in justice, while qasata, meaning [khiyar]... that is, the thing dried up and its straight direction was spoiled.

And We have certainly enjoined those who were given the Book before you (meaning the People of the Torah and the Gospel, and the other earlier scriptures that preceded Islam), and you (O People of the Qur'an, in your Book): "Be mindful of God" (that is, affirm the oneness of God, obey Him, and do not associate anything with Him). But if you disbelieve, then to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth (meaning that God has angels who are more obedient to Him than you). And God is ever Self-sufficient (ghaniyy), free of need of all His creation, not needing anything that is in their hands.

Poverty (faqr) is incapacity for that and its absence. This is the view taken by the [Mu'tazilah].

The first view is more correct in this regard in the case of the witnessed and the unseen, and the Muslims' usage of describing one another as ghaniyy and faqir. And God knows best.

﴿And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and God is sufficient as Disposer of affairs (wakil).﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verse 136–141:

O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger, [the verse] ...

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: This verse was revealed concerning 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Asad and Usayd, the two sons of Ka'b, Tha'labah ibn Qays ibn Ka'b, Salam (the nephew of 'Abdullah ibn Salam), Salamah (his brother), and Yamin ibn Yamin. These were the believers among the People of the Book. They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we believe in you and in your Book, and in Musa and the Torah, and 'Uzayr, but we disbelieve in whatever else there is of books and messengers." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to them:

"Rather, believe in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad, and in his Book, the Qur'an, and in every Book that came before it." [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 234.]] [391] They said: "We will not do that." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed: "O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger, and the Book which He has sent down upon His Messenger" — meaning the Qur'an — "and the Book which He sent down before" — meaning the earlier books: the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and all the earlier books. "And whoever disbelieves in Allah..." up to His words "has strayed far astray" — meaning, an error far removed. When this verse was revealed, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, we believe in Allah and His Messenger, and in the Qur'an, and in every messenger and book that came before the Qur'an, and in the angels and the Last Day. We do not differentiate between any of them, as the Jews and Christians did," "and we are Muslims [submitting to Him]." Thus they entered Islam.

Al-Dahhak said: It refers to the Jews and Christians. The meaning of the verse: "O you who have believed" — in Musa and the Torah and 'Isa and the Gospel — "believe in Muhammad and the Qur'an."

It was also said: it was revealed specifically concerning the Jews. The meaning: "O you who have believed" at the beginning of the day, "believe" at the end of the day. This corresponds to His words: "And a party of the People of the Book said: Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day..." the verse.

Abu al-'Aliyah and a group of commentators said: this verse is addressed to the believers, and its interpretation: "O you who have believed, believe" — that is, persist and remain steadfast in faith. It is like His saying to His Prophet (ﷺ): "So know that there is no god but Allah" — that is, remain upon what you are upon. And like His saying: "Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward" [[Surah al-Ma'idah: 9.]], meaning: Allah has promised those who believe, upon their faith, among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who are in this story, forgiveness and a great reward. The verse revealed in the Book is His saying: "And when you see those who engage in [mocking] Our verses, turn away from them" [[Surah al-An'am: 68.]], the verse.

Al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: Every innovator in religion and every heretic until the Day of Resurrection enters into this verse.

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih: This statement is confirmed by His saying, mighty and majestic: "And those who fear [shirk and mockery] are not accountable for them in anything, but it is a reminder" — that is, they remind them and admonish them with the Qur'an — "that perhaps they will fear" mockery of Muhammad and the Qur'an. "Indeed, you would then be like them" — if you sit with them, then you are like them. "Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hell, all together. Those who wait [with malice] for you" — that is, they await for you the reversals — meaning the hypocrites. "If there is a victory for you from Allah" — meaning support and spoils — "they say: 'Were we not with you?'" — upon your religion — "so give us a share of the spoils." "And if there is a portion for the disbelievers" — meaning a state and dominance over the Muslims — "they say," meaning the hypocrites: "Did we not gain control over you?" — did we not inform you of the resolve of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Companions, and let you know their secrets?

The lexicographers said: "Did we not gain control over you" means and prevail over you. He said: "istahwadha" means "ghalaba" (prevailed).

In a hadith: "'Umar was our hawadh," meaning he prevailed over our affairs in truth.

Al-'Ajjaj said:

"He drives them, and for him is a driver..." [as the Kumayt gathers the troop] — the Kumayt. That is, he overcomes them and gathers them. It is narrated with a zay in both places.

The grammarians said: istahwadha (اسْتَحْوَذَ) follows the original form; whoever says hāda yahūdu does not say except istāda yastadhu, though ahwadha yahwadhu is also used, as some said: "ahwadhtu" [and "atyabtu"] with the meaning of "ahadhtu" and "aṭabtu." He said: "istahwadha" — he extracted it in its original form. "And we protected you from the believers," — we prevented you from attacking the believers. "So Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection," — meaning between the people of faith and the people of hypocrisy — then He will decide between them. "And Allah will never give the disbelievers any way over the believers."

Ikrimah and al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: "a way" means proof.

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And Allah will never give the disbelievers any way over the believers" — meaning the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) — "a way" meaning dominance over them.

'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "And Allah will never give the disbelievers any way over the believers" — in the Hereafter.

And in this verse is evidence that the hypocrite is not a believer, and that faith is not merely verbal affirmation; for if faith were verbal affirmation, they would thereby be believers.

And it is also evidence for the truth of the Prophethood of the Prophet (ﷺ), because the people were concealing their beliefs, and Allah, mighty and majestic, made His Messenger aware of their beliefs, and this was a proof for him against them, since they knew that none knows the secrets of hearts except the Creator, mighty and majestic.

**Al-Tha'alibi's commentary (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 4, verses 142–147:**

﴿Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah﴾

Its tafsir (exegesis) has already passed.

﴿And He is the one who deceives them﴾

That is, He repays them for their deception. This is because on the Sirat (the bridge over Hell) they are given light, just as the believers are given light. When they pass on the Sirat, that light is taken from them, while the believers remain looking by their light. The hypocrites then call out to the believers: ﴿Wait for us, that we may borrow from your light.﴾ The angels on the Sirat answer them: ﴿Go back behind you and seek light﴾ [Footnote: Surah al-Hadid 57:13.]. They know that they cannot return. Then the believers, fearing that their own light might be extinguished, say: ﴿Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent﴾ [Footnote: Surah al-Tahrim 66:8.].

﴿And when they stand﴾

That is, when they prepare themselves ﴿for prayer, they stand lazily﴾.

That is, reluctantly, meaning they do not intend by it the face of Allah. So if anyone sees them, they pray; otherwise they leave and do not pray. ﴿They show off to the people﴾

That is, to the believers, by praying. ﴿And they remember Allah only a little.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas and al-Hasan said: He said that only because they pray it for show and to be heard. If they had intended by it the face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, it would have been much.

Qatadah said: The remembrance of the hypocrites is little because Allah does not accept it, and whatever Allah mentions is little, while whatever Allah accepts is much.

﴿Wavering between that﴾

That is, hesitating and bewildered between disbelief and faith. ﴿Neither to these nor to those﴾: they are not among the believers, so that what is due to the Muslims is due to them, nor are they among the disbelievers, so that what is taken from the disbelievers is taken from them. So they are neither with these nor with those.

Al-Qasim ibn Tahman reported from Qatadah: They are not sincere believers, nor are they openly associating partners with Allah. ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, you will not find for him a way﴾, that is, a path to guidance.

It has been mentioned to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to give an example of the believer, the hypocrite and the disbeliever: they are like a group of three who came to a river. The believer crossed and was saved. Then the hypocrite crossed, and when he nearly reached the believer, the disbeliever called to him: "Come to me, for I fear for you." The believer called to him: "Come to me, for with me is guidance." The hypocrite kept wavering between the two, until he came upon harm and perished. The hypocrite remained in doubt and suspicion until death overtook him while he was in that state.

Abdullah ibn Umar reported from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of the hypocrite is only that of a lone sheep among two flocks, going toward this one at one time and toward that one at another time, not knowing which of them to follow." [Footnote: Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/222, with variation.]

Then He mentioned the believers and forbade them from doing what the hypocrites did.

So the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers. Do you wish to give Allah against yourselves a clear authority?﴾

Then He mentioned the stations of the hypocrites, saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire﴾, meaning at the bottom of a tower of the Fire. Al-Darak and al-Darak are two dialects, like al-Ta'n and al-Ta'n, al-Nahr and al-Nahr, and al-Yabs and al-Yabs.

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: ﴿the lowest depth of the Fire﴾ refers to locked coffins in the Fire, which close over them. ﴿And you will not find for them a helper [an aid].﴾

From Awf, from Abu al-Mughirah al-Qawwas, from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: "Indeed, the most severely punished people on the Day of Resurrection are the group of hypocrites, and those among the People of the Table who disbelieved, and the people of Pharaoh." [Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/182.]

Al-Tha'alibi said: This is confirmed in the Book of Allah, the Exalted. As for the People of the Table, it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, I will punish him with a punishment by which I will not punish anyone among the worlds﴾ [Footnote: Surah al-Ma'idah 5:115.]. As for the people of Pharaoh, it is His saying: ﴿Enter the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment﴾ [Footnote: Surah Ghafir 40:46.]. And as for the hypocrites, it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire﴾ [Footnote: Surah al-Nisa' 4:145.].

﴿Except for those who repent from hypocrisy, and reform their deeds, and hold fast to Allah﴾, that is, they trust in Allah, ﴿and make their religion sincerely for Allah. Those are with the believers in their religion.﴾ Al-Farra' said: "With the believers" means "from among the believers." Al-Qutaybi said: He deviated from their manner of speech out of anger toward them, so He said ﴿those are with the believers﴾ and did not say "those are the believers." ﴿And Allah will give the believers in the Hereafter a great reward﴾, which is Paradise.

The letter ya' was omitted in the script of "yu'ti" just as it is omitted in pronunciation, because the ya' drops from the spoken form due to its being sukun (vowelless) and the lam of "Allah" being sukun. Likewise His saying ﴿the Day the caller calls﴾ [Footnote: Surah Qaf 50:41.], the ya' is omitted in the script for this reason. Likewise ﴿We will call the guardians of Hell﴾ [Footnote: Surah al-'Alaq 96:18.] and ﴿the Day the caller calls﴾ [Footnote: Surah al-Qamar 54:6.]. They said: This ya' is omitted because of the meeting of two sukun letters.

As for His saying ﴿ma kunna nabgh﴾ [Footnote: Surah al-Kahf 18:64.], it is omitted because the kasrah indicates the ya', so it is dropped because the ya' is heavy. It has also been said that the ya' was omitted from "al-muna" and "al-da'" because you say "da'i" and "munad," and the lam was dropped with it just as it was dropped before the entry of the alif and lam.

As for His saying ﴿And by the night when it passes﴾ [Footnote: Surah al-Fajr 89:4.], the ya' is omitted because it falls between verse-endings (ra'us al-ayat), where omission is permitted.

﴿What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe?﴾ In the verse there is inversion and transposition; its sense is: "What would Allah do with your punishment if you believe and are grateful?" This is because gratitude does not benefit without belief in Allah. Allah, the Exalted, made His creation know, by His grace, that His punishing His servants does not increase His kingdom, and His leaving their punishment for their deeds does not diminish His authority. ﴿And Allah is Shakir (Appreciative), Knowing﴾: He appreciates the little of your deeds and knows their multiplication for you, from ten up to seven hundred times.

The people of language said: The origin of shukr (gratitude) is the manifestation of a blessing and speaking about it. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, speak of it﴾ [Footnote: Surah al-Duha 93:11.]. Some people of language mentioned that shukr is derived from the Arab saying "shakur," used when its fat appears from a small amount of fodder. So Allah, the Exalted, named Himself Shakir, though He is pleased from His servants with a little worship after the rank of tawhid (monotheism).

Some of the Mu'tazilah (a rationalist theological school) said: The description of Allah as Shakur and Shakir is by way of metaphor, because shukr in reality is acknowledging the favors of the Benefactor. Since the Eternal, may His remembrance be exalted, rewards the obedient for their obedience, His rewarding them for it was called shukr by extension. In their view, praise (hamd) is not the same as shukr, because hamd is the opposite of blame (dhamm), while shukr is the opposite of kufr (ingratitude). It is said to them: If it is not permissible for the Creator, the Exalted, to be Shakir in the true sense for the reason you mentioned, then it is not permissible for Him to be Muthib (rewarder), because the Muthib is one who repays another for a blessing that was given to him first. Otherwise it would not be permissible for Him to be Shakir in the true sense, and shukr from Allah, the Exalted, is reward.

From the servants, it is obedience, and the real meaning of responding to an act of obedience with something else is this: when you meet Allah's commands with your obedience, you have thanked Him, and when Allah meets your obedience with His reward, He has thanked you for it.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verses 148–152:

﴿Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech﴾, meaning foul speech, ﴿except by one who has been wronged﴾. He has thus permitted the wronged person to seek redress against his wrongdoer by supplication, ﴿and Allah is ever Hearing [of the supplication of the wronged] and Knowing [of the punishment of the wrongdoer]﴾. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿But whoever avenges himself after being wronged, those — there is no path [of blame] against them﴾ [Surah ash-Shura: 41].

Mujahid said: This refers to the guest who arrives and is not hosted, or whose right is denied, or whose hospitality is done badly. Allah has granted him license to mention what was done to him. He claimed that a guest came to a people who treated him badly in hospitality, so he complained about them, and this verse was revealed as a license to complain.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verses 153–159:**

﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a Book from heaven﴾, to the end of the verse. And this is:

Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and Finhas ibn 'Azura said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "If you are truly a prophet, then bring us a Book from heaven, as Musa brought." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a Book from heaven﴾. ﴿They had asked Musa for something greater than that﴾, meaning the seventy whom Musa (peace be upon him) took out to the mountain. ﴿They said, "Show us Allah openly"﴾, meaning plainly and visibly. ﴿So the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing﴾. ﴿Then they took the calf after the clear proofs had come to them﴾. ﴿So We pardoned them for that, and did not uproot them﴾. ﴿And We gave Musa clear authority﴾, to the end of the verse.

Meaning the nine signs.

﴿And We raised the mountain over them by their covenant﴾, and ﴿We said to them, "Enter the gate prostrating"﴾. Qatada said: "We used to say it is one of the gates of Bayt al-Maqdis." It was also said: it is Iliya. It was also said: it is Jericho. It was also said: it is a village of theirs.

﴿And We said to them, "Do not transgress in the Sabbath"﴾, meaning do not wrong by hunting the fish in it. ﴿And We took from them a solemn covenant﴾, meaning the covenant Allah made with them concerning hunting. ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant﴾, meaning: because of their breaking of their covenant. This is like His saying ﴿for a mercy from Allah﴾ (Qur'an 3:159), and ﴿after a little while﴾ (Qur'an 38:11), and ﴿a host there, defeated﴾ (Qur'an 23:40). That is: by mercy, and after a little while, and by a host there.

﴿And their disbelief in the signs of Allah, and their killing of the prophets without right, and their saying, "Our hearts are closed"﴾. Nay, ﴿Allah has sealed them for their disbelief﴾. The construction of the verse is: their breaking of the covenant, their disbelief, their fighting, and their saying, "Allah sealed their hearts," and His cursing them. ﴿So they do not believe﴾, meaning: none of those who denied the messengers believe, except those upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal. Whoever Allah has sealed upon the heart will never believe. Then He said, the Exalted: ﴿except a few﴾, meaning 'Abd Allah ibn Salam. It was also said its meaning is: they do not believe, neither a few nor many.

﴿And their disbelief, and their saying against Maryam a great slander﴾, when they accused her of fornication. ﴿And their saying, "We killed the Messiah, 'Isa son of Maryam, the Messenger of Allah"﴾, to the end of the verse.

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: 'Isa (peace be upon him) passed by a group of Jews, and they said: "The immoral son of the immoral woman, the fornicator son of the fornicating woman." They slandered him and his mother. When 'Isa heard that, he invoked against them and said: "O Allah, You are my Lord and I am Your servant. I was created from a spirit You breathed into me, and I did not accuse anyone of my own accord. O Allah, curse whoever has reviled me and reviled my mother." Allah answered his supplication and transformed those who had reviled him and his mother into swine. When the chief of the Jews saw what had befallen their leader, he was terrified and feared his earlier invocation. The Jews then united in their resolve to kill 'Isa. They gathered around him and began to question him. He said to them: "You have disbelieved, and Allah hates you." They became exceedingly angry at his words and rushed at him to kill him. Allah the Exalted sent Jibril, who brought him into a small room that had an opening in its roof. He ascended with him to heaven through that opening. Yahuda, the chief of the Jews, ordered a man of his companions called Tatyanus to enter the small room and kill him. When Tatyanus entered the room, he did not see 'Isa inside it. They thought that he was fighting him there. Allah the Exalted cast the likeness of 'Isa upon him. When he came out, they thought he was 'Isa, so they killed him and crucified him.

Muqatil: The Jews appointed a watchman over 'Isa who went around with him wherever he went. 'Isa climbed the mountain, and the angel came and seized him by the armpits and raised him to heaven. Allah the Exalted cast the likeness of 'Isa upon the watchman. When they saw him, they thought he was 'Isa, so they killed him and crucified him. He kept saying: "I am not 'Isa, I am so-and-so son of so-and-so," but they did not believe him, and they killed him.

Al-Suddi said: They imprisoned 'Isa twice in a house. A man from among them entered upon them, and Allah the Exalted cast the likeness of 'Isa upon him, and 'Isa was raised to heaven through an opening in the house. They entered upon him and killed him, thinking he was 'Isa.

Qatada: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah, 'Isa son of Maryam, said to his companions: "Which of you will have my likeness cast upon him, and he will be killed?" A man from the people said: "I, O Prophet of Allah." So he was made to resemble 'Isa, and Allah the Exalted prevented 'Isa and raised him to Himself. When Allah raised him to Himself, He clothed him with feathers and dressed him in light, and removed from him the pleasure of food and drink. He became with the angels, circling the Throne. He was human, angelic, heavenly, and earthly.

Wahb ibn Munabbih: Allah revealed to 'Isa when he was thirty years old, then ﴿Allah raised him to Himself﴾ when he was [thirty-]four years old, and his prophethood lasted [three] years.

The words of the Exalted ﴿and their saying﴾, meaning the Jews, ﴿"We killed the Messiah, 'Isa son of Maryam, the Messenger of Allah"﴾. So Allah the Exalted refuted them: ﴿They did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them﴾. ﴿And indeed those who differ concerning him are in doubt about it﴾.

Al-Kalbi: Their disagreement about him: the Jews said, "We killed him and crucified him." A group of the Christians said, "Rather, we killed him." Another group of them said: ﴿They did not kill him, neither these nor those; rather Allah raised him to Himself﴾ [and we are looking at him]. Those who were present when Tatyanus was killed said: "Did you not see that he was killed and crucified?" This is their disagreement and their doubt.

Muhammad ibn Marwan said: It is said that Allah placed the likeness of 'Isa upon the face of Tatyanus, but did not cast upon him the likeness of his body and form. When they killed him and looked at him, they said: "The face is the face of 'Isa, but it is really Tatyanus." It has also been said that the one who was made to resemble 'Isa and crucified in his place was an Israelite man called Iyshu' ibn Madin.

Al-Suddi said: Their disagreement about him was that they said: "If this is 'Isa, then where is our companion? And if this is our companion, then where is 'Isa?" Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him for certain﴾, meaning they did not kill 'Isa with certainty. ﴿Rather, Allah raised him to Himself﴾.

Al-Farra' and al-Qutaybi said: The pronoun in His saying ﴿to Himself﴾ refers to knowledge, meaning: "They did not kill knowledge with certainty," just as it is said, "I killed it by knowledge," and "I killed it by certainty," meaning by opinion and by hadith.

Al-Miqna' al-Kindi said:

"Thus we report of it to the women who are proud ... [....] [[Unreadable text.]] for us, with certainty."

This interpretation is supported by what Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And they did not kill him for certain﴾, meaning: they did not kill him by their assumption with certainty. ﴿And Allah was ever Mighty﴾, meaning strong in exacting vengeance from the Jews. So He gave power over them to Tughra ibn Itsiyanus [[In Tafsir al-Qurtubi (6/10): Butrus ibn Astisanus al-Rumi; in the margin, from another manuscript: Naṭus ibn Istinanus.]] the Roman, who killed a great slaughter among them. ﴿Wise﴾, meaning He passed judgment upon them [with the curse and wrath].

﴿And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in him before his death﴾. Al-Ustadh al-Imam said: Its meaning is: "And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in him." He recited His saying: ﴿And there is none of us but has a known station﴾ (Qur'an 37:164), meaning: there is none of us but has a known station.

And His saying: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾ (Qur'an 19:71), meaning: there is none of you but will pass over it. The poet said:

"If you said, there is no one among her people [who] would not [be] ... she surpasses them in lineage and beauty."

[The verb is written with a kasra on the ta', a dialect of some Arabs; when they gave the ta' a kasra, the hamza was changed into a ya'.]

The meaning: there is no one among her people who surpasses her, then the word was omitted.

From Qatada, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Abu Malik and Ibn Zayd: the two pronouns refer back to 'Isa. The meaning: ﴿there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in 'Isa before the death of 'Isa﴾, when he descends from heaven at the end of time, and then no one of the People of the Book will remain but that he believes in him, until the religion becomes one religion, the religion of Islam. This is the narration of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayra.

Qatada also narrated from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Adam, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The prophets are brothers by different mothers, and their religion is one. I am the closest of people to 'Isa son of Maryam, because there was no prophet between me and him. Soon the son of Maryam will descend among you as a just judge. When you see him, he is a man of medium height, inclining to redness and whiteness, with straight hair, as if his head were dripping, even if no water has touched it. He will break the cross, kill the swine, abolish the jizya, and wealth will overflow. He will fight people for Islam until Allah destroys in his time all religions except Islam, and there will be one prostration to Allah the Exalted. Allah will destroy in his time the lying Dajjal. This is like His saying ﴿for a mercy from Allah﴾ (Qur'an 3:159), and ﴿after a little while﴾ (Qur'an 38:11), and ﴿a host there, defeated﴾ (Qur'an 23:40). That is: by mercy, and after a little while, and by a host there.

﴿And their disbelief in the signs of Allah, and their killing of the prophets without right, and their saying, "Our hearts are closed"﴾. Nay, ﴿Allah has sealed them for their disbelief﴾. The construction of the verse is: their breaking of the covenant, their disbelief, their fighting, and their saying, "Allah sealed their hearts," and His cursing them. ﴿So they do not believe﴾, meaning: none of those who denied the messengers believe, except those upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal. Whoever Allah has sealed upon the heart will never believe. Then He said, the Exalted: ﴿except a few﴾, meaning 'Abd Allah ibn Salam. It was also said its meaning is: they do not believe, neither a few nor many.

﴿And their disbelief, and their saying against Maryam a great slander﴾, when they accused her of fornication. ﴿And their saying, "We killed the Messiah, 'Isa son of Maryam, the Messenger of Allah"﴾, to the end of the verse.

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: 'Isa (peace be upon him) passed by a group of Jews, and they said: "The immoral son of the immoral woman, the fornicator son of the fornicating woman." I was created from a spirit You breathed into me, and I did not accuse anyone of my own accord. O Allah, curse whoever has reviled me and reviled my mother." Allah answered his supplication and transformed those who had reviled him and his mother into swine. When the chief of the Jews saw what had befallen their leader, he was terrified and feared his earlier invocation. The Jews then united in their resolve to kill 'Isa. They gathered around him and began to question him. He said to them: "You have disbelieved, and Allah hates you." They became exceedingly angry at his words and rushed at him to kill him. Allah the Exalted sent Jibril, who brought him into a small room that had an opening in its roof. He ascended with him to heaven through that opening. Yahuda, the chief of the Jews, ordered a man of his companions called Tatyanus to enter the small room and kill him. When Tatyanus entered the room, he did not see 'Isa inside it. They thought that he was fighting him there. Allah the Exalted cast the likeness of 'Isa upon him. When he came out, they thought he was 'Isa, so they killed him and crucified him.

He was human, angelic, heavenly, and earthly.

Wahb ibn Munabbih: Allah revealed to 'Isa when he was thirty years old, then ﴿Allah raised him to Himself﴾ when he was [thirty-]four years old, and his prophethood lasted [three] years.

Those who were present when Tatyanus was killed said: "Did you not see that he was killed and crucified?" This is their disagreement and their doubt.

Muhammad ibn Marwan said: It is said that Allah placed the likeness of 'Isa upon the face of Tatyanus, but did not cast upon him the likeness of his body and form. When they killed him and looked at him, they said: "The face is the face of 'Isa, but it is really Tatyanus." It has also been said that the one who was made to resemble 'Isa and crucified in his place was an Israelite man called Iyshu' ibn Madin.

Al-Suddi said: Their disagreement about him was that they said: "If this is 'Isa, then where is our companion? And if this is our companion, then where is 'Isa?" Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. Al-Miqna' al-Kindi said:

"Thus we report of it to the women who are proud ... [....] [[Unreadable text.]] for us, with certainty."

"If you said, there is no one among her people [who] would not [be] ... she surpasses them in lineage and beauty."

[The verb is written with a kasra on the ta', a dialect of some Arabs; when they gave the ta' a kasra, the hamza was changed into a ya'.]

The meaning: there is no one among her people who surpasses her, then the word was omitted.

The meaning: ﴿there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in 'Isa before the death of 'Isa﴾, when he descends from heaven at the end of time, and then no one of the People of the Book will remain but that he believes in him, until the religion becomes one religion, the religion of Islam. This is the narration of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayra.

"Thus we report of it to the women who are proud ... [....] [[Unreadable text.]] for us, with certainty."

"If you said, there is no one among her people [who] would not [be] ... she surpasses them in lineage and beauty."

Security will prevail upon the earth in his time, so that lions will graze with camels, panthers with cows, wolves with sheep, and children will play with one another. They gathered around him and began to question him. He said to them: "You have disbelieved, and Allah hates you." They became exceedingly angry at his words and rushed at him to kill him. Allah the Exalted sent Jibril, who brought him into a small room that had an opening in its roof. He ascended with him to heaven through that opening. "Thus we report of it to the women who are proud ... [....] [[Unreadable text.]] for us, with certainty."
