Some of them said: The pronoun in ﴿in him﴾ refers back to Muhammad (ﷺ), and the pronoun in ﴿his death﴾ refers back to the People of the Book.

This is the narration of Hammad ibn Humayd from 'Ikrima, who said: No Jew or Christian dies until he believes in Muhammad (ﷺ). It was also said: the pronoun in ﴿in him﴾ refers back to Allah the Exalted: ﴿and there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in Him before he dies﴾ at the moment of witnessing death, but his faith will not benefit him at the time of severity. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾, that 'Isa has conveyed to them the message of his Lord, and acknowledged for himself servitude to Him. This is like His saying: ﴿And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them﴾ (Qur'an 5:117), and that a prophet is a witness over his community. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness﴾ (Qur'an 4:41), to the end of the verse, and He the Exalted said: ﴿And the Day We raise from every nation a witness﴾ (Qur'an 16:84).

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verses 153–159:**

﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a Book from heaven﴾, to the end of the verse. And this is:

Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and Finhas ibn 'Azura said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "If you are truly a prophet, then bring us a Book from heaven, as Musa brought." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a Book from heaven﴾. ﴿They had asked Musa for something greater than that﴾, meaning the seventy whom Musa (peace be upon him) took out to the mountain. ﴿They said, "Show us Allah openly"﴾, meaning plainly and visibly. ﴿So the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing﴾. ﴿Then they took the calf after the clear proofs had come to them﴾. ﴿So We pardoned them for that, and did not uproot them﴾. ﴿And We gave Musa clear authority﴾, to the end of the verse.

Meaning the nine signs.

﴿And We raised the mountain over them by their covenant﴾, and ﴿We said to them, "Enter the gate prostrating"﴾. Qatada said: "We used to say it is one of the gates of Bayt al-Maqdis." It was also said: it is Iliya. It was also said: it is Jericho. It was also said: it is a village of theirs.

﴿And We said to them, "Do not transgress in the Sabbath"﴾, meaning do not wrong by hunting the fish in it. ﴿And We took from them a solemn covenant﴾, meaning the covenant Allah made with them concerning hunting. ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant﴾, meaning: because of their breaking of their covenant. This is like His saying ﴿for a mercy from Allah﴾ (Qur'an 3:159), and ﴿after a little while﴾ (Qur'an 38:11), and ﴿a host there, defeated﴾ (Qur'an 23:40). That is: by mercy, and after a little while, and by a host there.

﴿And their disbelief in the signs of Allah, and their killing of the prophets without right, and their saying, "Our hearts are closed"﴾. Nay, ﴿Allah has sealed them for their disbelief﴾. The construction of the verse is: their breaking of the covenant, their disbelief, their fighting, and their saying, "Allah sealed their hearts," and His cursing them. ﴿So they do not believe﴾, meaning: none of those who denied the messengers believe, except those upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal. Whoever Allah has sealed upon the heart will never believe. Then He said, the Exalted: ﴿except a few﴾, meaning 'Abd Allah ibn Salam. It was also said its meaning is: they do not believe, neither a few nor many.

﴿And their disbelief, and their saying against Maryam a great slander﴾, when they accused her of fornication. ﴿And their saying, "We killed the Messiah, 'Isa son of Maryam, the Messenger of Allah"﴾, to the end of the verse.

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: 'Isa (peace be upon him) passed by a group of Jews, and they said: "The immoral son of the immoral woman, the fornicator son of the fornicating woman." They slandered him and his mother. When 'Isa heard that, he invoked against them and said: "O Allah, You are my Lord and I am Your servant. I was created from a spirit You breathed into me, and I did not accuse anyone of my own accord. O Allah, curse whoever has reviled me and reviled my mother." Allah answered his supplication and transformed those who had reviled him and his mother into swine. When the chief of the Jews saw what had befallen their leader, he was terrified and feared his earlier invocation. The Jews then united in their resolve to kill 'Isa. They gathered around him and began to question him. He said to them: "You have disbelieved, and Allah hates you." They became exceedingly angry at his words and rushed at him to kill him. Allah the Exalted sent Jibril, who brought him into a small room that had an opening in its roof. He ascended with him to heaven through that opening. Yahuda, the chief of the Jews, ordered a man of his companions called Tatyanus to enter the small room and kill him. When Tatyanus entered the room, he did not see 'Isa inside it. They thought that he was fighting him there. Allah the Exalted cast the likeness of 'Isa upon him. When he came out, they thought he was 'Isa, so they killed him and crucified him.

Muqatil: The Jews appointed a watchman over 'Isa who went around with him wherever he went. 'Isa climbed the mountain, and the angel came and seized him by the armpits and raised him to heaven. Allah the Exalted cast the likeness of 'Isa upon the watchman. When they saw him, they thought he was 'Isa, so they killed him and crucified him. He kept saying: "I am not 'Isa, I am so-and-so son of so-and-so," but they did not believe him, and they killed him.

Al-Suddi said: They imprisoned 'Isa twice in a house. A man from among them entered upon them, and Allah the Exalted cast the likeness of 'Isa upon him, and 'Isa was raised to heaven through an opening in the house. They entered upon him and killed him, thinking he was 'Isa.

Qatada: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah, 'Isa son of Maryam, said to his companions: "Which of you will have my likeness cast upon him, and he will be killed?" A man from the people said: "I, O Prophet of Allah." So he was made to resemble 'Isa, and Allah the Exalted prevented 'Isa and raised him to Himself. When Allah raised him to Himself, He clothed him with feathers and dressed him in light, and removed from him the pleasure of food and drink. He became with the angels, circling the Throne. He was human, angelic, heavenly, and earthly.

Wahb ibn Munabbih: Allah revealed to 'Isa when he was thirty years old, then ﴿Allah raised him to Himself﴾ when he was [thirty-]four years old, and his prophethood lasted [three] years.

The words of the Exalted ﴿and their saying﴾, meaning the Jews, ﴿"We killed the Messiah, 'Isa son of Maryam, the Messenger of Allah"﴾. So Allah the Exalted refuted them: ﴿They did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them﴾. ﴿And indeed those who differ concerning him are in doubt about it﴾.

Al-Kalbi: Their disagreement about him: the Jews said, "We killed him and crucified him." A group of the Christians said, "Rather, we killed him." Another group of them said: ﴿They did not kill him, neither these nor those; rather Allah raised him to Himself﴾ [and we are looking at him]. Those who were present when Tatyanus was killed said: "Did you not see that he was killed and crucified?" This is their disagreement and their doubt.

Muhammad ibn Marwan said: It is said that Allah placed the likeness of 'Isa upon the face of Tatyanus, but did not cast upon him the likeness of his body and form. When they killed him and looked at him, they said: "The face is the face of 'Isa, but it is really Tatyanus." It has also been said that the one who was made to resemble 'Isa and crucified in his place was an Israelite man called Iyshu' ibn Madin.

Al-Suddi said: Their disagreement about him was that they said: "If this is 'Isa, then where is our companion? And if this is our companion, then where is 'Isa?" Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him for certain﴾, meaning they did not kill 'Isa with certainty. ﴿Rather, Allah raised him to Himself﴾.

Al-Farra' and al-Qutaybi said: The pronoun in His saying ﴿to Himself﴾ refers to knowledge, meaning: "They did not kill knowledge with certainty," just as it is said, "I killed it by knowledge," and "I killed it by certainty," meaning by opinion and by hadith.

Al-Miqna' al-Kindi said:

"Thus we report of it to the women who are proud ... [....] [[Unreadable text.]] for us, with certainty."

This interpretation is supported by what Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And they did not kill him for certain﴾, meaning: they did not kill him by their assumption with certainty. ﴿And Allah was ever Mighty﴾, meaning strong in exacting vengeance from the Jews. So He gave power over them to Tughra ibn Itsiyanus [[In Tafsir al-Qurtubi (6/10): Butrus ibn Astisanus al-Rumi; in the margin, from another manuscript: Naṭus ibn Istinanus.]] the Roman, who killed a great slaughter among them. ﴿Wise﴾, meaning He passed judgment upon them [with the curse and wrath].

﴿And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in him before his death﴾. Al-Ustadh al-Imam said: Its meaning is: "And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in him." He recited His saying: ﴿And there is none of us but has a known station﴾ (Qur'an 37:164), meaning: there is none of us but has a known station.

And His saying: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾ (Qur'an 19:71), meaning: there is none of you but will pass over it. The poet said:

"If you said, there is no one among her people [who] would not [be] ... she surpasses them in lineage and beauty."

[The verb is written with a kasra on the ta', a dialect of some Arabs; when they gave the ta' a kasra, the hamza was changed into a ya'.]

The meaning: there is no one among her people who surpasses her, then the word was omitted.

From Qatada, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Abu Malik and Ibn Zayd: the two pronouns refer back to 'Isa. The meaning: ﴿there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in 'Isa before the death of 'Isa﴾, when he descends from heaven at the end of time, and then no one of the People of the Book will remain but that he believes in him, until the religion becomes one religion, the religion of Islam. This is the narration of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayra.

Qatada also narrated from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Adam, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The prophets are brothers by different mothers, and their religion is one. I am the closest of people to 'Isa son of Maryam, because there was no prophet between me and him. Soon the son of Maryam will descend among you as a just judge. When you see him, he is a man of medium height, inclining to redness and whiteness, with straight hair, as if his head were dripping, even if no water has touched it. He will break the cross, kill the swine, abolish the jizya, and wealth will overflow. He will fight people for Islam until Allah destroys in his time all religions except Islam, and there will be one prostration to Allah the Exalted. Allah will destroy in his time the lying Dajjal. Security will prevail upon the earth in his time, so that lions will graze with camels, panthers with cows, wolves with sheep, and children will play with one another. Then he will remain on earth for forty years, then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him and bury him. Recite, if you wish: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in him before his death﴾ 'Isa son of Maryam." [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/406, and Sahih Ibn Hibban: 15/233, with variations in all, and Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 6/30.]]

[394] Abu Hurayra repeated it three times.

'Ikrima, Mujahid, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi: The pronoun in the Exalted's saying ﴿in him﴾ refers back to 'Isa son of Maryam, to the People of the Book who believe. The meaning: ﴿there is none of the People of the Book, anyone, but will surely believe in 'Isa before his death﴾ when he sees the angel, and then his faith will not benefit him, because everyone upon whom death descends witnesses himself, until the truth becomes clear to him from falsehood in his religion. This is the narration of Abu Hurayra, from Abu 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas. They said: No Jew or People of the Book will remain but that he believes in 'Isa, even if he is burned, drowned, falls from a height, is attacked by fish, is eaten by a predator, or dies in any other manner. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/27.]]

It was said to Ibn 'Abbas: "What do you think if he falls from the top of a house?" He said: "He will speak it in the air." Then he was asked: "What do you think if one of them has his neck struck?" He said: "His tongue will stammer it."

The reading of Ubayy supports the soundness of this interpretation: "before their death."

Al-Kalbi said: I left Kufa until I came to Tabat, which is a village before Wasit. I stayed there, and I found Shahr ibn Hawshab, and we discussed this verse: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in him﴾. Shahr said: The stipend was distributed that day in Wasit, and al-Hajjaj ordered the stipend to be placed before him. He began to call out a man, and the man would take his stipend by stating what he said. He called my name, and I came on my thin, shabby horse, wearing shabby clothes. When al-Hajjaj saw me, he said to me:

"O Shahr, why do I see your clothes shabby and your horse shabby?" I said: "May Allah set right the Amir. As for what you mentioned about my horse, I bought it, and I did not spare myself good. As for what you mentioned about the clothes, the believer's clothing is what covers his nakedness." He said: "No, but you are a man who dislikes silk and criticizes those who wear it." I said: "I do not dislike that, nor do I criticize those who wear it." He said: Then he called for a piece of silk for him and gave it to me, and I poured it over him. When I wanted to leave, he said to me: "Come here." I returned, and he said: "A verse from the Book of Allah the Exalted. I have never recited it without something stirring in my soul about it." I said: "May Allah set right the Amir, what is it?" He recited this verse: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in him before his death﴾. "Indeed, I am brought a captive from among the Jews and Christians, and I order their necks struck, yet I do not hear him say anything." I said: "When the Jew is present at death, the angels strike his face and his back, and say: 'O enemy of Allah, 'Isa son of Maryam came to you as a servant and a prophet, and you disbelieved in him.' He says: 'I have believed in him, that he is a prophet and a servant.' He believes in him when his belief no longer benefits him. And the Christian is brought, and they say to him: 'O enemy of Allah, 'Isa came to you as a servant and prophet.' He says: 'He is God and the son of God.' He believes in him when his belief no longer benefits him."

Shahr said: Al-Hajjaj looked at me and said: "Who related this hadith to you?" I said: "Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya." He was reclining, so he sat up, then tapped the ground with his staff for a while, then raised his head to me and said: "You have taken it from a clear spring. You have taken it from its source." [[Tafsir al-Qur'an of al-San'ani: 1/178.]]

Al-Kalbi said: I said: "O Shahr, what did you intend by saying: 'Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya told me,' when he disliked him and disliked what came from them?" He said: "I wanted to anger him."

Some of them said: The pronoun in ﴿in him﴾ refers back to Muhammad (ﷺ), and the pronoun in ﴿his death﴾ refers back to the People of the Book.

This is the narration of Hammad ibn Humayd from 'Ikrima, who said: No Jew or Christian dies until he believes in Muhammad (ﷺ). It was also said: the pronoun in ﴿in him﴾ refers back to Allah the Exalted: ﴿and there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in Him before he dies﴾ at the moment of witnessing death, but his faith will not benefit him at the time of severity. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾, that 'Isa has conveyed to them the message of his Lord, and acknowledged for himself servitude to Him. This is like His saying: ﴿And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them﴾ (Qur'an 5:117), and that a prophet is a witness over his community. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness﴾ (Qur'an 4:41), to the end of the verse, and He the Exalted said: ﴿And the Day We raise from every nation a witness﴾ (Qur'an 16:84).

**Then, because of the wrongdoing of those who became Jews**, that is, what was mentioned earlier of their breaking the covenant, their disbelief in the signs, their slander against Mary, and their saying: ﴿We killed the Messiah﴾.

The construction of the verse is ﴿Then, because of the wrongdoing of those who became Jews ... and their hindering [others] from the way of God﴾. *Wa bisaddihim* means they turned themselves and others away from the way of God, from the religion of God, ﴿much﴾. ﴿And their taking of usury, though they had been forbidden it, and their consuming of people's wealth wrongfully﴾, such as the bribes they took from their common folk, and what they took in exchange for the oaths of the books they had written and then claimed were from God, and what they took as bribes in judgment. This is like His saying: ﴿and their consuming of the unlawful gain﴾. We punished them by forbidding them good things, and whenever they committed a grave sin, some of the good things that had been lawful to them were made unlawful. This is shown by His saying: ﴿And to those who became Jews We forbade every animal with claws﴾, and ﴿And to those who became Jews We forbade what We have already related to you before﴾.

**A subtle point.** He said to them, ﴿We forbade them good things﴾, and He said to us, ﴿He makes lawful for them the good things﴾, and He said: ﴿Eat of what God has provided for you, lawful and good﴾. So He did not forbid us anything because of our sins. Just as we were secured from the prohibition of the good things mentioned in this verse, we hope that He will secure us in the Hereafter from the painful punishment. God the Exalted said: ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment﴾, because He combined the two in mention.

**Another subtle point.** In the prohibition of good things He used the term *"upon them"*, and in the punishment the term is general, because the prohibition is a matter that has already occurred, while the punishment is future. He knew that among them there would be those who believe and thereby be secured from punishment. So He said: ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment﴾. Then He excepted the believers among the People of the Book, saying: ﴿But those firm in knowledge among them﴾, meaning the People of the Book are not all alike, as we have mentioned, but rather the firm in knowledge who repent and seek deliverance, ﴿and the believers believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and those who establish prayer﴾.

**They differed on the grammatical case of *al-muqimin* (those who establish).**

Ā'isha and Aban ibn Uthman said: it is a scribal error. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and those who became Jews and the Sabians and the Christians﴾, and His saying: ﴿Indeed these two are sorcerers﴾. Some grammarians said: it is in the accusative of praise, and the Arabs do this in describing a single thing when the description is extended with praise or blame, changing the i'rab of its beginning and middle. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And those who fulfill their covenant when they make it, and the patient in adversity﴾. It was also said that it is in the accusative by an implied verb, its estimate being "I mean the establishers of prayer", in the sense of "mention those who descend, and they are the good ones."

Others said: its position is in the genitive. They differed about what it is attached to. Some of them said: its meaning is ﴿But those firm in knowledge among them, and among the establishers of prayer﴾. It was said its meaning is ﴿they believe in what was revealed to you and to the establishers of prayer﴾. Some said its meaning is ﴿they believe in what was revealed to you of the Book, and the establishers of prayer﴾.

Then they differed about who they are. It was said: they are the angels. It was said: they are the prophets. It was said: they are the believers. It was said: they are the believers among the People of the Book, and they are the firm in knowledge.

**His saying: ﴿Indeed We have revealed to you﴾ and the rest of the verse.** It was revealed concerning the Jews. When God the Exalted revealed His saying: ﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a book from heaven﴾, up to His saying: ﴿And God is ever Mighty and Wise﴾,

when He exposed them, mentioned their defects and sins, they became angry and said: ﴿God has not sent down anything upon a human being﴾. So He revealed ﴿Indeed We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah﴾. God made Noah the second of the Chosen One (ﷺ) in two places in His Book concerning the people of the covenant, by His saying: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah﴾. The second is in the revelation, when He said: ﴿Indeed We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah﴾.

If it is asked: what is the wisdom in placing Noah before the other prophets, when among them is one better than him? It is said: because he was the father of mankind, God the Exalted said: ﴿And We made his descendants the ones who remain﴾. It was also said: because he was the first prophet of the prophets of the law, and the first caller and warner against polytheism.

It was also said: because he was the first whose nation was punished for rejecting his call, and he destroyed the whole earth by his supplication against them, since he was the longest-lived of the prophets.

It was also said: he is the eldest of the prophets, and his miracle was in himself, because he lived a thousand years, his age did not diminish, his strength did not decline, and his hair did not turn gray.

It was also said: because no prophet exerted himself in religion as Noah did, and no one endured the harm of a people as Noah endured. He called his people night and day, openly and secretly. He was struck and insulted until he fainted, and when he recovered he called again and exerted himself. A man among them would take his son by the hand and say: "My son, beware of this one, for he is a lying sorcerer." God the Exalted said: ﴿And the people of Noah before, for they were more wrongdoing and more rebellious﴾. And it was said: [illegible word] on the Day of Resurrection after Muhammad (ﷺ). It was also said: because his station was gratitude. God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed he was a grateful servant﴾. So just as [illegible word] the Qur'an, so also Noah (peace be upon him) [illegible word]. And it was said: the first to be called to Paradise will be those who praise God in every state.

﴿And We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes﴾, who are the sons of Jacob, ﴿and Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon, and We gave David the Psalms﴾. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, and Hamza read *Zuburan* with a damma on the *zay*, meaning the plural of *zabr* and *zabur*, as if He said: "We have written pages after him", i.e., written ones. The rest read it with a fatha on the *zay*, as the proper name of David's book, called the Psalms.

David used to go out into the desert and recite the Psalms, and the scholars of the Children of Israel would stand with him and stand behind him. The people would stand behind the scholars, and the jinn would stand behind the people, the greatest of them behind the greatest, in a vast open land, and the people would stand for this greatest of the jinn. The beasts of the mountains would come, and when they heard David's voice they would stand before him in wonder at what they heard. The birds would come and shade David, Solomon, the jinn and mankind, in a number that none could count but God the Mighty and Majestic; they would flutter over their heads. Then the predators would come and mix with the livestock and the wild animals, because of what they heard, even those who had never seen such a thing. It was said to him: "That is the intimacy of obedience, and this is the loneliness of disobedience."

Talha ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Burda, Abu Musa, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to me: "If you had seen me last night while I was listening to your recitation, you would have been given a flute of the flutes of the family of David." [Sahih al-Bukhari 6/112, chapter on the beauty of voice in recitation; Sahih Muslim 2/193.] [395] I said: "By God, O Messenger of God, if I had known you were listening to my recitation, I would have beautified my voice and made it more melodious."

When Umar (may God be pleased with him) saw him, he would say: "Remind us, O Abu Musa," and he would recite in his presence.

Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, who had reached the Jahiliyya, narrated: "I have never heard a tambourine, nor a cymbal, nor a flute more beautiful than the voice of Abu Musa. He used to lead us in the dawn prayer, and we would wish he would recite Surah al-Baqara because of the beauty of his voice." [Al-Taghanni bil-Qur'an: 26; Siyar A'lam al-Nubala: 3/392.] [[illegible word]] Where the particle of comparison is removed, the meaning is: "as We revealed to Noah and to messengers."

It was also said its meaning is: "and We related to you messengers," in the accusative by an implied verb of mention. In another reading: ﴿And messengers We have related to you before, and messengers We have not related to you﴾, and ﴿And God spoke to Moses directly﴾. This surah is Madinan, sent down after al-An'am, which was Meccan, as the Qur'an was sent down in its parts.

**Messengers as bearers of good news and warners.** God the Exalted named the prophets with these two names, saying: ﴿Mankind was one community, then God sent the prophets as bearers of good news and warners﴾. Then He named the messengers specifically with this name, saying ﴿bearers of good news and warners﴾. Then He named our Prophet specifically with these two names, saying: ﴿Indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of good news, and a warner, that you may believe in God and His Messenger﴾, ﴿so that mankind will have no argument against God after the messengers﴾. Thus they would say: "You did not send us a messenger so that we might follow, nor did You send down a book to us." He said in another verse: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "No one is more jealous than God the Exalted." [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 8/118.] [396] Therefore my Lord has forbidden the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden. No one is more inclined to praise from God the Exalted, and therefore He praised Himself, may His majesty be exalted. No one loves excuse more than God the Exalted, and therefore He sent the messengers and revealed the books.

**﴿But God bears witness to what He has revealed to you﴾** and the rest of the verse. Know that God the Exalted bore witness to seven things. First, to monotheism, when He said: ﴿God bears witness that there is no god but Him﴾. Second, to justice: ﴿And sufficient is God as a witness﴾, ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of God﴾. God the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you﴾, and He said: ﴿Say: God is witness between me and you﴾, and He said: ﴿So bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses﴾. Third, to the deeds of His servants: ﴿On the Day God will raise them all together and inform them of what they did﴾, and He said: ﴿We were witnesses over you﴾, meaning you were engaged in it, and He said: ﴿And God is witness over what you do﴾. Fourth, over all things: ﴿Is it not sufficient that your Lord is a witness over all things?﴾. Fifth, over the lying of the hypocrites: God the Exalted said: ﴿God knows that you are His messenger, and God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars﴾. [Sahih al-Bukhari 6/112, chapter on the beauty of voice in recitation; Sahih Muslim 2/193.] [395] I said: "By God, O Messenger of God, if I had known you were listening to my recitation, I would have beautified my voice and made it more melodious."

When Umar (may God be pleased with him) saw him, he would say: "Remind us, O Abu Musa," and he would recite in his presence.

Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, who had reached the Jahiliyya, narrated: "I have never heard a tambourine, nor a cymbal, nor a flute more beautiful than the voice of Abu Musa. He used to lead us in the dawn prayer, and we would wish he would recite Surah al-Baqara because of the beauty of his voice." [Al-Taghanni bil-Qur'an: 26; Siyar A'lam al-Nubala: 3/392.] [[illegible word]] Where the particle of comparison is removed, the meaning is: "as We revealed to Noah and to messengers."

It was also said its meaning is: "and We related to you messengers," in the accusative by an implied verb of mention. In another reading: ﴿And messengers We have related to you before, and messengers We have not related to you﴾, and ﴿And God spoke to Moses directly﴾. This surah is Madinan, sent down after al-An'am, which was Meccan, as the Qur'an was sent down in its parts.

**Messengers as bearers of good news and warners.** God the Exalted named the prophets with these two names, saying: ﴿Mankind was one community, then God sent the prophets as bearers of good news and warners﴾. Then He named the messengers specifically with this name, saying ﴿bearers of good news and warners﴾. Then He named our Prophet specifically with these two names, saying: ﴿Indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of good news, and a warner, that you may believe in God and His Messenger﴾, ﴿so that mankind will have no argument against God after the messengers﴾. Thus they would say: "You did not send us a messenger so that we might follow, nor did You send down a book to us." He said in another verse: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "No one is more jealous than God the Exalted." [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 8/118.] [396] Therefore my Lord has forbidden the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden. No one is more inclined to praise from God the Exalted, and therefore He praised Himself, may His majesty be exalted. No one loves excuse more than God the Exalted, and therefore He sent the messengers and revealed the books.

**﴿But God bears witness to what He has revealed to you﴾** and the rest of the verse. Know that God the Exalted bore witness to seven things. First, to monotheism, when He said: ﴿God bears witness that there is no god but Him﴾. Second, to justice: ﴿And sufficient is God as a witness﴾, ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of God﴾. God the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you﴾, and He said: ﴿Say: God is witness between me and you﴾, and He said: ﴿So bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses﴾. Third, to the deeds of His servants: ﴿On the Day God will raise them all together and inform them of what they did﴾, and He said: ﴿We were witnesses over you﴾, meaning you were engaged in it, and He said: ﴿And God is witness over what you do﴾. Fourth, over all things: ﴿Is it not sufficient that your Lord is a witness over all things?﴾. Fifth, over the lying of the hypocrites: God the Exalted said: ﴿God knows that you are His messenger, and God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars﴾. Sixth, over the law of the Chosen One: He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Say: God is witness between me and you﴾, meaning a witness over the Qur'an. ﴿But God bears witness to what He has revealed to you, He revealed it with His knowledge﴾, and the rest of the verse.

Ibn Abbas said: The chiefs of Mecca came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, tell us first about your description and attributes in their book." They claimed that they did not recognize him. A group of Jews entered upon the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said to them: "By God, I know that you know that I am the Messenger of God." [397]

They said: "We know." So God the Exalted revealed: ﴿If they deny you and reject you, but God bears witness to what He has revealed to you, He revealed it with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness, and sufficient is God as a witness.﴾

**Then, because of the wrongdoing of those who became Jews**, that is, what was mentioned earlier of their breaking the covenant, their disbelief in the signs, their slander against Mary, and their saying: ﴿We killed the Messiah﴾.

The construction of the verse is ﴿Then, because of the wrongdoing of those who became Jews ... and their hindering [others] from the way of God﴾. *Wa bisaddihim* means they turned themselves and others away from the way of God, from the religion of God, ﴿much﴾. ﴿And their taking of usury, though they had been forbidden it, and their consuming of people's wealth wrongfully﴾, such as the bribes they took from their common folk, and what they took in exchange for the oaths of the books they had written and then claimed were from God, and what they took as bribes in judgment. This is like His saying: ﴿and their consuming of the unlawful gain﴾. We punished them by forbidding them good things, and whenever they committed a grave sin, some of the good things that had been lawful to them were made unlawful. This is shown by His saying: ﴿And to those who became Jews We forbade every animal with claws﴾, and ﴿And to those who became Jews We forbade what We have already related to you before﴾.

**A subtle point.** He said to them, ﴿We forbade them good things﴾, and He said to us, ﴿He makes lawful for them the good things﴾, and He said: ﴿Eat of what God has provided for you, lawful and good﴾. So He did not forbid us anything because of our sins. Just as we were secured from the prohibition of the good things mentioned in this verse, we hope that He will secure us in the Hereafter from the painful punishment. God the Exalted said: ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment﴾, because He combined the two in mention.

**Another subtle point.** In the prohibition of good things He used the term *"upon them"*, and in the punishment the term is general, because the prohibition is a matter that has already occurred, while the punishment is future. He knew that among them there would be those who believe and thereby be secured from punishment. So He said: ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment﴾. Then He excepted the believers among the People of the Book, saying: ﴿But those firm in knowledge among them﴾, meaning the People of the Book are not all alike, as we have mentioned, but rather the firm in knowledge who repent and seek deliverance, ﴿and the believers believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and those who establish prayer﴾.

**They differed on the grammatical case of *al-muqimin* (those who establish).**

Ā'isha and Aban ibn Uthman said: it is a scribal error. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and those who became Jews and the Sabians and the Christians﴾, and His saying: ﴿Indeed these two are sorcerers﴾. Some grammarians said: it is in the accusative of praise, and the Arabs do this in describing a single thing when the description is extended with praise or blame, changing the i'rab of its beginning and middle. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And those who fulfill their covenant when they make it, and the patient in adversity﴾. It was also said that it is in the accusative by an implied verb, its estimate being "I mean the establishers of prayer", in the sense of "mention those who descend, and they are the good ones."

Others said: its position is in the genitive. They differed about what it is attached to. Some of them said: its meaning is ﴿But those firm in knowledge among them, and among the establishers of prayer﴾. It was said its meaning is ﴿they believe in what was revealed to you and to the establishers of prayer﴾. Some said its meaning is ﴿they believe in what was revealed to you of the Book, and the establishers of prayer﴾.

Then they differed about who they are. It was said: they are the angels. It was said: they are the prophets. It was said: they are the believers. It was said: they are the believers among the People of the Book, and they are the firm in knowledge.

**His saying: ﴿Indeed We have revealed to you﴾ and the rest of the verse.** It was revealed concerning the Jews. When God the Exalted revealed His saying: ﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a book from heaven﴾, up to His saying: ﴿And God is ever Mighty and Wise﴾,

when He exposed them, mentioned their defects and sins, they became angry and said: ﴿God has not sent down anything upon a human being﴾. So He revealed ﴿Indeed We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah﴾. God made Noah the second of the Chosen One (ﷺ) in two places in His Book concerning the people of the covenant, by His saying: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah﴾. The second is in the revelation, when He said: ﴿Indeed We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah﴾.

If it is asked: what is the wisdom in placing Noah before the other prophets, when among them is one better than him? It is said: because he was the father of mankind, God the Exalted said: ﴿And We made his descendants the ones who remain﴾. It was also said: because he was the first prophet of the prophets of the law, and the first caller and warner against polytheism.

It was also said: because he was the first whose nation was punished for rejecting his call, and he destroyed the whole earth by his supplication against them, since he was the longest-lived of the prophets.

It was also said: he is the eldest of the prophets, and his miracle was in himself, because he lived a thousand years, his age did not diminish, his strength did not decline, and his hair did not turn gray.

It was also said: because no prophet exerted himself in religion as Noah did, and no one endured the harm of a people as Noah endured. He called his people night and day, openly and secretly. He was struck and insulted until he fainted, and when he recovered he called again and exerted himself. A man among them would take his son by the hand and say: "My son, beware of this one, for he is a lying sorcerer." God the Exalted said: ﴿And the people of Noah before, for they were more wrongdoing and more rebellious﴾. And it was said: [illegible word] on the Day of Resurrection after Muhammad (ﷺ). It was also said: because his station was gratitude. God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed he was a grateful servant﴾. So just as [illegible word] the Qur'an, so also Noah (peace be upon him) [illegible word]. And it was said: the first to be called to Paradise will be those who praise God in every state.

﴿And We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes﴾, who are the sons of Jacob, ﴿and Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon, and We gave David the Psalms﴾. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, and Hamza read *Zuburan* with a damma on the *zay*, meaning the plural of *zabr* and *zabur*, as if He said: "We have written pages after him", i.e., written ones. The rest read it with a fatha on the *zay*, as the proper name of David's book, called the Psalms.

David used to go out into the desert and recite the Psalms, and the scholars of the Children of Israel would stand with him and stand behind him. The people would stand behind the scholars, and the jinn would stand behind the people, the greatest of them behind the greatest, in a vast open land, and the people would stand for this greatest of the jinn. The beasts of the mountains would come, and when they heard David's voice they would stand before him in wonder at what they heard. The birds would come and shade David, Solomon, the jinn and mankind, in a number that none could count but God the Mighty and Majestic; they would flutter over their heads. Then the predators would come and mix with the livestock and the wild animals, because of what they heard, even those who had never seen such a thing. It was said to him: "That is the intimacy of obedience, and this is the loneliness of disobedience."

Talha ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Burda, Abu Musa, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to me: "If you had seen me last night while I was listening to your recitation, you would have been given a flute of the flutes of the family of David." Then He named the messengers specifically with this name, saying ﴿bearers of good news and warners﴾. Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 4, verses 167–173:

Indeed, those who disbelieved and barred (others) from the way of Allah have strayed far astray. Indeed, those who disbelieved and did wrong, meaning the Jews, whom Allah the Exalted knew would not believe, Allah will not forgive them nor guide them to a path, meaning the religion of Islam, except the path of Hell, meaning Judaism, to abide therein forever. And that is ever easy for Allah. Up to His saying, the Exalted: "O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess (ghuluww) in your religion." The verse was revealed concerning the Nestorians, the Jacobites (al-Maria'qubiyya), the Melkites (al-Malikaniyya) and the Marqusiyya, and they are the Christians of Najran. This was because the Jacobites said to Jesus: "He is God." The Nestorians said: "He is the son of God." The Marqusiyya said: "He is the Spirit of God." So Allah the Exalted revealed: "O People of the Scripture," meaning, O People of the Gospel, who are the Christians, "do not commit excess (ghuluww) in your religion," that is, do not be strict in your religion so that you fabricate lies against Me. The root of ghuluww is going beyond the limit in everything. It is said: "He exaggerated (ghala) with the girl, her flesh and her bones," when she hastened into youth and surpassed her peers (la-dat), (the la-dat being plural of lidda: the age-mate, the one born with you and raised with you), and he exaggerates with her, ghuluwwan and ghala'an.

Khalid al-Makhzumi:

"Slender, with a waist girdled in fine form, in the first flush of youth, the bones of her grew in exaggeration."

[Lisan al-Arab: 15/132.]

"And do not say about Allah except the truth." Do not say that Allah has partners or a son. Then He explained the state and description of Jesus, so He said: "The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, is only a messenger of Allah." He is the one who is wiped (mamsuh), purified of sins and defilements that are found in people, just as a thing is wiped of the harm that is in it so that it becomes pure. Jesus son of Mary is not the son of God but the Messenger of God [and His servant. He said: "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet."] By this He refuted both the Jews and the Christians together. "And His word," meaning His saying "Be!" and he was, a human being without a father. This is His saying: "Indeed the example of Jesus to Allah is like that of Adam; He created him from dust" (Al 'Imran 3:59), up to the end of the verse. It has also been said: it is the good news that Allah gave to Mary about Jesus and His message to her through the tongue of Gabriel. This is His saying: "When the angels said: O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good news of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah" (Al 'Imran 3:45). He also said: "Confirming a word from Allah... which He cast (alqaha) to Mary," meaning He informed her and made her aware of it, just as it is said: "I cast to you a good word" (alqaytu ilayka kalima hasana). "And a spirit from Him," up to the end of the verse.

Some of them said: its meaning is "and a breath from Him," because Gabriel blew into the sleeve (of Mary's garment), and she conceived by the permission of Allah. So He said: "and a spirit from Him," because by His command was the Messiah. And perhaps (it is called spirit) because it is a wind that comes out of the spirit [thus in the original]. Dhu al-Rumma described the sparks of fire that fall from the flint:

"I said to him: strike it toward yourself and kindle it with your breath, and make for it a fuel of appropriate measure."

[Lisan al-Arab: 2/460, where it reads: "and make it for it a fuel (qutayya)," and so in Taj al-Arus.]

"And make for it fuel by measure." What indicates this is His saying: "And she who guarded her chastity" (al-Anbiya 21:91), up to the end of the verse. This is the meaning of the saying of 'Udhra.

Abu 'Ubayda said: he was a human being by the reviving of him by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. What indicates this is the saying of al-Suddi: "and a spirit from Him," meaning created from His presence. It has also been said: its meaning is "and a mercy from Allah," Jesus being a mercy to whoever witnessed and believed in him. What indicates this is His saying in al-Mujadila: "and He strengthened them with a spirit from Him" (al-Mujadila 58:22), meaning He strengthened them with a mercy from Him. So the "spirit" here is by revelation: He revealed to Mary the good news, and revealed to Mary the Messiah, and revealed that he is the son of Mary. What indicates this is [His saying: "with a spirit from Him"], meaning by revelation. And He said in Ha Mim, the Believer: "He casts the spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants" (Ghafir 40:15). And He said: "And thus We revealed to you a spirit of Our command" (al-Shura 42:52), meaning Our revelation. It has also been said: "guide us by the spirit of Gabriel." So He said: "And His word which He cast to Mary." And He also cast to her a spirit from Him, which is Gabriel. What indicates this is His saying in al-Nahl: "Say: the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus) has brought it down" (al-Nahl 16:102). Its counterpart in al-Shu'ara is: "The Trustworthy Spirit (al-Ruh al-Amin) has descended with it" (al-Shu'ara 26:193). He also said: "And We strengthened him with the Holy Spirit" (al-Baqara 2:87). And He said: "He sends down the angels with the spirit by His command" (al-Nahl 16:2), meaning Gabriel. He said: "Then We sent to her Our Spirit" (Maryam 19:17). The Spirit is the revelation, meaning by the attribution to Him for specification, as in His saying to Adam, peace be upon him: "And I breathed into him of My spirit" (al-Hijr 15:29).

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard the Master Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: Harun al-Rashid had a Christian slave who was a physician, and he was the most beautiful of Allah's creation in face, the most complete in manners, and the most gathered in the qualities by which one seeks access to kings. Al-Rashid was fond of his becoming Muslim, but he refused, and al-Rashid kept giving him hopes [but he refused]. So one day he said to him: "Why do you not believe?" He said: "Because in your Book there is a proof against whoever adopts it." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "His saying: 'and His word which He cast to Mary, and a spirit from Him.' Is this not the religion of the Christians, that Jesus is a part of Him?" [So the heart of al-Rashid was distressed (ghamma) by that], and he summoned the scholars and jurists, but none of them could remove that doubt, until it was said: the pilgrims of Khurasan arrived, and among them was a man called Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from the people of Marw, an imam among the people of the Qur'an. He summoned him and brought him together with the slave. He asked the slave, and he repeated his statement. Ali ibn al-Husayn was struck silent at the moment and could not answer, so he said: "O Commander of the Faithful, Allah has known in His prior knowledge that such a youth would question me in your assembly, and that His Book has not been devoid of my answer, and it is not present to me at this moment. I vow to Allah that I will not eat until I reach what is in it, its due, if Allah wills." Then he entered a dark room and closed its door on himself, [and occupied himself] in reciting the Qur'an until he reached the sura al-Jathiya, "And He subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him" (al-Jathiya 45:13). He cried out at the top of his voice: "Open the door, for I have found it!" They opened (the door), and he called the slave and recited the verse to him in the presence of al-Rashid, and said: "If His saying 'and a spirit from Him' requires that Jesus be a part of Him, then it must be that whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is a part of Him." The Christian was silenced, became Muslim, and al-Rashid rejoiced greatly, and Ali ibn al-Husayn was given a splendid gift. When he returned to Marw, he composed the book "al-Nazair fi al-Qur'an," a book which has no equal in its field.

"So believe in Allah and His messengers, and do not say: Three." Abu 'Ubayda said: its meaning is, "and do not say: they are three."

Al-Zajjaj said: "Do not say: our gods are three." This is because they said: Father, Son and the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus). "Desist from your disbelief, it is better for you," up to His saying: "The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah" (al-Nisa 4:172).

This was because the delegation of Najran said: "O Muhammad, why do you disparage our companion?" He said: "And who is your companion?" They said: "Jesus." He said: "And what should I say?" They said: "You say that he is the servant of Allah and His messenger." He said to them: "It is no shame for Jesus to be a servant of Allah." They said: "Indeed." So the verse was revealed: "The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah," up to the end of the verse.

He did not feel disdain, nor did he consider himself great, nor did he [conclude (yakhtatim)] [thus in the original]. Its root is anfa (disdain) and avoidance, and its root in the language comes from their saying: "I wiped the tears (nakaftu al-dam'a) when I removed them with my finger from my cheek."

The poet said:

"They spent the night, and had it not been for what is recounted of them from the oath, the tears would not have been wiped from your eyes."

"Nor do the angels brought near." They are the bearers of the Throne; they do not refuse to be servants of Allah. Because among the disbelievers there were those who took the angels as gods, so He mentioned them, then warned them, saying: "Whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant, He will gather them all to Himself" (al-Nisa 4:172).

The arrogant and the humble. "As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will pay them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty" in [the multiplication] of what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

"And as for those who disdained His worship and were arrogant against prostration, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper" (al-Nisa 4:173). Then He said: "Allah is the Protector of those who believe" (al-Baqara 2:257).

They opened (the door), and he called the slave and recited the verse to him in the presence of al-Rashid, and said: "If His saying 'and a spirit from Him' requires that Jesus be a part of Him, then it must be that whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is a part of Him." The Christian was silenced, became Muslim, and al-Rashid rejoiced greatly, and Ali ibn al-Husayn was given a splendid gift. When he returned to Marw, he composed the book "al-Nazair fi al-Qur'an," a book which has no equal in its field.

"So believe in Allah and His messengers, and do not say: Three." Abu 'Ubayda said: its meaning is, "and do not say: they are three."

Al-Zajjaj said: "Do not say: our gods are three." This is because they said: Father, Son and the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus). "Desist from your disbelief, it is better for you," up to His saying: "The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah" (al-Nisa 4:172).

This was because the delegation of Najran said: "O Muhammad, why do you disparage our companion?" He said: "And who is your companion?" They said: "Jesus." He said: "And what should I say?" They said: "You say that he is the servant of Allah and His messenger." He said to them: "It is no shame for Jesus to be a servant of Allah." They said: "Indeed." So the verse was revealed: "The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah," up to the end of the verse.

He did not feel disdain, nor did he consider himself great, nor did he [conclude (yakhtatim)] [thus in the original]. Its root is anfa (disdain) and avoidance, and its root in the language comes from their saying: "I wiped the tears (nakaftu al-dam'a) when I removed them with my finger from my cheek."

The poet said:

"They spent the night, and had it not been for what is recounted of them from the oath, the tears would not have been wiped from your eyes."

"Nor do the angels brought near." They are the bearers of the Throne; they do not refuse to be servants of Allah. Because among the disbelievers there were those who took the angels as gods, so He mentioned them, then warned them, saying: "Whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant, He will gather them all to Himself" (al-Nisa 4:172).

The arrogant and the humble. "As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will pay them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty" in [the multiplication] of what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

"And as for those who disdained His worship and were arrogant against prostration, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper" (al-Nisa 4:173). Then He said: "Allah is the Protector of those who believe" (al-Baqara 2:257).

The Qur'anic phrase ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you a proof from your Lord﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), up to His words ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalala (the estate of one who leaves neither ascendant nor descendant)﴾.

Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir and Abu al-Zubayr narrated from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: "I fell ill, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to visit me, together with Abu Bakr. When they reached me, they found that I had fainted. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed ablution, then poured some of his ablution water over me, and I regained consciousness. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how should I dispose of my wealth? I have seven sisters, and I have no child and no father.' He did not answer me at first. Then he went out and left me. Then he returned to me and said: 'O Jabir, I do not see you dying from this illness of yours. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed concerning your sisters, and has assigned them two-thirds.'" [Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/55] [398], and he recited this verse ﴿They ask you for a ruling﴾ to its end.

Jabir used to say: "This verse was revealed concerning me." [Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/4, hadith 2887.]

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas: this verse was revealed concerning Jabir and his sister. He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have a sister, so what is due to me [and what is due to her]?"

Then this verse was revealed, and it began with the man. It is said that he died before his sister.

Sa'id, from Qatada, said: Some of them said "concerning the kalala," so they said, "O Prophet of Allah (ﷺ)," and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse ﴿They ask you for a ruling﴾, meaning they seek information from you and question you. ﴿Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalala﴾.

Al-Sha'bi said: Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, differed concerning the kalala. Abu Bakr said: it is what remains apart from a child. Umar said: it is what remains apart from a father.

Then Umar said: "Truly, I am ashamed before Allah to oppose Abu Bakr."

Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "That the Prophet (ﷺ) had explained it among them would be dearer to us than the world and all that is in it: the kalala, the caliphate, and the forms of usury."

Muhammad ibn Sirin said: This verse was revealed while the Prophet (ﷺ) was on his journey to the Farewell Pilgrimage, and beside him was Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman [and beside him was Umar]. The Prophet (ﷺ) conveyed it to Hudhayfa, and Hudhayfa conveyed it to Umar, who was riding behind Hudhayfa. When Umar became caliph, he asked Hudhayfa about it, hoping that he had its explanation. Hudhayfa said to him: "By Allah, you are truly foolish if you thought that your rule would compel me to tell you what I did not tell you on that day when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) imparted it to me. [By Allah, I will never add anything to it, ever]." Umar said: "I did not mean this, may Allah have mercy on you." Then Umar said: "Whoever I explained it to, it was not made clear to me, and whoever witnessed it, you made it understood to him, but I did not understand it." [Al-Musannaf of Abd al-Razzaq: 10/304, hadith 19193, abridged.]

Tariq ibn Shihab said: Umar took a shoulder blade, gathered the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), and said: "I will certainly issue a ruling concerning the kalala, one that women will speak of in their chambers." Then a snake came out of the house, and they dispersed. They said: "If Allah had wished to complete this matter, He would have completed it."

Abu al-Khayr said: A man asked Utba about the kalala. He said: "Do you not wonder at this? He asks me about the kalala. No matter ever occupied the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) as much as the kalala occupied them" [in the source: "troubled"] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/60].

Umar addressed the people on Friday and said: "By Allah, I leave after me nothing more important than the kalala. I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it, and he was never as harsh with me about anything as he was about it, until people criticized me and he said: 'The verse at the end of Surah al-Nisa suffices you.'" [Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/58; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/594.] It was also called the Summer Verse, because it was revealed in summer.

Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said in his sermon: "Truly, the verse that Allah revealed in Surah al-Nisa concerning the obligatory shares was revealed concerning the child and the parent. The second verse is concerning the husband, the wife and the siblings from the mother's side. The verse with which Surah al-Nisa concludes concerns some of them."
